Cardinals' One-Word James Conner Update Raises Questions
full_text:
Arizona Cardinals fans have been wondering where running back James Conner is at in his return to play.
So too has everybody else.
It's been well over a full calander year since Conner went down with a right foot injury (first described as an ankle before eventually corrected by then-coach Jonathan Gannon). Conner, after just three weeks, was ruled out for the season but managed to make a return in 2026's iteration of training camp.
Conner didn't participate in any team drills but did do individual portions through the beginning of camp. He ultimately wasn't spotted at practice in any capacity towards the end of preseason, and he hasn't featured in any sort of game during the 2026 season.
We're now seven games deep into the regular season and Conner has yet to be pulled from his injured reserve slot, which does have a designation to return.
Is Conner going to play at all this season?
"Potentially," said Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur when asked about Conner returning.
"That's all I could give you there."
This conflicts from what Cardinals general manager Monti Ossenfort told Arizona Sports 98.7 FM last week, where he said Conner is "really close" to a return.
What's going on with Conner?
The veteran running back restructured his contract to stay with the Cardinals this offseason after being labeled as a cut candidate. When Arizona signed Tyler Allgeier in free agency and drafted Jeremiyah Love with the third overall pick, many were curious to see how Conner would fit into the Cardinals' backfield.
There was hope he would be healthy and fully ready to make an impact in LaFleur's new offense, though that's been nowhere close to the case.
While Conner is a coveted locker room leader, Bam Knight's recent surge in play does make Conner expendable. As the league's trade deadline approaches, he's very much a candidate for a deal.
It's also possible the Cardinals would do right by the veteran running back and release him if that's what Conner desires. Teams looking to make a playoff push are constantly looking for players such as Conner for talent and leadership reasons.
The Cardinals, without Conner, have struggled in the run game. Arizona ranks in the bottom ten for team rushing yards per game and average yards per carry this season.
Arizona's been very silent of where Conner stands during his rehab, almost to concerning levels.

title: Cardinals RB Jeremiyah Love Gets Exciting Week 8 Injury Update
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are getting Jeremiyah Love back to the practice field this week.
Love, who has missed the last two games with an ankle injury, will take the field on Wednesday as the Cardinals prepare to face the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8.
"We'll see as the week goes," head coach Mike LaFleur said at his Monday press conference. "Jeremiyah will be out there at practice on Wednesday, so we'll see how the week goes."
Love, the third overall pick, initially dealt with a different ankle injury during Arizona's preseason. However, up until Week 6, he hadn't missed a regular season game.
The rookie running back has been managing his new ankle injury for weeks before the Cardinals made the call to shelf the Notre Dame product. Arizona said injured reserve, which would require Love to miss at least four weeks, wasn't on the table.
The Cardinals dropped to 2-5 after their Week 7 loss to the Denver Broncos on Sunday. Their backfield has been headlined by Bam Knight and Tyler Allgeier. Knight, particularly, has been strong in Love's absence.
"Bam's doing a really good job. He's running the ball well and obviously brought an explosive element to the run game that was needed," LaFleur said when asked if Knight would still have a role. "So yeah, Bam will still have a role, but I'm excited to get Jeremiyah back, particularly at practice this week."
Arizona's rushing offense ranks in the bottom ten of NFL teams for rushing yards per game (96) and average yards per carry (3.7).
There's hope Love's emergence back into the lineup can also add a new layer to the Cardinals' passing attack, where Love's route-running against linebacker matchups should be extremely advantageous for their struggling offense.
We'll get our first injury report for Week 8 after Wednesday's practice, though this is undoubtedly a massive step in the right direction for Love's return.

title: Cardinals' Josh Sweat Trade Rumors Heat Up as 2 New Teams Emerge
full_text:
ARIZONA — Rumors around Arizona Cardinals OLB Josh Sweat continue to materialize as we approach the league's Nov. 10 trade deadline.
Yesterday, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler suggested the Dallas Cowboys were interested in Sweat's services. Today, after Arizona's Week 7 loss to the Denver Broncos, two other teams have been thrown into the mix by NFL insider Jordan Schultz.
"I think we're heading to a very active NFL trade deadline. We could see anywhere from 12 to call it 20 trades. And two teams I'm watching very closely? The 49ers and Bears. I've heard both teams connected to several defensive players including rushers Josh Sweat, Khalil Mack and also DeForest Buckner," Schultz said on The Pivot :
Jordan Schultz links the Bears to Josh Sweat, Khalil Mack and DeForest Buckner + names not necessarily on the trade block. He adds that he’s be shocked if Chicago didn’t make a move before the NFL Trade Deadline. pic.twitter.com/idX357lnLz
The 49ers would be an interesting move, as trading within the division is typically a no-no. However, San Francisco could sweeten that deal by paying a little extra to get Sweat on their team.
The Bears, meanwhile, would complete the foursome of NFC North teams who have former prominent Cardinals on their squad. Sweat, if acquired by Chicago, would see familiar faces in Detroit (Drew Petzing), Green Bay (Jonathan Gannon) and Minnesota (Kyler Murray).
Something both teams have in common? Success. The 49ers are 6-1 while the Bears are 5-2. Both are clearly looking to make a Super Bowl push, which could lead to a potential bidding war for Sweat's services.
Sweat has two sacks on the regular season after a chaotic offseason surrounding the health of his knee, absence in the offseason and reported trade interest/requests after the Cardinals fired Gannon.
Sweat is reportedly hoping to land a new contract, as the final two years of his deal carry no guaranteed money. He also might be looking to jump ship from a 2-5 football team after failing to help build success in the desert.
Speaking with reporters earlier this offseason, Cardinals general manager Monti Ossenfort shot down any truth to trade rumors around Arizona's top pass rusher.
"I'd say [trade] discussions that come by that, there's always a lot of talk that goes around that. We have no interest in trading Josh. We're excited to have him," he said back in August. "Some of those discussions [we're] going to keep private. But excited to have Josh here, [he] had a great year last year. Excited for more good things out of him this year."
Of course, things can change, especially if the price is right.

title: Cardinals WR Reveals He's Having Season-Ending Surgery
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are set to lose wide receiver Jalen Brooks for the rest of the 2026 season.
Brooks, in an Instagram post on Monday, says he has to get an "emergency surgery" on his wrist and added he, "doesn't need any phone calls, just prayers."
Brooks met with local reporters after the Cardinals' Week 7 loss to the Denver Broncos and appeared to be in obvious discomfort when speaking. He finished his post with:
"I'll be done for the season, God is in control of my next steps much love."
Arizona Cardinals WR Jalen Brooks announces via his Instagram that he's done for the season following an injury to his wrist. pic.twitter.com/Y4jCi3BdTc
This is a big blow for the Cardinals' offense, who was counting on its depth receivers to step up after trading away Marvin Harrison Jr. weeks ago. After scoring under 20 points in back to back weeks, they'll be under an even bigger microscope as injuries accrue across the board, from the offensive line to running backs and now receivers.
Brooks was a productive preseason player who was buried in a Cardinals offense headlined by Trey McBride and Michael Wilson. However, it was Brooks who was propelled into more playing time after Harrison was dealt.
Brooks had a huge catch in Arizona's upset win over the Los Angeles Rams two weeks ago, which helped the Cardinals kick a game-winning field goal just moments after Brooks dropped an open pass.
“How amazing is just having to be resilient in this league?" Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said when asked about Brooks after Week 6.
"... There's always a chance you're going to have to go out there and have to win it. And for him to make that play and Jacoby to rip it in there, it just says a lot about just that Jalen Brooks and his mindset. And it's cool. A lot of good learning moments for for these guys. We can start plugging them in in the redzone and maybe he doesn't get into this situation.”
Brooks will finish his 2026 season with five receptions for 81 yards. Arizona will look to Simi Fehoko and Reggie Virgil as players who can step up in his role. With Wilson and McBride commanding attention, there should be ample opportunity for backup receivers to make plays for the Cardinals.
The Cardinals travel to Dallas to face the Cowboys in Week 8. LaFleur is set to meet with reporters later this afternoon and is expected to confirm the news of losing Brooks for the season.

title: 3 Key Takeaways From Arizona Cardinals’ Week 7 Loss
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals were unable to build on their upset victory against Los Angeles last weekend. Instead, the Cardinals flew back down to earth, falling to the Denver Broncos 30–16 in Week 7.
With this defeat, the Cardinals have now lost 10 consecutive home games.
"It sucks. You hate losing," head coach Mike LaFleur said postgame. "I hate playing not-good football more than I hate losing cause good football can lead to wins unless they make so many plays.
"Credit to them. That is a good football team. It's a well-coached football team. They're going to win a lot of football games, but I know we can play better than that."
Arizona's offense needs to execute better in the red area. Against the Broncos Sunday, the Cardinals went 1-for-5 inside the red zone.
In their last ten red zone trips, Arizona has scored only one touchdown.
"We're moving the ball, and we're not finishing. That's a collective deal with coaching and playing," Mike LaFleur told J.P. Shadrick and A.Q. Shipley on the Cardinals Locker Room Show.
"There was opportunities to make plays. There's opportunities to call better plays. There's opportunities to have some better scheme. So it's a collective deal right now. Again, like I told the guys, we're not going to panic after one week. But now we've had two weeks where we haven't cashed it in."
Due to their recent struggles, the Cardinals now rank last in the league in red-zone scoring percentage (touchdowns only) at 42.8%, per TeamRankings.
Jacoby Brissett is going to need an ice bath after this one. The Cardinals quarterback was under siege the entire afternoon.
Denver's "Orange Crush" defense recorded 13 quarterback hits and a season-high 27 quarterback pressures, per Next Gen Stats.
"He got hit a little bit," LaFleur said to the media postgame. "With their defensive structure, you knew we were going to have to get it over the top. When you do that, you're going to hold onto the ball a little longer."
Coach LaFleur wasn't lying. Brissett 2.82-second time to throw was his longest this season, but it was all for naught. Per Next Gen Stats, the Cardinals allowed a pressure rate of 50.9%. Simply put, Arizona's offensive line was outclassed against Denver's front.
The Broncos didn't come into this week's matchup as an offensive juggernaut. Per Next Gen Stats, Denver ranked 26th in scoring (19.0 PPG), 31st in yards per game (252 YPG), and 32nd in yards per play (4.4).
However, against the Cardinals, the Broncos matched their season high, scoring 30 points. On the day, Denver produced 377 total yards of offense, and 6.7 yards per play.
The Cardinals continue to struggle on defense. They have allowed 30+ points in five of their last six games. Through seven weeks, Arizona's defense has allowed the most points in the NFL.

title: The Good, The Bad, The Ugly: Broncos Spoil Larry Fitzgerald's Jersey Retirement
full_text:
Sunday was supposed to celebrate the career of Arizona Cardinals Hall of Fame wide receiver Larry Fitzgerald. In some sick irony, the Cardinals did their best impression of the many teams Fitzgerald played on  -- falling short of a victory.
Behind a backdrop of orange and navy in Glendale, Arizona came back down to earth from last week's highs, falling back into the loss column, 30-16 to the Denver Broncos at State Farm Stadium. The Cardinals are now 2-5 on the season ahead of its date with the Dallas Cowboys next weekend in Arlington, Texas.
Here is the good, the bad, and the ugly from Arizona's Week 7 performance:
A gold jacket in Canton awaits McBride at the end of his career if he maintains his dominance on the football field. Like Larry Legend, who attended this afternoon, McBride was once again the lone bright spot for a struggling football team.
McBride had his best statistical game of the season, reeling in 10 receptions on 13 targets for a season-high 111 yards and Arizona's only touchdown of the game. The Cardinal tight end leads his position group in the NFL with 49 catches.
Arizona struggled to finish drives and adapt to pressure, settling for field goals or punts on drives that ended quickly. McBride's largest catch of the afternoon, a 27-yard pickup, was negated by a sack on the next play and two incompletions, ending the Cardinals' first fourth-quarter drive on downs.
With no Jeremiyah Love for a second consecutive week, the brunt of the Cardinals' rushing attack fell on the shoulders of Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight once again. Establishing the run wasn't the focus against Denver, as the offensive line struggled to open viable lanes for big gains.
Knight led the Cardinals' rushing attack with 48 yards on seven carries. Most of his yards came from Arizona's only explosive run, a 29-yard carry on its third drive. Allgeier limped out to just 19 yards on his eight times with the rock.
Many aspects of this afternoon's game apply here, from the offense's inability to finish drives and settling for field goals to the wideouts going mostly silent. Nothing was as adverse as the Cardinals' defense against Denver, who posted its second 30-point game of the season.
The defense's positives against the Rams last weekend stayed in the City of Angels. The Broncos dominated in the air and on the ground, posting one of their best statistical games of the season despite a slow first-half start.
Broncos quarterback Bo Nix dished up the Cardinals' secondary for 222 yards, with multiple explosive tosses of over 20-yards. The former Auburn-Oregon product burned Arizona for a massive 62-yard rushing touchdown in the second quarter.
A microcosm of the Cardinals' defense occurred on a Nix dump-off to running back RJ Harvey in the third quarter. Multiple Arizona defenders missed tackles during Harvey's 52-yard house call to grow Denver's lead to 20-6.
As they've done many times this season, the Cardinals' defense has been the "pick-me-up" for struggling or lackluster offenses.
The Cardinals will hit the road and face Dallas at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, on Sunday at 10 a.m. Arizona time.

title: Cardinals’ Jacoby Brissett Decision Is Only Delaying the Inevitable
full_text:
GLENDALE — The Arizona Cardinals insist on delaying the inevitable.
The team dropped to 2-5 after Sunday's loss to the Denver Broncos, one where the Cardinals' offense again failed to come alive. Their red zone woes continued from last week, which led to their second straight outing with less than 20 points scored while marking their third instance in the first seven weeks of play.
The Cardinals fell 30-16 against a talented Denver defense, which ranked as one of the tougher units entering today and very much stamped their reputation, hitting Jacoby Brissett 13 times and limited the Cardinals' offense to just 5-of-17 on third-down conversions with only one touchdown in five red zone trips.
Arizona's offense under the first-year play-calling of Mike LaFleur will again be led by Brissett in Week 8 against the Dallas Cowboys , LaFleur confirmed post-game.
When pressed about what Brissett brings to the table, LaFleur offered:
"I'm not even going to talk about any of the individuals. It's us collectively. We just gotta finish better," he said.
"... We had opportunities to make some plays that we didn't, and when we get to the point where we're going to flip this thing, we got to make those plays. This is a collective deal in terms of coaching and playing, but we can make that easier on ourselves."
Brissett has started every game for the Cardinals since striking a re-worked contract in the early stages of training camp, ending an offseason-long holdout that guaranteed more money on the final of a two-year deal.
There are several problems plaguing the Cardinals at this point in time, ones that will eventually be dug into later this week. Brissett, in totality, is not the biggest issue Arizona's offense faces at this point in time.
However, he's clearly not a solution to the team's 2-5 start to the season, and that in itself is an issue that LaFleur and the rest of the coaching staff is going to have to acknowledge sooner rather than later.
While Brissett's profile resides in a veteran passer who can hang in the pocket and take care of the ball, his ceiling and quick trigger when throwing the ball largely caps what the Cardinals can do. LaFleur's offense was expected to be innovative, though Arizona's attack has been largely stagnant through their first seven weeks.
The Cardinals could get away with the "we believe he gives us the best chance to win games now" mantra early in the season, where hope is still alive and teams aren't sinking to the bottom of the standings.
Arizona's now 2-5 with little optimism of a quick turnaround on either side of the ball. The Cardinals need to change something, that's not negotiable. And to Brissett's defense, his offensive line has been below par while his pass-catchers, to various extents, haven't lived up to their billing.
Yet a quarterback is supposed to be the engine that makes an offense go, and the Cardinals have stalled out more times than not.
While it's admirable for LaFleur to prioritize winning here and now, a move to the likes of Gardner Minshew or even Carson Beck wouldn't signal a team that's throwing in the towel — it would be Arizona acknowledging Brissett's simply capped in the potential he can carry this offense to.
It feels like only a matter of when — not if — the Cardinals make a change. However, the longer Arizona delays the inevitable benching of Brissett for other opportunities, the bigger of a hole they're going to dig themselves.

title: Instant Reactions: Bo Nix Exposes Cardinals' Biggest Problems
full_text:
For a week, optimism filled Arizona Cardinals land.
After the Cardinals beat the division-rival Los Angeles Rams ahead of their Week 7 matchup with Denver, there was hope they could beat a Broncos team that, despite its strong record, had some weaknesses.
However, that wasn't the case. The Broncos downed the Cardinals 30 to 16 at State Farm Stadium, pushing Arizona to 2-5 on the season.
Four big takeaways from their Week 7 loss:
Defensive coordinator Nick Rallis' unit was the main headline in the win over the Rams, as the defense played extremely well. Their defense again started strong for the Cardinals this week, with the defensive line pressuring Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix early in action, which included a sack by defensive end Darius Robinson.
At the end of the first quarter, the Cardinals held the Broncos to only two field goals and no touchdowns; however, that changed for the rest of the game.
Things went downhill for the Cardinals' defense when they made a struggling Bo Nix look like legendary scrambling San Francisco 49ers quarterback Steve Young. Nix scrambled for a 62-yard Denver touchdown, going untouched to the end zone.
The big plays continued when Nix hit Broncos running back R.J. Harvey for a 52-yard touchdown on a screen pass. The Broncos blocked this screen well, but Arizona's defense saw Harvey weave in and out of traffic on his touchdown reception, which was dissapointing especially after they tackled so well against the Rams last week.
Simply put, this Cardinals defense was dissapointing. While they did have some good moments, it was erased by some horrendous defensive play.
As awesome as tight end Trey McBride and wideout Michael Wilson are, the Cardinals still need another viable pass catcher. The Cardinals' pass game struggled heavily in this matchup despite quarterback Jacoby Brissett actually threading some nice deep passes that the Cardinals' pass-catchers couldn't haul in.
A big issue is that the Cardinals lack a speed threat on the outside. McBride and Wilson specialize more in strength and possession rather than being downfield burners, and such was even the case when Marvin Harrison Jr. was present.
The NFL's best offenses have great speed threats, such as Khalil Shakir on the Buffalo Bills and Luther Burden III on the Chicago Bears. Adding a player with that skillset could greatly help head coach Mike LaFleur's offense.
While Nix didn't have an amazing game, he played the kind of game Cardinals fans have wanted from their own signal caller. Nix moved the ball downfield without turning it over. On the day, Nix threw one touchdown pass, no interceptions, and finished with an 88.6 passer rating.
Going into the season, Arizona was expected to get these types of games from Brissett. However, that has not been the case. Brissett has turned the ball over more than expected and hasn't made the best reads.
Cardinals fans aren't expecting Brissett to play at the level of an MVP like Josh Allen of the Buffalo Bills or Lamar Jackson of the Baltimore Ravens. The main issue is the simple stuff Brissett has struggled with.
I still don't think the Cardinals' infrastructure is great for any quarterback, but after this game, going with Gardner Minshew or Carson Beck is the right choice.
After a week where the Cardinals didn't score a touchdown and settled for six field goals in the red zone, their Week 7 red zone offense wasn't much better against Denver, going one for five on the day. The Cardinals' lone touchdown came when Brissett found McBride for a touchdown on a seven-yard pass.
Arizona's lack of red-zone execution over the past two weeks is very concerning. The Cardinals' more possession-heavy personnel should make for a better red-zone offense. However, that has not been the case.
Out of all the issues the Cardinals have, this is the one that will cost them the most games. Settling for field goals consistently can not win you a game every week. Hopefully, head coach Mike LaFleur can turn the red-zone offense around. If not, it's going to be a very long back half of the season.

title: 9 Winners And Losers From Cardinals Loss to Broncos
full_text:
ARIZONA — It was close, until it wasn't.
The Arizona Cardinals emerge from their Week 7 clash with a 30-16 loss to the Denver Broncos, dropping their record to 2-5 on the season.
Don't let the final score fool you — the Cardinals were outplayed today, especially in the second half.
Winners and losers from Arizona's loss to the Broncos:
It's time to start those conversations again.
After an impressive win last week in Los Angeles, the Cardinals' defense is back to their typical standard of play after allowing 30 points to a struggling Denver offense. Bo Nix looked more than a competent quarterback, which is saying something.
Rallis' crew has now allowed 30 or more points in five of Arizona's seven games this season.
How much longer does he last?
Robinson needed to have a strong third season to get himself back on track, as the former first-round pick very much filled the "bust label" and couldn't shed it through the first two years of his career.
However, Robinson's silently had a strong 2026 season, which continued today with a sack on Bo Nix, his second on the year.
He ended the day with four tackles, tied for third-most on Arizona.
With multiple safeties sidelined, it was Garrett Williams who primarily operated as Budda Baker's partner in crime on the backend. Even with the Cardinals thin at cornerback, Arizona opted to take their best available corner and place him at safety over Dadrion Taylor-Demerson.
That didn't last long, as Williams missed a tackle on an explosive Broncos pass while being responsible for a deep coverage bust down the field on another. He was replaced by Taylor-Demerson and played sparingly the rest of the way.
With Jeremiyah Love again out of action, the Cardinals leaned on Bam Knight once again to shoulder the load for Arizona's backfield.
Acknowledging the dropped touchdown pass in the first half, Knight did have an overall solid day — they just didn't run the ball all that often. Knight finished with seven rushes for 48 yards, a 6.9 YPC average.
He also added three receptions for 15 yards.
Look, there's penalties every game. It's hard to play a smooth game from start to finish, and it's especially dependent on the crew of officials. And while the Cardinals have shown to have a penalty problem in the past, this is a general take for both Arizona and Denver. Both teams ranked in the bottom half of the NFL in terms of total penalties for the 2026 season entering today.
The amount of flags thrown at State Farm Stadium was ridiculous. 20 total penalties for over 170 yards is eye-opening.
Happy National Tight Ends Day, Trey!
McBride, after scoring just once in his last four games, found the end zone for Arizona and ended their red zone woes after connecting with Jacoby Brissett on a seven-yard touchdown to get the Cardinals' offense going.
McBride's had a string of quieter games compared to his usual standard, though he bounced back with a nice ten reception, 111 yard and one score outing.
Brissett, after leading the Cardinals on a game-winning drive against the Rams last week, has come back down to earth. Hard.
Brissett completed 27 of 48 passes for 272 yards and one touchdown with no interceptions.
He was extremely limited in his operations of the offense, again, especially in the red zone.
On a brighter note for the Cardinals, Larry Fitzgerald was inducted into the team's Ring of Honor at halftime, where the Hall of Fame receiver spoke and saw his famous No. 11 immortalized forever in Arizona history.
It was a special day for a special player and fans who never got to see their hero officially say goodbye after he retired in 2020. Even with a loss, it was still an incredible day for Cardinals fans and Fitzgerald.
Brissett had a whopping 13 quarterback hits today to pair with two sacks. Entering today, he had one of the NFL's fastest average times to throw, and the Broncos got after him early and often.
Arizona's offensive line featured a rookie seventh-round pick at left tackle and their effective fourth-string right guard, which was pitted against a Broncos front seven who had 60 pressures through six games entering today.
Brissett, while clearly having ownership of issues in Arizona's offense, simply was under duress the entire day. His offensive line never stood a chance.

title: Falcons Star Jessie Bates Proves He's the Heartbeat of Atlanta's Defense
full_text:
ATLANTA – The Atlanta Falcons stunned the undefeated San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. They forced four turnovers and locked down in the second half to win 29-20.
There was plenty to love in the win, but a familiar face led the way.
Falcons safety Jessie Bates III has been a menace to opposing teams since arriving in Atlanta, and he was again on Sunday. He snagged an acrobatic interception that likely kept points off the board for the 49ers, then delivered the game-sealing play in the fourth quarter, punching the ball away from tight end George Kittle to force another turnover.
This interception by Jessie Bates III is UNREAL. SFvsATL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/R4UDkkfGcb
“That interception is as good as it gets,” head coach Kevin Stefanski said. “We needed a play in that moment. The ball skills and the wherewithal and the awareness, the toe-drag swag, that's pretty damn good for a safety. So, really proud of Jessie for just being so aware of that football and making a play and then knocking it out later. I mean, he's playing at a high level.”
Bates’ ability to create turnovers isn't new, but his performance against San Francisco reminded everyone how valuable he can be to Atlanta's defense.
According to Tori McElhaney, only four players have recorded at least six career games with both an interception and a forced fumble. Five of Bates' six such performances have come in a Falcons uniform.
For his teammates, it was little surprise to watch him deliver.
“That’s who he is as a player,” quarterback Michael Penix Jr. said. “Obviously, as a person, he’s great as well. But what we saw out of Jessie (on Sunday) is who he is. That’s who we see every day: just a guy with a nose for the football who makes big-time plays whenever we need them. So it was awesome to be able to see him do that.”
Since 2023, Bates has 14 interceptions, including three returned for touchdowns, and 10 forced fumbles. No player has more combined takeaways in that timeframe.
The production has made Bates one of the NFL's most disruptive defensive backs, but his value to Atlanta extends beyond the raw numbers. He has served as a team captain every year as a Falcon and has been one of the defense's most dependable leaders.
That leadership mattered almost as much as his takeaways on Sunday, with Kendal Daniels wearing the green dot as the defensive signal-caller. The rookie linebacker was an incredible story, but he credited Bates as the calming presence he needed throughout the game.
“Jessie is everybody's role model,” linebacker Josh Woods said. “Just the way he prepares, how smart he is, how he handles himself day in and day out. You know exactly who you're going to get, what you're going to get. If I had to place a heartbeat on our defense, I would say it's Jessie Bates for sure.”
For a team still finding its identity under Stefanski, that influence matters even more, and it extends well beyond his on-field play. His preparation, football intelligence, and consistency have helped establish this standard.
Bates has been doing that since he arrived in Atlanta. Against the 49ers, he reminded everyone why the Falcons' defense keeps running through him.

title: Falcons Sign Former Philadelphia Eagles Tight End, per Report
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are signing former Philadelphia Eagles tight end E.J. Jenkins to their practice squad, per Aaron Wilson , adding another player with ties to the NFC East organization.
Jenkins appeared in all six games for Philadelphia this season, starting two contests. He did not record a reception but contributed on special teams, finishing with two tackles. The tight end played 79% of the Eagles’ special teams snaps and 18% of their offensive snaps before being released.
Jenkins joins a growing list of former Eagles who have found their way to Atlanta.
Jenkins joins safety Sydney Brown, wide receiver Jahan Dotson, defensive back Robert Longerbeam, defensive end Za’Darius Smith, wide receiver Olamide Zaccheaus and quarterback Andy Dalton as players with Philadelphia ties connected to the Falcons.
Jenkins entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent with the New York Jets in 2023 after playing college football at St. Francis, South Carolina, and Georgia Tech.
Originally a wide receiver, Jenkins transitioned to tight end during his professional career. His 6-foot-6 frame provides the size to contribute as a blocker while offering developmental potential as a receiving option.
After the Jets released him during roster cuts in August 2023, Jenkins joined the Eagles’ practice squad. He also spent time with the Las Vegas Raiders’ practice squad before returning to Philadelphia in January 2024.
Jenkins recorded the first touchdown of his NFL regular season career during the 2024 campaign, catching a seven-yard pass from quarterback Tanner McKee in Philadelphia’s Week 18 victory over the New York Giants.
He remained in the Eagles’ organization through their Super Bowl LIX championship season, appearing in eight regular season games and all four postseason contests.
Jenkins has recorded one career regular-season reception for seven yards and a touchdown. His contributions have primarily come through special teams and providing depth at tight end.
The move gives the Falcons another option at tight end while adding depth to their practice squad. Jenkins’ experience playing special teams could be particularly valuable as Atlanta evaluates its roster for the remainder of the season.
His limited offensive production means he will likely need to earn opportunities through practice and his contributions in other phases of the game. However, his familiarity with the Eagles’ system and experience on a championship roster provide additional background as he begins another opportunity.
Jenkins will now look to turn his latest opportunity into a chance to contribute in Atlanta.  For now, the tight end provides additional depth and special teams experience as the Falcons continue building their roster for the second half of the season.

title: Kyle Pitts, Nick Muse Make National Tight Ends Day Count in Falcons’ Win Over 49ers
full_text:
National Tight Ends Day gave the Atlanta Falcons another reason to appreciate their tight end room, but Kyle Pitts Sr. and Nick Muse made sure the occasion came with production on the field.
The Atlanta Falcons defeated the San Francisco 49ers 29- 20 on Sunday at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, handing the previously undefeated visitors their first loss of the season.
Pitts and Muse each caught a touchdown from Michael Penix Jr., helping Atlanta overcome an early deficit and secure a statement victory.
For Pitts, National Tight Ends Day is one of the best occasions on the NFL calendar.
“It’s definitely one of the greatest holidays beside Christmas,” Pitts said.
The Falcons tight end backed up his enthusiasm with another touchdown reception, continuing a productive stretch in which he has scored in three consecutive games. Pitts finished with five catches on five targets for 22 yards and a touchdown, while also reaching 300 career receptions.
HAPPY NATIONAL TIGHT ENDS DAY KP! FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/CwdtcwKPHk
He became the sixth youngest tight end in NFL history to reach that milestone, adding another accomplishment to his career as one of Atlanta’s primary receiving threats.
However, Pitts was not the only tight end who found the end zone. Muse delivered one of the afternoon’s most memorable moments when he caught his first career NFL touchdown in the second quarter.
Trailing 14-3, Atlanta needed a spark. Penix found Muse on a first-and-goal play from the one-yard line, giving the tight end a milestone he will remember long after Sunday’s victory.
Our MUSE on National Tight End's Day! FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/UQNMR1Pvrb
Pitts was thrilled to see his teammate get his opportunity.
“It was amazing,” Pitts said. “I love when the tight end scores, especially on our holiday.”
Pitts added that seeing Muse record his first was special.
“It was pretty cool to see him be his first, and, you know, we’ll cherish that moment,” Pitts said.
The touchdowns highlighted a tight end group that contributed beyond the scoreboard. Austin Hooper recorded two receptions for 21 yards, while Charlie Woerner added a nine-yard catch and continued to provide a physical presence as a blocker.
Their combined numbers were particularly important in a game that demanded Atlanta respond after falling behind early. The Falcons eventually took control, using a balanced team effort to finish off San Francisco and improve their standing in a competitive NFC.
For Pitts, the victory offered the perfect combination of individual achievement and team success. He reached a career milestone, extended his touchdown streak, and watched another member of his position group score his first NFL touchdown.
National Tight Ends Day may only come once a season, but Atlanta’s performance showed the value of having multiple tight ends capable of making a difference when their opportunities arrive.

title: Falcons Defense Sends Clear Message After Beating Undefeated 49ers
full_text:
ATLANTA – The word “identity” swirled around the Atlanta Falcons ’ locker room on Sunday evening. Winless at home this season and, more often than not, outnumbered in their own stands, the Falcons' defense knew the assignment started with them.
“Identity is a good word,” head coach Kevin Stefanski said. “You can talk about it until you're blue in the face, and you can put it on a T-shirt, but we gotta go do it. We gotta go be who we say we are, and I thought today we did that.”
They were tasked with slowing down an undefeated San Francisco 49ers team that, despite a depleted wide receiver room, was loaded with stars. Christian McCaffrey, Brock Purdy, George Kittle, and an overpowering offensive line are more than enough for Kyle Shanahan's wizardry. His unit was third in scoring offense (29.5) and second in EPA/play (+0.16).
“That’s a great offense, great coaches, and a quarterback and team playing as well as anybody in this league,” Stefanski said about the 49ers. “So, you’re not going to shut them out. We understood it was going to be a 60-minute game.”
After the first three possessions, it looked like the Falcons would be just another team the 49ers checked off en route to a playoff run. They raced to a 14-3 lead and piled up 150 yards, with Christian McCaffrey nearly hitting 100 yards on his own.
San Francisco was in full control.
The Falcons’ defensive identity had wavered in recent weeks. Against the 49ers, it held.
“We didn't have the first half that we would like,” defensive lineman Gervon Dexter Sr. said. “To come out and make those adjustments and do some of those things and fix some of those things and come out, that takes a detailed team.”
Atlanta never fully shut down the 49ers, but they punished them for every mistake. San Francisco outgained Atlanta by 105 yards, but the Falcons forced four turnovers, including on both of their final two possessions, plus another turnover on downs. They sacked Purdy twice, defended seven passes, and finished with six tackles for loss.
The Falcons’ defense gave the 49ers everything they could handle.
“We want to get off the field early enough, so we're going to be able to make the big plays, the game-changing plays,” Maason Smith said. “We want to continue on that road throughout the rest of the season.”
And after running for 105 yards in the first half, San Francisco managed just 18 rushing yards in the second. A hampered McCaffrey played a role, but so did this Atlanta defense's mentality.
“They're a team that prides themselves on running the ball, and everything we do is centered around stopping the run,” linebacker Josh Woods said. “They got some leaky yards, whatever. They had some good runs. But it was definitely an identity game. It was a heavyweight fight.”
The Falcons had plenty of heroes, including safety Jessie Bates III and rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels , but this was a total team win for this defense. Woods believes this group earned some of that respect on Sunday.
Now, the challenge is doing that again.
“It’s an identity game every week,” cornerback A.J. Terrell Jr. said, “and just being able to go out and do what we practice all week, and just going out there trying to prove us right. Prove we are who we are. So, every week is an identity game.”

title: Falcons Rookie Goes From Scary Injury to Game-Sealing Hero in One Week
full_text:
ATLANTA – Seven days ago, Kendal Daniels was rushed to Grady Hospital following a scary injury at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. On Sunday, the rookie linebacker sealed the Atlanta Falcons ’ Week 7 win over the San Francisco 49ers with an interception and fumble recovery.
Daniels spent nearly 10 minutes on the turf as medical staff tended to him after he took a knee on the helmet. That personnel ultimately immobilized him and carted him off the field. In the hours following the game, media members saw him walking in the locker room, and there was a sense of relief.
What came next is still hard to believe.
He not only recovered, but did so in time to suit up and play against the previously undefeated 49ers. He filled in for Divine Deablo, wore the green dot, led the Falcons in tackles, and recorded two takeaways.
Head coach Kevin Stefanski called it remarkable, and the player called it the craziest week of his life.
“I've never not walked off the field after an injury,” Daniels said after the game. “Mentally, I had to be prepared and going back home and just making sure I was okay mentally more than anything, and not playing timid. I've never not gotten up from an injury. So, being stretched off the field ­– I won't let it happen again. It was a bad feeling, and I'm blessed to be able to play this week.”
Daniels avoided a major injury last week, but he couldn't move his neck in the days after the game. By Wednesday, he was practicing and feeling better each day.
“He’s a dog,” defensive lineman Gervon Dexter Sr. said. “Not a lot of players will go out there and play after something like that happened. He did, and he got all our respect in this building.”
Linebacker Josh Woods spoke with Daniels on Sunday after the “scary” injury, but never doubted that he would be down for long.
“He’s got whatever ‘it’ is,” Woods said. “Everything that he does is pretty dope. Then, for last week to go how it went, and then for him to have the game that he had today, it's a testament to his preparation. He's kind of got that ‘X-factor’, that ‘it’-thing about him.”
That ‘it factor’ showed in the waning minutes on Sunday.
Daniels’ interception snuffed out a 49ers possession that started at midfield and could have put San Francisco in front. The Falcons had just gone three-and-out, and it felt like momentum had flipped entirely in the away team's favor.
Instead, the rookie stepped in front of a Brock Purdy pass and returned it to the Falcons’ red zone. Nick Folk converted the field goal, making it a two-score game.
He recovered a fumble on the next drive, and that officially ended it.
“He put his head down and goes to work every day,” Maason Smith said. “He understands that nothing is given. Everything is earned. When you have size and speed like him, with a mind like his, and you combine both of those things together. Man, there's nothing but excellence waiting to happen.”

title: Winners and Losers from Falcons' 29-20 Win Over 49ers
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons upset the San Francisco 49ers 29-20 in Sunday's Week 7 matchup.
It's the biggest win of the season for a Falcons team coming off a loss to the Bears last week, and it’s now their first home win of the season.
Here are the winners and losers from Atlanta's victory at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.
Penix delivered an efficient performance against San Francisco, completing 25 of 34 passes for 213 yards and three touchdowns without throwing an interception. The Falcons quarterback consistently made the most of his opportunities, helping Atlanta score enough points to secure a nine-point victory.
Penix's three touchdown passes were the highlight of his afternoon. He connected with Drake London, Kyle Pitts, and Nick Muse for scores, spreading the ball around and keeping the 49ers' defense from focusing on one primary target.
Atlanta's passing attack was particularly effective in the red zone, where the Falcons capitalized on their opportunities. Penix also demonstrated improved decision-making by protecting the football and avoiding costly mistakes.
The Falcons managed just 25 yards of offense in the first quarter, making their eventual offensive production even more impressive. Penix helped Atlanta overcome that sluggish start and finish with a winning performance against one of the NFC's top teams.
Smith was one of Atlanta's biggest defensive difference makers, recording a sack, forcing a fumble, batting down a pass, finishing with two tackles for loss and adding a quarterback hit.
His performance demonstrated the impact he can make when he consistently disrupts opposing offenses. Smith affected San Francisco's passing game with his pressure while also making plays behind the line of scrimmage.
The forced fumble was an especially important moment in a game where Atlanta needed its defense to deliver timely stops.
Smith's performance was one of the most encouraging individual developments from Sunday's victory. Atlanta will need that type of production from its defensive line as it moves forward through the season.
Daniels had a memorable afternoon after entering the week with questions surrounding his availability following last week's injury concerns.
The rookie linebacker made his presence felt in Atlanta's 29-20 win, recording three tackles and one assist while contributing to a defense that made several crucial plays.
Daniels also recovered a late fumble to help the Falcons close out the victory. Jessie Bates III punched the ball out, and Daniels was in position to secure the recovery, giving Atlanta possession at a critical point in the fourth quarter.
BOOM! @KendalDaniels__ picks it off! FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/7VBExpgNMh
After uncertainty about whether he would be able to play, Daniels' return was an encouraging development. Not only was he back on the field, but he also made an important contribution to a win over a talented opponent.
For a young defender, being available after an injury scare and making a decisive play in a game of this magnitude is a significant moment. Daniels deserves credit for getting back on the field and helping Atlanta finish the job.
Jessie Bates just always seems to be around the football. Bates came through with one of the game's biggest defensive plays, intercepting Brock Purdy in the red zone to prevent San Francisco from capitalizing on a scoring opportunity.
The veteran interception was a momentum-changing play, particularly because it denied the 49ers a chance to add points in a close contest. Bates displayed excellent awareness and positioning to make the takeaway when Atlanta needed a stop.
JB3 in his own league 🔥 FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/1mdXYHdXKY
He also helped seal the victory late in the fourth quarter by punching the ball out and creating the fumble that Daniels recovered.
Bates showed why having an experienced playmaker in the secondary is so valuable. His interception helped prevent San Francisco from scoring, while his forced fumble helped Atlanta regain possession and protect its lead.
In a game where the Falcons needed their defense to make plays at critical moments, Bates delivered twice.
National Tight Ends Day turned into a productive occasion for Atlanta's tight end group, which contributed two touchdown receptions and an important career milestone.
Pitts led the way with five receptions for 22 yards and a touchdown. His scoring reception was one of Penix's three touchdown passes, and Pitts also reached 300 career receptions during the game.
Austin Hooper added two receptions for 21 yards, while Charlie Woerner caught one pass for nine yards. Nick Muse finished with two receptions for two yards and a touchdown, providing another scoring option for Atlanta.
Our MUSE on National Tight End's Day! FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/UQNMR1Pvrb
Muse's touchdown was particularly valuable because it demonstrated the Falcons' ability to find production beyond their established offensive playmakers. Pitts also delivered in the red zone, helping Atlanta turn a passing opportunity into points.
The group provided Penix with reliable targets throughout the game, and having multiple tight ends contribute helped diversify the offense.
Pitts reaching 300 career receptions was a notable individual accomplishment, but the entire group deserves recognition for helping Atlanta secure the victory.
Atlanta's kickoff return unit provided an important boost in field position, with Zachariah Branch and Khalil Herbert combining for 126 return yards.
Branch delivered a 60-yard return, while Herbert added a 38-yard return to open the second half. Both plays gave the Falcons opportunities to start drives with favorable field position and helped generate momentum.
Explosive returns can have a significant impact in close games, especially when an offense is working to establish consistency. Atlanta's return unit helped ease some of that pressure by creating opportunities for Penix and the offense.
Herbert's return to begin the second half was particularly important because it gave Atlanta a strong start coming out of the locker room.
The Falcons received a boost from their special teams, and the return unit deserves recognition for helping the team control field position in a nine-point victory.
The Falcons’ offensive line took a lot of criticism after last week’s loss to the Bears. On Sunday, not only did they not give up a sack, but the 49ers weren’t credited with even a hit on Penix.
Atlanta's opening quarter was far from ideal, as the Falcons managed just 25 yards of total offense and punted on both of their first two drives.
Against a San Francisco team that entered the matchup undefeated, the slow start put unnecessary pressure on the defense and prevented Atlanta from establishing an early rhythm.
The Falcons struggled to sustain drives, leaving little room for error against a dangerous opponent. Although Penix eventually settled in and threw three touchdown passes, the opening quarter demonstrated how quickly the offense can stall when it cannot consistently move the chains.
Atlanta deserves credit for adjusting and finding ways to score, but a 25 yard opening quarter is not a formula the team should want to repeat. Against other playoff contenders, a similarly sluggish start could prove much more costly.
The Falcons got the result they wanted, but the early offensive struggles remain an area to address moving forward.
Atlanta's run defense had some difficult moments against San Francisco's ground attack, allowing 123 rushing yards on 23 carries. That amounted to approximately 5.3 yards per attempt, giving the 49ers opportunities to move the chains on the ground.
Kaelon Black led San Francisco with 63 rushing yards on 12 carries, including a 30-yard run and a touchdown. Christian McCaffrey added 39 yards on seven attempts and another rushing touchdown.

title: 7 Bite-Sized Takeaways as Atlanta Falcons Hand 49ers First Loss 29-20
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons continued their roller coaster season with a XX-XX upset win over the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. After arguably their worst performance of the season last week against the Chicago Bears, the Falcons got one of their best against the 49ers.
Last week, rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels suffered a scare when he experienced neck pain after a hit. He was stretchered off, but walked back into the locker room after the game.
He used his 6'5 frame to get a crucial interception to snatch back momentum from the 49ers in the fourth quarter.  Then he recovered a George Kittle fumble with a minute left in the game for the final dagger.
From worrying about his future to making arguably the biggest play of his football career, what a difference a week makes.
BOOM! @KendalDaniels__ picks it off! FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/7VBExpgNMh
The Falcons got off to another slow start against the 49ers, falling behind 14-3 before reeling off 16 straight points to take the lead. The defense stepped up with McCaffrey missing some time with a leg injury, and they got a pair of key turnovers.
Penix heated up, pushing the ball to eight different targets in the first half.
How did the Chicago Bears limit Bijan Robinson? They kept the ball for 40 minutes. The Falcons learned from that last week. While the Falcons were scoring 23 unanswered points, they ran 36 plays to 6 at one point.
Box score scouts and fantasy football owners aren't going to be impressed with Falcons' wide receiver Jahan Dotson's numbers. He had just one catch for six yards. But he also induced two key penalties on third down to extend a Falcons drive at the end of the third quarter. The big one was a 20-yard pass interference that put the Falcons in field goal range.
Turnovers: 49ers 4, Falcons 0
Penix looked a little antsy to start. Then he settled in and started dealing. He threw three touchdowns last week against the Bears, but some of that could be attributed to garbage time. No such case on Sunday against the 49ers.
He had three touchdown passes again this week, including a nice touch pass to tight end Nick Muse. Maybe one of the biggest growth points for Penix is the ability to flush a bad play. He missed a wide-open Drake London on a deep shot, but instead of letting it affect him, he followed it with one of his best passes of the day, a 21-yard seam to London.
Cookin' with the SAUCE 🔥 @DrakeLondon_ FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/ljV4yxVwac
The Falcons kept Penix protected, and Penix rewarded them. The 49ers didn't have a sack or even a QB hit credited to them.
The Falcons ran a direct snap for tight end Charlie Woerner. They threw a play-action touchdown pass to Nick Muse. Austin Hooper had a catch for 10 yards in the first half. They were slower getting Kyle Pitts Sr. involved, with just two targets for six yards, both receptions coming in the last three minutes.
Someone got in Tommy Rees' ear at halftime, because Pitts had three catches, including a touchdown on the Falcons' opening drive of the second half. Four tight ends were active, and all four had catches.
HAPPY NATIONAL TIGHT ENDS DAY KP! FOX | NFL+ pic.twitter.com/CwdtcwKPHk
James Pearce Jr.'s eight-game suspension ends after next week's game in Tampa. The Falcons miss his speed. The defensive front for the Falcons is excellent at getting penetration and collapsing the pocket, but they're not fast enough to catch mobile quarterbacks who escape the initial pressure.
49ers quarterback Brock Purdy isn't nearly as comfortable in a two-minute offense if Pearce is pinning his ears back and coming off the edge.
Atlanta has this terrible habit of following a terrific performance with a stinker. They go on the road next week to face a suddenly resurgent Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Bucs got Baker Mayfield back and blew the doors off the Panthers in Charlotte.
At 3-4, the Falcons are in a good spot, but they have to start showing some consistency.

title: Kyle Pitts Sr Has a Chance to Make National Tight Ends Day Special for Falcons
full_text:
Sunday's National Tight Ends Day gives Atlanta Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. another opportunity to make an impact, and offensive coordinator Tommy Rees believes the talented pass catcher can play a major role in the team's success.
Pitts has delivered several memorable performances on National Tight Ends Day throughout his career, including a two-touchdown outing against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2024.
With Atlanta looking to maximize its offensive potential, offensive coordinator Tommy Rees thinks he knows how to unlock more production.
“I think he’s at his best when he has the ball in his hand in open space,” Rees said. “Kyle’s shown that throughout his entire career. He certainly has shown that over the last few weeks.”
Rees also discussed creating opportunities for the tight end to use his athleticism after the catch.
“Again, it’s our job to put him in position to have those plays,” Rees said.
Pitts has a history of producing on National Tight Ends Day, providing an encouraging storyline heading into Sunday's game.
Across five National Tight Ends Day games from 2021 through 2025, Pitts has recorded 26 receptions for 369 yards and two touchdowns, averaging 5.2 catches and 73.8 receiving yards per game.
His most productive performance came in 2021 against the Miami Dolphins, when he caught seven passes for 163 yards. In 2024, Pitts delivered another standout performance against the Buccaneers, catching four passes for 91 yards and two touchdowns.
Pitts also caught nine passes for 59 yards against Miami in 2025, setting a career high for receptions across his five appearances. His other performances included three catches for nine yards against the Cincinnati Bengals in 2022 and three receptions for 47 yards against Tampa Bay in 2023.
Although his production has varied, Pitts has demonstrated the ability to deliver impactful performances on occasion. His challenge now is helping Atlanta establish a more consistent passing attack.
Rees acknowledged the frustration surrounding Atlanta's recent performance but expressed appreciation for Pitts' work and patience as the team looks to get him more involved.
“There wasn’t a lot of happiness on Sunday, to be completely honest,” Rees said. “I’m happy for Kyle because of the work he’s put in, the patience he’s had, to get him going.”
Rees' comments reflect the importance of establishing Pitts as a consistent contributor rather than relying on occasional flashes of production.
Rees made the expectation clear when discussing what the Falcons need to accomplish offensively.
“For us to reach our full potential, he’s got to be a big part of that,” Rees said.
For Rees and the Falcons, the priority is ensuring Pitts remains a consistent part of the offense, beginning Sunday against the 49ers... on National Tight Ends Day.

title: 3 Crucial Keys for Falcons to Beat 6-0 49ers in Week 7
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons face a major test Sunday when they welcome the undefeated San Francisco 49ers to Mercedes-Benz Stadium. At 2-4, Atlanta needs a statement victory against a 6-0 San Francisco team that has established itself as one of the NFL’s most complete squads.
The 49ers enter the matchup averaging 29.5 points and 366.7 total yards per game, while allowing just 18.3 points and 300 yards per contest. The Falcons have the offensive talent to challenge San Francisco, but they will need to execute in three critical areas to pull off the upset.
Atlanta’s best opportunity to control the game begins with Bijan Robinson. The Falcons rank fourth in the NFL with 149.5 rushing yards per game and average an impressive 5.1 yards per carry. Robinson has been a major part of that success, recording 641 rushing yards on 111 carries through six games, averaging 5.8 yards per attempt.
However, San Francisco presents a difficult challenge. The 49ers allow just 90.2 rushing yards per game, ranking eighth in the NFL.
Atlanta must find ways to get Robinson into space, utilize outside runs and involve him as a receiver. Sustaining the ground attack would help keep Brock Purdy and the San Francisco offense on the sideline while creating more manageable situations for quarterback Michael Penix Jr.
The Falcons’ defense must find a way to slow down an offense averaging 29.5 points per game. San Francisco averages 238.5 passing yards per contest, and they are the league's best in EPA, according to Sumer Sports .
Atlanta’s biggest weakness has been defending the pass. The Falcons surrender 252 passing yards per game, ranking 28th in the NFL. That makes Sunday’s matchup particularly concerning against a 49ers offense capable of exploiting coverage breakdowns. Atlanta may have caught a break with the 49ers missing their top two receivers , Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel, but Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle still present a big challenge underneath.
Getting pressure on Purdy without consistently committing extra defenders will be crucial. Atlanta needs its defensive line to win individual matchups, force hurried throws, and prevent Purdy from comfortably working through his progressions. The secondary must also limit yards after the catch and avoid giving up explosive plays.
Atlanta cannot afford to give an undefeated opponent extra possessions. Turnovers have been a concern for the Falcons, who average two giveaways per game, making ball security a significant factor heading into Week 7.  At -7, the Falcons are 31st in the NFL in turnover differential.
San Francisco’s defense allows only 18.3 points per game and limits opponents to 300 total yards per contest. The Falcons will need to turn productive drives into touchdowns rather than settling for field goals or coming away empty-handed.
Penix must make smart decisions, protect the ball, and take advantage of opportunities when San Francisco’s defense leaves openings. Atlanta also needs to improve its execution on third downs to sustain drives and keep its defense rested.
The Falcons have the rushing production to challenge San Francisco, but beating the 49ers will require more than moving the ball between the 20-yard lines. If Atlanta controls the clock, pressures Purdy and wins the turnover battle, it will give itself a legitimate chance to deliver a much-needed home victory.

title: Marvin Lewis Could Help Fix The Ravens' Defense. If Jesse Minter Calls, He'll Listen
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens badly need someone with NFL head coaching experience on their staff, ASAP, to try to help the franchise pull out of a seven-season funk with a collapsing second-half defense.
Rookie head coach Jesse Minter seems overmatched and bewildered right now – allowing 35 unanswered points to the Bengals Sunday was a nadir for the once-proud defense  – and some alarming missteps from the offseason are already coming to roost. Building one of only two coaching staffs in the NFL that included no one with former NFL head coaching experience was really something, especially for how novice most of the staff was , and there are obvious issues with players being undisciplined to the system once playing with a lead, repeated communication mishaps, pathetic tackling and massive issues with pass rush and coverage.
The general manger is out of his depth, too, and already made a ridiculously desperate trade for a slumping offensive lineman in concussion protocol, and who has been running the team as if his job might be in the balance. Eric DeCosta should have been fired when head coach John Harbaugh was, and he seems to be squirming now . The building in tense, the GM, coach and players have proven to be chokers; the two-time MVP quarterback (Lamar Jackson) is injured, the team can’t manage its messaging about his high-ankle sprain in a coherent manner ( abhorrent PR is very much their brand ) and they’ve blown 13-point leads in successive weeks to division foes.
Worst of all, they have DeCosta-ed – losing a game in which they lead by double-digits in the second half – a record 17 times since the start of 2019 (he is the constant) – and already done it three times this season in Minter’s first seven games. As always, we have a plan to help the perpetually underachieving franchises in this town; the Ravens should have hired Marvin Lewis when they put the staff together and they need to call him now (like I did Monday).
The Commanders just brought in former head coach Steve Wilks to help their overwhelmed young defensive coordinator and the Cowboys brought in Mike Pettine to do the same thing and head coach DeMeco Ryans took over play calling on defense in Houston and the Broncos, who nearly went to the Super Bowl last year and could do so this year, turned things around once head coach Sean Payton took over offensive play calling.
Lewis ran the Ravens defense at its heights, had a great run as Bengals head coach, helped young head coach Antonio Pierce as an assistant head coach with the Raiders in 2024, and follows the league closely doing syndicated calls of NFL games on the radio. He’s watching Ravens film, he knows their culture and history like few could, and he is at a stage in his career where it’s not about his padding resume, but rather helping young coaches succeed in a place he cares deeply for.
So when I tooK the pulse of the Ravens systemic issues with Lewis on “The Daily Flock Show” (a deep dive on their defensive woes) Monday I had to ask if he’d try to help his buddy Ozzie Newsome out and be a resource for Minter if the team reached out. Lewis wouldn’t consider leaving his home in Arizona for much, but this would pique his interest should the Ravens do the right thing.
“Well, I would be remiss in saying I wouldn’t listen,” Lewis said about any hypothetical Ravens interest. “You’ve got to listen. And there are people you want to help, and more important than me; it’s somebody I would want to help and support. That’s what’s important more than anything.”
When former Ravens defensive mastermind Mike Macdonald left to become head coach in Seattle – the one that got away – he didn’t bring in a family member to be his mentor, he secured the services of successful former head coach and defensive coordinator Leslie Frazier. They won a Super Bowl in Year Two. It should have been a prerequisite for Minter’s staff, and the Ravens have a history of doing this sort of thing in-season, be it Dean Pees and Jerry Rosburg rejoining the franchise out of quasi-retirement .
He was invaluable for Pierce, he has recent experience at Arizona State University as well so still understands how to relate to young players and his wealth of experience is unlike anything on this staff currently. He did special projects for Pierce, helped with inactives and was a sounding board for him to sit in on coordinator meetings throughout the week and offer insight to the head coach in private.
“Thursday and Friday he gave me about four minutes in practice where I could go over a special situation that may come up in the game, where it’s a backed-up situation for the offense or the offense threw a big pass and now it has the ball at the 25-yard-line. And I wouldn’t tell those coordinators what the situation was going to be for the day, because we wanted them to think on their feet and be ready to call it that way …
“A lot of things like that I did, and I was a part of the defensive meetings and I’d look at the opposing defense and would go in and talk to the offensive coaches. “When you do this, this is always their response.’ We saw a little bit of that yesterday (in the Ravens game) I think in how Cincinnati kept building their formations.”
The Ravens badly need new eyes and ears in their meeting rooms. Here’s their second half rankings:
Yards Per Play: 6.0 (29th) Passing Yards : 147 (29th) Yds/Att.: 8.0 (30th)
INT/Att .: 0.00% (T-last) First Downs : 12.3 (30th) 3rd Down: 44% (24th)
QB Rating: 117.0 (28th) Comp % : 71.3% (28th) TD-INT : 8-0 (32nd)
Both of Minter’s starting corners were embarrassed by the Bengals Sunday, Lewis noted in our discussion how much Nate Wiggins was attacked, while Marlon Humphrey lost the plot in coverage and suffered in tackling. Their corners and safeties do not have an interception all season; their culture is warped and on Monday Minter hinted at how deep it runs.
“We have guys that care and want to do it right,” Minter said, “but there's also moments in the game where it's like, 'Who's the guy that's going to grab everybody together, get them together on the sideline? I think as a team, we're working through who that is.
“Who is that person? Who are those players? There’s guys that want to do it, and then there's guys that maybe they're dealing with something, or they're not playing the way they want to play, so they don't feel like they can do it in those moments.”
Maybe a former head coach could help the rookie figure out how to bring it out of them.

title: Were Ravens Surprised Lamar Jackson Missed Bengals Game? Could He Play Sunday? Jesse Minter Explains
full_text:
Ravens rookie head coach Jesse Minter continues to speak in guarded and cryptic tones about the status of two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson ahead of a critical game at Buffalo in Week 8. The team is nearing the midpoint of the season in a downward spiral and Jackson, recovering from what he called a "high-ankle sprain," has arguably a greater impact on regular-season wins and losses than any NFL player.
Minter’s defense is getting overrun in the second half of games – allowing 114 points in the second half, most in the NFL – with some in rival NFL front offices believing the young coach needs help from a former head coach/defensive coordinator to fix systemic issues in their game-day process. In two straight weeks the offense has failed to score in the second half with back-up Snoop Huntley filling in, while the defense blew a 13-point lead to the Browns and Bengals.
The Ravens have an NFL record 17 losses with a double-digit lead since 2019, the collapses have only gotten worse under Minter – allowing 35 unanswered points Sunday at hom e was a new low – and while general manager Eric DeCosta’s rosters are undoubtedly a major part of the problem ( his job security should be under intense scrutiny after head coach John Harbaugh was already fired for all the late-game debacles), Minter is in the crosshairs now and badly needs his best player back.
After asserting for three weeks – during which Jackson never once practiced fully – that the star was “day-to-day” with an ankle injury that the team was certainly couching as not too severe – Minter stayed away from that wording on Monday. But he uttered it again as recently as Friday, although Jackson made it clear in his remarks on Friday that the injury was extremely painful, saying he still has been unable to run normally since suffering the injury in Week 4.
“I think he’ll be in a decent spot but we'll know a lot more on Wednesday,” Minter said.
It’s fair to assume at this point that Jackson will not play until he is able to practice fully with no setbacks. The CBS broadcast of Week 7’s game referred to “swelling” over the weekend after limited practice Wed-Fri as the cause for Jackson being downgraded to out on Saturday after being listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report.
“I’m not going to speak really on the details of anybody’s injury,” Minter said. “… Look, if he’s able to play and is healthy enough to play and play the way he needs to play, then he will play.”
The CBS broadcast also asserted that the Ravens were surprised that Jackson was not able to face the Bengals. To that Minter said, “I would say a little bit,” pointing to an ongoing feeling-out process with the ankle.
Of course, the backdrop to the situation is the fact that Jackson is the rarest of superstar quarterbacks in his prime who has reached a point in his contract with no future guarantees beyond this season. He carries an untenable $85M cap hit in 2027, with a no-trade clause and a no-franchise tag clause, which gives him NBA levels of leverage over where he plays next season and how much he makes .
Minter continues to say that Jackson is “working his butt off” to return as soon as his body will allow him, and he has repeatedly refereed to this decision as one the team and QB and medical staff would make together. The Ravens win 70% of their regular season games that Jackson starts and are a losing franchise without him since he took over as starter midway through the 2018 season.
His career arc with them has been highly unusual throughout, demanding a trade at one point and getting no interest as a de-facto free agent on a non-exclusive tag, which later become fodder in an NFLPA collusion case. Given the strange backdrop between player and team, calling this a “day-to-day” injury for the better part of a month seems to have been another unforced error by this franchise.
Beating Buffalo coming off a bye would be a stretch and the Ravens have a quick turnaround hosting Jacksonville on Thursday night in Week 9.
