title: Panthers Were Praised for Offseason Signing, But It Hasn't Worked Out At All
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers had a reality check on Sunday afternoon, getting completely obliterated by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . The 43-13 beatdown was embarrassing for both sides of the ball, especially the defense, which surrendered 258 rushing yards.
Many thought that this game would be ugly, but ugly for both sides, not just for Carolina. Tampa Bay won by 30 points, with QB Baker Mayfield throwing for just 66 yards and no touchdowns.
The last time a team won with their QB throwing for fewer than 50 yards was Christmas of 2025, when the Vikings beat the Lions.
So yes, the defense is the number one problem from Sunday's debacle. However, it wasn't the only major issue.
Panthers QB Bryce Young was pressured on over 68% of dropbacks against the Buccaneers, the most in any of Carolina's six games this season.
What's even more alarming is that this isn't the first game of the year where Young was pressured on over 60% of dropbacks. In Week 3, against the Browns, Young was pressured on over 63% of dropbacks.
Both alarming performances from the offensive line, a unit that was revamped in the offseason through both the NFL Draft and free agency.
On Sunday, one of Carolina's biggest offseason signings was dreadful, making the offseason praise now look foolish.
Not only was Walker abysmal on Sunday against Tampa on Sunday, but he's been underwhelming all season.
ESPN's Mike Kaye pulled up Next Gen Stats to put Walker's struggles in perspective.
#Panthers LT Rasheed Walker, according to @NextGenStats , has allowed a team-leading 34 QB pressures (including four sacks) on 257 pass sets. Seven pressures (including three sacks) came against Tampa Bay.
The lack of production thus far is beyond the worst-case scenario when Walker was signed in free agency. What's even more baffling about it is that Walker was really good as a pass blocker in 2025 for the Packers.
In 2025, Rasheed Walker played 986 snaps, and only allowed five sacks for the entire year. Furthermore, Walker posted a 93.8 pass-block rate in 2025, which ranked 11th in the NFL.
Now, less than halfway through 2026, Walker has already allowed four sacks, three of them in a single game.
Bryce Young was awful against Tampa Bay. Giving up points or giving up exceptional field position is always a QB problem, but it sure doesn't help that the left tackle, who protects Young's blindside, is giving pass rushers free sacks.
The other big problem is that Carolina has to stick with Walker moving forward, because Taylor Moton  suffered a fractured fibula in the game against Tampa Bay on Sunday. If Moton were healthy, then he could start at right tackle, and Walker could compete for reps with rookie Monroe Freeling.
Now thats not an option, as it hasn't been for most of the season anyway. If there's no improvement moving forward, then Carolina could explore outside options as the trade deadline approaches.
Preston is an experienced sports writer focusing on NFL, College Football, NBA, and MMA topics. He is a passionate Charlotte and Oklahoma sports fan and graduated from the University of Science and Arts Oklahoma in 2025 with a Bachelor of Arts in Communications degree with a focus in journalism.

title: Apparently, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers Still Own the Carolina Panthers
full_text:
Cue legendary Pro Football Hall of Fame coach Vince Lombardi.
It was the classic “what could go wrong, did go wrong” game for the first-place Carolina Panthers. And that was just the first half on Sunday afternoon at Bank of America Stadium.
Dave Canales’s team trailed 33-6 at intermission, and by that time the team’s offense, defense, and special teams contributed to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ point total.
Calijah Kancey sees the open field on the Buccanneers' scoop and score 💥 pic.twitter.com/YH7gyTwIbv
Carolina’s defense surrendered 147 yards rushing and three offensive touchdowns in the first 30 minutes of play. Canales’s club turned over the ball three times before intermission. The Panthers were down 17-0 early in the second quarter after Buccaneers’ defensive tackle Calijah Kancey scooped up a Bryce Young fumble and returned it 32 yards for a touchdown.
Something you NEVER see: A blocked PAT turns into Zyon McCollum's 2-pointer. pic.twitter.com/p268pVNAky
And just after the Panthers finally woke up from their cat nap, things got a little crazier. Young found tight end Darren Waller for a 50-yard touchdown less than two minutes later. However, the PAT was blocked and Tampa cornerback Zyon McCollum returned the prize for two points and a 19-6 lead. The Bucs tacked on two more touchdowns and took a 27-point advantage into the locker room.
Tykee Smith gets the INT off of Bryce Young #WeAreTheKrewe #TBvsCAR pic.twitter.com/srgCceuI63
When it was all said and done, the final verdict was an ugly 43-13 home loss by Canales and company. Young came into the game with only a pair of interceptions. On Sunday, he was picked off twice and lost a fumble that was returned for a touchdown. In fact, after giving up the football just four times during their 3-2 start, the Panthers committed four turnovers in the stunning 30-point loss.
Yes, Carolina remains the only team in the NFC South that does not have a losing record. However, Sunday’s loss was a little reminder that while the Panthers unseated the Bucs last season as division champions, their recent history in this rivalry can’t be ignored.
Bucky Irving with his SECOND touchdown of the day 🔥 TBvsCAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/fz7kxCXD6Y
Dating back to the start of this decade, the Panthers dropped to a disappointing 2-11 in 13 meetings with the Buccaneers. The clubs will renew acquaintances in Week 12 on a Monday night at Tampa, a place that Carolina hasn’t won at since 2017 (the Panthers defeated Tampa Bay, 37-26, at London in 2019 in what was a home game for the Bucs). And it’s safe to say that Young has had his hands full against Todd Bowles’s defenses.
In seven games vs. the Buccaneers, the four-year pro has completed just 126-of-217 throws (58.1 percent) for 1,393 yards, eight touchdowns and four interceptions. He has been sacked a disturbing 20 times (3 times by Tampa defensive tackle YaYa Diaby on Sunday), lost two of his six fumbles and the team is 1-6 in those contests.
Canales and his club don’t have much time to feel sorry for themselves. The Panthers will be at Lambeau Field on Thursday night to face Matt LaFleur’s Green Bay Packers.
Russell S. Baxter has been writing and researching the game of football for more than 40 years, and on numerous platforms. That includes television, as he spent more than two decades at ESPN, and was part of shows that garnered five Emmy Awards. He also spent the 2015 NFL season with Thursday Night Football on CBS/NFLN.

title: Panthers Stock Report: Finding Winners After Sunday's Disaster Wasn't Easy
full_text:
Finding guys for the stock-up side wasn't exactly easy this week.
That's what happens when you lose 43-13 at home to Tampa Bay . The Panthers turned it over four times, gave up 258 yards on the ground and were down 33-6 at halftime. There were plenty of options for stock down. Stock up took a little more work.
I'm bending the rules a little with Darren Waller because he caught one pass. But when that one pass goes for a 50-yard touchdown in a game where almost nothing else worked offensively, I'll allow it.
It was a really nice play, too. Waller got behind the defense, Bryce Young put the ball where it needed to be and suddenly Carolina had its first touchdown of the afternoon. Of course, Tampa Bay blocked the extra point and returned it for two, so the good feeling didn't last very long.
My bigger question is why Waller only got one target. I know Young was under pressure most of the afternoon, but Waller has shown he can still make plays down the field. If the Panthers are going to have him out there, I'd like to see them find a way to get him more involved.
Look, the game was over when Anthony Tyus III scored. Everybody knew it, but I'm still putting him here.
Tyus got six carries and finished with 28 yards, including a 12-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter. It was his first NFL touchdown, and I don't really care that Carolina was down 37 points when it happened. That's still a pretty cool moment for a rookie.
I'm also getting curious about what Tyus could do with a few more touches. I'm not saying he needs 15 carries next week, but six carries for 28 yards isn't bad. Give him a few more opportunities and see what happens.
We've talked a lot about Young looking different this season. He had been taking better care of the football, making plays when Carolina needed them and starting to look a lot more comfortable running the offense. None of that was there Sunday.
Young finished 14-of-27 for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. He also lost a fumble that Calijah Kancey returned for a touchdown. That's three turnovers from your quarterback in a game where Carolina couldn't afford to give Tampa Bay anything extra.
The offensive line was bad, too. Young was sacked five times and spent way too much of the afternoon trying to get away from pressure. I'm not putting everything that happened on him, but some of those decisions were his, and this was easily the worst we've seen him play this season.
I'm not changing my opinion of Young because of one game. He was bad Sunday, and both things can be true.
This one annoyed me more than anything else Sunday.
I thought Carolina had finally figured some things out on defense . After Chicago ran for 291 yards in the opener, the Panthers had gotten much better against the run and had allowed only 81 rushing yards combined over the previous two games.
Then Tampa Bay came in and ran for 258. Bucky Irving went for 106 yards and two touchdowns, Kenny Gainwell had 88 and Sean Tucker added another 52. The Buccaneers ran the ball 49 times, so it wasn't like Carolina didn't know what was coming.
Baker Mayfield threw 11 passes all afternoon. That's it. Tampa Bay basically spent the day saying, "We're going to run it again," and Carolina never gave them much reason not to.
That's what would worry me going into Green Bay. The Packers are going to watch this film, and I have a pretty good idea what they're going to want to test first.
David Moore's muffed punt was one of those plays where you could almost feel the game starting to get away from Carolina.
Tampa Bay recovered at the Panthers' 18 and turned it into a field goal. The defense actually did its job there and kept the Buccaneers out of the end zone, but Carolina was already having enough problems without handing Tampa Bay the ball in scoring range.
Then came the blocked extra point after Waller's touchdown. Zyon McCollum took it the other way for two points, turning what should've been Carolina's first real reason to feel good into another Tampa Bay celebration.
I thought about putting Moore here by himself, but that felt a little unfair. Sunday wasn't one guy having a bad day on special teams. It was another part of the team making mistakes on an afternoon where mistakes were already everywhere.
I could probably keep going with the stock-down list, but you get the point. Not much went right Sunday, and the Panthers have a short week to make sure one really bad game doesn't turn into two.

title: Panthers Plummet in NFL Power Rankings After Disastrous Loss
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers had a perfect opportunity to put the NFC South on notice . At 3-2, they were in first and facing the banged-up 1-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers. What transpired was, quite literally, one of the ugliest games of football we've had the displeasure of watching in a long time .
Before that, the Panthers were surging. They had won two in a row over teams that have been in the playoffs a lot lately. They returned home after a big win with a chance to really put the NFL on notice and arrive.
They failed to do so, and justifiably, they tanked in the NFL Power Rankings as a result.
In all three phases, the Panthers were crushed by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Special teams were astonishingly bad. The run defense channeled its Week 1 form. The offense looked like the unit from years past, with abysmal pass protection.
The Panthers even got outcoached by, with all due respect, someone who has been on the hot seat for a long time now. It was ugly, so it's no surprise that they've crashed and burned in the weekly rankings. They deserve it.
Sporting News' Vinnie Iyer dropped them from 17th to 20th in the Power Rankings this week. Last week, we complained that 17 might be too low . 20 might be too high after that debacle.
"The Panthers faced every kind of terror in their loss to the Buccaneers at home, killing everything positive that was rolling with Bryce Young and the defense. The awful run defense keeps haunting them as they gave up another 258 in Week 7. They don't have much time to sulk with a Thursday night game at Green Bay," Iyer wrote.
Carolina doesn't have much time to prepare and try to get back to their winning ways. They're up on Thursday Night Football against the Green Bay Packers, which is not an ideal matchup. That is shaping up to be another loss, which would drop them to 3-4 after such an inspiring start.
The good news with that is that they only have to live with this failure for a few days. Normally, this would last a week or longer, but the Thursday kickoff means there will be something else to talk about soon.
The Panthers have been quite good this year, especially after Week 1. They laid an egg at a bad time, and they deserve every bit of the immense criticism they are receiving this week.
Zachary Roberts is a journalist with a wide variety of experience covering basketball, golf, entertainment, video games, music, football, baseball, and hockey. He currently covers Charlotte sports teams and has been featured on Sportskeeda, Yardbarker, MSN, and On SI.

title: Panthers Can't Wait Until It's Too Late to Fix Their Cornerback Problem
full_text:
The Panthers should be getting some help at cornerback soon, with Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson both working their way back from injuries . Dave Canales sounded pretty optimistic about where each of them stands, which is obviously good news for a secondary that's been trying to get by without both of its starters.
Even with those two getting closer, I'd still be looking for another corner.
That really doesn't have much to do with what Baker Mayfield did Sunday. He threw for only 64 yards and attempted 11 passes in Tampa Bay's 43-13 win . The Buccaneers didn't need him to do much because they ran for 258 yards and controlled the game that way.
For me, it's more about what Carolina has behind Horn and Jackson and what happens if one of them isn't ready as quickly as expected. We've already seen both starters go down at the same time. I don't think I'd want to take the chance of being in the same spot again later in the season.
There's no question the Panthers are better when Horn and Jackson are on the field. If both come back healthy over the next few weeks, cornerback suddenly looks a whole lot better than it does right now.
The problem is you're putting a lot of faith in both guys staying healthy the rest of the way. Horn has missed time throughout his career, and Jackson is working his way back from groin surgery. Maybe both return and don't miss another game, but I'm not sure that's something I'd want to bet on if I'm Dan Morgan.
Carolina elevated Robert Rochell from the practice squad again for Sunday's game, and he's given the Panthers another option while they've been short-handed. But there's a difference between getting through a few weeks and having enough depth for the rest of the season. Another injury at corner could put Carolina right back in the same situation.
That's why I'd rather see the Panthers address it before they have to.
I'm not talking about giving up a Day 2 pick or chasing some big-name corner just because the Panthers are sitting at 3-3. I wouldn't do that, especially with a team that's still trying to figure out exactly where it stands.
But I'd absolutely make some calls.
If there's a veteran available for a late-round pick, or maybe somebody buried on another depth chart who Carolina thinks can help, that's the type of move I'd be interested in. The Panthers don't need somebody to come in and take Horn's or Jackson's job. They need another corner Evero can trust if one of those guys isn't available.
That might not be the kind of move that gets everybody excited at the trade deadline, but it could matter a lot more a month from now.
If Carolina was sitting at 1-5 right now, I'd probably feel completely different about this. Keep the draft picks, let the younger guys play and use the rest of the season to figure out what you have.
But that's not where the Panthers are. They're 3-3, and as bad as Sunday was, they had won three of four before Tampa Bay came to town. I'm still not completely sure what this team is, but I've seen enough to think there's at least a chance Carolina is playing meaningful football in November and December.
That's why a smaller move at corner makes sense to me. It doesn't mean Morgan has to suddenly act like the Panthers are one player away from a Super Bowl. It just means giving a team that's put itself in a decent position a little more protection at one of the thinnest spots on the roster.
Maybe Horn and Jackson come back, stay healthy and none of this becomes an issue. That's obviously the best-case scenario. But we've already seen what this secondary looks like when both starting corners disappear from the lineup at the same time.
If the Panthers are still hanging around later this season, I'd rather have another corner sitting there and not need him than need one and realize they should've made the move weeks ago.

title: The Panthers Got Obliterated By the Buccaneers, But These 4 Things Matter
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers got crushed by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. It was an ugly game and a reminder, perhaps, of how far this team still has to go. It's best to forget about this one, but before we do, here are the most important things to remember.
The Panthers invested a ton up front on offense. They spent big on guards Damien Lewis and Robert Hunt. They signed Rasheed Walker and drafted Monroe Freeling. Yet, the offensive line is a mess. It's been bad all year.
Losing Taylor Moton for a second time is a huge blow because he's the only offensive linemen (with the exception of Damien Lewis) who seems capable of doing his job. It's a disaster, and the Panthers invested way too much for that to be the case.
The Panthers lost this game from the top down. You can blame almost everyone for this loss. Dan Morgan refuses to address injury depth issues. Dave Canales hardly ever has this team prepared to play.
Ejiro Evero cannot adjust . Brad Idzik may be innocent, but the offense was pretty bad, too. Some of that is not on him, but he certainly did the team no favors. From the top down, the Panthers failed today.
Yes, this was an ugly one. It's one that's best to forget about as soon as they review the film this week. Just move on and try to put it behind you. What should help is that this is not really a repeatable thing. The Panthers had a perfect concoction of things going wrong that just won't happen again.
The run defense was horrible. The pass protection was bad. Bryce Young was off. The special teams was horrific. Will all of those things happen in the same game again? It's unlikely. Today was just a perfect storm of bad things.
To Carolina's credit, last week was one of those games that allowed the Panthers to claim that they've "arrived." Winning winnable road games to get out to a good start is what good teams do. The Panthers did that, but that wasn't the final opportunity.
Division games matter a lot, even when one team is far behind the other. The Panthers had yet another chance to prove they've made the leap, and they just didn't look ready to do it. It's unfortunate in a very winnable division.

title: 3 Major Takeaways From Panthers' Complete Meltdown Against Buccaneers
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers had a chance Sunday to keep some momentum going after a 25-14 win in Philadelphia. Instead, they turned the ball over four times, couldn't stop the run and were basically out of this one by halftime. Tampa Bay led 33-6 at the break and rolled to a 43-13 win.
There isn't one thing you can point to and say that's why Carolina lost. The Panthers were bad on offense, bad on defense and even special teams got in on it. Tampa Bay didn't need much help, but Carolina gave them plenty anyway.
Here are my three biggest takeaways from a game the Panthers would probably like to forget.
I've defended Bryce Young plenty, and I still think we've seen some good things from him this season. Sunday just wasn't one of those days.
Young finished 14-of-27 for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. He also lost a fumble when Al-Quadin Muhammad got to him in the second quarter, and Calijah Kancey picked it up and returned it 32 yards for a Tampa Bay touchdown. That put Carolina down 17-0, and things never really got any better from there.
The offensive line certainly didn't do Young any favors. Tampa Bay sacked him five times, and there were plenty of snaps where he didn't have much time to do anything. Still, Young made some bad decisions of his own, and three turnovers from your starting quarterback are going to be tough to overcome no matter how well everyone else is playing.
That's probably the frustrating part for me. We've seen Young play better than this, take care of the football and make enough plays to give Carolina a chance. None of that showed up Sunday.
This might be the biggest head-scratcher of the whole game. Carolina had allowed only 81 rushing yards combined over its previous two games, but Tampa Bay had 147 by halftime Sunday and finished with 258.
Bucky Irving went over 100 yards with two touchdowns, Kenny Gainwell added 88 and Sean Tucker broke a 46-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter. The Panthers knew Tampa Bay wanted to run the football, too. Baker Mayfield was back after missing three games with a thumb injury, so there was no reason for the Buccaneers to put the game on his arm if they didn't have to.
They didn't. Mayfield threw the ball just 11 times, and Tampa Bay still won by 30 points. Why throw it when the Panthers couldn't stop the run?
We saw this against Chicago when the Bears ran for 291 yards in the opener. I thought Carolina had gotten away from games like that, especially after what we had seen from the defense lately . Sunday looked way too familiar.
There are games where you get beat, and then there are games where you seem determined to make everything harder on yourself. This was definitely the second one.
David Moore muffed a punt and handed Tampa Bay a short field. Young's fumble turned into a Buccaneers touchdown. Then Carolina finally got something going with a 50-yard touchdown from Young to Darren Waller, only to have the extra point blocked and returned the other way for two points. That pretty much sums up the afternoon.
Then there is the Taylor Moton injury. Moton had just returned last week after missing the first four games of the season, and now Dave Canales says he'll be "out for a while" with a broken fibula. That's a tough loss by itself, but it's even tougher after watching Young get sacked five times.
I'm not ready to throw away everything we saw from Carolina before this game because of one terrible afternoon. The Panthers are 3-3, and we've already seen them look like a completely different team at times this season. But Sunday was a pretty big reminder that they're not there yet.
The good news is it's only one game.
The bad news is there wasn't much about this one worth keeping.

He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: Grading Bryce Young in Carolina Panthers' Horrific Loss to Buccaneers
full_text:
Well, that was ugly. The Carolina Panthers got demolished by the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers , falling to 3-3 on the season. Carolina was never in the game, as the Bucs scored 17 unanswered points by the 11-minute mark of the second quarter.
Entering Week 6, Bryce Young was the league leader in passing yards per game, and had an elite turnover ratio of 11-2. That ratio has changed drastically now, after what's easily the worst performance of the season for Young and the Panthers overall.
Young didn't finish the game, being subbed out early in the fourth quarter after the Buccaneers scored their 43rd point.
There are certainly other directions to point the finger at for this loss , but Young was still abysmal.
Bryce Young finished the Week 7 loss completing just 14 of 27 passes, for 163 yards, 1 touchdown, 2 interceptions, and 1 fumble lost.
It doesn't get much worse than that; there's no team that can recover from that many catastrophic mistakes. Young's fumble resulted in a scoop-and-score for the Buccaneers, and his first interception put Tampa Bay deep in Carolina territory.
Bryce Young fumbles and the Buccaneers scoop and score!💥 pic.twitter.com/WmcvairNvy
Young was also sacked 5 times, which isn't fully on him because he was under pressure basically the entire game, being pressured on over 68% of dropbacks.
Part of the inefficiency was his failure to connect with his top receivers. Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker combined for 5 catches and 49 yards on the day, on 10 targets. For context, Darren Waller totaled more receiving yards than both receivers on just one catch: a 50-yard touchdown.
With such a crowded pocket and no time to process, Young looked like a deer in the headlights on a lot of throws.
This performance continues Young's trend of having no success against the Buccaneers, now 1-6 in his career against Tampa Bay. It's essentially the opposite of his dynamic with the Atlanta Falcons, a team he consistently shreds to pieces.
Outside of the 50-yard touchdown pass to Waller, Young's other 13 completions weren't consequential to the game, as the Panthers only had one drive that reached the red zone, and it was in the third quarter, with the game already out of reach.
Even with the Buccaneers totaling 258 rushing yards, Young still contributed significantly to the Panthers' Week 7 loss.
Before Sunday, Young had played as well as any QB in the NFL not named Josh Allen or Brock Purdy, but his performance against Tampa Bay will likely be the worst QB performance of the week.

title: Bears Catch a Huge Break on Seahawks Week 8 Injury Report
full_text:
While the Seattle Seahawks should soon be getting much healthier on offense, with running backs Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returning to the lineup soon, they also received some bad news in the injury department on Monday.
Offensive tackle Charles Cross has developed into a Pro Bowl-caliber player for Seattle. He has only allowed five pressures all season and has earned a 79.1 overall grade from Pro Football Focus (which ranks eighth among tackles).
Unfortunately for Seattle, the Seahawks will be without Cross for their Week 8 matchup against the Bears on Monday night. According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz , the star left tackle suffered a high ankle sprain in the fourth quarter of the team's Sunday night clash against Kansas City.
Veteran tackle Josh Jones, who started three games for Seattle last season, is expected to take over the starting job for however long he'll be out of the lineup. With 27 career starts, Jones has seen a lot of action throughout his career. He's a backup for a reason, though.
With the Bears playing on Thursday night, they have a three-day rest advantage over the Seahawks. Their mini-Bye Week could allow them to get T.J. Edwards back in the lineup. Montez Sweat will also return from a two-game suspension for violating the league's substance abuse policy.
Specifically, Sweat should boost a defensive line that has performed far better than expectations through the first seven weeks of the season. Chicago is tied for seventh with 19 sacks thus far.
The emergence of nickelback Kyler Gordon as a certifiable threat off the edge is a major reason for their pass-rushing success, but edge rusher Austin Booker has also played a key role. They're both tied for the team lead with four sacks.
Meanwhile, they've also gotten quality production from Daniel Hardy after he's filled in for Sweat over the past two weeks. He has one-and-a-half sacks and eight pressures ( according to PFF ), and might've carved out a role in the rotation until further notice .
Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold has found a home in Seattle, but he struggles when opposing defenses get pressure on him. His eight interceptions are tied for the most in the league.
With Seattle boasting one of the league's best defenses (they've allowed a league-low 233.9 yards per game), Monday's contest might be more of a defensive battle than Bears fans are accustomed to. They're in a great position to hold their own on the road, though.
Jerry Markarian has been an avid Chicago Bears fan since 2010 and has been writing about the team since  2022.  He has survived the 2010 NFC Championship Game, a career-ending injury to his favorite player (Johnny Knox), the Bears' 2013 season finale, a Double Doink, Mitchell Trubisky, Justin Fields, and Weeks 8-17 of the 2024 NFL season. Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: Ranking the Top Trade Candidates for the Bears as Deadline Looms
full_text:
The 2026 NFL season is about halfway over, and the Chicago Bears are at 5-2 after a sensational primetime win over the New England Patriots last Thursday. They're currently in second place in the NFC North and would be the No. 5 seed in the playoffs if the season ended today. But the season is not ending today, and there's still plenty of football left to play.
At this point in the season, the contenders are starting to distance themselves from the pretenders, and the Bears absolutely belong among the former. They're expected not just to make the playoffs, but to make a deep playoff run. With that in mind, and with the NFL trade deadline looming , let's take a look at a few likely trade candidates around the league and rank them based on who would make the biggest impact for the Bears' Super Bowl hopes.
On Monday, NFL insider Jay Glazer confirmed that the Bears are in pursuit of a deal that would bring Mack back to Chicago. At 35, Mack is no longer the game-wrecker that he was the last time he donned the navy and orange, but he would still bring a strong boost to Chicago's defensive line. In fact, he's actually in the midst of something of a renaissance season, earning an 81.6 impact grade from Pro Football Network .
Considering his age and his expiring deal, a deal for Mack likely wouldn't cost more than a Day 3 pick, and that would make this a no-brainer for GM Ryan Poles and the Bears.
Josh Sweat trade rumors have been swirling ever since the end of the 2025 NFL season, and for good reason. He's a good-not-great defensive end who's still on the right side of 30. That makes him a hot commodity in the NFL trade market, and the Bears should be aggressively pursuing him. He would instantly raise the floor of Chicago's defensive line to the level of a playoff contender and would make for an excellent running mate alongside Montez Sweat (no relation).
While Mack would likely be a one-year rental, a deal for Sweat would likely be a long-term move, and so the trade compensation would be significantly higher, likely a second-round pick and more. But it would be worth it to the Bears to maximize their current window with Caleb Williams still playing on a rookie deal.
The Colts fired long-time GM Chris Ballard last week, and that has the entire league making calls to Indianapolis about potential trades. They may not choose to be sellers at the deadline, but if they do, it's expected that the Colts' entire roster could be available for the right price, including two-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner.
Buckner is fed up with losing, as he's made clear in his recent postgame statements to Colts media, and no one can blame him. He could use a change of scenery with a true contender, and the Bears feel like a perfect fit. He would immediately become the best player on Dennis Allen's defensive line and at 32-years-old still has a couple good years left in him.
However, the Colts won't trade arguably their most popular player cheaply. A deal for Buckner would likely be significant, and he still carries a hefty salary cap hit, too.
A former Marine and Purdue Boilermaker, Pete has been covering the Chicago Bears since 2022 as a senior contributor on BearsTalk. He lives with his wife, two kids and loyal dog.

title: Bears Trade Rumor From NFL Insider Lists 3 Pro Bowlers Chicago is 'Connected To'
full_text:
Trade rumors continue to heat up around the Chicago Bears with a few weeks to go before the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, he's hearing the Bears are "connected to" interest in three different Pro Bowlers, as well as some players who aren't on the trade block. Schultz only named names with the three Pro Bowlers, though.
The list includes Indianapolis Colts defensive lineman DeForest Buckner, Arizona Cardinals edge rusher Josh Sweat and Los Angeles Chargers edge rusher Khalil Mack.
In addition to that, Schultz says the Bears are one of the teams he's "watching very closely" when it comes to trades.
"Two teams I'm watching very closely are the 49ers and Bears," Schultz said on The Pivot on Monday . "I've heard both teams connected to several defensive players, including rushers, Josh Sweat, Khalil Mack. Also, DeForest Buckner, along with some names who aren't necessarily on the trade block."
"I think both Chicago and San Francisco, Ryan, they want to be aggressive, and I'd be shocked if they don't make a move before the deadline," he added.
This is the second insider who has mentioned the Bears as a team that could be aggressive ahead of Nov. 10. FOX's Jay Glazer also said he expects the Bears to be aggressive , and he noted that Chicago has called about Mack.
You can follow along with our Bears trade deadline tracker right here to stay up to date with all of the latest rumors.
Mack, Sweat and Buckner are widely viewed as players who could realistically be on the move at the trade deadline next month. They were each mentioned in a recent column by ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport .
All three teams are in a massive hole, with the Chargers sitting at 0-6 and the Cardinals and Colts both at 2-5, so they fit the profile of teams likely to sell.
Buckner and Mack specifically are slated to be free agents next offseason, so it makes sense to unload them before they possibly leave next year, and Sweat will turn 30 in March and doesn't fit the long-term plans of the rebuilding Cardinals, who need all the draft capital they can get.
The Bears have needs on the interior of the defensive line and at edge rusher.
The Gervon Dexter trade has proven to be a mistake because the Bears are now lacking pass-rush juice up the middle, and Chicago hasn't been all that great against the run, either.
Buckner has traditionally been a very good run defender and he's an impact pass-rusher, as evidenced by his four sacks in seven games this season.
Mack and Sweat are two proven edge rushers who could turn the Bears' OK pass rush into an electric one. The Bears have some uncertainty there with Dayo Odeyingbo on injured reserve and they could use more depth overall.
Sweat only has two sacks this season, but he's coming off a 12-sack campaign, which was his second double-digit showing in four seasons. Mack is long in the tooth but has shown he's still got a lot to offer with his three sacks in six games, and he had 5.5 in 12 contests in 2025.
We would love to see the Bears come away with any one of these three players, but in a perfect world they get Buckner and one of the interior linemen.
Mack will be the fan-favorite for obvious reasons, but Sweat being younger and under contract for two more years might make him the more sensible option.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: What the Bears Need to Consider in Any Trade Pitch for Khalil Mack
full_text:
The trade winds continue to circulate in advance of the 3 p.m. Nov. 10 deadline, and especially around teams in the NFC North.
With all four teams over .500 and Minnesota unbeaten, the North is the place where teams with available talent need to focus trade efforts. The Bears are in a situation where they both n eed help and need to do more to bolster their chances than other North teams. They're essentially competing against North teams on the field but also in the trade market.
In reporting Sunday that the Bears already at least discussed a Khalil Mack trade with the Chargers, Fox's Jay Glazer added something else confirming their status as potential buyers .
"I think they’re going to be very aggressive," Glazer said on Fox. "Ryan Poles, that’s what he does — more aggressive than the other teams in that division.
"So I think they still need help on the defensive side of the ball. And I could see them trying to add some more weapons there.”
Mack would definitely not hurt. The Bears generated pass rush the last two games without Montez Sweat available because they blitzed their minds out against the Falcons and Patriots.
What the Bears really need is help stopping both the run, rushing the passer and defending the pass. Mack gets two of these done for them. In fact, at this moment is Pro Football Focus grade is better stopping the run than at rushing the passer.
Although Poles was not the GM who brought Mack to Chicago through the 2018 trade with the Raiders, he was the one who had to trade away a player who made an immediate impact in Chicago. Having been with the Chiefs organization, Poles knew very well at the time what they were giving up in their 2022 rebuild.
🧵Unpopular opinion alert: Ryan Poles is dangerously approaching Ryan Pace territory by consistently trading picks away. Pace did it to trade up, but Poles is doing it for veterans. In last 2 years, has traded 2nd, 4th, 4th, 5th, 6th, and 6th round picks away for veterans.
"With the excitement of the players we did bring in, I would say one of the harder things to do was the Khalil Mack trade," Poles told writers at the 2022 owners meetings following the trade with the Chargers."
They made the move in order to acquire more cap space and also received second- and sixth-round draft picks.
"There are a lot of things with analytics, age, play time," Poles said. "We put all of that together, and there's a timing mechanism as well. If you wait, what does that look like? If you do it now, what does that look like? We just thought right now it would allow the Bears to have more ammunition to add more players.
Ryan Poles needs to make a trade for  3 players: - #Chargers EDGE - #Buccaneers DB - #Colts DT If these trades get done, there is a very high likelihood Caleb Williams will be playing football in February. pic.twitter.com/Qo5xPoFXgN
"It was just looking at our future. It was looking at where we needed to go. It just seemed like the right time to do it in terms of value where we can help this team out now and in the future."
It obviously didn't work out the way Poles hoped under coach Matt Eberlfus, but Mack's return would generate fan excitement and also give them another edge who defends the run and pass.
Here are three things to consider when pondering the possibility of a Bears trade for Mack.
Mack ! Only 8.2 cap hit and he & his wife love it in Chicago. Happy wife happy life. https://t.co/ppuofh9bhe
Mack would have no problem fitting in with Chicago overall because he's been here before, but he also has familiarity with defensive coordinator Dennis Allen. The Raiders drafted Mack in 2014 when Allen was their head coach. Allen he was quickly fired in late September of that season before Mack even had one sack for his career.  As a fit in the locker room, there is no doubt Mack would blend in as he was never a real loud or domineering type. He blended in very quickly as one of the guys last time and has wherever he has played.
The Bears are not really desperate for another edge, unless Sweat is suspended again or gets hurt.  Their ideal addition would be a defensive tackle who provides a real push from the inside to stop the run and pass because they already have sufficient starting quality on the edge with Sweat, Austin Booker and will have Dayo Odeyingbo back from IR in the future from a quad injury. Playing four edge rushers on game day would be no problem if they had Mack. The rotation also has Shemar Turner in it now and he has had 20 plays at edge or lining up over tackle in two games with solid PFF grades both stopping the run and pass despite his total inexperience.
Some names to watch ahead of the NFL’s Nov. 10 trade deadline: pic.twitter.com/6THEK7IFqT
A better asset to acquire would be the defensive tackle who takes double teams off Grady Jarrett or another play-making defensive tackle like Jarrett, who also rushes the passer effectively. For this reason, someone like 6-foot-7, 295-pound, 32-year-old Colts defensive tackle DeForest Buckner could be a good fit. He is being mentioned often as available for trade because his contract expires after this year, Indianapolis fired GM Chris Ballard, and he is the athletic type of defensive tackle Allen favors for his scheme and not a blob or roadblock type. Buckner's only drawback is his run defense has tailed off in recent years. Karon Payne is also rumored to be on Washington's trading block and he might be a better fit than Buckner because he does stop the run, although his rush is below Buckner's standard.
Mack is a 269-pound outside linebacker in a 3-4 scheme. At this stage in his career, he's probably more of a fit for the Bears' 4-3 base than a 3-4 because he'd have very few pass coverage responsibilities. He moved seamlessly into the Bears' 3-4, which was later scrapped. Basically, Mack has played effectively wherever he has gone and in whatever system he played.  At 35, he remains a consistent and effective player against the run and pass, and had three sacks in his first four games this season.
At this point between the reporting of @JayGlazer , @AdamSchefter , and @RapSheet its imminent the #Bears will trade for a major difference maker on defense. Whether it’s Khalil Mack, Josh Sweat, or someone else not previously mentioned is anyone’s guess.
This is twofold. They could easily afford Mack on the payroll for this year because his remaining salary cap hit due this year per Overthecap.com would be just below $5 million and the Bears have just over $9 million available. He was operating only on a one-year deal with the Chargers this year after his contract there expired following the 2025 season. That's the Bears' cap cost. The other cost involved, of course, is what they would need to give up to get Mack. Would they go as high as a Day 2 pick for him? It seems unlikely. A mid-rounder like a fifth or possibly a fourth would be the cap for someone who is 35 years old.

If they don't get Mack, it could be he winds up facing them in the NFC North. The Lions have been touted often as a destination for Mack and their defense has struggled greatly earlier this season, although they did produce a strong effort Sunday in beating the Packers.

ESPN's Bill Barnwell on Saturday put forth a column calling the Lions the ideal team to acquire Mack and proposed the trade should be a fourth- and sixth-round pick to the Chargers for both Mack and cornerback Donte Jackson. Detroit is badly in need of secondary help.

title: Bears Trade Deadline Tracker: Every Rumor For Chicago With 2 Weeks to Go
full_text:
With the NFL trade deadline falling on Nov. 10, the Chicago Bears have about two more weeks to improve their roster before that avenue is closed for the rest of the season.
This year's trade deadline is a week later than it was last year, with the NFL deciding to push it back a week . That was a smart move because it opens up the possibility for more trades because teams will have a bit more clarity on where they stand.
After starting the season 5-2 , the Bears look like a true contender, so we'd expect them to make at least one move, and more specifically, a move on the defensive side of the ball.
With two weeks left to go, trade rumors are already swirling around the Bears. You can follow all of the latest ones in our tracker below. The newest rumor is at the top.
NFL insider Jordan Schultz is another reporter saying the Bears are expected to be aggressive, and he linked them to interest in two edge rushers, Josh Sweat and Khalil Mack, and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner in an appearance on "The Pivot."
"Two teams I'm watching very closely are the 49ers and Bears," Schultz reported. "I've heard both teams connected to several defensive players, including rushers, Josh Sweat, Khalil Mack. Also, DeForest Buckner, along with some names who aren't necessarily on the trade block.
"I think both Chicago and San Francisco, Ryan, they want to be aggressive, and I'd be shocked if they don't make a move before the deadline."
We've of course heard plenty of connections to Mack, but Sweat and Buckner are two new names.
Sweat would be a fine addition to the edge rushers room given his history of production with eight or more sacks in three of the past four seasons, and Buckner would solve the Bears' need for more pass-rush juice and run defense help up the middle.
Here's even more smoke to the fire that the Bears are trying to acquire Khalil Mack.
FOX NFL insider Jay Glazer reported on Sunday that the Bears have "already talked to" the Chargers about a Mack trade.
Glazer also said he believes the Bears will be "more aggressive" than their NFC North counterparts.
"I know they've already talked to, you know, the Chargers, saying, 'Hey, what about a guy like Khalil Mack?' I think they're going to be very aggressive. Ryan Poles, that's what he does. More aggressive than the other teams in that division," Glazer said.
With that, Mack to the Bears continues to pick up steam.
During a segment on Sunday morning, ESPN's Adam Schefter touched on the Khalil Mack situation and, while doing so, said, "You have to wonder if a team like the Chicago Bears will keep calling."
That seems to imply the Bears have already called Los Angeles about a trade for the nine-time Pro Bowler, but he may also just be saying the Bears could be persistent in inquiring about Mack if they are turned down by the Chargers at first. We can't say for sure.
If it is indeed the former, the plot thickens.
ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport wrote on Sunday that the Bears are "expected" to make a play for Los Angeles Chargers edge rusher Khalil Mack.
"There is expected to be interest in Mack from teams such as the Chicago Bears, but the Los Angeles Chargers have given no indication that they are willing to make any trades at this time. The Chargers (0-6) insist they are trying to win games, but that doesn't mean they're not going to get calls on Mack in the coming weeks," Rapoport and Schefter said.
The Chargers' stance on trading Mack might be "no" right now, but at 0-6, they would be silly not to, especially with the possibility that Mack could retire after this season, something he contemplated before deciding to play in 2026.
The Bears absolutely need more depth at edge rusher. We need not look further than what has transpired in the last few weeks to know that is the case after Dayo Odeyingbo got hurt and landed on injured reserve and Montez Sweat got suspended .
The reality is, things can change very quickly, so while the Bears have a positive situation now, that may not be the case all year.
Adding to that, there is no such thing as too much help at edge rusher and the Bears can increase their chances of making a Super Bowl run by beefing up the position.
Acquiring Mack would certainly do that, as the future Hall of Famer and former Bear has three sacks in six games this season.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: Why Jaxon Smith-Njigba Won't be the Bears' Biggest Headache vs Seahawks in Week 8
full_text:
In case you didn't stay up for Sunday Night Football, you missed an incredible fireworks show. Seattle Seahawks wide receiver and reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year Jaxon Smith-Njigba put up 150 yards and one touchdown on just nine catches. The Kansas City Chiefs came into that game knowing that Smith-Njigba was their biggest matchup problem on defense and they still couldn't slow him down, and that's going to be a problem for Seattle's next opponent, the Chicago Bears.
As good as he was and is, however, Smith-Njigba is not the boogeyman that the Bears should be most worried about ahead of next week's Monday night showdown. Instead, the biggest threat to ending Chicago's winning streak at two will be on the sidelines: Seahawks head coach and defensive play-caller Mike MacDonald.
Kansas City Chiefs running back and former Seahawk Kenneth Walker III entered Week 7 having put up at least 100 rushing yards in four of five games so far this year, averaging an incredible 6.3 yards per carry. But the Seahawks shut the lights off on Walker , holding him to a paltry 36 yards on 14 carries. Patrick Mahomes had thrown for at least 225 yards and two touchdowns in three of his last four games; Seattle held him to 165 yards and zero touchdowns. In fact, for the first time in his NFL career, Mahomes didn't get to the red zone even once.
Simply put, when Seattle's defense is on, it's arguably the best in the league. They're No. 1 and No. 10, respectively, in ESPN's pass rush and run stop win rates . They've given up some high scoring games this year, sure. But they proved on Sunday night that they have the horsepower to choke out even the best offenses, and that's going to be a problem for Chicago.
The Bears are not built to win a defensive slog. If they can't move the ball consistently on offense, they're going to fall behind in a hurry if their opponent has even a halfway decent offense. Look at the Bears' disastrous Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers for an example. Tyson Bagent started in place of the injured Caleb Williams and looked like a deer in headlights. At the same time, Jordan Love and the Packers offense streaked down the field, putting up points in bunches en route to a 31-7 win.
Smith-Njigba is going to get his next Monday, make no mistake about that. I wouldn't be surprised if Chicago's vulnerable secondary gives up nearly 200 receiving yards and multiple scores to him alone. If Caleb Williams and the offense can't keep up with that kind of pace, it's going to get ugly real fast.
Bears fans can hope for a miraculous Week 8 game in which Dennis Allen's defense somehow keeps the ball out of Smith-Njigba's hands and knocks Seattle's offense off of its game plan, but that looks more and more like a pipe dream. The  most realistic path to victory for Chicago is winning a shootout in Seattle, but how can they get that done when we just watched the mighty Chiefs get absolutely stone-walled for 60 minutes? That's the Gordian knot that Johnson must unravel.
Hopefully, the Bears will have Kyle Monangai back from injury by that time. Having both him and D'Andre Swift in the backfield would go a long way towards keeping the offense on track. Losing Cole Kmet to a season-ending injury hurts, but they still have Colston Loveland. And then, of course, there's quarterback Caleb Williams, who is playing like a legit MVP candidate . Seattle's defense may be terrifying, but so is Chicago's offense.
To undo the Goridan knot, Alexander the Great drew his sword and cut through the ropes, a brutally simple and effective solution to a daunting problem. Johnson's solution to beating Seattle may prove to be equally as obvious: pound the rock and let Caleb Williams cook. We'll see in one week.
A former Marine and Purdue Boilermaker, Pete has been covering the Chicago Bears since 2022 as a senior contributor on BearsTalk. He lives with his wife, two kids and loyal dog.

title: NFL Insider Confirms 'Aggressive' Bears Have Begun Pursuit of Khalil Mack Trade
full_text:
As Chicago Bears fans dream of a potential Khalil Mack reunion, it appears the team is has already taken a step toward making it happen.
On Sunday, FOX's NFL insider, Jay Glazer, revealed that the Bears have already put in a call to the Los Angeles Chargers to inquire about the availability of Mack.
Glazer also noted that he believes the Bears are going to be the most aggressive team in the NFC North when it comes to making a move at the trade deadline.
"I think of the teams in the NFC North, there's going to be one team that's going to be really aggressive when it comes to the trade deadline. I think that will be the Chicago Bears," he said .
"I know they've already talked to, you know, the Chargers, saying, 'Hey, what about a guy like Khalil Mack?' I think they're going to be very aggressive. Ryan Poles, that's what he does. More aggressive than the other teams in that division."
Glazer's report came on the same day ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported that the Bears are expected to have interest in Mack as the deadline approaches.
"There is expected to be interest in Mack from teams such as the Chicago Bears, but the Los Angeles Chargers have given no indication that they are willing to make any trades at this time," the ESPN reporters wrote. "The Chargers (0-6) insist they are trying to win games, but that doesn't mean they're not going to get calls on Mack in the coming weeks."
Trade buzz has been swirling around the Chargers because of the fact that they're 0-6 and going nowhere.
Mack in particular has been widely speculated about because he checks the boxes of someone who could get traded because he's on a one-year contract and may hang up his cleats after 2026.
There are so many reasons why bringing Khalil Mack back makes sense for the Bears. The feeling of nostalgia in bringing a fan-favorite back to Chicago would be overwhelming.
For starters, Chicago needs more depth at edge rusher. The Bears have gotten solid production out of the position this season, but they could certainly use more.
Mack has shown he's got plenty of gas left in the tank with three sacks in six games this season and acquiring him would give the Bears an edge rushers room capable of pushing this defense forward.
Not to mention, we've seen how quickly things can change there in the last few weeks, when the Bears lost Dayo Odeyingbo to injured reserve and Montez Sweat to a suspension.
Thankfully, Kyler Gordon has turned into Reggie White , which has helped cover for their losses. However, Chicago can't depend on that all the time.
Then we have the aspect of how much adding Mack boosts the culture, which is already good to begin with. Mack is a leader and his mere presence just makes this team better.
Lastly, there is no long-term commitment necessary here, which is important to note because the Bears' financial outlook isn't great, with Over The Cap noting the Bears are currently slated to be $1 million over the cap next offseason.
Mack is scheduled to be a free agent in 2027, and there's also a chance he may retire after he mulled doing so after last season .
Add it all up and it's not hard to see why trading for Mack is a no-brainer decision for the Bears. Now, general manager Ryan Poles just has to seal the deal to bring Mack home.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: NFC North Standings: Where Bears Sit After Vikings, Packers & Lions Games in Week 7
full_text:
The Chicago Bears were idle on Sunday after playing their Week 7 game on Thursday night, and that left Chicago watching their division rivals over the course of the day.
Of course, the Bears emerged victorious over the New England Patriots in their Week 7 contest, 30-24, and moved to 5-2. As a result, they were sitting in second place going into the weekend.
The other three NFC North teams were in action on Sunday, with the Minnesota Vikings taking on the Indianapolis Colts and the Green Bay Packers facing the Detroit Lions.
Here's a look at the results of those contests, followed by the updated NFC North standings.
In what was one of the ugliest games of the Sunday slate, the Vikings found a way to beat the lowly Indianapolis Colts, 16-10.
The Vikings managed just 275 yards of total offense and could not get much going on that side of the ball, but Brian Flores' defense is really, really good and shut the Colts down throughout, limiting Indianapolis to just 218 total yards.
With the win, the Vikings moved to 6-0 and Minnesota is the only unbeaten team in the NFC, and one of two unbeaten teams in the NEL, along with the Kansas City Chiefs, who play on Sunday night.
What a bizarre game this was.
Both teams did everything they could to hand the game over to the other and there were countless questionable penalties, especially on the Packers, miscues and terrible coaching decisions (we're looking at you, Dan Campbell).
Nevertheless, the Lions managed to be slightly less awful than the Packers en route to a 20-17 victory on a field goal in the closing seconds.
Fun fact: Packers kicker Trey Smack has two field goal attempts of 35 yards or less that have been missed or blocked and the rest of the league has one combined this entire season, according to ESPN Research .
1. Vikings (6-0 2. Bears (5-2) 3. Lions (4-2) 4. Packers (4-3)
With the Lions beating the Packers, the Bears hold on to second place going into Week 8, but they failed to gain any ground on Minnesota, who has a multi-game lead over Chicago.
Meanwhile, the Packers' loss sends them to the cellar in the division and the Lions move out of that spot into third place.
The Bears draw the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night in Week 8 while the Packers will take on the Carolina Panthers on Thursday night and the Lions will host the Vikings on Sunday.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: Five Ways the Bears Can Improve Even After Starting Season 5-2
full_text:
Any team can improve, even those among the unbeaten ranks.
The Bears were 24-point losers just three weeks ago at Green Bay and even after consecutive impressive wins they can still find ways to up their performance.
Here are five big ways Caleb Williams and the offense or Dennis Allen's defense can improve after the mini-bye week when they go to Seattle, and when they return home Nov. 8 to play resurgent Tampa Bay.
Bears’ WR Luther Burden III with the fumble and the Panthers recover. pic.twitter.com/T5o12SZuDn
This may easily have escaped the attention of some but only the Chargers and Saints had lost more fumbles than the Bears going into Week 7 games. Last year the Bears lost seven fumbles for the entire season. This year they have already lost six, egregious and otherwise.
Love D'Andre Swift but another fumble? pic.twitter.com/h2qrVLcWOy
This is a recording, stop dropping passes. Yes, Johnson said they had to stop this after the loss to the Rams in the playoffs season. He even got rid of one of their worst perpetrators, Olamide Zaccheaus. Yet, whether it's Rome Odunze or Colston Loveland or one of the backs, someone always seems to come up with a dropped pass. They finished with the fifth-most drops last year with 29. So they have improved -- they had the sixth most dropped passes going into Sunday games.
Colston Loveland with a bad 3rd down drop. One play later makes up for it with a big time catch. Unflappable. First 5 games 13 catches for 110 yds the last two games 13 catches for 134 yards. 📈 #DaBears #Bears pic.twitter.com/H3tsHimRbO
Going into Sunday's games, the Bears had the fifth-most penalties with 53, although they were certain to move down in ranks with some other teams just behind them and still playing this week. They were worst most of last season, but this is still an embarrassing level.
"I'm proud of the fact that right now -- we're not playing very clean football, very disciplined football from a penalty standpoint there's too many pre-snap penalties and there's too many holding penalties right now for us - but despite those, our guys still find a way to get back on track and overcome," Johnson said. "I've been a part of teams where you get one penalty and that just derails the whole drive and that's it. That's not what's happening to us right now. I look forward to the day that we clean those up and see what that looks like.”
🚨 #Bears WR Jahdae Walker was EJECTED from the game after headbutting a defender. 🐻 Completely unnecessary and unacceptable. There’s no room for that kind of mistake, especially in a close game. Chicago HAS to clean up these undisciplined penalties moving forward. #DaBears … pic.twitter.com/2ctc7ICOPP
Typical was the first drive of the game against Atlanta. They went 67 yards for a touchdown on the possession and had three penalties, including a hold on Theo Benedet.
It might seem like missed tackles would be their biggest problem, especially after the way they handled the short Patriots pass before halftime on Thursday. But they actually were tied for 11th fewest missed tackles going into Sunday and stand to be even better after those games. Actually, their problem has been defending deeper throws and no one would be surprised by this after the way they let the Packers complete long throws and even did it against Atlanta the following week. On Thursday, the Patriots tried to test this and Tyrique Stevenson got back to knock one down. Perhaps they are improving or will. According to NFLGSIS statistics, the Bears have given up the fifth highest average gain per completion on deep passes to the right side (16.86), the third highest average gain on deep passes over the middle (29.13), and the 11th highest gain per passes completed against them to the left side (13.69). Their pass defense overall hasn't been great, as rookie safety Dillon Thieneman is their top tackler with 43. If the safety makes the most tackles, it can be a sign things are not going right on defense -- although Dennis Allen does call on his safeties to be all over the field.
Jordan Love updated career vs Bears 136/203 Cmp/Att | 67.0 Cmp% 1,892 Pass Yds | 9.3 Yards/Att +81.8 Total EPA | 0.41 EPA/Play 15 TDs | 2 Ints 7.4 TD% | 1.0 Int% 117.3 Passer Rtg pic.twitter.com/fXuFcGCBJ6 https://t.co/GOajAYrNKC
Even after they improved and were 4-for-5 and 3-for-4 the last two games in the red zone at scoring TDs, the Bears still rated only 19th in TD percentage for the red zone going into Sunday. At the root of their problem is their inability to move the pile in close on runs. D'Andre Swift is tied for the third-most rushing TDs inside the 10 in the NFL with six but he averages 1.85 yards per run inside the 10. Derrick Henry, for instance, has averaged 2.5 yards per rush inside the 10 and leads in TD runs inside the 10. Swift has only 13 yards on 12 carries inside the 5. Kyle Monangai also is below 2.0 yards per run inside the 10, althoug he has been hurt the last two weeks. It's not a terrible problem and they can offset this with short passes or Williams keepers. Other teams have similar issues in close. KC's Kenneth Walker, for instance, averages only 1.6 yards inside the 10. But they can make things much easier for themselves by getting more TD runs inside the 5.
This problem could be over with Williams back healthy, and definitely could be once Monangai is healthy again after toe and finger issues.
In red zone trips with Caleb Williams the Bears are scoring TDs at an 80% rate The only 2 non-TD drives were a fumble and a kneel down https://t.co/cDlVP35TxV

title: Give Ben Johnson Extra Time to Prepare and Here's What Bears Can Expect
full_text:
A day after Ben Johnson's Bears beat one half of the Super Bowl XL teams, he paused to look at what's coming with extra time now to prepare to face the other team from  last year's title game, the Seahawks.
"Thought they did a really nice job; finding a way to get a win like that on a short week," Johnson said of his team. "Takes a lot of mental preparation over the course of a few short days to make sure we download the game plan and put it to life like they did.
"Credit to the staff as well for getting that job done and I’m looking forward to taking a step back and catching our breath here this weekend.  Gives us a chance to evaluate where we're at personnel wise, schematically. Almost like a mini-bye week in a lot of regards also."
Is this necessarily good for the staff, though? The rest always helps players, no doubt. However, Johnson's ability to get the Bears ready for Thursday's win over New England with only a few days of work kept in line with a trend he has shown in coaching.
Now, he faces the opposite situation with the extended mini-bye weekend in his pocket. There's extra time for Seattle to prepare, as well. Seattle's extra time is very limited, though, since they're playing a Sunday night game with the Chiefs, followed by the Monday night game against the Bears.
I owe you honesty. Chicago would be my pick to come out of the NFC today. Can’t apologize for it. Ben Johnson is in his bag, and Caleb Williams may be the most talented QB in the conference. I just lost likability points, didn’t I? pic.twitter.com/ekMBq5kqGi
A couple of trends are at work in this case for Bears fans to consider with their team, and also another with the Seahawks.
The one trend with Seattle is how coach Mike Macdonald has been very good at getting his team ready when given extra time, even if it is just one extra day. Meanwhile, the same cannot entirely be said for Johnson with the Bears.
Macdonald is in his third season as Seattle coach, and during his tenure Seattle is 11-3 when he has more than the normal week to get the team ready for a game.
You know who else has been the villains? The Patriots w/ Brady & The Chiefs w/ Mahomes. They were villains for many years. And I’ve been hoping and praying that I’d get to watch my Bears be the villains one day. 🐻 ⬇️
Considering Seattle missed the playoffs with a 10-7 record in his first year, was 3-3 this season going into Sunday night this season besides their 2025 Super Bowl season,  the11 wins Macdonald has had with extra time accounts for a huge amount of their victories.  Of the wins they've had under Macdonald, 40.7% came during a longer work week. This includes their playoffs and the Super Bowl last season.
The other side, and of more concern for the Bears, is how Johnson's team has done when he had extra time. The Bears are only 3-4 in games when Johnson has extra time to get them ready.
Are they putting too much into game plans? Some of the opponents have been very strong, and that has to be taken into account, but 3-4 when your team is 17-9 in two seasons is not saying much for his ability to use the extra time wisely.
Baldy, can we all agree Ben is a top 3 play caller in the league?
If there is a ray of hope here, it's how Johnson is trending up.
The Bears are 2-0 this season when he had extra time. They were only 1-4 last year.
The only win the Bears had last season when Johnson had extra time was their bye week and they needed a late Jayden Daniels fumble to beat Washington 25-24. They lost to the Rams in the playoffs with one less day to prepare after they had beaten the Packers. They also lost the season opener to Minnesota, their regular-season game to Green Bay following their Black Friday win over the Eagles, and then to the 49ers after they beat the Packers at Soldier Field in the regular season.
However, this year they beat the Eagles with an extra day to prep on Monday night, and also won their opener over Carolina with all offseason and preseason to prepare.
Former NFL Great Mark Schlereth goes all in on Ben Johnson. The league has finally seen behind the fake tough guy curtain. pic.twitter.com/kmxbV12ycP
Much can go into these numbers beyond prep time, of course.  The opponent and how they lost matters. For instance, they lost the game last year at San Francisco but no one is going to blame the way Johnson had the offense prepared. They had 38 points. It was the defense faltering.
Perhaps Johnson just needed time as the head coach to get the trend working his way. Another number says this could be the case. That one is how he did prepping his offense in Detroit when he had an extra day.
Although Johnson wasn't head coach, he was the coordinator who called plays and came up with game plans — with head coach Dan Campbell overseeing, of course.
"The Bears believe in him" @howaboutafresca and @SwollenDome make the case that Ben Johnson is the best head coach in the NFL right now pic.twitter.com/qJft2l644B
The Lions were 13-4 when Johnson was offensive coordinator and had more than a week to prep. In fact, some of Detroit's most impressive offensive efforts occurred while Johnson had extra time to prepare and was a coordinator.
One of their biggest regular-season wins and blowouts was at Dallas in 2024 when they won 47-9 after they had extra time to get ready.
The great majority of Johnson's "40-burgers" over three seasons with Detroit came when he had extra time to get the offense ready. They scored 42 on Seattle, 41 at San Francisco, 42 against the Chargers in L.A., 40 against Carolina, and 41 at home against the Bears with extra time in victories. They also had 42 against Buffalo in a loss.
This could all work the Bears' way on Monday Night Football in Seattle, but something must give because Seahawks will have a similar trend working their way.

title: Bengals Are on Pace for Historic Season After Dominating Win Over Ravens
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals earned their second straight victory this season with a convincing 35-13 beatdown of the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday.
While the final score is what everyone is talking about, things didn't look good at halftime. The Bengals were shut out in the first half before ripping off 35 straight points to win a pivotal divisional matchup.
Joe Burrow and the offense found their rhythm, and so did the team's defense. The performance on Sunday continues to put this version of the Bengals on a path that could make them one of the more special teams in the franchise's history.
Paul Dehner Jr. shared that the Bengals' point margin this season is the third-highest since 2000 and fifth in the NFL.
After Sunday's win, the Bengals have a +41 point margin this season. The Bengals have scored 163 points this season and have allowed 122.
Taking a closer look at the franchise's history, the 2005 Bengals have the best point margin at +71, with the 2015 team in second at +60.
There's still a long way to go if the 2026 Bengals want to make history, but Sunday's second-half performance proves this team has what it takes.
It's clear this Bengals offense can score in bunches. Burrow tossed all four of his touchdowns in the second half on Sunday.
The offense is averaging 345 yards per game, but on Sunday, the team flew by that number, finishing with 359 yards. Yes, the offense is what moves the needle, but what about the defense?
Al Golden's unit should get a tip of the cap for keeping the team in the game in the first half, allowing the Ravens only 13 points. But their second-half shutout deserves just as much praise as the offensive onslaught.
The Bengals had four sacks on Sunday, putting them at a tie at the top of the chart for most sacks in the NFL with 21. This front office had a mission to make the defensive line better, and did just that with the additions of Boye Mafe and Dexter Lawrence.
This team has shown flashes of brilliance. The next step is putting it all together for four quarters. Statistics continue to show the Bengals are one of the best all-around teams in the league, they just haven't hit their full potential. That should put the rest of the league on notice.

title: Zac Taylor Updates Injury Timelines For Erick All, Kyle Dugger Entering Titans Week
full_text:
The Bengals had two injuries pop up during Sunday's thrilling comeback win against the Ravens . Erick All (knee) and Kyle Dugger (quad) got knocked out of the game, and Bengals head coach Zac Taylor updated their outlook for Week 8 on Monday.
All's already had that right knee operated on multiple times this decade, causing him to miss the entire 2025 season.
Still, there's no confirmation on the severity yet as Cincinnati signed Cam Grandy to the roster in the mean time. Dugger is out at least for this week with his issue.
"He'll definitely be out this week, and we'll get more information on his quad," Taylor said before touching on when they'll know more surrounding All. "I'm not sure. It could be in the next day. I'm not positive on that."
All did sound optimistic about the outlook after the game. The fact he talked to any media at all is a good sign.
Both players are important for Cincinnati's depth on either side of the ball.
All played a season-high 33 snaps last week and was pacing towards close to that on Sunday, while Dugger posted a season-high 54 in Week 3 before getting injured and returning to play 11 snaps on Sunday.
Cincinnati got great impact from the rest of the roster to still win without them.
"Yes, I think we know who we are. At the end of the day, from a personnel standpoint, I think no matter who we're going against, we know who we are," Orlando Brown Jr. said after the win. "We know what we're capable of, which is fortunate, from the way that this team is built from a talent standpoint, the type of characters that we have in here and [with] the type of men in here. So, at no point in time would I tell you that we weren't going to stay the course. We had to come together at the end of that first half, make a commitment to one another to be more physical and violent and be able to go out there and finish."
Cincinnati should be getting names like Andrei Iosivas and Jalen Davis onto the practice field and off of injured reserve soon. They are continuing to knock on wood with great health as we head toward the midway point of the 2026 season.
Taylor and the rest of the roster have Tuesday off before returning for a normal three-practice week on Wednesday. They battle the Titans at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.
Spoke with Erick All Jr. at his locker postgame. Had street clothes on but no brace. Was standing and smiling. Said he’ll know more Monday but he’s hoping and praying for encouraging news.

title: Report: Bengals Signing Familiar Tight End Ahead of Titans Matchup
full_text:
The Bengals added another new name to the 53-man roster on Monday. WLWT's Charlie Clifford reported the team is signing tight end Cam Grandy for this week and beyond.
The team is back to a full roster. They plucked Grandy off of the Minnesota Vikings practice squad in what could be a sign of Erick All's injury fallout.
"The Bengals are signing tight end Cam Grandy off the Vikings practice squad to their 53-man roster, a league source tells WLWT. Grandy played a role in Cincinnati in 2024 & 2025 and is now back," Clifford posted on X.
Grandy has appeared in 13 career games with seven catches for 35 yards. All of those appearances have been with the Bengals from last season and 2024. He did not appear in any 2026 games so far.
Cincinnati is fresh off a massive AFC North win over Baltimore.
They flipped a 13-0 halftime deficit into a 35-13 win.
"[In the] second half. The first half was about third downs. We did a poor job on both sides of the ball on third down," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said on Sunday. "We didn't convert more than, like, a third-and-1. I think Ja'Marr [Chase] caught one early, but we didn't convert on the three main drives we had. Defensively, I don't know what the stats were in the first half, but I know they converted [almost] every one of them. Now, we did a good job limiting them to some field goals on two of those drives, which was key. But we just never really got in a rhythm. And [during] halftime, we came in here and took a deep breath. I thought guys really handled themselves well, and we came out and scored five straight touchdowns in the second half. [The] defense got five straight stops, and that's how you have to do it.
"That's how you go on the road and win. We had the turnover plus some fourth-down stops that count as more. I don't know how many. So, I'm just really proud of the way the guys responded, just took a deep breath, kept their composure, led, and went out there and put together as good a second-half performance as I've ever seen."
Cincinnati and Grandy are preparing for Tennessee at home this week.
