title: Bengals Stars Post Elite Pro Football Focus Grades Against Ravens, Best Team Mark of 2026 Season
full_text:
The Bengals impressed with their Pro Football Focus grade in Week 7. A 35-13 win over a division rival will do that as Cincinnati stormed back from a 13-0 halftime thud to the clear victory.
All in all, it was the team's highest-graded performance of the season at 85.9 overall. Two Bengals posted 90-plus offensive grades in the game: Tee Higgins (91.4) and Joe Burrow (91.2) .
Both were major catalysts for the comeback and played arguably their best games of the season at the right times. Burrow is now the clear best QB in PFF's database this season. He boasts a 91.2 overall grade in 2026; the next closest quarterback is Brock Purdy (85.5).
Higgins has been just as good, ranking third among all qualified receivers with a 91.4 overall grade during the 2026 season.
The rest of the top five offensive grades yesterday went to RB Samaje Perine (82.2), WR Ja'Marr Chase (79.1), and TE Erick All (77.6).
At the bottom, Cincinnati only had five players log more than 15 snaps and earn 65 or lower grades: Guard Dylan Fairchild (62.7), center Ted Karras (60.8), guard Dalton Risner (58.5), WR Mitchell Tinsley (55), and WR Dohnte Meyers (42.3).
Flipping to defense, DE Boye Mafe (90.2) continues to prove the Bengals right for picking him over potentially paying Trey Hendrickson this past offseason. He had a team-high five QB pressures in the game and three tackles.
The free-agent train continued with DT Dexter Lawrence (90) right behind him with four pressures. DT Jonathan Allen (86.5) also played a standout game. All three of those 2026 free agents have been slam-dunk additions for Cincinnati.
Two other players tallied 70-plus defensive grades: DE Cedric Johnson (74.6) and DT B.J. Hill (74.3).
Flashing to the bottom of the barrel, there were five high-snap players to earn 57 grades or worse: CB Dax Hill (56.3), safety Jordan Battle (54.2), CB DJ Ivey (53.7), DE Cashius Howell (47.1), and LB Demetrius Knight Jr. (36.6).
Cincinnati only missed three tackles, with one each for Battle and Knight.
They can clean up those mistakes this week before taking on the fifth-lowest-graded overall team in the league on Sunday, Tennessee (64.2 overall).

title: Zac Taylor Praises the Play of Boye Mafe, Pass Rush in Statement Win Over Ravens
full_text:
It was the tale of two halves for the Cincinnati Bengals in their 35-13 win over the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday.
The Bengals went to the locker room at halftime trailing 13-0. Then, 35 unanswered points were put on the board, sending the crowd in Baltimore to the parking lot a little early.
The Bengals' offense is receiving a lot of praise for their second-half performance, and rightfully so. However, the defense pitched a shutout in the second half that deserves its own kind of praise.
Domination in every aspect of the game led to the Bengals' dominant second half. What also needs to be highlighted after this performance is who the Bengals brought in this offseason to bolster their defensive line.
Defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence has been the shining star when it comes to offseason additions. But edge rusher Boye Mafe's stock continues to rise with each passing week.
The Bengals sacked Ravens quarterback Tyler Huntley four times on Sunday. Mafe accounted for 1.5 sacks. In his postgame comments, Bengals head coach Zac Taylor shared his thoughts on the team's edge rush and Mafe's performance in the win.
"Awesome. (Mafe) just affects the passer, and he got the two sacks," Taylor answered when asked about the performance of Mafe and the rest of his defensive line. "Cashius (Howell) got his first one, and seeing Dexter finish it off there, a lot of guys were coming into the backfield getting hands on them."
Taylor made a good point. It wasn't just the defensive line that was getting in the backfield. Safety Bryan Cook accounted for a half sack in Sunday's win.
The second half on Sunday was the performance that is expected from this team each and every time they step on the field. Now, it's about doing that for four quarters.
It sounds cliché, but this game was the biggest game so far this season for the Bengals. With the win, the team stays afloat in a division where everyone continues to find a way to win. Getting a division victory in a situation like this is paramount.
Looking ahead, the Bengals have a chance to separate themselves from the pack with their November schedule.
The Bengals' next three games are against the Tennessee Titans, the Atlanta Falcons, and a revenge matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers.
This team showed what their full potential can look like. Now, they need to prove they can put it together for a full game as the most important time of the year arrives.

title: 6 Winners and 2 Losers From Bengals' Dominant Comeback Win Over Ravens
full_text:
After an abysmal first half, the Bengals scored 35 unanswered points in the second half to blowout their division rival Ravens 35-13 in Baltimore. They're 4-2 on the season following the win.
Here are six winners and two losers from Sunday's victory.:
Burrow started the game rattled from the Ravens blitz. That changed drastically from the moment the second-half started as he completed 10-straight passes and led 5-straight touchdown drives.
He connected with seven different receivers in the game, finishing 22-of-30 for 292 yards, four touchdowns, no interceptions and a passer rating of 143.3.
A good football team does not look as unprepared coming out of a bye week as the Bengals did on Sunday. Head coach Zac Taylor had two weeks to get this Bengals team prepared to face the Ravens, and instead they looked completely undisciplined.
Throughout the entire first half the offense managed only three first downs and 59 total yards. They only possessed the ball for 7:40. The Ravens had the ball for 22:40.
Tee Higgins did not record a catch in the first half, and it is a major reason why the offense failed to gain any ground to start. That changed in the second half as he recorded four catches in the first 10 minutes of the third quarter for 61 yards and a touchdown.
With the Ravens defense focusing heavily on Ja'Marr Chase, Higgins took advantage with six receptions for 148 yards and a touchdown.
Not once, not twice, but three times the Bengals defense surrendered a first-down on third and long. On the games opening drive, Tyler Huntley found Zay Flowers on 3rd & 9 who diced through the Bengals defense for a 48-yard score.
Later in the first half, Huntley found Flowers again on a 3rd and 16 for a 20-yard catch. The lack of discipline in long third down situations must improve.
The Bengals prized offseason addition showed up in a huge way yet again. Lawrence created havoc for the Ravens offense all day and played a big role in holding Derrick Henry to 45 yards on 17 carries.
He staked his exclamation point on the day with his fourth sack of the season late in the fourth quarter. Lawrence has transformed the defensive line for this team.
Mafe consistently created pressure in this game and proved the Bengals right to pay him in free agency over signing Trey Hendrickson to a lucrative deal. Mafe ended the day with 1.5 sacks, two quarterback hits and a tackle-for-loss.
He looks the part of an ascending player who's ceiling could match Hendrickson's as a pass rusher and possibly beyond considering his ability to defend the run. Hendrickson finished with two quarterback hits, but didn't have a tackle or a sack.
Gesicki only had 12 catches heading into Sunday's game, but he's a reliable red zone threat. That trend continued against the Ravens. He caught the Bengals first touchdown of the day on the opening drive of the third quarter that cut the deficit to 13-7. Gesicki has now hauled in five touchdowns on just 13 receptions, and continues his streak as one of Burrow's favorite red zone targets. He has a touchdown in five of six games.
Howell finally got home for his first NFL sack this week on a critical 3rd & 11. He has routinely created pressure as a true pass-rusher this season, and should only continue to improve with each week that passes.

title: 'I Was Pretty Lights Out' - Joe Burrow Assesses Ravens Performance In Rare Way As MVP Play Continues
full_text:
Joe Burrow is usually pretty coy about his play game-to-game, but there was no hiding his excitement about Sunday's showing. Burrow didn't get many chances in the first half across the 35-13 bullseye on Baltimore, but he lit them up in the second half.
The veteran MVP candidate passed for four TDs in consecutive games to round out 292 yards in the air (22-30 completions). Most of that in the final 30 minutes.
"I think I played really well," Burrow said. "The first half was what it was, and obviously would have liked to have some of those back, but we didn't turn the ball over. That played a big part, and the second half I think I was pretty lights out. Yeah, I'll watch the tape and ask me again on Wednesday, but I think for the most part I was pretty good.
"Just trying to treat every play like it's its own universe and trying to critically think about what's required of me on the play and where the defense is going to tell me to go with the football, and they're going to have to adapt quickly sometimes in a play depending on what the defense is showing or what presents."
According to Sumer Sports, Burrow went 16/18 for 249 yards and 4 touchdowns in the second half against the Ravens. Burrow's 21.24 Total EPA in the second half is the 4th best second-half performance out of 2,204 qualifiers since 2022.
When Cincinnati's back sat firmly on the wall. He answered the call and diced up the home team.
The Bengals had to win that game to keep a majority percentage playoff projection on the board and not fall to the bottom of the division. Add in no Lamar Jackson, and the opportunity was too good not to see vintage Burrow.
His Week 7 outing notched a 92.6 ESPN QBR, the second-best outing of the week so far and good enough to launch him up to third among all QBs on the season tally (77.6 overall).
If he keeps playing like this and the Bengals win at least 12-13 games, keeping the MVP trophy out of his hands will be hard.
"We know who we have to be, and we let our big-time players go and make big-time plays. That's what the NFL is all about. You know you can do all these different things, but at the end of the day, you just gotta go make plays, gotta execute what's called, and that's what we did," Burrow concluded.
Onto Tennessee and Week 8.

title: 'Got To Step This S*** Up' - Ja'Marr Chase Delivers Halftime Speech to Fuel Bengals Win Over Ravens
full_text:
Ja'Marr Chase hammered home his captain traits in a massive winning way on Sunday afternoon. The Bengals trailed Baltimore 13-0 at halftime, and he came into the locker room delivering an impassioned speech to get the offense going.
The team posted its fewest first-half yardage tally since 2018. Then they ripped off nearly 300 yards in the next 30 minutes for a 35-13 win.
It ignited Amariis Mims, Joe Burrow, and more.
"Really fired us up, man. I saw it in his eyes, man," Mims said to FOX 19 and more at his locker. "We were not gonna leave here without going in. And I've always said when One talks and he gets that fire in front of him, everybody needs to shut up and listen. Because, as I said, he is not only the best receiver in the NFL, but probably one of the best players in the NFL, in my opinion.
"So when a guy like that talks, you shut up, and you listen, because it's very important. And we all did hear it, and we all shut up, and we heard it. And it worked, we came back and scored 35 straight points, and they scored zero. So that was definitely a speech that I don't mind him giving every week. If that's the case, if we're gonna do that, we need to give it every week."
Mims had a big smile on his face as Burrow got sacked just one time thanks in large part to arguably the best pass-blocking right tackle in the NFL this season.
Chase delivered with five catches for 62 yards and a score, while Tee Higgins continued his elite efficiency season with six catches for 128 yards and his own end zone trip.
"We had 15 plays, maybe two or three possessions, and it didn't go our way at all," Chase said about the speech reasoning at his locker. "We had opportunities to get the ball out of our hands. Joe was putting up with too much pressure, and I came in here screaming, saying somebody got to make a play. Somebody got to make a play, and I told the offense we can't look at our defense the whole time. We got to step this s*** up and make something work."
“Yeah, Ja’Marr went in there and got after everybody a little bit and got everybody fired up. That certainly plays a part, but at the end of the day, we just executed," Burrow noted.
Cincinnati is up to seventh in the AFC after that win and is right on pace with the rest of the AFC North contenders. The next conference win opportunity awaits against Tennessee at home this week. A team the whole locker room wants to start faster against.
Check out the full comments below:
Ja'Marr Chase delivered a halftime speech, and the Bengals delivered an unforgettable second half in Baltimore. "I've always said, when (No.) 1 talks, everybody needs to shut up and listen." Amarius Mims via @GSorrentinoTV in Baltimore. pic.twitter.com/SHvkh6LBER
"I came in here screaming: somebody's got to make a play for us." Strong reaction from Ja'Marr Chase on his halftime message to the team (via @GSorrentinoTV ). #Bengals @FOX19 pic.twitter.com/4acLRz3P11

title: 'Just Bread And Butter' - Zac Taylor, Joe Burrow Detail How Bengals Offense Stormed Back Against Baltimore
full_text:
What a difference one break can make.
Cincinnati's offense sputtered in its limited opening chances against Baltimore on Sunday. But then things changed in a big way across the final 30 minutes of a 35-13 win.
The attack hummed through the air and scored five touchdowns to flash the ceiling this whole team can reach. Bengals head coach Zac Taylor and quarterback Joe Burrow dove into the second-half barrage after the rare win.
According to our Jay Morrison, it marked the Bengals' first second-half shutout since Week 14, 2023, in a 34-14 win against the Colts. They trailed 13-0 at the break.
"We got ourselves in rhythm, but we found some things that are just bread and butter, Cincinnati Bengals . We got ourselves in some really good rhythm. Found some really good runs too," Taylor noted. "I thought the backs and the lines did an excellent job in the run game, getting us what we needed. Maybe we didn't have a 15-yard run, but that's not what we needed in this game. We just needed to stay on track so we can come back and try to hit him with another throw."
The throwing hit indeed as the team dropped back 31 times and ran 20.
Burrow carved up the Ravens for 292 yards, four touchdowns, and no turnovers.
"We made some nice adjustments in the second half that I think helped us. And at the end of the day, we just executed and made a lot of plays," Burrow said about the big moments in the final few frames. "We just started calling some of our base stuff. O-line protected great, and really we just got the ball in Ja'Marr (Chase) and Tee's (Higgins) hands as many times as we could."
Cincinnati needed to keep pace in the AFC North as the only team playing in the division this week.
They leave right in the thick of the division race with Pittsburgh and Cleveland. Both of them won on Sunday, while Baltimore fell to last place.
"We know who we are. We know who we have to be, and we let our big-time players go and make big-time plays," Burrow said. "That's what the NFL is all about. You can do all these different things, but at the end of the day, you just gotta go make plays, gotta execute what's called, and that's what we did."
Cincinnati has boosted its playoff odds to over 75% after the win and has the third-best point differential in the AFC now.
Things are clicking with a few below .500 teams up next. The Titans roll into town next Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.
First time the #Bengals have blanked a team in a second half since Week 14, 2023 in a 34-14 win against the Colts.

title: Even After an AFC North-Leading 5–2 Record, Not Everyone Has Warmed Up to the Browns
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns’ 5-2 AFC North-leading record with all five victories occurring in a come-from-behind fashion have impressed many in and around the NFL.
More than a few outlets are still skeptical that Cleveland can continue this brand of tight, play-from-behind, overall-point-deficit brand of football all the way to the team’s first division title since 1989 in the extinct AFC Central, despite five remaining games against teams with losing records, including three clubs at 2-5.
Projections to win the AFC North, according to ESPN Analytics: 🏈 Bengals (4-2): 68.3% 🏈 Steelers (5-2): 15.7% 🏈 Ravens (4-3): 10.5% 🏈 Browns (5-2): 5.5%
For example, ESPN Analytics has Cleveland with the worst chances among all four teams at just 5.5 percent, and Cincinnati as heavy favorites (68.3 percent) after Week 7 action.
Squawka has even less faith, putting the Browns chances at just 4.9 percent. That’s pretty far off from where they currently see the Bengals, at 59.9 percent.
And CBS Sports has a slightly better number for the Browns, at 8.6 percent probability of winning the division, but still lagging behind the other three clubs.
So…. @CBSSports still has the Browns having the lowest chance to win the AFC North despite’s wins over BAL and PIT pic.twitter.com/WBAf8xnIWQ
The Athletic’s Playoff Simulator is a bit more generous with the Browns after their Week 7 win, putting their chances at a division title at 17 percent, while parking Cincinnati’s odds at 45 percent. This model has the Browns basically tied with Baltimore, also at 17 percent, just below the Steelers’ 21 percent. Cleveland’s upcoming game is a road match at Pittsburgh, who they haven’t swept in a regular season since 1988, so a win on Sunday could surely flip the script for the Browns.
Where the Browns have made impressive gains is in the betting markets, where they started the season off at +2100. Even before Sunday’s game, Cleveland was being listed in the +1000 to +1800 range, but after beating the Titans in a hard fought battle on the road, the Browns’ odds have improved to the +585-+700 range, depending on the sportsbook.
For starters, Cleveland is carrying a -13 point differential , the only team in the division in the red after Week 7. Meanwhile, the Bengals are operating at +41 on the same stat. When push comes to shove, will the Browns be able to manufacture enough points to keep on winning down the road?
Then, there’s the four remaining divisional games on deck. Cleveland has yet to face the now heavy favorites Bengals, which they will do in Weeks 13 and 18. And, presumably, the Ravens will have Lamar Jackson back from injury in time for their Week 16 rematch.
Of course, next week’s test at Accrisure Stadium will be a big one, as the Browns face off against the Steelers for the second time this year after a tight win on a Thursday night. Remember, sweeps occur in the AFC North at a much lower rate than what league-wide averages show.
Then, of course, there’s the question of how long do you expect to continue to win on the games’ last drive , a model that’s been proven unsustainable over the long run over and over again.
The Browns cleaned up a number of things this Sunday against the Titans , but keep in mind it was a 1-5 opponent still looking for its first home win in eight tries on the other side of the field.
There’s no denying that Cleveland has been playing with fire, so it’s logical for so many to still be skeptical about the Browns until they prove they can win without the late-game drama.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Browns Rookie Spencer Fano Is Already Changing Cleveland's Offensive Line
full_text:
As the saying goes, “football is won in the trenches,” and that remains true for the Cleveland Browns.
The Cleveland Browns have struggled offensively throughout the 2026 season. Before the Titans matchup, the Browns ranked 28th in points per game and 29th in yards per game. That changed against Tennessee. The Browns exploded for 491 total yards and 27 points, driven by strong performances from multiple key skill players.
Quinshon Judkins with a big run to pick up the first down 🏃 CLEvsTEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TZiyT6cL3n
While many will focus on Deshaun Watson’s 308 passing yards or Quinshon Judkins’ 96 rushing yards and 2 rushing touchdowns, a budding star on the offensive line was also key to the Browns' victory.
The Cleveland Browns selected Utah offensive tackle Spencer Fano with the ninth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, signaling high expectations for his future. Despite playing right tackle during his final season in college, the Browns expected Fano to flip to the all-important blindside left tackle position, which he had experience with earlier in his career.
Fano has started every game at left tackle for the Browns this season, and while it hasn’t been all positive , Fano had a true breakout during the Browns' most recent matchup against the Tennessee Titans.
Spencer Fano earned his highest PFF grade of the season during the Browns' Week 7 matchup against the Tennessee Titans. Fano received an initial grade of 92.2 , making him the highest-graded offensive player for the Browns in their 27-24 win.
Fano’s breakout came against a strong Titans defensive line that features star names like defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers, making his performance more impressive despite the Titans' now 1-6 record.
Love to see this. KC - orbit motion decoy (holds BS LB) Fano - down block on Simmons (All-Pro) Boston - crack block on PS safety Barber - counter kickout Fannin - counter pull for PS ILB Judkins - tight course, make CB miss Every key player mentioned here is 22yo or younger. pic.twitter.com/XW4Xue6x7h
Fano has shown flashes of greatness in his young career, but this is his most complete NFL game yet. If Fano can continue to build on performances like this throughout his rookie season, the Browns may have their left tackle for many years to come.
While the Titans' defensive front is no slouch, the next challenge comes against one of the league's best, the division rival Pittsburgh Steelers. While history is not on Cleveland’s side, the Browns haven’t won in Pittsburgh during the regular season since 2003. If Fano can build on this performance against a Pittsburgh defensive front featuring T.J. Watt, Alex Highsmith and Cam Heyward, the sky may just be the limit for the young tackle’s career.

title: 5 Winners, 2 Losers From Browns Win Over Titans
full_text:
The Browns are now 5-2 seven weeks into the 2026 NFL season, to absolutely no one's surprise, after winning another game in the final seconds against the Tennessee Titans. Cleveland was down two touchdowns early in the game, but battled back in a huge way that ended up being their strongest offensive showing of the season.
There are a lot of points to note from the win, so let’s start off with the winners from Sunday.
Believe it or not, Watson’s 308 passing yards vs. Tennessee were the most in his Cleveland career, and the first time that he has thrown for 300+ since January 3rd, 2021, also against the Titans. His previous high with Cleveland was 289 in 2023, which came against, you guessed it, the Tennessee Titans.
Apart from the interception, Watson was very efficient in the passing game, getting the ball to the playmakers and giving them a chance to run with it. His rushing touchdown from nine yards out also gave Cleveland the cushion in the fourth quarter to leverage the game their way. Watson has now led the Browns to five game-winning drives this year, and is just the third quarterback since 1970 to have a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of a season, joining Troy Aikman in 1990 and Matthew Stafford in 2016.
Sunday was a breakout day for Quinshon Judkins; he rushed for 96 yards on 17 carries for two touchdowns. Those 5.6 yards per carry were the second-highest of his career so far, and it was because the offensive line was creating space for him. According to Next Gen Stats, Judkins averaged 2.3 yards before contact per carry, which was a season high and the first time this year he was over 1.0+ yards before contact.
Dylan Sampson was at last back in the backfield as well, and he showed off his speed totaling 77 yards on just nine touches, averaging 8.5 yards per touch.
What a breakout game it was for Concepcion; KC caught eight passes for 129 yards, and 82 of those yards came after the catch. Those 82 yards after the catch were a season-high for him, and his 55 yards after contact were the most by a wide receiver this season (NGS). He also was able to help in the run game, breaking an 18-yarder on an end around.
Might as well put the entire passing game on here, huh? Fannin was another guy who excelled after the catch, as 59 of his 91 receiving yards came after the catch. His 36-yard catch put Cleveland and the next winner right where they wanted to be.
While Szymt did miss a 43-yarder early in the fourth quarter, he stepped up when it mattered yet again, nailing a 32-yarder for a walk-off win. Szmyt now has four field goals that won Cleveland the game through seven weeks.
It is difficult to find losers for Cleveland from this game, but there are a couple.
Tony Pollard has Cleveland’s number as the Titans running back had another career day vs. the Browns, putting up 155 total yards and three touchdowns. The Browns are now 20th in the league in rushing yards allowed per game at 116.4, something that will hopefully get cleaned up later in the season.
Ward showed some flashes, hitting multiple slant routes to rookie Carnell Tate and second-year guy Elic Ayomanor for some nice gains. Apart from those throws, though, there wasn’t a ton of flashes, as he notably missed a touchdown on their final drive to Daniel Bellinger.
Ward is far from the Titans' first problem, but with the team at 1-6 and his stats are what they are, it may be alluring for Tennessee to look at those top QBs in next year’s class.
Hi, I’m Paul, I’m from Northeast Ohio, and a recent graduate of Kent State University. As an Ohio native, I’m a huge fan of the Browns, Guardians, and Cavaliers. Just don’t ask me about my favorite college team, though.

title: If The Browns Keep Winning, Will Deshaun Watson Land a Big Deal?
full_text:
It is no secret that Deshaun Watson has been great this season for the Cleveland Browns . Through seven weeks, he has led the NFL in game-winning drives with five.
Looking forward, the Browns can absolutely keep winning games with Watson at the helm. There may even be a chance for a division title and playoff push.
But after the 2026 season is all said and done, what is in store for Watson? This is the final year of his previously historic five-year contract .
Let's look at three options for the Browns.
Understandably, if Watson takes the Browns to the playoffs, he will most likely get an extension.
Realistically, even if he were to get injured and miss the remainder of the season, Cleveland has seen enough to most likely pay the former first-round pick.
At this moment in time, Watson getting a new deal is the most likely situation.
Patrick Mahomes         Deshaun Watson - 5-1 record                    - 5-2 record - 1,474 pass yards       - 1,482 pass yards - 9 pass TD                    - 7 pass TD - 4 INT                             - 3 INT - 64.9 comp%               - 64.8 comp% - 71 rush yards… pic.twitter.com/vhQoVvPj5O
However, one fact stands out.
Deshaun Watson isn't getting any younger. At 31 years old with a deep injury history, there definitely is a risk when offering a new deal.
Additionally, with Shedeur Sanders patiently waiting his turn, does another contract drive him out of town? Let's look at the options if Watson is done after this season.
In a given situation where the Browns decide to move on, Shedeur Sanders is slated to be the next guy in line for Cleveland.
When was the last time the Browns had the chance to develop a quarterback behind one that was consistantly winning games?
Unless Sanders gets impatient and wants to find an opportunity elsewhere, he will have plenty of experience seeing the system executed when he gets his chance to step in
Before the 2026 season began, many fans thought the Browns would be looking forward to the 2027 NFL Draft with a top pick by this part of the season.
Still, Cleveland has the option to draft a quarterback, develop him behind Watson for a year, and trade Sanders.
This option may actually make the most sense for the Browns. Not only does it allow them to go after a first round talent, but they can also bring back Watson for another year or two to develop their draft pick and trade Sanders.
Who knows, maybe there is another team that has been eyeing Sanders from a distance and will give up a decent package for the young quarterback.

title: Where Browns Got it Right, Where Browns Got it Wrong vs. Titans
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns went into Nashville and rocked the Tennessee Titans to improve to 5-2 and maintained first place in the AFC North. The Browns once again relied upon a game-winning field goal against the lowly Titans, but the numbers tell a different story. The offense got plenty right in the road win, but there were also some aspects of the game that they got wrong.
Deshaun Watson had his first 300-yard game in his career with the Browns. Receivers were open and the ball was placed in a position to allow them to run after the catch. KC Concepcion shined in that role, amassing 129 receiving yards by juking, spinning, and breaking tackles. Watson got Harold Fannin Jr. involved and he made an incredible play to put them into field goal range at the end of the game. He had 91 receiving yards and he has to be a contributor on offense for the unit to play up to its potential.
The Browns welcomed the return of Dylan Sampson and utilized his speed on screen passes to gain crucial first downs. Watson threw an interception early in the game, but otherwise he protected the football and was only sacked one time.
The defense got eaten alive last season against the Titans’ running game, resulting in a loss. The defensive line has a new play style this season with more depth, but they again lacked to control the line of scrimmage. Tony Pollard averaged over five yards per rush on his way to 129 rushing yards. He started the game with a 36-yard rushing touchdown for an early lead.
The Browns have been feast or famine in stopping the run this season as they also had a lot of tackles for loss. When they were not hitting Pollard in the backfield, there were holes big enough for him to get to the secondary. The rushing defense’s potential was on full display during a goal line stand by getting a turnover on downs at the one yard line.
Grant Delpit and Emmanuel McNeil-Warren have been fantastic at playing near the line of scrimmage and helping the defensive line get pressure. But when they are not there, the holes have to be covered up.
The offense finally got their top-two running backs in the huddle for the first time this season and the attack looked greatly improved. Quinshon Judkins averaged 5.6 yards per rush on his way to a season best 96 yards. Sampson also had six carriers for over 7 yards per rush. The offense converted five-third downs in part to solid rushes on first and second downs.
Todd Monken even used Concepcion to rush the football , and he had a long run, setting up the offense. The successful rushing attack opened up the pass game as the Titans could not blitz Watson as often.
The Browns dominated in every statistic, except they lost the penalty battle. They had eight penalties for 48 yards. The yards were not much, but the timing was critical. The defense forced the Titans to punt late in the game on a critical drive, and they were relying on their place kicker to boot the ball. The special teams unit came out with 12 men on the field and a penalty was called, resulting in a first down for the Titans.
At both the end of the first and second halves, the offense found a way to score. At the end of the first half, the Browns marched down and Monken kept calling plays with time dwindling. He got the ball out quick and to the sidelines, and the Browns kicked an easy field goal to close out the half.
The offense got the ball back with around a minute left in the game and they got chunk plays to cruise down the field. They used the clock masterfully and the offense methodically got a chip-shot field goal to win the game. All five of their wins have come in game-winning fashion .
Graduated from Bowling Green State University with a Journalism degree. Written and contributed to numerous media outlets. Cleveland sports victim.

title: Biggest Takeaways From Browns Victory Over Titans
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns took down the Tennessee Titans 27-24 in their Week 7 matchup.
While the Brown and Orange walked away with the win, there are some major positives and negatives that we saw in the game.
Let's break down some of the biggest factors we saw out there on the field.
Maybe Tony Pollard has a grudge against the Browns' defense and pulls out his best performances when facing them. Regardless, the defense did a terrible job stopping the league's worst offense.
Coming into the game, the Titans ranked dead last In offensive yards per game, with 263.3. Against the Browns, they put up 322.
Time after time, Pollard would break down the Browns' run defense, which led to Cam Ward dicing up the secondary with quick passes and slant routes.
While there were some great plays made at times, it was very unsettling to see the Browns continually struggle against one of the statistically worst offenses in the entire NFL.
DESHAUN WATSON GO AHEAD TUDDY pic.twitter.com/KuhyT1ebzs
You could really argue that Deshaun Watson had two game-winning drives in this matchup.
He started by leading the Browns down the field and finding the end zone with his legs to take a late lead. After the defense gave up a touchdown, he once again marched Cleveland down the field and into field goal range with no time remaining.
At some point, it feels like the juice has to run out with these game-winning drives.
However, it is great to see the Browns finally getting the quarterback they traded for four years ago. As long as he can keep up the production, the Browns will keep winning games.
One of the statistics the Browns actually took advantage of was the fact that Tennessee allows the 21st most rushing yards per game in the NFL.
For the first time this season, Quinshon Judkins was able to produce for the Browns as he did in his rookie season.
On the game, Judkins finished with 96 rushing yards on 17 carries (5.6 yards per carry) while finding the endzone twice.
By far, the Browns run game looked the best it did all season. As a whole, Cleveland had 183 rushing yards on offense.
Week after week, the Browns can't seem to stay out of their own way.
Averaging nine penalties per game on the season coming into the game, Cleveland got flagged one shy of their mark to be at with a total of eight flags.
Still, multiple drives were halted and ruined thanks to simple mistakes.
One example to think about is Zion Johnson getting two holding penalties in the span of three plays. That surely has to be some sort of record somewhere.
No matter how ugly, a win is still a win.
While it would've been much nicer to see the Browns play better against a team they probably should've blown out, they still got the job done .
A lot of credit in this game has to go to Todd Monken. No matter what happened, good or bad, he kept his guys focused on the game and managed to come away victorious.
Cleveland truly has found their guy with Monken, and he continues to prove it week after week.
Louis Timura is a student sports broadcaster and content creator. He currently attends Ashland University while pursuing a degree in Digital Media Production.

title: Why Not Another? Browns Kicker Andre Szmyt Comes Up Clutch in Win Over Titans
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns just keep getting the job done.
On Sunday, Oct. 25, the Browns improved to 5-2 on the 2026 campaign, beating the Tennessee Titans on the road from Nissan Stadium 27-24, with a game-winning field goal from kicker Andre Szmyt being the difference maker.
Sunday marked the fifth time this season the Browns have won on a game-winning drive led by quarterback Deshaun Watson, and the third time that Szmyt has been the hero.
This is also Andre Szmyt’s fifth career game-tying or go-ahead FG in the final two minutes, passing Dustin Hopkins (4) for second most by a Browns kicker this century (behind Phil Dawson, 10) [via ESPN Research] https://t.co/nFm1w83K0j
"We got to give the fans something to watch and enjoy. It boosts the NFL ratings, so I know they loving that," Browns Pro Bowl defensive back Denzel Ward said at the conclusion of the game.
Ward also played a major part in the victory, snagging his second interception of the season and 20th in his illustrious career. He also finished with two tackles.
While Ward obviously put it a great way, there were others who echoed his sentiment and shed more light onto the Browns' fifth win of the campaign. Here are three must-hear quotes following the victory:
Of course, wins are going to be wins.
But even though the Browns didn't look the prettiest on Sunday, Monken reiterated that these games haven't looked the same. Whether it's a win or a loss, the Browns are making improvements across the board in different areas.
It would be nice to see the Browns play a clean, near-perfect game, but sometimes you take what you can get.
"That was a fun one," Monken said postgame. "Never looks the same but feels the same."
Browns coach Todd Monken: “That was a fun one. Never looks the same but feels the same.” pic.twitter.com/foodG7IzNx
Monken wasn't going to let KC Concepcion's incredible game go unnoticed.
The rookie finished with eight receptions on 10 targets, going for 129 yards. He averaged 16.1 yards per reception, consistently getting involved in the Browns' offense from the start.
He also tacked on three carries for 23 yards on the ground.
Postgame, Monken complimented Concepcion.
“Real dude, man. He's a real dude," he said. "Coming out of the draft, everyone said that about him. When you visit him and you're around him, like, he's diligent, he's humble, competitive, got unbelievable fight."
Todd Monken on KC Concepcion (career-high 152 scrimmage yards): “He’s a real dude.”
The thoughts from Monken were echoed by Concepcion himself, as he would go on to share that he believed Sunday would be his breakout game.
"I enter every week expecting to have a game like this," he said. "This week it was my breakout game, so I just can't wait to keep stacking weeks."
On the campaign, he now has 30 receptions for 315 yards. He has yet to find the endzone, but if Sunday can be repeated at all down the line, that certainly will change.
Watson finished Sunday's game with a whopping 308 yards through the air on 36 attempts , completing 25 of them in the process. He averaged 8.6 yards per reception, while also throwing one interception.
Besides his lone blemish that came in the first, he had a great game.
However, while the Browns are up to five wins , he doesn't think the team is done just yet.
"We haven't even reached our peak," Watson said postgame.
Browns QB Deshaun Watson: “We haven’t even reached our peak.”
The Browns will look to remain atop the AFC North this coming weekend when they face the Pittsburgh Steelers for the second time this season.
The two sides will collide on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 1:00 p.m. EST from Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh.

title: Browns Get Lucky Break As Two Major Defensive Contributors Cleared For Titans Game
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns should be entering Sunday's showdown against the Tennessee Titans with all the momentum in the world.
Following a strong 4-2 start to the 2026 NFL regular season, the Browns have now gained an extra edge as two major defensive contributors were cleared to play.
On Sunday, Oct. 25, just hours before the Browns were set to take on the Titans from Nissan Stadium, the team released the inactive report, with both cornerback Denzel Ward and linebacker Quincy Williams not listed. The two had been dealing with injuries throughout the week and were questionable.
Denzel Ward is ACTIVE (right hand) for #Browns v #Titans Inactives: QB Taylen Green (3QB) LB Justin Jefferson CB Noah Igbinoghene RB Audric Estime DT Mike Hall Jr. C Parker Brailsford
The only inactives are quarterback Taylen Green, linebacker Justin Jefferson, cornerback Noah Igbinoghene, running back Audric Estime , defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr. and center Parker Brailsford.
Each of these comes as no surprise and will likely not have too big of an effect on the outcome.
#Browns CB Denzel Ward (hand) is ACTIVE for today's game against the Titans.
All week long, there was speculation surrounding Estime's involvement on the gridiron on Sunday. He was dealing with a hand injury, specifically something with his finger.
Head coach Todd Monken did expect him to play, though.
"Knowing Denzel, we expect him to play , but we'll see," Monken said during the week.
Ward has been the Browns' most reliable defensive contributor since he arrived way back in 2018.
This season, he has contributed 25 total tackles, three pass deflections, two forced fumbles, one quarterback hit and one interception. While he hasn't had many flashy moments yet, he has stayed healthy and remained a consistent presence on the field.
If he keeps up his current pace, he will set a career-best in total tackles.
Against Cam Ward and a relatively pass-heavy offense, Ward will have a chance to continue his recent streak of good play.
Like Ward, Williams has been en fuego as of late.
Playing in all six games to begin the campaign, Williams has 40 combined tackles with three for a loss. He has also contributed three quarterback hits and one sack, all while routinely putting physical shots on the opposition. He has a team and league best of three forced fumbles.
He has also tacked on two pass deflections.
Whether it is the rushing or passing attack, Williams has found a way to impact both areas of an opposing offense.
Fortunately, all week long, Williams was singing the song that he was going to be playing this weekend. Following the Browns' close-knit win over the Ravens last weekend, he had been dealing with neck soreness.
"Just a little soreness," Williams said on Thursday. "Missed yesterday just for precautionary stuff, get some tests done and everything and I was back out there today moving full speed. Moving, it feels good. Just did a little check right there...good for Sunday."
Having nearly every go-to option back from injury on both sides of the ball gives the Browns the perfect opportunity to improve to 5-2 on the campaign and stay atop the AFC North standings.
The Browns and Titans kick things off at 1:00 p.m. EST.

title: Browns Put Themselves in Unique Position Ahead of Sunday Outing Against Titans
full_text:
It's time to see what the Cleveland Browns can do at pretty much full strength.
Following a slow start to the season in the injury department, Weeks 3 through 6 gave the Browns a lot to be concerned about. Key contributors on both sides of the ball were banged up and held off the gridiron.
But ahead of the Browns' Week 7 matchup with the Tennessee Titans, countless players were deemed healthy enough to suit up.
Of the bunch, the running back room's Dylan Sampson and Quinshon Judkins stand out, as neither has been healthy at the same time this season outside of the first quarter of Week 1. With both back and ready to go , the Browns have a chance to finally get the rushing attack going.
Their returns certainly make things interesting, though, as along the way, backups Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime have held down the fort pretty well.
So, on Sunday, Oct. 25, how will the Browns coaching staff use Sampson, Judkins, McLaughlin and Estime?
According to the official depth chart , Judkins is RB1, with Sampson, McLaughlin and Estime following in that order.
Through the first five games of the 2026 campaign, the second-year back has only posted 221 yards and one score on 73 carries. He is currently averaging a measly 3.0 yards per carry.
Coming off an injury last season, it was expected that he might not have as quick of a bounce, especially out of the gates, but Cleveland's play calling has him running right up the gut quite often. Not only is he not a workhorse, physical back in that capacity, but he also isn't getting the right holes created by the offensive line.
On Sunday, it would be nice to see the Browns limit his snap count, just to keep him healthy, but also give him more time to breathe if that is the way they plan to continue using him.
On Sampson's end, he is the speedster of the running back room.
As they did in 2025, he should continue being the team's go-to receiving back. Last year, he hauled in over 30 receptions for just north of 250 receiving yards and two touchdowns. With the Browns' offense finally becoming a bit more dynamic, he should get some usage by Watson outside in the flats.
Sampson is a player you just have to let get loose.
Just Hours Before Sunday's Game, Estime Was Ruled Inactive
Now, here is where things get interesting for the Browns.
A team very rarely brings two players back from injury and thrusts them immediately into the heavy workload they previously had, especially at the running back positions where hits are taken left, right and center, meaning both McLaughlin and Estime should see time in the backfield Sunday.
Of the two, McLaughlin seems the most fit to see meaningful time on the field, having already made a pretty nice impact in limited opportunities.
He has 11 carries for 72 yards and one touchdown on the ground, while also grabbing four receptions for 14 yards.
Like Sampson, he has tremendous speed, and if he gets loose, he can take even the simplest of looks for six.
Now, if any of Sampson, Judkins or McLaughlin come up short and a goalline punch is needed, that is where Estime could see time on the field.
In his Browns debut last week, he found the end zone on a two-yard carry.
While he may not seem like a realistic option for many reps, he still certainly does have a role in Cleveland's offense. The only question will be what it looks like now with Sampson and Judkins back from injury.
The Browns and Titans will go toe-to-toe on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1:00 p.m. EST from Nissan Stadium in Nashville. The Browns will look to improve to 5-2 on the young 2026 campaign.

title: Browns Sign Standout DT Maliek Collins To Two-Year Extension Amid Strong Season
full_text:
Veteran defensive tackle Maliek Collins has signed a two-year, $30 million extension with the Cleveland Browns ahead of their Week 7 matchup with the Tennessee Titans .
The deal includes $23 million guaranteed, according to NFL Network insider Ian Rapaport.
Collins, 31, has seemed to have found a home in Cleveland after bouncing around the NFL. Collins was selected by the Dallas Cowboys in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft out of Nebraska. After four seasons in Dallas, he spent one season with the Las Vegas Raiders.
He then went on to play three seasons with the Houston Texans and one with the San Francisco 49ers before signing with Cleveland.
The #Browns and standout DT Maliek Collins have agreed to terms on a 2-year extension for $30M with $23M in total guarantees,  agent Drew Rosenhaus tells me and @AdamSchefter . pic.twitter.com/rIJIcfP2DF
Collins has been a key piece for this Browns defense since signing with the team in 2025. Collins posted a career year in his first season with the Browns before going down with a tricep injury in week 13 that kept him out for the remainder of the season. In 12 full games, Collins posted 25 tackles, 6.5 sacks, and 1 fumble recovery.
Now fully recovered, Collins looks to replicate that impact in 2026.
The Browns' defense has been the catalyst for their unprecedented 4-2 start, and Maliek Collins has played a major role in it. After giving up 34 points in week one against the Jacksonville Jaguars, Mike Rutenberg's unit has allowed just 17.6 points per game.
The unit ranks 4th in the NFL with 65 total pressures and 6th in pressure rate at 40.4%. In addition, the unit has not allowed a 300-yard passer in 50 consecutive regular-season contests.
The Browns' defensive line unit raised many question marks coming into the season following the departure of Myles Garrett. Garrett was traded in the offseason to the Los Angeles Rams after nine seasons in Cleveland.
Through four games, the unit has answered the call by being one of the best units in football. A key reason for this is Maliek Collins' ability to make those around him better. Second-year defensive tackle Mason Graham was finding his stride in his rookie season before Collins's went down with his injury.
Although the sample size was small, Graham's play was noticeably worse following the injury to Collins. Since then, Graham has come into this season playing like one of the best defensive tackles in football.
The impact Maliek Collins brings cannot be overstated. After standing out in the first six weeks of the season, the Browns are rightfully rewarding the veteran, keeping him in Cleveland for the years to come.
Cody Croy joined the BIGPLAY Sports Network in June 2026 to cover the Ohio State Buckeyes and Cleveland Browns On SI.

title: Biggest Takeaways From Cowboys' Week 7 Win Over Injury-Ravaged Eagles
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys finally broke through with a win on Monday night, beating the Philadelphia Eagles, 38-21.
This was the perfect opponent for the Cowboys, as the Eagles were absolutely ravaged by injuries coming into this game and simply didn't have the horses to run with Dallas for a full four quarters.
Even still, the Eagles hung tough and ran nearly even with Dallas for three quarters before the Cowboys managed to pull away in the fourth.
Now, a look at the biggest takeaways from the Cowboys' Week 7 win over the Eagles.
The Cowboys scored 38 points on Monday night, which was nine more than they scored in the previous two games combined. It was a much-needed showing after Dallas struggled recently .
Dak Prescott had some bad throws, so it wasn't all good through the air, but he threw three dimes on his trio of touchdown passes. Dallas' offensive line also had solid protection upfront to give him time to get rid of the football.
George Pickens, CeeDee Lamb and Ryan Flournoy all finished north of 50 yards, and Lamb scored twice and Pickens had a touchdown, also.
Javonte Williams had the biggest bounce-back game, as he ran hard and showed great patience and vision behind an offensive line that had one of its best run-blocking showings of the year.
Williams finished with a career-high 155 yards on 25 carries and scored. He averaged 6.2 yards per carry after coming into the contest averaging just 3.4 yards per tote.
We would normally be thrilled with the Cowboys giving up just 21 points after how bad this defense has played in 2026, but context is important here. Dallas' unit was bad in the first and third quarters, but was good in the second and fourth.
The Cowboys are extremely fortunate the Eagles' offense is as banged-up as it is because this game could have ended much differently.
If Saquon Barkley was healthy, he might have run for 150 because he was picking up solid gains at will when he was able to stay on the field, which wasn't often. Barkley ended up exiting the game early for good.
Dallas' pass defense wasn't great, either.
A signal-caller more competent than Tanner McKee with better weapons than the likes of Hollywood Brown, Darius Cooper and rookie Makai Lemon would have picked Dallas' secondary apart like we have seen quarterbacks do all season.
Head coach Brian Schottenheimer's decision not to call a timeout after a 14-yard catch by CeeDee Lamb late in the second quarter proved to be a bad one. Dallas ended up kicking a field goal to finish off the half, and they did so on third down and with one timeout in their pocket.
Then, before Aubrey's second field goal in the fourth quarter, Dallas had a third-and-8 at Philly's nine-yard line and Schotty decided to call for a handoff to fullback Hunter Luepke, for whatever reason.
That was his second give-up play of the game. The first white-flag play came on the second-to-last drive of the first half, when the Cowboys were deep in their own territory and didn't even attempt to throw a pass on third down and instead surrendered by handing it off to Williams. Luckily, the Cowboys' defense made a stop on the following series.
Christian Parker will make his weekly appearance here, also. The Cowboys defensive coordinator just will not adjust and blitz more, which is especially egregious when he's facing a backup quarterback he should be challenging.
Nothing about this game gave us more confidence in Schottenheimer and Parker.
The Cowboys had a whopping seven first half penalties and shot themselves in the foot on both sides of the ball.
Dallas did clean things up in the second half, but they're going to pay the price against better teams if they have more halves like the one on Monday night.

title: Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb Show Brotherly Love To Joe Milton After Cowboys ' Win
full_text:
It wasn't all bad blood at Lincoln Financial Field for Monday night's NFC East showdown between the Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles . Sure, there were plenty of boos, but the game also brought some people back together.
During the broadcast, we got to see Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones cozying up with ESPN blowhard Stephen A. Smith . Then, after the game, we got to see another reunion that tugged more on the heartstrings of Cowboys Nation.
Cameras captured star quarterback Dak Prescott finding Joe Milton III , who the Eagles signed off the Cowboys' practice squad roster earlier this month, to chat it up after the game.
While they were sharing some special time together, star wide receiver CeeDee Lamb came crashing into the shot and jumped on Milton to give a giant hug.
brotherly love 💙 pic.twitter.com/6UUENBqJDz
While the Cowboys' offense may have had a couple of down weeks before getting back on track against the Eagles in Week 7, which led to some fair criticism directed at head coach Brian Schottenheimer, the post-game interaction showed just how strong the bonds being built in the locker room are.
Milton was beloved in the Cowboys locker room, and it was difficult to see him get poached from another team, especially a hated division rival. And for Milton, it must be tough sitting on the opposite sideline and watching your former team obliterate your new one, which is currently in shambles.
But at least Milton got to enjoy that special moment after the game. And, who knows, if Tanner McKee continues to struggle, we could see Milton get an opportunity to start some games down the final stretch of the season.
As for Prescott and Lamb, they did their parts on Monday night in getting the struggling offense back on track.
Prescott finished the game throwing for three touchdowns and no interceptions, while Lamb hauled in five catches for 84 yards and two scores. That's one way to break out of a slump, and hopefully, that positive momentum will continue as we prepare to turn the calendar over to November.
Up next for the Cowboys is a return home where they will welcome the Arizona Cardinals to AT&T Stadium at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX.

title: George Pickens Blows Kiss To Eagles Cheerleader in Hilarious Troll Move
full_text:
Leading up to Monday Night Football against the Philadelphia Eagles, Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens was at the center of plenty of criticism .
It appeared that Pickens was thrown under the bus by head coach Brian Schottenheimer for his lack of blocking in the run game, while Cowboys legend turned Monday Night Football color analyst Troy Aikman ripped an unnamed Dallas receiver for running sloppy routes.
Many believed Aikman was talking about Pickens, but on Monday night, Pickens put the noise behind him and did his part in the team's 38-21 victory over the Eagles on the road .
Pickens finished this week's game with four catches for 57 yards, one massive hurdle, and a touchdown. Oh, he added a little blown kiss to an Eagles cheerleader, as well.
While Coach Schottenheimer and the rest of the Cowboys offense would probably prefer that Pickens doesn't go leaving his feet and attempting to leap over defenders every week, the game is better when he is having fun.
There was no clearer sign of that than when Pickens hauled in a big first-down catch before blowing an Eagles cheerleader a little kiss.
pic.twitter.com/oGsR5xyl7l
And when Pickens is having fun, he has shown the ability to produce and find the endzone. There are some things that you have to give players a little freedom with, and when it comes to Pickens, letting him get loose is the key to him finding success. Sometimes, he just needs to reel it in.
Luckily, everything appeared to go smoothly in Week 7, and the Cowboys offense got back on track after two stagnant weeks. Then, in the fourth quarter, the Cowboys' defense pitched a rare shutout that catipulted the team to victory.
Hopefully, they will be able to keep that momentum rolling with a string of three consecutive primetime games behind us. Dallas will return to action in Week 8, back at home to kick off November against the struggling Arizona Cardinals, who have lost five of their last six outings.
Kickoff between the Cowboys and Cardinals is set for 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX with Tom McCarthy on play-by-play, Robert Turbin as analyst, and Tiffany Blackmon providing updates from the sidelines. Let's hope that the offense can continue to roll, and that the Cowboys can enter the new month on a winning streak.

title: 5 Winners & 2 Losers From Cowboys Much-Needed Week 7 Victory Over Eagles
full_text:
The term "must-win" is often overused, especially this early in the season. That wasn't the case for the Dallas Cowboys entering their Monday Night Football matchup with the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7.
Both teams were 2-4, but the Eagles were on a four-game losing streak and were without their starting quarterback, Jalen Hurts , and two starting receivers , while Saquon Barkley was limited as well with a hamstring injury. This is a game they had to win to keep within striking distance of the New York Giants in the NFC East, and a loss would have been devastating for a team facing relentless questions entering the game.
It wasn't pretty, and the defense still had far too many mistakes, but the Cowboys were able to walk out of Philly with a 38-21 win. Let's take a look back at this important victory and see who stood out as both winners and losers for America's Team.
Dallas said all week they needed to stick with the run, and they finally did. The results spoke for themselves as Javonte Williams ran for more than 100 yards for the first time this season. He not only topped the 100-yard mark, but also bested his previous career high of 135 yards . Williams finished with 155 yards and one touchdown on 25 attempts, helping the Cowboys set the tone.
Quinnen Williams was the Cowboys' big acquisition at the 2025 NFL trade deadline, and he was supposed to usher in a new era defensively. He was even signed to a three-year, $105.9 million extension this offseason, making him the face of the defense.
Through seven games, he's struggled to consistently live up to that billing. Against the Eagles, he had two miscues on the first two drives. On the opening drive, Williams was called for a neutral zone infraction. On the second drive, he had a far worse penalty.
Philadelphia fumbled the ball on fourth-and-one and Williams recovered the fumble. It didn't count, however, as Williams was penalized for being lined up offside. That gave the Eagles a fresh set of downs, and instead of Dallas getting the ball back, Philadelphia continued its drive and took a 14-10 lead.
George Pickens came under fire this week when Brian Schottenheimer called him out for his lack of effort as a blocker. During the first half, Pickens was giving more effort, even serving as the lead blocker on a six-yard screen pass to Ryan Flournoy. That said, he's an elite receiver for what he can do when the ball comes his way, which he reminded the world on the snap following the screen.
On third-and-three from the 21, Dak Prescott targeted Pickens in the back of the end zone, and he made a remarkable fingertip grab. Even more impressive than the catch was how he got both feet down with just inches to spare.
George Pickens. Snatched that. 🤯 What a throw from Dak! pic.twitter.com/AaOLxegVIW
Much like Quinnen Williams, Justin Barron had costly penalties back-to-back. First, he was called for holding on a kickoff following the Eagles' first touchdown, which forced them to start at their own 18. His second penalty, however, was an absolute killer.
Philadelphia had just scored after a 13-play, 76-yard drive to take the lead 14-10. Tyler Goodson responded with a 91-yard kickoff return for a touchdown, but it didn't count as Barron was flagged for another hold.
CeeDee Lamb is one of the best wideouts in the NFL and he once again had a stellar outing. He scored the Cowboys' first touchdown of the game, and made an made an excellent adjustment to bring that one in.
CEEDEE TEEDEE DALvsPHI on ESPN⁰Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/LxHUKFN2Ne
He had a second touchdown in the second half to give Dallas the lead back following a great drive from the Eagles, and that should have been his third of the game. Late in the first half, Lamb was wide open and should have been able to walk into the end zone, but the pass was slightly off target from Prescott. Lamb still somehow hauled it in for a 30-yard gain, which allowed Dallas to score a field goal right before the half.
Hard to get more wide open than CeeDee Lamb here DALvsPHI on ESPN⁰Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/dv18lWu4Hw
Lamb finished with 74 yards and two touchdowns on five receptions, giving the offense the spark they needed to get the job done.
The Dallas defense has been desperate for a game-changer, and DeMarvion Overshown might be what they've been missing. Overshown returned to action for the first time since Week 1 and was able to make multiple big plays. He batted down a pass on Tanner McKee in the first half and had a tackle for loss in the third quarter. His best play came in the fourth quarter, though, when Overshown stopped a promising drive from Philadelphia by picking off a pass from McKee. Dallas was up by 10, and this turnover allowed them to put the game away and improve to 3-4.
There was plenty of pressure on Dak Prescott going into this game after the Cowboys had back-to-back poor offensive showings. They scored just 16 in the loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and 13 in the loss to the Green Bay Packers. During those two games, Prescott had two touchdowns and four interceptions, which led many people to doubt him .
Prescott responded well in the NFC East showdown by completing 15-of-27 passes for 212 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions. There's still a lot to get right before we can believe in this team, but Prescott and the rest of the Cowboys did what they were supposed to do on Monday.

title: Troy Aikman Brought To Tears During David Moulton Tribute on Cowboys-Eagles Broadcast
full_text:
The NFC East took center stage on Monday Night Football to wrap up Week 7, with the Dallas Cowboys facing off against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field .
But while everyone was tuned in for some football, it was important for the ESPN broadcast to take a moment to honor a close friend and colleague, sports radio personality David Moulton , who worked on Monday Night Football for the past several years.
Moulton passed away over the weekend after a six-year battle with stage four renal cell cancer. He was just 59 years old.
Aikman and Joe Buck had a close relationship with Moulton, previously working with him on FOX NFL coverage on Thursdays and Sundays, so they took some time during the fourth quarter to remember their late colleague and friend. During the tribute, Aikman was brought to tears.
Troy Aikman was emotional as ESPN remembered David Moulton on the Cowboys-Eagles MNF broadcast. 📺🎙️❤️ https://t.co/V3pajPW08c pic.twitter.com/Ke7wL3orrD
It was a touching moment and showed just how much Moulton meant to the team. After news of Moulton's death, Aikman shared some words about the longtime spotter, who he called his"right -hand man," and his brave battle.
“Since 2018, David Moulton has been my right-hand man in the broadcast booth,” Aikman wrote on Instagram. “What started as a professional relationship became a friendship I have cherished. David was loyal, dependable and a warrior until the very end. He deserved better .
"My heart breaks for his family and all who loved him. I’m grateful for the years we shared and will miss him deeply. Rest in peace, big guy.”
Moulton's wife, Julie, confirmed his death in a heartbreaking statement on Saturday.
“It is with a completely shattered heart broken into a million pieces I share that my loving husband, David, died last night while in hospice care at the Douglas Center for Caring,” she wrote, according to the Fort Myers News-Press . “David battled stage four renal cell cancer for six long years. It metastasized to his bones two years ago. He never stopped fighting or trying new treatments. He loved life and loved each and every one of you more than words can express. We are so thankful for the love and support you all have given us.
“My sweet husband you are finally free of pain and with all our heavenly angels. Thank you for blessing us with the gift of you and for sharing your beautiful life with all of us. Cherish every second and he did. Love you.”
Our deepest condolences go out to Moulton's family and friends during this incredibly difficult time.

title: Jerry Jones Cozies Up With Notorious Cowboys Hater Stephen A Smith During Eagles Game
full_text:
It's only Week 7 , but the Dallas Cowboys are already in "must-win" territory . They're just 2-4 and have had one terrible defensive outing after another, which has their season on life support.
Their hope is that they can take advantage of an injured Philadelphia Eagles team on Monday Night Football . Just about everything is in their favor with Jalen Hurts and DeVonta Smith out , but the Cowboys are still struggling, much to the delight of their millions of haters.
None of those haters is more notorious or as loud as Stephen A. Smith, the ESPN personality who goes on live air and laughs hysterically at the Cowboys whenever they lose. Shockingly enough, Dallas owner Jerry Jones was seen cozying up with Stephen A. in his suite during the broadcast.
ESPN shows Stephen A. Smith in a suite with Jerry Jones again after Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb connect for a Cowboys TD. https://t.co/KZpDrdXds7 pic.twitter.com/rv2YKfqmsQ
Of course, Jones is allowed to hang out with whoever he wishes, but this feels rather insulting to the fan base. Jones claims he wants nothing more than to win a championship and is quick to say he believes this fan base deserves it. It's hard to believe Jones has much consideration for the fan base, however, when they see him buddying up with someone who so openly pokes fun at them.
When it comes to Smith, it's fair to say there are many fan bases who aren't fans of his. That could include the Eagles, after Smith made light of Lane Johnson's sudden retirement .
A former Dallas and Philadelphia wide receiver took notice of this and wasn't happy. Terrell Owens called for Smith to be suspended , saying his comments were reckless.
“I don’t understand how there are no consequences for Stephen A.’s actions, especially with ESPN and Disney being the corporations they are, for him to speak so insensitively about a topic like mental health the way he did,” Owens said on the Get to The Point Podcast . “Why isn’t he suspended? For him to speak so recklessly to a guy and then try to backtrack and say he’s had mental health issues. If you knew that, then you’re smart enough not to speak on something affecting millions of people, millions of people, and something that’s a very sensitive topic."
Smith has never been a stranger to controversy, and it's odd to see Jones, who is often on the receiving end of his ridiculous rants, allowing Smith to sit with him and his family.

title: Cowboys Legend Dez Bryant Threatens Teen, Slaps Phone Out Of Hand In New Parking Lot Video
full_text:
On Monday afternoon, it was revealed that Dallas Cowboys legend Dez Bryant was handcuffed and placed on the ground during a tense encounter with police after a traffic incident. During the encounter, a police officer briefly pointed their gun at Bryant while he was lying on his stomach.
Bryant said the incident began when aggressive drivers cut him off in traffic, and they ended up at the same restaurant in Southlake, Texas. Bryant was cited for assault by contact and was requested to make a court appearance in Southlake before November 20.
Since news of the incident went public, more information has been shared online with video showing Bryant threatening a teenager involved and slapping his phone out of his hand. Bryant told Avery "get your partner before I break him down.”
Bryant continued, “I’m fixing to f*ck these little motherf*ckers up. Like, real talk. I'll break you down. Don't give a f*ck about none of that... You think I give a f*ck about the law? No, not at all. Because we're going to get them cameras and see who looks like an idiot.
Dez Bryant slaps phone out of teen's hand in video of parking lot altercation: 'I'm not playing with you' https://t.co/bsx0mjNrRu pic.twitter.com/hY9tBp4hYc
The New York Post has video of the altercation between Bryant and the teenagers .
While Bryant says he was acting in self-defense and called for fairness and a full investigation, Reyes says he suffered a hand injury and will be suing Bryant. The Southlake Police Department also shared a detailed statement on the entire incident with the Post.
“Several callers reported that multiple individuals were involved in the altercation as well as a possible weapon,” the statement read. “Based on that information, officers drew their firearms upon arrival as a precaution to address any potential threats and ensure the safety of everyone at the scene. Several individuals were temporarily detained as part of the investigation. No firearms were recovered at the scene.
“The altercation reportedly began as a traffic incident near Kimball Avenue, where one of the involved individuals, identified as 37-year-old Desmond Bryant, reported he was cut off by another motorist. Both parties subsequently entered the parking lot, where an argument ensued and the alleged assault occurred.
Bryant's assault charge is a Class C misdemeanor. Bryant also issued a lengthy statement on the incident, saying he is the true victim and doubling down on his story that the others involved in the incident threatened to shoot him.
"The guy who had threatened to shoot me pulled up beside me, said he was going to shoot me, then hit the gas, parked, and jumped out of the car talking sh*t," Bryant wrote on X. "I started talking sh*t back. He said, 'I got something for you,' and went back to his car as if he were about to get a gun. I told him, 'If you pull that gun, you better use it, because otherwise I’m about to beat your ass .'
"He went from threatening to shoot me to recording me on his phone. I slapped the phone out of his hand, and he called the police right after that. Honestly, I’m waiting to hear the recording where someone supposedly called and said there was a gun involved. As soon as the officers arrived, the young adult and I were talking trash back and forth. I don’t understand why the officer got out of the car and pointed a rifle directly at me.

title: Cowboys Make Surprising Change to Green Dot Responsibilities vs Eagles
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are looking to turn their season around following a 2-4 start, and that begins with Monday night's matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field.
Despite the team's poor performance through the first six weeks of the season, the Cowboys still have a shot at hosting a playoff game due to how poor the NFC East is this season . A postseason berth is well within reach, but Dallas will need to figure out some way to improve the defense before worrying about a potential playoff spot.
The Cowboys are returning some key defensive players against the Eagles after multi-week absences, including linebacker DeMarvion Overshown and cornerback Cobie Durant. Both have been out after suffering hamstring injuries early in the season.
Overshown wore the green dot on defense in Week 1's loss to the New York Giants before exiting with injury. The coach-to-player communications have looked different since then. It was expected he would reclaim that role ahead of Monday night against Philadelphia, but the Cowboys coaching staff has elected to go in a surprising direction instead.
Per reports from team sideline reporter Kristi Scales, Overshown will not wear the green dot against Philadelphia. That responsibility is now being given to Cowboys linebacker Shemar James.
Cowboys rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham was also a potential candidate to wear the green dot but it's clear Dallas' defensive staff wanted to make a change. The Cowboys are without starting linebacker Dee Winters against the Eagles due to an Achilles strain he suffered in last week's loss to the Green Bay Packers.
A fifth-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft by the Cowboys, James has appeared in 20 career games (six starts) while posting 104 total tackles (49 solo), 1.5 sacks and one forced fumble. He had 91 total tackles as a rookie last year and has appeared in all six games this season.
Though James, who played 544 defensive snaps as a rookie, has the experience of last year to lean on, it's still a bit surprising the Cowboys didn't give the green dot to Overshown or Barham.
After Winters suffered the Achilles injury last week, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer made it clear he's been impressed with how some of the other linebackers have stepped up.
This included both James and Justin Barron, who he spoke highly of.
"We're getting a lot of guys reps. Shemar James, like I said, is doing a really good job," Schottenheimer said. "Justin Barron last night did a really good job. We put him in on a couple passing situations. They actually tried him on a little wheel route immediately when he came in the game and he played it beautifully. That's a position that normally gets dinged up and beat up a little bit, and both those guys Shemar and Justin have played really well for us."
Cowboys fans will have to wait and see if James can live up to this praise against the Eagles.

title: Broncos HC Sean Payton Gets 'Quite Honest' About Using Marvin Mims Jr.
full_text:
Among the footnotes included in the Denver Broncos' 30-16 victory over the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday was the deployment of Marvin Mims, who returned to his prior role as the team's primary returnman.
Whereas the team had two players back deep in recent weeks, Mims was flying solo against the Cardinals , returning two punts for eight yards and four kicks for 103 yards, including a 39-yard scamper, at State Farm Stadium.
Perhaps more importantly, Mims saw an uptick in usage on the offensive side, catching two passes for 53 yards — highlighted by a 47-yard catch-and-run — across 16 snaps, running as the No. 3 WR behind Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton.
This was perhaps by design, as Broncos head coach Sean Payton reiterated his long-standing desire to craft additional opportunities to get the ball in Mims' hands.
“We’re trying to get him touches. He’s one of our explosive playmakers," Payton told reporters via conference call on Monday. "Quite honestly, we need to get him more touches on offense, and we’ll do that. A lot of it had to do with the way they were kicking off. We kind of, you noticed, went more to a single returner and certainly that first one (return) that puts us at midfield was a big one for us.”
It was an overall banner day for both units; Denver's offense hung three touchdowns on Arizona's hapless defense, one of which was preceded by a blocked punt. Kicker Wil Lutz also made all of his extra points and went three-for-three on field goal attempts.
“I think the quickest way to improve your team is in the kicking game and then in your defensive and offensive fronts," Payton said. "If you talk about taking care of the football and playing well on special teams, you’re going to give yourself a chance. I think [Special Teams Coordinator/Assistant Head Coach] Darren [Rizzi] and his group have done a real good job.”
The stakes become ratcheted much higher for the Broncos on Sunday, when they'll welcome the rival Kansas City Chiefs to Empower Field at Mile High for a battle of 5-2 versus 5-1. Winner takes sole control of the AFC West around the midway point of the 2026 campaign.
With WR Pat Bryant (ankle) expected to miss another game, and considering Patrick Mahomes is on the other sideline, Denver may look to lean on its passing attack — and Mims is likely to see a handful of targets.
Payton should make good on his vow and find ways to get Mims more involved. He's proven to be a reliable deep threat with reliable hands and a knack for the clutch. The All-Pro special-teamer could even be the deep threat if Waddle (chest) is forced to miss Week 8.
“I’ve said this a hundred times, but divisional games are always important and they typically kind of move," Payton said Monday of the upcoming tilt. "I don’t see rivalry weeks in the NFL. They’re generally divisional games where you have an important game against a division opponent. So I don’t see the Auburn-Alabama. I don’t see the Ohio State-Michigan. That’s just from being in this league long enough and doing it long enough.”
