title: Sean Payton Offers 'Explosive' Take on Jonah Coleman's Growing Role
full_text:
If you watched the Denver Broncos' 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals, you could feel a big shift .
Bo Nix looked like his old self , shaking off the rust from the broken ankle he suffered back in January and regaining his confidence. He made history with his 62-yard touchdown run and 52-yard touchdown pass to RJ Harvey.
The Broncos' offense still showed a few warts of inconsistency, but overall, it was a big step forward, and exactly the type of get-right game Nix and company needed. One of the reasons it felt so different offensively was the presence of rookie running back Jonah Coleman.
After spending four weeks on injured reserve, the Broncos activated Coleman for this game , but we weren't sure how the rookie would fit into the offensive flow of things. It's rare to see a player — let alone a rookie — go from the training table on IR to leading the team in offensive touches, but that's what happened.
Coleman led the team with nine carries for 53 yards and caught two passes for 15 yards. He also showcased his proficiency as a pass protector , further earning the trust of Nix and his coaches.
After a night to sleep on it and watch the film, Broncos head coach Sean Payton shared his thoughts on Coleman's performance in the desert amid Mile High speculation over who this team's No. 1 running back is.
“He played well. The touches he had were explosive," Payton said of Coleman on Monday morning.
Payton doesn't go out of his way to compliment rookies, but he gave Coleman some love. That says a lot.
It could be a sign of things to come, as Payton said that Coleman's 11 touches in Week 7 came the hard way; the rookie earned the role he was given on Sunday, and he absolutely capitalized on the opportunity.
"Like anything else, I think it’s something you earn," Payton said of Coleman. "He’s done a good job of that."
Coleman has only been active for three games this season. He's touched the ball in two of those games, and his impact has been palpable.
The Broncos' run game was much more productive with the rookie in the backfield. Coleman's burst and vision set him apart from Dobbins and Harvey. Unlike his Week 2 performance against the Jacksonville Jaguars , Coleman showed down-to-down consistency against Arizona.
As a veteran, Dobbins has good vision, but he's lacked burst this season. Harvey has burst in spades, but he lacks vision. The two backs only combined for nine carries against the Cardinals, matching Coleman's total number of totes.
On one third-quarter scoring drive, Coleman kept moving the chains with three runs for 18 yards. Once the Broncos made it to the goal line, Dobbins was inserted into the lineup, and he was able to punch it in from one yard out.
Fantasy football people would say that Dobbins "vultured" a touchdown that should have gone to Coleman, given how the rookie carried that drive as a between-the-tackles runner. But Payton has to play the political game, and he very much appreciates Dobbins.
So even though Coleman's touch and snap share outpaced Dobbins, Payton made sure to give his veteran back the opportunity to score a touchdown for the third straight game. To his credit, Dobbins didn't let his coach down, but the back's energy seemed a bit off.
For example, after his third-quarter touchdown at State Farm Stadium, Dobbins didn't celebrate with teammates in the end zone, but instead trotted off to the sideline and immediately sat down on the bench. That vibe will be something to monitor moving forward, especially given the rumors coming out of the Broncos' locker room post-game that Dobbins didn't make himself available to the media.
In the Broncos' season-opening loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, Coleman dressed but didn't touch the ball. Dobbins actually had his most proficient day as a runner against the Chiefs, averaging 4.5 yards on eight carries.
I would expect to see a heavy dose of both Coleman and Dobbins this Sunday in the Broncos' rematch with the Chiefs. After Kansas City lost to the Seattle Seahawks in Week 7, this next game at Mile High will determine which team leads the AFC West.
Given the burst and playmaking ability Coleman has shown this season, it wouldn't be a surprise to see him once again out-earn Dobbins in touches and snaps. The rookie is a complete back, which means he doesn't have to come off the field on third down, though that's often when Payton will look to get Harvey involved in the offense.
Entering Week 7, the rumor mill was rife with nuggets connecting the Broncos to various running backs ahead of the November 10 trade deadline, including Jonathan Taylor . With two games left until the deadline, Coleman's emergence may have cooled Denver's jets on the possibility of trading for a running back.

title: Film Room: Bo Nix's Cardinals Performance Changes the Conversation
full_text:
The Denver Broncos offense finally came alive, blasting the Arizona Cardinals 30-16 on Sunday afternoon at State Farm Stadium. This was the perfect “get-right” game for the Broncos, as Arizona’s defense ranks among the worst in the league at allowing explosive plays.
Despite some inconsistencies throughout the game, this was by far Bo Nix’s best performance since the AFC divisional round playoff game against the Buffalo Bills last season. He unlocked the passing offense early, finally found his legs as a runner, and took advantage of his opportunities to make plays within the structure of the offense.
Nix finished the game 15-of-29 for 222 yards and a touchdown, and added another 73 yards on seven carries with a 62-yard touchdown run .  That touchdown run was massive because it allowed the offense to relax and exhale, jolting some confidence into a maligned unit that has struggled to get anything going all year.
We’re taking a long look at the explosive plays in this week’s film room.
This might be the best throw Bo has made all year. He hasn't shown the confidence to rip the Dig over the head of the LB at all. This was a great way to start the game. pic.twitter.com/aMOn5DXEOu
Sean Payton’s offense features a lot of dig routes, and Nix hasn’t connected on them nearly as often as he should. It’s a staple of the passing game, and the Broncos have several receivers who succeed when running them.
Denver opened the game in an empty shotgun set, and the Cardinals run a quarters coverage shell. Notice how deep the safeties get in their drops, opening a huge window over the middle of the field for Courtland Sutton on the in-breaker.
This might be Nix’s best throw of the year. Watch as he uses a subtle pump fake to freeze linebacker Jack Gibbens, then rips a throw right over his head. I hope this throw gets plastered all over the locker room to prove to Nix that he doesn’t need to be hesitant to “let it rip” over the middle of the field.
The longest rushing touchdown by a QB in Denver Broncos history. Nobody had their eyes on Nix. Kudos to Adam Trautman for manipulating his defender downfield. pic.twitter.com/xqxe6vRBXD
Welcome back, Bo Nix! This 62-yard touchdown run was the longest rushing touchdown by a quarterback in Broncos history, the longest rush by a quarterback since Justin Fields ripped a 67-yard touchdown run in 2022, and the longest rushing touchdown of any player in the league this year.
This is a great process from Nix, as he navigated a muddy pocket and slashed through the Cardinals' defense at a top speed of 19.9 miles per hour. Arizona was in man coverage across the board, and nobody had their eyes on Nix when he escaped the pocket.
The Broncos run a sail concept to the right side of the field, drawing nearly every defender to that side and opening up a ton of grass for Nix to exploit.
Watch tight end Adam Trautman carefully. He does a fantastic job of manipulating his defender while Nix is taking off. He even flashes his hands to show a target, even though Nix is already several yards downfield. There wasn’t a defender within four yards of Nix until he got inside the 5-yard line.
This one felt good. It breathed life into the offense as a whole, but it also breathed confidence into Nix.
This is a perfect play call into the blitz. The OL has nobody to block downfield. Troy Franklin with a huge block, as well. pic.twitter.com/8lXpp0sb97
On the Broncos’ first possession of the second half, they executed a beautiful screen pass to running back RJ Harvey for a 52-yard touchdown. This play was historic for Nix, as he became the fifth quarterback in NFL history to record a 50-yard rushing touchdown and a 50-yard passing touchdown in the same game.
This is a beautiful play call by Payton. The Cardinals sent Mack Wilson and Kalen King on a blitz, and the Broncos' offensive line executed perfectly. Left guard Ben Powers is the only player with anybody to block for the first few yards, and Harvey was instantly off to the races.
Explosive run and screen plays can only happen if receivers are doing their job as blockers down the field. Watch Troy Franklin work over Garrett Williams and allow Harvey room to the inside. That’s textbook execution.
Shout-out to Erick Trickel, who called a 50-yard Harvey touchdown on a screen play in his bold predictions this week . Erick pulled some great numbers on the Cardinals' defense against screen plays for Dove Valley Deep-Divers Podcast , and nailed this prediction square on the head.
Cover 2 Hole shot. Burke bites on the out route and Bo puts a good ball on Mims before the safety can rotate over. pic.twitter.com/b8rSkQbJ3J
On the following offensive drive, Nix beats the Cardinals with a hole shot in Cover 2. Good things happen when Marvin Mims Jr. gets involved in the passing game, and Nix makes cornerback Denzel Burke pay for biting on tight end Evan Engram's out route.
Nix’s eyes are in the right place here, which helps to draw Burke to Engram. This is a good throw and an even better play by Mims, who slips a tackle in open space and scampers for a 47-yard catch-and-run.
Rip the seam into Tampa 2. Mack Wilson can't even get his head turned around. Excellent throw on the back-shoulder. This is promising stuff. pic.twitter.com/9fI4CljqRb
Our last play is incredibly exciting stuff from Nix. Arizona is in Tampa Cover 2, and Nix rips a back-shoulder throw to Jaylen Waddle up the seam. This is a tight-window throw, and Nix had the confidence to put it on Waddle with the safety crashing down.
First, Nix does a great job identifying the matchup, with Waddle drawing coverage from Mack Wilson running the pole. Nix hits his back foot and lets it fly, putting a great throw in the perfect place for Waddle to come down with it. Wilson doesn’t even get his head turned around, and Waddle makes a great catch for a 27-yard gain.
Nix still had a lot of frustrating issues this week, but I really liked the confidence he played with for most of the game. He showed better poise in the pocket, stepped into a handful of throws, and gave his playmakers opportunities downfield.
This was a great building-block game for Nix, as several of these plays suggest. His early-season timidity was hampering the offense, so it was a breath of fresh air to see him let his hair down and hunt with the football.
Nix got active with his feet to open things up and stayed aggressive when he had the opportunity. If he can keep this level of play, this offense has a chance to right the ship and be a dangerous unit for the rest of the season.

title: Broncos' Player Grades From 30-16 Win Over Cardinals
full_text:
The Denver Broncos took care of business by beating the Arizona Cardinals 30-16 , a team now at 2-5 and viewed as one of the worst in the NFL this year as they undergo a rebuild.
The Broncos were expected to win, and they did, with great play on both sides of the ball, but they still had concerning moments they need to correct before the Kansas City Chiefs arrive next Sunday for a rematch.
This week, the Broncos' player grades are mostly positive, but it's a one-game sample size. Some of these performances, even a few of the good ones, will need to be even better next week.
This game could be a springboard for greater consistency, especially on offense. That said, let’s get into the grades.
Both Broncos linebackers were all over the field against the Cardinals. Strnad didn’t have as productive a game in the box score, but he played well in coverage, rallied to the ball when he allowed a catch, and played well against the run, finishing with six tackles.
It's time for the Broncos to turn to Coleman fully, and not just because of what he did in this game, but also because of the play and attitude of J.K. Dobbins. In his first game back from injured reserve, Coleman ended the day with 11 total touches for 69 yards — nine for 54 rushing and two for 15 receiving — and was trusted late in the game to run out the clock.
Nix's first-half performance wasn't great, especially through the air, but he flipped the script in the second half and showed he's still a threat with his legs, with a 62-yard rushing touchdown .
BO NIX 62-YARD TOUCHDOWN RUN DENvsAZ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/sxC4uWF33r
Nix's pocket presence still needs improvement, though. He's still bailing the pocket when there isn’t pressure, but this could be a springboard for improvement, as it was a step forward with several explosive passing plays.
Alex Singleton | LB | Grade: 78.9
Singleton had some coverage lapses, as expected, but he wasn’t a liability and was flying around the field in the run game. He added pressure and big hits, which brought energy to the team, and finished with 19 tackles .
Dondrea Tillman | OLB | Grade: 76.4
Tillman had a great game on a limited snap count and has become an effective weapon when he sees the field. He could probably go to another team and thrive as a third rusher, but he sits as the fourth outside linebacker in Denver, but he does his job consistently whenever he hits the field.
Ja’Quan McMillian | CB | Grade: 76.3
McMillian has issues in coverage, especially against bigger matchups, but he has a nose for the ball and for generating takeaways. He didn’t have one against the Cardinals, but he got close a couple of times and stays mostly consistent in coverage. He is looking for a big extension.
RJ Harvey | RB | Grade: 74.8
Harvey is an explosive player who thrives in space, and he showed that with a big touchdown on a screen pass. There are still issues as a rusher, but the coaches just need to accept that Harvey isn’t a between-the-tackles runner and that they need to get him into space.
Quinn Meinerz | RG | Grade: 71.8
Meinerz was a mauler up front and did well in pass protection. He remains the Broncos' best offensive lineman and led the interior unit to its best game of the season.
Center Luke Wattenberg and left guard Ben Powers also played well, while the tackles, including Garett Bolles, were poor against the Cardinals.
Marvin Mims Jr. | WR | Grade: 70.1
Mims finally showed some effort on offense, even when the ball wasn’t going his way. That has been a concern with his play since 2024, and this was the first game he looked like he gave 100% on every snap he was out there. His returner inconsistencies have raised some questions, though.
Jahdae Barron | CB | Grade: 28.1
Barron had a tough task covering Trey McBride often, but he made it easier on Arizona at times. Barron was grabby throughout the game, and the Cardinals kept going to the refs about it, which may have led to two late defensive pass interference calls against him.
Devon Key | S | Grade: 30.6
The Broncos got a good game out of Key against the Seattle Seahawks, but he struggled against the Cardinals, as did Taylor Rapp. The play of both fill-in safeties made it clear that the Broncos need Talanoa Hufanga back as soon as possible.
Mike McGlinchey | RT | Grade: 32.4
There were multiple plays where McGlinchey had to choose between two rushers and ended up blocking no one. He has always had issues in pass protection, but normally made up for it as a run blocker. That didn’t happen in this game, and it isn't happening this season.
Troy Franklin | WR | Grade: 40.5
Weirdly, Franklin's blocking kept his grade from being even worse. As a receiver, both his routes and after the catch, he was, to be blunt, lazy. He didn’t put in the effort to get the ball, and yes, he was dealing with contact, but not enough to keep him from giving more effort to the catch, as shown on the botched flea-flicker at the end of the first half.
Adam Trautman | TE | Grade: 42.3
Trautman's best play came on Nix’s touchdown run, where he really sold the route and pass to keep his defender in coverage with his back to the ball as the quarterback streaked downfield. Were it not for Trautman, it probably wouldn't have been a touchdown. Suffice it to say, his best block in this game came without actually blocking a defender.
D.J. Jones | NT | Grade: 45.6
Jones played well overall, but a handful of plays hurt his grade. Without these five snaps, Jones's grade would have been 60.3. His struggles against double teams are a consistent issue, but the Cardinals didn’t put him in that position often.

title: Broncos' Biggest Winners and Losers From 30-16 Victory Over Cardinals
full_text:
The Denver Broncos defeated the Arizona Cardinals 30-16 on the road to get to 5-2 in the standings. It sure didn't look or sound like an away game, with the overwhelming number of Broncos fans at State Farm Stadium.
With the Kansas City Chiefs losing to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday night, the stage is set for the Broncos' rematch with Patrick Mahomes and company next week at Mile High. The Broncos have the chance not only to balance the scales against the Chiefs and avenge their Week 1 loss, but also to make headway at the top of the AFC West at the halfway point of the season.
As we sift through the aftermath of the Broncos' fifth victory of the season, let's talk about this team's biggest winners and losers.
Nix finished with 295 yards from scrimmage, but it was his 62-yard touchdown run that seemed to reignite his confidence. He also tossed a 52-yard touchdown pass to RJ Harvey, becoming the fifth player in NFL history to record a rushing and passing touchdown of 50-plus yards in the same game.
Nix finished 15-of-29 passing for 222 yards and a touchdown. After the game, Nix toyed with a local media corps that had been skeptical that he had fully healed from his fractured ankle suffered back in January.
"You believe me now?" Nix asked with a smile from the post-game podium.
BO NIX 62-YARD TOUCHDOWN RUN DENvsAZ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/sxC4uWF33r
Nobody should be questioning Nix's health anymore, and his big game in the desert seemed to salve whatever was ailing him between the ears in his recovery from that serious injury.
Barron deserves a lot of credit for holding down the fort amid Patrick Surtain II's injury, but he had a rough game against the Cardinals. Barron was penalized twice for pass interference, and he allowed four of five targets to be completed for 41 yards.
Barron did finish with five tackles, and while his coverage was sticky, Jacoby Brissett was able to exploit him, especially one-on-one against tight end Trey McBride. Let's hope this game doesn't affect Barron's confidence too much because he's been a plus player over the past month.
The rookie returned from injured reserve and made a huge impact in his first game back. Coleman's burst brought an energy to the Broncos' ground attack that had been missing.
He also did well as a receiver out of the backfield and in pass protection. He finished with 69 yards from scrimmage on 11 touches, and averaged 6.0 yards per carry as a rusher.
The rookie Jonah Coleman making something out of nothing DENvsAZ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/wjeHrq6ZEi
The Broncos' run game is looking up with Coleman back on the field.
Dobbins went from getting 17 carries last week to just six on Sunday, mainly because Coleman was efficient when he was on the field. Alas, Dobbins was only able to generate 23 rushing yards on those carries, though he did find the end zone on a 1-yard touchdown.
Dobbins did have a nice 13-yard run erased by an illegal shift penalty, so he did have a few nice runs. But his burst is nowhere close to that of the rookie.
I expected Sean Payton to balance the running back touches, but not in the rookie's favor. It could be a sign that there's a new RB1 in the Broncos' backfield.
Bonitto was a terror all day long, finishing with a team-high six pressures on Brissett. Alas, Bonitto wasn't able to get home for a sack, but his presence was felt all game long.
With a solid head of steam built up over the past few weeks, it's very possible it could culminate in a big Bonitto night next week against the Chiefs and their undrafted rookie left tackle.
Waddle makes the "losers" side of the ledger, though it wasn't all his fault. As a receiver, he was solid, catching four of his seven targets (team high) for 48 yards, including a long of 27 down the right seam.
Alas, with the Broncos trying to protect a lead and kill the clock late, Payton decided to get cute and run an end-around, and Waddle bobbled the tossed exchange, fumbled it, and then fell on the ball as Josh Sweat landed on top of him, injurying his chest.
The injury didn't look good for Waddle, who was shortly thereafter escorted to the locker room never to return. With how well Coleman was running the ball late, it was an unnessary risk that Payton has already accepted the blame for, calling the play call "dumb." Let's hope Waddle's injury isn't as serious as it looked.
Harvey only carried the ball three times for six yards, but his two catches for 54 yards and a touchdown made a big difference in this game. On his 52-yard touchdown, Payton perfectly timed a screen to exploit the Cardinals' blitz-happy defense, and Nix, Harvey, and the Broncos' offense executed it to a 'T.'
RJ Harvey takes the screen pass 52 yards for a TD! DENvsAZ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/symyT3Qo6D
It was Harvey's first receiving touchdown of the season and well deserved. Given the burst he shows as a runner, he's deserving of more carries than he's gotten of late, but it appears he's going to take a back seat in that department to Coleman and Dobbins.
Singleton finished with a season-high 19 tackles (12 solo), and was a whirling dervish out there. He was penalized for a ticky-tack roughing the passer call, but the veteran linebacker was a difference-maker out there.
In coverage, Singleton didn't hold up so well, allowing four of five targets to be completed for 38 yards, but he cleaned up those plays well. The team captain has a legitimate chance at notching 200 tackles this season.

title: Broncos QB Bo Nix Makes NFL History in Week 7 Win Over Cardinals
full_text:
Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix added another piece of NFL history to his growing legacy in the Mile HIgh City.
In Sunday's win over the Arizona Cardinals , Nix became the fifth player in league history to record passing and rushing touchdowns of at least 50 yards, according to Next Gen Stats.
Nix joins Justin Fields, Lamar Jackson, Cam Newton, and Ace Parker of the 1938 Brooklyn Dodgers as the only players to ever accomplish that feat.
Appearing more confident both as a passer and runner, Nix completed 15-of-29 passes for 222 yards and one touchdown, a 52-yard screen to running back RJ Harvey who took it to the house. Nix also added 73 rushing yards, including a 62-yard scamper in which he went untouched up the middle of Arizona's defense.
"When he's making plays, it gets the whole team juiced," defensive end Zach Allen said in his postgame gathering with reporters.
Nix completed balls to nine different receivers, with Courtland Sutton totaling a team-high three catches for 45 yards. Harvey (54 yards), Marvin Mims (53 yards), and Jaylen Waddle (48 yards) were also all involved.
“Listen, I think for our team, offensively, all those of those things. Yeah, I mean, the confidence inside of the building relative to his ability hadn’t changed at all," head coach Sean Payton said of Nix after the game. "I appreciate some guys, sometimes you’re answering questions about whether or not… and there’s not one time where we were… he’s our guy. And it was good to see him play well and it was good to see us block well and make some plays down the field.”
The Broncos were also aided by the return of rookie running back Jonah Coleman, who converted carries into 54 rushing yards and helped chew clock in the second half, despite Denver losing the overall time-of-possession battle, 33:18-26:42.
Mired in a mental slump to this point, Nix's touchdown run -- the longest such play by a quarterback in franchise history -- might've been the spark he desperately needed to turn around the second half of his season, and lead 5-2 Denver confidently back into the postseason.
It was the get-right game against an inferior opponent that many believed would transpire . He didn't put up Star Wars numbers, but what he did series-to-series passed the smell test in different orders of magntitude compared to past few games.
Now the question becomes: Can Nix and company keep this monentum rolling into Week 8, when they'll meet a familiar foe in Kansas City that presents a much tougher matchup than the hapless Cardinals did.
"I thought we played a good game offensively, but there are still several things we would like to get better at," Nix said after the game.

title: 3 Big Takeaways From Broncos' 30-16 Win Over Cardinals
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are 5-2 after beating the Arizona Cardinals 30-16 on the road.
You'd be forgiven for thinking this game was played at Mile High, though, as the stands at State Farm Stadium were thronged with Broncos Country. Having so many fans at their back on the road seemed to give the Broncos some juice, especially in the second half.
The Broncos can now look ahead to their Week 8 rematch with the Kansas City Chiefs, and gear up for the opportunity to make some headway in the divisional race.
What did we learn from the Broncos' fifth win of the season? Here are three key takeaways.
Nix didn't need a big 300-yard passing game to regain his confidence; it came flooding back on the heels of a 62-yard rushing touchdown. The play came at the bottom of the second quarter, with Arizona's secondary running some match coverage with everyone's backs turned to the ball.
Nix capitalized, showcasing some impressive speed as he nearly went untouched all the way. It was the longest quarterback rushing touchdown in Broncos history and the longest in the NFL since 2022.
BO NIX 62-YARD TOUCHDOWN RUN DENvsAZ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/sxC4uWF33r
Nix finished the day with seven rushes for 73 yards. Generating some success on the field with his legs seemed to spark something in Nix, but he was already looking much better before his big run.
The Broncos challenged Arizona's defense vertically, and while Nix was unable to connect on some of those shots (one of which was a big Troy Franklin drop on a flea-flicker), it showed a refreshingly aggressive mindset, both on the part of the quarterback and Sean Payton, the play-caller.
Nix came just shy of totaling 300 yards from scrimmage. He went 15-of-29 as a passer for 222 yards with a touchdown. His two longest throws of the day were a 47-yard catch-and-run by Marvin Mims Jr. and a 52-yard RJ Harvey touchdown that came on a perfectly timed and well-executed screen to exploit the Cardinals' blitz-happy defense.
Nix's get-right game last season came in Week 7, although the Broncos had to wait until the fourth quarter to see him break loose. There's just something about Week 7 for Nix, it would seem.
This game had to go a long way toward solving the between-the-ears struggles Nix has dealt with this season. Exhale, Broncos Country. Nix is going to be fine.
The Broncos have been linked to Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor in the NFL rumor mill, but with Coleman returning to the field for the first time since Week 2, GM George Paton may be far less motivated to look elsewhere ahead of the trade deadline.
The Broncos have two more games between now and the deadline to ultimately decide on whether to make a trade, but their backfield simply looked different on Sunday. Coleman contributed in every way, catching passes out of the backfield, picking up blitzers in pass protection, and showing some burst and vision to make plays as a runner.
Coleman finished the day with nine carries for 54 yards and two receptions for 15 yards. Just as we saw in Week 2, the rookie was crucial late in the game, helping to keep the chains moving with some tough running as the Broncos protected a multi-score lead.
The rookie Jonah Coleman making something out of nothing DENvsAZ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/wjeHrq6ZEi
J.K. Dobbins was solid, finishing with 23 yards and a touchdown on six carries, while Harvey only carried thrice for six yards. Dobbins's touchdown should have gone to Coleman, by rights, as the rookie did the heavy lifting on that drive at running back. The fantasy folks would say Coleman got "vultured" by Dobbins.
The Broncos' backfield is headed in the right direction. Coleman looks primed to carry the torch as this team's No. 1 running back moving forward, and as Week 7 showed, that still leaves plenty of room for Dobbins and Harvey to have a role.
The Broncos decided not to dress cornerback Patrick Surtain II, downgrading him to out shortly before kickoff . Riley Moss, Jahdae Barron, and Kris Abrams-Draine held down the fort again amid the officiating crew's torrent of yellow laundry. That's a topic for another time.
Late in the game, with the Broncos protecting a two-score lead, Payton called a trick play of sorts, sending wide receiver Jaylen Waddle on an end-around instead of just giving the ball to Coleman, who had been efficient on that drive. Nix tossed the ball to Waddle, but the receiver bobbled it, and fumbled, falling on the ball to save the possession. Alas, Josh Sweat fell on top of Waddle, with the ball seemingly digging into his chest.
Waddle was injured on the play. After a quick trip to the blue tent, he was escorted to the locker room. It was reported as a chest injury, which is an ailment he's been dealing with for the past two weeks. He may have aggravated it.
Waddle finished the day with four receptions for 48 yards, including a great 27-yard catch down the right seam. The Broncos are going to need their newest receiving weapon. Fingers crossed.
If that wasn't scary enough, All-Pro defensive end Zach Allen went down with a hamstring injury late. It takes a lot for the big fella to go down, but Allen was at least able to walk off the field on his own power.
With the Chiefs up next at Mile High, let's hope that it's nothing major for Waddle and Allen. We'll be looking for updates on these injured key players.

title: Broncos' Make Game-Time Decision on Pat Surtain II vs. Cardinals
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are in the desert to take on the Arizona Cardinals .
The game's inactives just dropped. Let's take a look, starting with the Broncos.
Surtain was listed as questionable for this game , but the Broncos are going to play it safe. With Riley Moss fully back in the saddle, and given the rise of Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine, the Broncos can afford to get by without Surtain for one more game. Circle Week 8 for Surtain's return.
Hufanga suffered an ankle injury in Week 5. This will be his second missed game, which is why the Broncos elevated safety Taylor Rapp again from the practice squad. Hopefully, Hufanga can return next week alongside Surtain.
Casey and Bentley are rookie draft picks who've yet to dress this season. They probably won't dress, unless there are injuries ahead of them on their respective depth charts.
Both Jackson and Onyedim being inactive is interesting. It implies the Broncos aren't too worried about Arizona's ground attack. Onyedim, the team's highest draft pick this year, has been a healthy scratch in each game.
At a certain point, you've got to wonder when Onyedim is going to get his shot. Then again, Sai'vion Jones has finally been getting some action on defense, and like Onyedim, he was a third-round pick last year who spent his rookie campaign as a healthy scratch, mostly.
Still, given that Denver ranks 31st against the run and Onyedim was one of the 2026 draft class' best run-defending defensive tackles, his inactivity is curious. The Broncos' defensive line gets after the quarterback like no one else, but they're struggling to stop the run.
As for Ehlinger, he'll dress as the emergency quarterback, but he officially goes down as a healthy scratch. That's one of the newer NFL rules, and the Broncos exploit it every week.
👀 our inactives for #DENvsAZ : 📰 » https://t.co/janx2byozb pic.twitter.com/NXDe4kpAh6
Budda Baker is playing. He was listed as questionable but he's dressing.
The big hits here for Arizona are the absences of Love on offense and Nolen on defense. The Broncos will see a lot of running back Tyler Allgeier, and with Nolen out, there's an even bigger opportunity to get the ground game rolling.

title: Broncos a Team to Watch in Jonathan Taylor Trade Sweepstakes, Insider Claims
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is little more than two weeks out, and the rumor mill is cranking.
Since the Indianapolis Colts fired their general manager, Chris Ballard, the Denver Broncos have been linked to running back Jonathan Taylor all week in the rumor mill. But on Sunday, as Week 7 got underway, ESPN insider Adam Schefter gave the Taylor-to-Denver rumors a heaping dose of credibility.
"The first player to watch in Indianapolis is Jonathan Taylor. There's going to be a lot of interest in Taylor around the league. Teams like the Seattle Seahawks, the Minnesota Vikings, the Denver Broncos, and the Green Bay Packers, who made a run at Jonathan Taylor a couple of years back. [They] could decide to call Indianapolis again," Schefter said on Sunday NFL Countdown .
If Schefter said it, there's something burning at the source of that smoke, even if it's just an ember. And I think, right now, the Taylor possibility is just that: an ember.
The Broncos are through their first six-week gauntlet, and the schedule is now opening up for them. Meanwhile, they just activated rookie running back Jonah Coleman , and the Broncos believe that the best is yet to come from J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey.
If anything, the 4-2 Broncos will be buyers ahead of the November 10 trade deadline, but that's a big if. For the first time in a while, the Broncos have a full complement of draft picks in 2027, and their roster is starting to age, so infusions of youth will be key for the future.
I'm not sure Sean Payton is trying to hear that right now, though. Not after he came within a single game of leading the Broncos to the Super Bowl — a goal that would have been realized had Bo Nix not suffered his ankle injury in the divisional round.
Payton wants to win now because Nix won't be on his rookie contract forever. The third-year quarterback may be slumping, but the Broncos still view him as the future franchise quarteback.
Payton has said playing quarterback is the toughest thing to do in the NFL if you don't have a run game. The Broncos haven't had a viable run game this season, which has only exacerbated Nix's issues.
Re-signing Dobbins and keeping him healthy was supposed to give Nix the run-game foundation he needed to build on in Year 3. Maybe it was the level of competition those first six weeks, maybe it was the culmination of all Dobbins's serious injuries, but he hasn't looked like the player we saw for 10 games last season.
Coleman could be the answer, but pinning a team's rushing hopes on a rookie returning from injured reserve, regardless of his draft pedigree, would be ill-advised. The Broncos have three games left to decide whether to make a play for Taylor, unless another team beats them to the punch.
Taylor already has 492 rushing yards and seven touchdowns this season, though he is averaging a career-low 4.0 yards per carry. He's one of the best backs in the NFL, though, and would immediately upgrade the Broncos' backfield.
If the Broncos want to beat out other potential Taylor buyers, it might take upwards of a second-round pick, plus more, to pry him off Indy's hands. The Broncos will have to decide whether he'd be worth the cost, and they'd have to absorb his new two-year, $44 million contract.
But Denver would have Taylor all the way up until he hit the 30-year-old mark before having to decide on what to do next. Because he has so many miles on his tires, even at 27, there's a chance the Broncos could get him for a third-rounder plus some 2028 late-round capital. Maybe.
We know the Broncos are interested if Schefter is saying it. Let's see if it motivates the likes of Dobbins, Harvey, and Coleman, starting on Sunday at State Farm Stadium as the Broncos take on the Arizona Cardinals .

title: 5 Bold Broncos Predictions vs. Cardinals: Bo Nix's Reckoning
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are preparing to take on the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. The Cardinals are a feisty 2-4 team and are already exceeding expectations.
This isn't a gimme game, despite what some people say. That being said, the Cardinals aren't exactly a good team either.
The Broncos can't overlook this opponent, but this game is a chance to do some maintenance on offense and get the unit firing on all cylinders.
And now it's time for this week's bold predictions. If the Broncos can realize these predictions, it could put them on the winning track for the rest of the season.
Nix has been seeing ghosts when looking deep after some early interceptions and near turnovers, which explains, in part, the ultra-conservative passing approach we've seen for weeks. This is a good game to work on correcting his hesitancy, as the Cardinals rank 31st in explosive pass-play rate allowed.
The Cardinals suffer multiple coverage breaks per game. They have serious issues with their linebacker coverage, and their secondary isn't the best.
The Broncos have no better opponent remaining on the schedule than Arizona to help Nix break out of his shell. The Nix reckoning is coming.
This pairs with my previous prediction; there is ample opportunity to get Harvey involved in the passing and running game. The Cardinals are the NFL's fourth-worst defense when it comes to covering running backs, despite having one of the lowest rates of targets to backs.
Part of this is due to Arizona's secondary issues. The Cardinals' linebackers will be mismatched covering Harvey, and they struggle against outside runs, which is where the Broncos' second-year back can be used in the ground game.
Harvey finishes with 100-plus receiving and 50-plus rushing yards.
The Cardinals haven't allowed many sacks this year (only 12), and they have the eighth-lowest sack percentage and pressure rate. However, they do allow one of the fastest times to pressure (sixth-fastest).
Given how much pressure the Broncos can generate, as long as they can bring down Brissett, they're poised to have a big day in the sack department. If this prediction comes true, it'll be only the third time in franchise history that the Broncos will have posted three straight games with at least five sacks.
This pass rush is on a roll, and that momentum continues in the desert.
Thanks to the pressure up front and forcing a mistake from Brissett, Barron nabs an interception and returns it to the house. Barron is aggressive in coverage, and it sometimes backfires, but it pays off in this game.
Brissett throws an underneath route under pressure, and Barron jumps it for the first pick-six of his career. He actually had one as a rookie, but it was called back due to a defensive holding penalty far away from the play.
Through the first six games, the Broncos have gotten close to a return touchdown. Harvey in particular has had multiple long returns that were a block or an avoided tackle away from being a touchdown.
The Cardinals have lapses on kickoff coverage, which create the opening for a special teams touchdown. The Broncos have had a third-phase score brewing for weeks, but the stars finally align against Arizona, whether it's Harvey or Marvin Mims Jr.

title: 5 Risers, 3 Fallers After Detroit Lions First Division Win
full_text:
The Detroit Lions handled business and earned a win over the Green Bay Packers in Week 7 of the NFL season.
While it wasn't the cleanest effort, the Lions overcame some of their self-made adversity and ultimately secured a divisional victory in their first NFC North clash of the season.
Here are risers and fallers following the Lions' Week 7 win over the Packers.
Branch was somewhat limited in his return from a torn Achilles, as he played 45 snaps. However, head coach Dan Campbell stated that they took the restraints off at halftime, as he proved to be acclimating well after missing the first five games of the year.
The Alabama product recorded an interception, which was his first since the 2024 season, and provided a spark for the defense. Moving forward, the Lions will continue to increase his workload and he will likely be a difference maker for a secondary that has struggled in his absence.
After a sluggish start to the season, Williams has been finding a groove . He has scored twice in each of the last two games, and has had at least 90 yards in two of the team's last three games.
Williams is the team's bona fide No. 2 option behind Amon-Ra St. Brown, and will continue to be relied upon to produce at a high level. Though the start to the season caused some concerns, Williams appears to be fully out of that funk and should be consistently contributing moving forward.
Viewed as exclusively a special teams contributor, Dorsey got some opportunities on defense and delivered in a big way. Detroit's secondary has been much maligned, and for good reason, through the first five games, but Dorsey delivered a spark in the win over the Packers.
In 14 snaps, Dorsey earned a Pro Football Focus defensive grade of 87.7 and allowed just one completion for five yards on four targets. He earned a shoutout from Campbell in the postgame, and should be a bigger part of the rotation moving forward.
The Lions signed the journeyman Carter after the season-ending injury to Tom Kennedy, and he showed why he's been coveted throughout his career. Carter averaged 26 yards on his two kick returns, and had a 15-yard punt return that he nearly sprung for a huge gain.
Detroit has been angling to get more production out of the return game, and Carter appears to be suited to deliver in that aspect of the game.
With the injury to Devin White, there were opportunities available for a third linebacker in Detroit's defense. It was Nowaske who received the most snaps in that role behind Jack Campbell and Derrick Barnes.
Though it was only 14 snaps, Nowaske showed that he is capable of contributing. He's become a very valuable part of Detroit's linebacker rotation, and appears to be climbing the depth chart midway through his fourth professional season.
Mays got off to a slow start in his Lions debut, as he had a role in two costly turnovers. First, he accidentally punched the ball out of the hands of Jahmyr Gibbs on a late drive in the first half where the Lions appeared poised to extend their lead before halftime.
After halftime, a miscue on a snap between Mays and quarterback Jared Goff resulted in a fumble and subsuquent score on the ensuing drive from the Packers. Mays could certainly shake off the rust and bounce back, but with how well Juice Scruggs was playing he will certainly face some scrutiny.
LaPorta made plenty of headlines with his comments regarding the ongoing contract situation. He addressed the situation and made legitimate claims as to why it's important, but didn't make a huge impact in Sunday's game.
After a strong start to the season, LaPorta was kept in check by the Packers' defense. Part of this was due to the Lions targeting St. Brown and Williams on a majority of passes, while it also had to do with the Packers having a good plan for him.
LaPorta had just one catch for 18 yards, which was his lowest output of the season and the first time he's been held to just one catch in his career since Week 7 of the 2024 season.
Izien did not record any defensive snaps for the second-consecutive game. The former Tampa Bay Buccaneer was limited to exclusively special teams duty, with rookie Keith Abney logging 34 snaps even after Branch returned.
As Branch continues to acclimate, the Lions will increase his workload. At this juncture, it looks as though Abney is ahead of Izien, which means the veteran may continue to be kept out of the defensive rotation unless an injury occurs.
Sports journalist who has covered the Detroit Lions the past three NFL seasons. Christian brings expert analysis, insights and an ability to fairly assess how the team is performing in a tough NFC North division.

title: 3 Things We Learned About Detroit Lions After Win Over Packers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions recorded arguably their biggest win of the 2026 season on Sunday, defeating the NFC North rival Green Bay Packers, 20-17.
It was a gritty performance from Dan Campbell's squad which did not play its cleanest game, but still did enough right in order to secure the Week 7 victory.
For starters, Kelvin Sheppard's defense, aided by the return of Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch, stepped up big time in the divisional affair.
It limited Green Bay signal-caller Jordan Love to under 300 yards passing and kept the Packers’ pass-catching duo of Christian Watson and Matthew Golden in check. Both receivers were held under 60 yards and out of the end zone.
Plus, the Lions’ run defense delivered a strong effort, holding Green Bay to just 60 total yards on the ground on 19 carries (3.2 yards/carry).
And Branch had his fingerprints all over the standout performance from Sheppard's unit.
In his first taste of action since tearing his Achilles in Week 14 of the 2025 season against the Dallas Cowboys, the defensive back made his presence known.
He logged four total tackles and a pass defensed, and came through with a crucial interception of Love to start the fourth quarter. It wasn't an easy pick to come up with, either.
On the play (third-and-21), the Packers were backed up deep in Lions territory and Love decided to heave the football. It landed past the 50-yard line, where Branch high-pointed the ball and grabbed it out of the air, beating Watson for the 50/50 ball.
BRIAN BRANCH IS BACK GBvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/F1Pa2vK3fI
It was a prime example of Branch's next-level athleticism and the immense impact he can make in the back-end of Detroit's defensive backfield .
“You go through an injury like that; the amount of rehab and things that go into all of that to get back to where you're ready to play at a high level in the NFL," Lions head man Dan Campbell said of Branch after the game. "You get back to some of what you are, and he's not even fully back yet as far as just the rust. Every rep he takes he's going to get better and better. It's not an easy road. That was a huge play. Everybody loves (Branch) because he's a great teammate and a productive football player. He can just find the ball.”
Campbell & Co. direly missed the Alabama product, and there's no question he played an integral role in the Lions securing the win in the divisional tilt.
Undoubtedly, the defense is leaps and bounds better with Branch healthy.
On Sunday, it also became evident that Cade Mays was not quite ready to anchor the line.
Playing in his first game since being acquired by Detroit this offseason, Mays had a hand in two turnovers: a Jahmyr Gibbs fumble to close the first half and a botched snap in the opening seconds of the second half.
Meanwhile, on a positive note, it became apparent the Lions’ offense can afford to be less than perfect every so often.
Offensive coordinator Drew Petzing's unit was just good enough against Green Bay, and that was more than fine in the Week 7 divisional clash.
Veteran signal-caller Jared Goff threw a ball or two that could have been picked, and the ever explosive Jahmyr Gibbs was contained fairly well by the Packers for most of the game. Yet, it didn't matter on Sunday.
Goff still came through with big-time throws to the likes of Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams when it counted the most, and Gibbs ran out the clock in the fourth quarter, setting up Jake Bates for the game-winning field goal as time expired.
Refreshingly, in the Week 7 contest , the Lions’ offense did not have to lead the way and score 30-plus points in order to get into the win column. Instead, the defense took on the protagonist role, allowing Petzing's unit to take a much-deserved backseat.
It was a perfect example of the complementary football that Campbell often preaches about – a winning brand of football that the best teams play on a consistent basis.
And if the Lions want to rise to the top of the NFC, they'll need to play a lot more of that type of football moving forward, including in Week 8 against the undefeated Minnesota Vikings.
Simply, it's the only way Detroit will be able to make a Super Bowl run in 2026.

title: Lions Provide Key Injury Updates: Will St. Brown, Rakestraw Miss Practice?
full_text:
The Detroit Lions had two players with minor injuries, following the teams Week 7 contest against the Green Bay Packers.
Head coach Dan Campbell, speaking to local reporters, updated the minor ankle injuries to wideout Amon-Ra St. Brown and cornerback Ennis Rakestraw.
Both are not currently expected to miss the Vikings game, but could miss one single practice on Wednesday.
Rakestraw played 31 percent of defensive snaps against Green Bay, as Detroit's secondary rotation was effective in limiting the explosive plays in a 20-17 home victory.
If Rakestraw has any setbacks, Roger McCreary, Khalil Dorsey and Keith Abney both have the opportunity to step in during his absence.
Detroit's former second-round pick was urging coach Campbell to play even more in the first half in his first game returning from a torn Achilles tendon.
"I asked for God just to have a clean game and we all had a clean game," said Branch. "We executed. We still left a lot of plays out there again, that comes with it. But we all played a hell of a game and I'm just proud to be a part of the secondary. We done been through a lot and now it's time to hit the ground running now."
He added later, "Just telling him when I get out there, my adrenaline going, so I'm ready to go. The plan was to pitch count. I kind of didn't like it, but they were smart for doing it and I just thanked them because they were looking out for me.”
Branch earned his first interception of the 2026 season. He expressed, "Oh, it felt good. Just to grabbing the pick the first game out, that's nothing but God.”
With each performance since the Bills loss, the team's defense has steadily gained confidence.
"Shepp called a hell of a gameplan, put everybody in the right spot," said Branch. "And again, once we execute it's wraps and that's all we got to do moving forward is execute his game plan.”

title: Grades: Lions Earn Early Season Statement Win Over Division Rival
full_text:
The Detroit Lions overcame some adversity, made some of their own breaks and came out with a win in their first divisional game of the season.
On Sunday, the Lions outlasted the Packers with a last-second field goal from Jake Bates to earn a 20-17 win and move to 4-2 on the season.
Here are grades for each position group based on performance in Sunday's game.
The Lions' game plan was clear from the start, as Jared Goff was letting it rip . He connected with Jameson Williams for a 16-yard touchdown on the opening drive, and was 13-for-17 for 204 yards before halftime.
Things started on a dire note in the second half, however. Goff and center Cade Mays, who was making his season debut, mishandled a snap and the Packers recovered.
Goff was ultimately able to respond, firing another touchdown to Williams in the third quarter. The veteran also drew a pair of key roughing the passer penalties, including one on the final drive.
He finished the game 22-of-32 for 303 yards and two touchdowns, and remains without an interception through six games.
Jahmyr Gibbs had a costly fumble in the first half, as he was wrestled to the ground and had the ball punched out on accident by center Cade Mays. The fumble occurred in the red-zone, and prevented the Lions from expanding their 10-7 lead late in the first half.
However, Gibbs was able to deliver in key moments. He had the game-sealing first-down run, as he took a toss to the left and passed the sticks on third-and-6 before sliding to the turf to set up the game-winning kick.
Overall, Gibbs finished with 116 rushing yards on 29 carries, and added 27 yards on five catches.
It was a big start for the tandem of Jameson Williams and Amon-Ra St. Brown. Both wideouts had big plays early, with Williams putting Detroit on the board first with a 16-yard catch-and-run that culminated with him leaping into the end zone.
St. Brown, meanwhile, had seven catches for 135 yards before the half. Williams would add a second touchdown, while St. Brown finished with 153 yards on nine catches and 11 total targets.
Isaac TeSlaa was unable to haul in a back-shoulder throw in the end-zone, but did have a big catch for a first-down in the third quarter.
Sam LaPorta was held without a catch until the final drive of the game, when he hauled in an 18-yard toss from Goff. Other than LaPorta, Tyler Conklin was the only other option utilized in the passing game as he had a four-yard catch.
LaPorta, Conklin and Brock Wright were all utilized in the run game as blockers, with Larry Borom and Skyler Gill-Howard also being utilized in jumbo packages.
Cade Mays had a pair of unfortunate miscues in his first game as a Lion. After missing the first five games of the season with a wrist injury, Mays entered the lineup in place of Juice Scruggs at center. He inadvertantly punched the ball out from Gibbs in the first half, then had a mishandled snap exchange with Goff in the third quarter.
Elsewhere, the Lions were relatively effective up front. They allowed just one sack in Sunday's game, but had some instances where they couldn't get a push in the run game. The biggest example of this was when they were stuffed on fourth-and-1 backed up in their own territory.
The Lions' pass-rush was slowed , with the unit recording just one sack as Aidan Hutchinson got home in the first half. However, the defense was able to get consistent pressure on Love and keep the Packers' run game in check.
Detroit's defense held Green Bay to 3.2 yards per carry, with Josh Jacobs being limited to 36 yards on 11 carries in his first appearance of the season.
Jack Campbell had an early miscue when he fell down covering Packers tight end Tucker Kraft in the end zone, resulting in a score. Derrick Barnes had a big moment in the second quarter, however, as he caused an incompletion with a big hit to Christian Watson on a pass in the flats.
Barnes had a pair of unfortunate developments in the second half, however. He was beat in man-to-man coverage by Josh Jacobs on Jacobs' 25-yard touchdown catch. Then, he was called for unnecessary roughness on quarterback Jordan Love in the fourth-quarter, though the call was controversial.
A pivotal stretch occurred midway through the second quarter. Flushed from the pocket, Jordan Love heaved a third-down pass that was dropped by Lions defensive back Keith Abney II and looked to be a huge missed opportunity. However, the Packers elected to go for it, and D.J. Reed came up with a huge tackle for loss to force a turnover.
In the third quarter, the Packers were able to score on their first drive as Abney missed a tackle on Jacobs, who powered through the rookie and into the end-zone to give his team a 14-10 lead.
Brian Branch returned to action for the first time this season after rehabbing a torn Achilles, and notched his first interception since the 2024 season in the process.
After the game, Dan Campbell was complimentary of the entire unit, as the team utilized all of its cornerbacks including Khalil Dorsey, who has been used almost exclusively on special teams. Dorsey had a pair of big pass breakups in Sunday's game.
DeAndre Carter made his Lions debut Sunday and provided a spark in the return game. On two kick returns, he averaged 26 yards and had one that nearly popped but was called back for holding. He also had a 15-yard return on the one punt he fielded.
Special teams played a huge role in this game, as Packers kicker Trey Smack missed two chip-shots including one that D.J. Wonnum appeared to block in the fourth quarter after the Lions' failed fourth-down conversion.
Jake Bates remained perfect on the year with two field goals, including a 40-yarder in the first half and the game-winner from 22 yards out.
The decision to go for it on fourth-down backed up in their own territory will be lamented, as the offense was stifled. However, the explanation Campbell gave about getting the ball back at that stage tracks, and the team ultimately dodged further damage when Smack missed the ensuing field goal.
Defensively, the Lions did a good job bottling up the Packers' explosive offense and holding them to 17 yards. Getting Branch back helped, and the secondary as a whole found a way to come up with some big plays.
On offense, the Lions worked around some self-inflicted mistakes. Big performances from Gibbs, St. Brown and Williams helped fuel them, and ultimately it worked out in their favor.
Now, Detroit will have another big test awaiting them at home with the unbeaten Minnesota Vikings coming to town. It's a big opportunity for Detroit to get back into striking range for the division.

title: 8 Winners, 3 Losers in Detroit Lions Win Over Packers
full_text:
On Sunday, the Detroit Lions came back after a bye week to start divisional play, taking on the Green Bay Packers.
The Lions forced multiple stops in the first half, en route to a 10-7 halftime lead. The Packers took advantage of a turnover on the Lions’ opening drive of the second half to grab their first lead, but Detroit snapped back and executed when it mattered most, taking up the final three minutes of game clock to kick a game-winner as time expired. Detroit emerged victorious, 20-17.
Here are the winners and losers from the divisional affair.
The Lions All-Pro receiver has been a thorn in the NFC North’s side for nearly a half-decade, but Green Bay seemed to forget about St. Brown in the first half. The receiver found himself having a career day in the first half.
St. Brown started his damage with a simple out and up where his man could not keep up with him. That was the theme of the opening half, as the receiver slid behind coverage. The Packers surrendered 204 receiving yards in the first half, with the USC product accounting for 135 yards on seven catches on eight targets.
The Packers elected to finally cover the Pro Bowl receiver, holding him to 15 yards in the second half. That said, St. Brown finished with his fifth 150-yard receiving game of his career.
The Packers had a rough start to the game, with St. Brown and then Williams burning the secondary on back-to-back plays. Right after the former had an out-and-up for a big gain, Williams was open for another gain, and then was targeted a second time in the flat, which he took for a touchdown.
The Packers clamped up on Williams after that, only allowing one more catch in the first half as St. Brown ran wild. The halftime adjustments to cover St. Brown enabled the Alabama product to get free for two more catches for 40 yards on the Lions’ go-ahead scoring drive.
Williams capped that drive off with his second touchdown of the night, after an eligible Penei Sewell ran routes and helped free up Williams on a hitch route.
Branch made his return to the field on Sunday, and it was quite the successful return. The former Lions second-round pick aided a few defensive stops early. Branch helped the communication throughout the day, along with breaking up a pass.
His biggest play of the night, however, came to open the fourth quarter. Jordan Love took a shot deep with Christian Watson appearing to have a step on Khalil Dorsey. Branch, however, flashed over to high point the ball and ended a chance of a Green Bay go-ahead scoring drive.
Reed was strong on Sunday, despite the Lions allowing nearly 300 yards through the air. The corner made some of the biggest plays of the days when it was needed most. With Green Bay inside the Lions’ 10-yard line on fourth down, Reed sniffed out a screen and dropped Matthew Golden behind the line of scrimmage. That ended an impressive Packers streak, as they had converted their previous nine fourth-down attempts.
Reed also added a pass breakup late, knocking the ball out to force a punt. Most breakdowns on the day did not occur from Reed, and he quietly put together one of his best games in Honolulu Blue.
Hutchinson brought down Jordan Love for the only Lions sack of the game in the second quarter, providing a significant portion of the defensive stops needed. He also nearly picked off Love during the first half.
Hutchinson finished with five quarterback hits , while the rest of the team combined for one hit on the afternoon.
As the fourth quarter wore down, the Lions and Packers each got desperate to make a play. The Lions went for it on fourth down and got stuffed on a Jahmyr Gibbs run , giving the Packers the ball inside the Lions’ 30-yard line. That dragged out the Lions defense, which stood tall and forced a Trey Smack field goal attempt.
Wonnum made arguably the biggest play of the night, with the South Carolina product getting a few fingers on the Smack field goal, deflecting it and pushing it just wide.
While it was not a game that saw Jahmyr Gibbs go for over 150 total yards, Gibbs was quietly doing his role behind the scenes. Sonic finished the game with just over 130 total yards, crossing 100 yards in the final two minutes.
On the opening scoring drive, it was Gibbs picking up a blitz to enable a big play to Jameson Williams, who would follow that up with a score on the next play.
In the final two minutes, Gibbs faced a free touchdown twice and declined it both times, kneeling to make it second-and-2 before taking another kneel after converting a 3rd-and-6 on a toss play. That enabled the Lions to run the clock out and kick a field goal as time expired.
Bates was needed for all eight of his points on Sunday, with the Arkansas product kicking the Lions home to victory as time expired.
None of Bates’s field goals were particularly hard, but he was part of the end product that executed a win. His kickoffs were also strong, with the kicker forcing Green Bay to return the ball and not break their 30-yard-line. Full marks for the former Michigan Panther.
It was a rough opening to the season for Mays. The center was activated for Sunday’s contest after being the star free agent acquisition to the offensive line. In the first half, Mays provided a strong push in the opening series. That was offset by a false start penalty where the entire offense besides Mays moved.
Then, to make matters worse, Mays was knocked into Gibbs, forcing the back to fumble as the Lions were deep in Green Bay territory. It gave the Packers a way to escape, kneeling to end the half.
Mays did not have a strong start to the second half, either. The center had a bad exchange with Goff on the opening series, with the ball bouncing two yards past the line of scrimmage and being recovered by Green Bay. That enabled Green Bay to score a go-ahead touchdown on their ensuing drive.
Barnes had a rough outing Sunday. On two separate fourth-down plays , the Purdue product was tagged for a missed assignment in coverage. The Packers went 3-of-4 on fourth down in the opening half, and Barnes was the primary man giving free conversions to Green Bay.
To make matters worse, Barnes was again the primary man in coverage when the Packers had their go-ahead touchdown in the third quarter, and missed a shoestring tackle attempt as Josh Jacobs ran in for the touchdown.
Additionally, in the fourth quarter, Barnes was whistled for an unnecessary roughness penalty, albeit controversial, with Tom Brady lamenting the call on television.
After a loud week in off-the-field headlines, LaPorta had a quiet game on the field. He went the entire first half without a target, primarily showcasing his blocking. In the third quarter, the Lions faced a lull, and Goff airmailed a swing pass to LaPorta in the flat.
It was a very quiet day for the Iowa product who was coming off his best game of the season before the bye week. That said, when LaPorta was called upon on Sunday, he answered. LaPorta was open on his first target, and made the most of his second target, catching the ball for an 18-yard gain on the game-winning drive for Motown.

The former NFL tight end shared why he went for it on fourth-down in the fourth quarter and addressed the improved play of the defense, the return of Brian Branch.
“All right. That team's been playing really good football, won three in a row, and we had our hands full. That was a good win, man. I thought our defense really showed up. Everything we talked about -- the way we needed to play this game against that high offense, getting (Packers RB Josh) Jacobs back. We had to try to eliminate or limit what those two receivers (Packers WRs Christian Watson and Matthew Golden) could do and try not to let them behind us. Then I thought our back end, it wasn't perfect, but I thought they played really good back there, man. I thought we played sticky. I thought we were challenging. Some of our guys – I thought (CB Khalil) Dorsey, man, stepped in and did some big things. There was no panic, made some big plays downfield. That's something that has hurt most teams. We talked about it, and (Packers QB Jordan) Love's got the ability to find it. Front was disruptive, you know, we talked about being disruptive, trying to play with violence and trying to make it hard. Ultimately, man, I thought our defense really, really stepped up, and they were the big story of this game. Offensively, we really played pretty good until the two turnovers, and then we had one of those drives that we messed up that was not good, man. We didn't convert on the fourth down, and then the two takeaways. Really, we had some good things going, we just couldn't finish out. And that's frustrating, but at the end of the day, (QB) Jared Goff, one more time, putting it in his hands, man, he's playing at such a high level. We have a tremendous amount of trust. He's just going to take care of the football, do the right thing, make explosive passes when they're there, get it to the right person, manage the game when we need him to manage it, push the ball when we need him to push it. He's playing at such a high level. That offensive line, I thought, protected him very well. It was a good win, you know, it was a good win. Division win number one. Finally got a couple wins here, and now we'll get ready for Minnesota.”
“Well, I thought we would get it, number one. I really believed we would get that. Number two, I knew we would get the ball back if it didn't work out. And those were the key thoughts.”

He's not even fully back yet, as far as, just the rust. He's healthy. Every time, every rep he'll take, he's going to get better and better. But it's not an easy road, especially when, -- I mean, he loves the game, man. He's highly competitive. He wants to go. Really, the hard thing was managing him in the first half. He was all over me early and I said, 'Listen, we just got to be smart, see where you're at.' And once we got into halftime, it felt like we're good here. It's a huge play. Everybody loves BB because he's a great teammate and he's a productive football player, man. He just can find the ball. He's got a nose for it. And not only that, he knocked out some of those runs. He's just a heck of a football player.”
“Are you surprised? I could have told you that was going to happen. You know Saint. Saint was ready to go. Saint was ready to go after Arizona. He had to go through a whole Bye, though. He does what he does, and he's reliable. You can count on it. You can count on the production in the run game and the pass game, and he's going to make plays, and he's going to find a way to win a one-on-one and make criticals, and he did it once again today.”
“That was big. We kind of talked about that before this game. We knew where (WR Amon-Ra St. Brown) Saint would be at, and just, Jamo, man. Let's take that next step into the electricity, man. Making some of these catches, taking off with it. That game against Green Bay a year ago, he really took off, and he was kind of like, 'Man, let's find some of these again,' where we can get the ball in his hands and let him cut it loose. He made some huge plays for us. So those two guys, that O-line protecting (Lions QB Jared) Goff, letting Goff deliver these accurate balls for our guys so they could run with it was big.”
“Kind of big spot? Those are enormous, going in and coming out. That's the hardest thing is – we're excited, I'm excited that we won that game, but you can't do that. We were fortunate. We played pretty good football and played, in some regards, some of our best football. “Well, that's our guys. Those guys aren't going to give in or go in the tank or whatever. We were able to overcome, but it takes all three units. I mean, between – everybody had a hand in it. title: Lions Injury Update Confirms Star Avoided Serious Issue
full_text:
The Detroit Lions secured a massive divisional win over the Green Bay Packers on Sunday.
Playing their first divisional opponent of the season, the Lions overcame some mistakes and were ultimately able to earn a hard-fought 20-17 victory over the Packers to advance to 4-2 on the season.
Running back Jahmyr Gibbs played a pivotal part in the victory, notchng 116 rushing yards on 29 carries. The dynamic running back played a key part on the final drive, as he converted the final third-down to cement the win.
On that game-sealing run, however, Gibbs landed awkwardly trying to slide onto the turf inbounds to keep the clock running and prevent the Packers from getting the ball back. Though the landing wasn't smooth, head coach Dan Campbell stated that he should be okay during his postgame press conference.
"We got him checked. He should be good. That's that whole, is it really worth going down?" Campbell said. "Or should he just go score? Sometimes I question that. Maybe he should've just (scored). But, all good. That's a good win."
Gibbs had slid to the turf two plays prior, on first-down, two yards short of the chains. This was done in an effort to maintain the running clock, but it nearly backfired after the Lions jumped resulting in a five-yard penalty.
However, on third-and-6, quarterback Jared Goff pitched the ball to Gibbs who burst around the left side before sliding after getting the first down. This allowed the Lions to run the clock all the way down to one second before taking a timeout to set up Jake Bates' game-winning field goal.
Campbell's update is a sigh of relief for Detroit, as Gibbs is one of the team's most dynamic talents and one of the league's best running backs. Signed to a three-year contract extension in the offseason, the Alabama product is off to another strong start through six games in 2026.
Detroit's offseason saw the team deal David Montgomery, who was Gibbs' counterpart in the backfield, to the Houston Texans and cement Gibbs as their top running back moving forward. This has come with an increased workload for him, as he has had at least 20 touches in five of the team's six games.
Up to this point, Gibbs has notched 620 rushing yards and nine total touchdowns, with seven on the ground and two as a receiver. Sunday's game against the Packers marked the first one this year where Gibbs was kept out of the end-zone.
Sports journalist who has covered the Detroit Lions the past three NFL seasons. Christian brings expert analysis, insights and an ability to fairly assess how the team is performing in a tough NFC North division.

title: Key Takeaways From Detroit Lions 20-17 Victory Against Packers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions were only able to win two of their six division games last season. With how important it is to thrive in division play, the game against the Green Bay Packers in Week 7 was another test in one of the toughest divisions in the NFL
Detroit's offense has been tasked with carrying a defense that has many question marks. One aspect of the offense that has been successful has been Jared Goff executing play-action passes.
“I think just from his standpoint, one of the things that makes him so elite in that is his process. It's uncomfortable and you don't do it a ton in college anymore where you turn your back to the defense," said Drew Petzing. "You have to take in a ton of information pre-snap, and you have to know where your eyes need to go and who you need to locate on their side of the ball and on our side of the ball. And I think that's a huge part of the action game.
"He's done it at such a high level that I think even when that happens, he's able to calibrate quickly, figure out what's going on and make the proper decision almost every time. And that's really one of the main reasons I think he's excelled in that area.”
Turnovers were a factor in this contest, as Detroit allowed Green Bay back in the game late in the second-quarter and early in the second half.
After 60 minutes of action, Detroit was able to take advantage late of multiple personal foul calls and mistakes from the Packers, advancing their record to 4-2.
Here are the takeaways from the Lions' 20-17 victory.
Detroit's offense quickly took advantage of an early error by the Packers. After winning the opening coin toss, the Lions chose to defer.
Green Bay was able to march into the red zone, but were not able to punch it in to the end zone. A delay of game penalty forced the Packers to back up five yards, which proved to be costly , as kicker Trey Smack missed an easy field goal try.
Detroit quickly marched down the field for an opening touchdown. Goff found Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams early in the game.
The speedy wideout capped off the six-play, 80-yard drive with a 16-yard touchdown reception.
It was only the second touchdown for the Lions in the first quarter this season, and the first since Jahmyr Gibbs opened the regular season with a one-yard score against the Saints in Week 1.
29 straight games for Goff with TD pass! JAMO pic.twitter.com/9oABAir9TW
The Packers quickly tied the game, with Jordan Love leading his team on a 12-play, 74-yard scoring drive to answer Detroit's opening scoring drive.
Tight end Tucker Kraft proved to be difficult to coverage, as he secured a key fourth-down reception on the Packers second drive for a gain of 22 yards.
With the Packers in the red zone, Jack Campbell fell in coverage and Kraft took advantage. Love scrambled and connected with the talented tight end on a 14-yard touchdown.
Through their first two possessions, Green Bay secured six first-downs and were 2-for-5 on third-down.
Green Bay moved deep into Detroit territory midway through the second quarter, but a huge tackle for loss by cornerback D.J. Reed forced a turnover on downs inside Detroit's red-zone. The Lions would then go on a lengthy drive and looked poised to extend their lead before the half.
Goff connected with Amon-Ra St. Brown multiple times, and the veteran passer surpassed 200 passing yards before halftime. On second-and-10 from the Green Bay 12-yard line with :30 seconds to play, however, Detroit's fortunes changed for the worse.
Jahmyr Gibbs took a handoff for a short gain, but ran into center Cade Mays at the end of his run and the ball was jarred loose. The friendly fire resulted in a fumble that was recovered by Green Bay, ending the Lions' drive and sending the game to halftime with Detroit leading 10-7.
Disaster would strike again on Detroit's first drive of the second half. Mays, who was playing in his first game with the organization after a wrist injury sent him to injured reserve in training camp, had a botched snap exchange with Goff that resulted in another Packers recovery to start the third quarter.
The second fumble would have dire consequences, as the Packers took advantage of the short field and scored on a 25-yard touchdown from Love to Josh Jacobs.
The Packers were called for a couple of penalties that assisted the Lions keep their offensive drive alive in the third-quarter.
Linebacker Brenton Cox Jr. was called for roughing the passer and cornerback Brandon Cisse.
Campbell, similar to LaFleur earlier in the game, decided to go for it on fourth-down deep in the red zone. Unfortunately, Cisse pushed Williams out of bounds in the back of the end zone, keeping the score at 17-14.
Not on Branch’s watch pic.twitter.com/ABGm4f0ZWt
In the second half, Goff narrowly avoided tossing an interception, as the Packers defenders were not able to haul in passes that could have been picked off.
Green Bay was able to tie the score at 17-17.
With the football midway through the fourth-quarter, Campbell decided to go for it again on fourth-down, but this time deep in their own territory.
The Packers defense stuffed Gibbs, forcing a turnover on downs. The Packers failed to capitalize, as Smack missed a 35-yard field goal that was blocked partially by defensive end DJ Wonnum.
1.) Rookie Keith Abney dropped a third-down interception in the end zone after a throwaway toss by Love.
2.)  Goff passed Derek Carr (41,245) for the third-most passing yards through 11-career seasons in NFL history.
3.) Lions fan Cody DeLorenzo completed a 313-mile ultramarathon run for charity from Lambeau Field in Green Bay to Ford Field in Detroit with the game ball. The organization rewarded him with two Super Bowl tickets.
4.) After the Lions took the lead in the third-quarter, Khalil Dorsey and D.J. Reed both made plays on deep shots forcing a three-and-out for the Packers.
5.) Brian Branch earned his first interception of the 2026 season to end a Packers drive early in the fourth quarter.
6.) Lions cornerback Ennis Rakestraw injured his ankle and was listed as questionable to return in the fourth quarter.
7.) The Lions drove 71 yards in 10 plays to win the game, with kicker Jake Bates knocking through a 22-yard field goal as time expired to give the Lions the win.
