title: Grading Every Texans Position Group After Week 7 Loss to Giants
full_text:
The Houston Texans are now 2-5 following the events of an embarrassing Week 7 overtime loss at home against the New York Giants , coming up short 21-27.
And in the aftermath of the Texans' defeat, it's now time to hand out our weekly grades for just how each position group on the roster performed in their last game before heading into a much-needed bye week.
Let's sort through every position on the Texans' roster and break down a letter grade on how each performed in this one.
While we've certainly seen C.J. Stroud perform a whole lot better in multiple games this season, he certainly wasn't the reason the Texans came up short in this game. The offensive woes Houston fell into within this game felt like a play-calling issue rather than anything the guy under center couldn't do.
Stroud completed 60% of his passes for 157 yards, threw for two touchdowns to Marvin Harrison Jr. and a clutch fourth-quarter score to Xavier Hutchinson, and it was another week of no turnovers for the Texans' QB1. He at least gets a passing grade.
In a game that the Texans had just two running backs on the active roster, Woody Marks became the guy leading the way with all of Houston's work in the backfield this game, logging 19 carries for 66 yards, along with one reception for 15 yards.
It does feel as if the Texans have started to build at least some momentum on the ground over the past three weeks, which comes as an interesting outcome knowing that David Montgomery has been a non-factor in each of those games due to a groin injury.
What a bizarre game for the Texans' wide receiver room; one that became so highly acclaimed heading into the week for the depth and talent they had around the position, only to not utilize those pass-catchers as a big part of their game plan.
The Texans’ leader in targets in the wide receiver room? Xavier Hutchinson with six. Hutchinson and tight end Dalton Schultz combined for more looks their way than Nico Collins, Marvin Harrison, Jaylin Noel, and Tank Dell altogether. This cannot be a recurring theme in Houston's offensive game plan. Enough said.
Dalton Schultz did manage to turn in a bit of a better performance in this game than he's been accustomed to over the past few weeks since his breakout 140-yard game in Week 2 vs. the Cincinnati Bengals . He hauled in five of six targets for 45 yards.
However, outside of Schultz, we really didn't see much from this tight end room of five contributors, leading to the same question many fans and analysts have been asking for the past several weeks: why have so many tight ends on the roster if they aren't going to be a key part of the game plan? And where's Marlin Klein?
Protection-wise, the Texans' offensive line did quite alright. They helped this run game look a bit better than we've seen over the first four weeks, and Stroud only got taken down for one sack for no loss.
But, man, the penalties in this game were, in the words of DeMeco Ryans: "ridiculous." The Texans had eight flags thrown over the course of the game, and four of them came due to the offensive line: holding, illegal formation, false start, etc. Houston is now up to over 50 penalties through seven weeks, that's set them back a total of 500 yards.
This Texans' defensive line was anything but at the level we know them capable of being this weekend. Not only did they struggle to get consistent pressure on quarterback J.J. McCarthy, who was taken down for just three sacks on the day (two of them coming from defensive backs), but the way in which they defended the run was inexcusable.
The Giants averaged a whopping 5.5 yards per rush on 34 attempts on the day. And inevitably, it would be that lack of stout run defense that would be Houston's demise , thanks to a pair of explosive carries from Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary in overtime.
Henry To'oTo'o had a solid start to this game and put together what's certainly his best performance since returning from his shoulder injury from the start of this season with 10 total tackles, two tackles for loss, and 0.5 sacks.
However, a large part of the Texans' tackling issues also have to fall upon the shoulders of this linebacker unit as well. Azeez Al-Shaair logged just two solo tackles on the day, adding onto what's been a bit of an underwhelming season on his behalf. Maybe the injuries he's suffered over the past few weeks are playing a part in that.
Derek Stingley, to his credit, did his job in this game. He allowed just two catches for 33 yards and a 62.9 passer rating on the five plays he was targets. But as for Kamari Lassiter and Tremon Smith? Not the same type of performance.
Those two combined to allow 117 yards and six receptions on eight targets, and each allowed for over a 100.0 passer rating when targeted. Malik Nabers and Malachi Fields had their way, and the Texans' secondary struggled to have an answer.
The Texans' safety unit feels like the one area of this defense that played somewhat serviceably against the Giants. M.J. Stewart led the team in combined tackles (which is indicative of how poorly Houston was able to tackle in the first and second level of the defense), but he also had 0.5 sacks and a pass deflection in his first game starting in place of an injured Reed Blankenship .
Calen Bullock wasn't able to add to his interception total after boosting his tally in last week's game vs. the Jacksonville Jaguars, chipping in for just four tackles, but a takeaway sure could've helped Houston's chances of avoiding such an ugly loss at home.

title: Texans Dealing With Key Injury in WR Room After Loss vs. Giants
full_text:
The Houston Texans got hit with a reality check in their Week 7 loss vs. the New York Giants, as they would end up falling short in an overtime defeat, 21-27 that now sinks them to a 2-5 record on the year heading into the bye.
However, it seems the Texans were also hit with a key injury in their wide receiver room in the midst of their Week 7 loss, according to head coach DeMeco Ryans .
And that injury was to none other than second-year wide receiver Jaylin Noel, who ended up leaving in the middle of Sunday's contest against the Giants before inevitably being unable to return.
Per DeMeco Ryans' post-game press conference following Houston's loss vs. the Giants, the Texans' head coach revealed that Noel had suffered a turf toe injury against New York.
"Jaylin Noel had a turf toe injury. He's still being evaluated," Ryans said on Sunday.
Obviously, there's not a ton of information that we can gather from Ryans' post-game comments when it comes to Noel's status moving forward. However, a turf toe injury––depending on the exact severity––is one that can lead to some missed time for any player in the league.
Noel finished the game against the Giants with just two receptions for a loss of three yards. According to KPRC2 's Aaron Wilson, Noel was also reportedly in a walking boot following the Texans' loss.
The good news for the Texans is that they'll be heading right into their bye week following the events of their Week 7 loss. Which means, for Noel, he'll have an extra week of rest to bank on before he'll be tasked with suiting up for Houston's next game.
However, even with that extra time off, there's a chance that Noel could be due to miss some time for the Texans moving forward–– which would undoubtably be a big loss to Houston's offense knowing how strong of a start to the season the second-year wideout has had through seven weeks.
Through the start of the Texans' season, Noel has put together a total of 19 receptions for 331 yards and two receptions, really becoming one of the team's most noteworthy playmakers in the passing game, even with the immense depth that's come to surround him in the wide receiver room.
His ability as a downfield playmaker, someone who can excel after the catch, and even as a kick returner has shown up big in his second year pro. Yet, depending on just how bad his new turf toe injury might be, there's a chance the Texans will be forced to push ahead without him for a few games moving forward.
If Noel is due to miss any time for the Texans' offense, C.J. Stroud will be forced to lean on some other playmakers in this wide receiver room that does have the depth to support a solid offense, even without the second-year talent.
Keep an eye on the obvious candidates of Nico Collins and Marvin Harrison Jr. to likely see more responsibilities in the Texans' offense in the weeks ahead.
Yet, you can also expect guys like Kayshon Boutte, Xavier Hutchinson, and Tank Dell to step up and provide the playmaking this offense could desperately utilize without one of their more potent names at the position group altogether.
We'll likely know more on Noel's long-term status a bit better once we get to next week's practice leading up to the Texans' Week 9 battle vs. the Los Angeles Chargers. However, certainly brace for the possibility that this offense could be without Noel for some stretch of time, depending on how bad the toe injury is truly deemed to be.

title: 3 Winners, 6 Losers From Texans' Deflating Week 7 Loss vs. Giants
full_text:
The Houston Texans have now dropped their fifth game in the first seven weeks of the 2026 NFL season a fter a brutal overtime loss against the New York Giants in Week 7 , 21-27.
There were a lot of blemishes of note for the Texans in this one. Players on both sides of the ball had their respective issues from start to finish in this game that ultimately led to Houston's fate looking as it did after extra time.
However, even throughout all of the chaos that the Texans faced on their home field in Reliant Stadium in Week 7, a select few names managed to shine through with a solid performance that provides a bit more optimism for their individual stock moving forward.
So as the dust is still settling from what's due to be considered one of the Texans' worst losses of this season, let's break down a set of three winners and six losers that set themselves apart from the crowd within Sunday's action.
Even in what was a pretty rough loss for the Texans' all around, you've got to give credit where it's due for the leader of Houston's run game in Woody Marks.
Marks was tasked to be the lead ball-carrier for the Texans throughout the day in a game where Houston had just two active running backs on the roster. And even after having to leave the game in the third quarter with an apparent leg injury, he managed to return and post a pretty solid stat line, all things considered.
19 rushes for 66 yards comes out to 3.5 yards per carry, and he also chipped in for a 15-yard reception in the process. He'll likely go back to splitting carries with his veteran counterpart in Montgomery after next week's bye, but for the time that he's been Houston's RB1, he's handled those expectations pretty well.
The Texans entered this game knowing that they were going to spread the ball around within their deep wide receiver room. And that's exactly what happened. All six active wide receivers on this roster managed to catch at least one ball over the course of this matchup vs. the Giants.
But in the process, the Texans found themselves essentially shutting out Collins of their game plan on that side of the ball entirely. Houston's star wideout finished the game with just two receptions for six yards; by far his lowest numbers of the season so far.
Of course, in a receiver room like the Texans have with many moving parts, there's going to be growing pains like there were in this game. Yet, coming out of the bye, Houston's can't afford repeat performances like this from Collins, knowing that he's the best talent on that side of the ball entirely.
Yes, Marvin Harrison Jr. did catch his first touchdown pass as a part of the Texans' receiver room. But that one play doesn't take away from just how limited he was over the course of the day in Houston's passing game.
That one six-yard touchdown reception was one of just four targets that Harrison Jr. was able to convert on throughout the day. After his hot start with the team just last week in London, you'd have expected those numbers to look a little bit better than they ultimately ended up being.
However, like Collins, the Texans now find themselves needing to figure out how to better include Harrison Jr. in their offensive plans after the bye. And if unsuccessful, it'll be hard for Houston's steep investment of a second-round pick to look like a wise move––especially if the losses keep on piling up.
One big bright spot for the Texans in an otherwise gloomy day in Houston: Tank Dell returned to the field for the first time in over 670 days. And in his first appearance back on the field, he turned in a pretty explosive 43-yard reception that turned out to be this offense's best play of the day––even if not exactly by design.
Dell didn't get involved much outside of that one play besides a two-yard rush in the second half. However, this day was bound to be a successful one for Dell knowing all the hard work it took to get back on the field once again since his devastating knee injury. Expect to only see more of him moving forward.
This game was another example of Texans Pro Bowl cornerback Kamari Lassiter not looking like his 2025 self, as he'd be a prime factor in what would be many explosive downfield plays from the Giants' offense over the course of the day.
Malik Nabers had his fourth-straight game with over 100 receiving yards. Malachi Fields chipped in for 88 yards on four catches. Perhaps those woes could be pinned on Houston's secondary as a whole, but there were multiple occasions in which Lassiter would simply get beat in his individual matchup, and thus let up a big chunk of play from J.J. McCarthy.
For this Texans' defense to be at its best, Lassiter's performance is a huge part of that. So far this season, he's been stuck in a bit of a third-year slump that Houston is now desperate for him to get out of.
The Texans' star edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. started off this season on about as high of a note as you could ask for. He had been a dominant force against opposing quarterbacks and offensive lines, having recorded a total of seven sacks through five games.
This showing from Anderson though would make for back-to-back games of failing to take down the opposing quarterback for a sack. His co-star on the Texans' defensive line, Danielle Hunter, took care of business for one himself, but Houston's Defensive Player of the Year candidate still left more to be desired.
In Henry To'oTo'o's second game back on the Texans' front seven from his shoulder injury that took him out for the first four weeks of the season, he made his impact felt in a multiple ways on the defensive side of the ball.
To'oTo'o became the Texans' second-leading tackler on the day (10) in a game where this defense really struggled in that department, while also recording two tackles for loss, one quarterback hit, and 0.5 sacks.
The Texans are going to need some of their key defenders around that side of the ball to step up over the next few weeks if they want to revert back closer to their 2025 selves. Thankfully, To'oTo'o held up his end of the bargain in Week 7.
No, we haven't forgotten about Texans second-round pick Marlin Klein. But it almost seems as if Houston's coaching staff has completely shut him out from their weekly plans entirely.
This would be Klein's fourth straight game of being deemed a healthy scratch on the Texans' active roster. His stat line has been stuck at his one catch for 21 yards ever since he made a nice play in the first game of Houston's season back in Week 1 against the Buffalo Bills, all because of what the team staff describes as a need to improve on special teams.
Well, the Texans' special teams can't look much worse than it does right now––at least outside of how Ka'imi Fairbairn has been performing as of late––so maybe it wouldn't hurt to give the day two pick a chance in the lineup moving forward.
While this blame for this loss could be put onto several names for the Texans, one aspect of the equation that can't go without some criticism is Houston's coaching staff––who didn't seem to have many redeeming qualities to bank on for this week in any of their three phases.
The offense looked without any dynamic ability and creativity compared to what was shown last weekend. The defense was an even worse blemish for Houston in this game, with their lack of tackling and lackluster coverage. Special teams still had their respective lapses. Penalties remained egregious, especially offensively.
And now at a 2-5 record on the year, it makes you wonder whether or not there's a change that needs to be made in some area of the Texans' personnel or coaching staff heading into the bye week.
At the very least, DeMeco Ryans needs to do some deep soul-searching of how to get this group back on track for the second half of the season. Right now, it's not looking too pretty.

title: 5 Key Quotes From Texans' DeMeco Ryans After OT Loss to Giants
full_text:
The Houston Texans dropped to 2-5 this weekend after logging a humbling overtime loss vs. the New York Giants on their home field , 21-27, that now leads this team into the bye week facing some big questions.
And after the Texans' latest loss, we were able to hear from head coach DeMeco Ryans at his post-game press conference, where he gave some candid thoughts on how he feels about his crew following the events of this contest.
Let's take a look at five key quotes from Ryans' post-game following up from Houston's overtime defeat:
The Texans' offense was far from as polished as they looked this time last week in London against the Jacksonville Jaguars. They had just 237 yards of total offense and went 3-12 on third-down.
As to why Ryans feels the offense struggled, he points to two factors: sustaining drives and converting on those third-down opportunities.
"We'll look at the film and see what happened offensively, but from my perspective, it comes down to third down," Ryans said of the Texans' offensive struggles. "You have to sustain drives and stay on the field on third down. We converted only three third downs, and that's definitely not good enough. That's not winning football."
"To beat a team like this, we knew we had to control the game. To control the game, you have to sustain drives. We didn't do that."
The Texans recorded eight penalties for 80 yards over the course of their matchup against the Giants. It's turned into a common trend for Houston to struggle when it comes to penalties this season, as they now average over eight flags per game through seven weeks.
Ryans went on to call the Texans' penalties ridiculous, and emphasized that the team has to get them fixed moving forward.
"The penalties are ridiculous. It keeps happening over and over again, so we have to find a way to fix it or get different people in so we don't make the same mistakes repeatedly."
The Texans looked extremely sloppy in pass coverage against a Giants offense that really didn't enter this game seen as the most daunting task to defend. In J.J. McCarthy's first start with New York, he finished with a solid 252 yards with over a 70% completion rate, while also not giving away a single turnover.
Between missed tackles, botched coverages, and explosive plays, the Texans' defense was far from the elite level we know they can be. DeMeco Ryans addressed those struggles in pass coverage after the game.
"When I look at the passing game, somebody has made an error somewhere in the coverage if a guy is wide open," Ryans said. "We don't design coverages for guys to be wide open. We have to be better with the details of what we're doing and make sure our eyes are focused on our assignments."
On a more positive note, the Texans were finally able to see Tank Dell back on the field for an NFL game for the first time in over 670 days. He finished the game with one big explosive catch-and-run for 43 yards.
Ryans called the return of Dell both "electric" and "fun to watch," while also hinting that the Texans will continue to increase his workload in the weeks to come.
"It was very electric seeing Tank come out of the tunnel. It was an awesome moment. You felt the energy from our crowd and the emotions running high as he ran out of the tunnel for the first time in two years.
Then he created an explosive pass play for us. It was fun to watch. I'm proud of Tank and all the work he's put in. I'm happy he was able to contribute and get some plays out there today. This is just a start for him. We expect to continue increasing his workload and see him do more for us and create more explosive plays."
The Texans, who now sit three games under .500, enter their Week 8 bye with a lot on their plate to fix. DeMeco Ryans knows that.
Ryan’s did note after the game that he's "not there yet" when it comes to making big personnel or staff changes. However, he did emphasize what the Texans do need to accomplish moving forward to turn the ship around in the right direction.
"We keep playing and practicing well. We keep putting in the work. At the end of the day, football comes down to blocking and tackling and running the football," Ryans said. "The fundamentals of the game don't change."
"We have to block better, stop holding and stop hurting ourselves with penalties. We have to protect better. We have to be able to beat man coverage and cover in man coverage. We have to tackle."
"There's no magical elixir that's going to drop out of the sky and fix everything. We fix it by putting in the work and getting better at the fundamentals of football. We have to own it as coaches and players, and we have to find a way to turn this thing around."

title: 3 Texans Takeaways From Egregious Overtime Loss vs. Giants
full_text:
The Houston Texans put together what could be their worst loss of the 2026 season yet in their Week 7 defeat at home against the New York Giants, with a final score of 27-21.
After the Texans pieced together a late fourth quarter comeback to force overtime behind a strong drive from Woody Marks and the offense , it wouldn't take long for Houston to drop the ball with extra time to now fall down to their fifth loss in seven weeks.
The Texans now sit at 2-5, look extremely disorganized in all three phases of the game, and have a real interesting bye week ahead to try and fix the plenty of woes that faced them throughout the day against New York.
But before even thinking of turning the page past this week, let's break down three of the biggest takeaways from the Texans' latest loss against the Giants:
Turn the clock back to the start of this season. Many who had seen how dominant this Texans defense was capable of being over the course of their 2025 campaign had expected them to be even better than they were previously, to the point that they were seen as among the best collective units in the NFL.
Now, seven weeks deep into the 2026 season, and this defense could have a real case of being among the bottom ten units in the league. Especially after this performance, we might've just been witnesses to some of their worst results of the year thus far.
Multiple blown coverages, explosive plays downfield, a ton of missed tackles, and a Giants run game that caught fire late in overtime all contributed to the calamity that resulted here on Houston's home field. In all, the Texans allowed over 400 yards throughout the day and came out to 6.5 yards per play from New York's attack.
Do the Texans decide to shift their personnel around? Maybe pivot back to Matt Burke as their defensive play-caller ? Whatever the answer might be, Houston is almost forced to make a big change on this side of the ball moving forward, knowing how talented this unit can be, but also factoring in the brutal results that have led to five losses in seven weeks of action.
Stop me if you've heard this before: the Texans struggled immensely with penalties throughout the day.
The Texans finished their overtime outing against New York racking up a total of 10 penalties for 80 yards. Five of those flags came from the offensive side of the ball for offensive holding, and really held back this scoring attack––whether it be because they set back the drive, or simply by negating a big play to gain some yards.
The Texans are now up to a total of 58 penalties for 508 yards called against them through seven weeks. That's an average of over eight calls against them for 72 yards per game.
It's pretty easy to tell that such a formula is far from a winning recipe. Those flags and undisciplined play have been a consistent issue for this Texans roster all season long, and turned out to be a major difference in this game en route to an embarrassing loss at home.
The Texans are now 2-5 heading into their Week 8 bye. The past two weeks of wins against divisional opponents had offered some optimism that things were turning around in the right direction for the second half of the season.
But now, it's extremely tough to have that same confidence in this team after the events of this loss.
The offensive side of the ball looked stagnant and lacked any true identity. The defense lost any identity that they had previously built up through all of last season, losing their ability to cover, tackle, and generate any immense number of turnovers. This team still has failed to win a game at home.
The Texans couldn't have asked for their bye week to hit at a better time. Of course, the Texans have proven from the events of last season that a mid-season turnaround could be well within the cards. It was when Houston was at a 3-5 record when they went on to win nine straight games to end the year out.
Yet at the same time, these first seven games of the season have seemed to prove that this Texans team is anything but the same group as last year. DeMeco Ryans needs to stay busy in the lab throughout the next week off to figure out how to fix this group to forge together a similar run, but it remains to be seen if that same fate even possible at this point.

title: Texans vs. Giants Inactives: Full List of Players Ruled Out for Week 7
full_text:
The Houston Texans and New York Giants have officially released their inactives lists leading up to kickoff for their Week 7 contest.
And for both sides, there's some key absences that are worth noting.
Let's take a look at the inactives list for both the Texans and Giants for this week, and break down who's due to be in and out of Sunday's action.
S Jalen Pitre S Reed Blankenship RB David Montgomery OL Blake Fisher OL Febechi Nwaiwu OL Nate Thomas TE Marlin Klein
The Texans will be dealing with a few injury concerns in the form of a few starters being inactive for this Sunday; three to be specific.
The most notable of the Texans' absences will be none other than their versatile nickel defender Jalen Pitre , who's due to miss a second-straight week with the shoulder injury he suffered back in Week 5.
Given that Pitre's status was deemed week-to-week upon the announcement of his injury, there's some optimism that he'll be ready to get thrown back into the lineup in time for Week 9 after next week's bye. However, Houston will have to make some key changes to their defense without him in the meantime.
The Texans will also be without another starter in their secondary as Reed Blankenship sits in concussion protocol. Blankenship was also listed to have a hand injury throughout this week in practice, so he'll be getting the day off for this game against New York.
Then, the Texans will also be down their starting running back, David Montgomery, who, like Pitre, will be missing a second straight week after first going down in Week 5 with a groin injury . You can expect Woody Marks to take a large share of the workload in the backfield this Sunday, especially knowing that Houston only has two running backs on their active roster.
Of the names that will be active who are due for some attention, two players on the Texans' end stick out.
Of course, wide receiver Tank Dell is the big story here as he'll officially be taking the field for an NFL gamr for the first time in over 670 days . But also, offensive tackle Braden Smith will finally be making his debut for Houston after missing his first four games of the season on injured reserve, and has been out of the mix for the past two weeks.
Now, with Blake Fisher ruled out for his first game of the season, it allows for Smith to get his first opportunity of the year, likely in a similar role as Fisher, being a jumbo tight end/sixth offensive lineman in certain personnel.
OL Josh Sills TE Theo Johnson OL Marcus Mbow CB Greg Newsome II CB Nikko Reed S Jevon Holland QB Jake Haener
The Giants will be down a select few names on their side of the equation as well. And two of the biggest absences that New York will be facing remain in their secondary.
Not only will Giants starting safety Jevon Holland be missing this game, but so will cornerback Greg Newsome, who each remain in concussion protocol for this one, and will leave New York's secondary a bit more depleted than usual.
For the Texans' offense that's just been finding some consistency through the air by the command of quarterback C.J. Stroud, that could set up for a much easier day on that side of the ball.
Kickoff between the Texans and Giants lands at 12 p.m. MT in Reliant Stadium, where Houston will have a golden opportunity to claim their third straight win right before hitting their mid-season break.

title: Why Derek Stingley Will Be Texans' Most Important Player vs. Giants
full_text:
The Houston Texans' Week 7 date vs. the New York Giants is right around the corner.
And for the Texans, it's a massive matchup for them to take advantage of. They enter the game as favorites of more than a touchdown , are looking to win their third straight game, while also heading into their Week 8 bye on a bit of a high note.
However, even while the Texans enter this one with the upper hand in terms of talent on paper, that doesn't mean this game is going to be easy–– especially against a talent like Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers . A standout game on his behalf could quickly make this game a bit more interesting to watch unfold.
And that's why, for the Texans, All-Pro cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. might be their most important player on the field this Sunday.
Throughout most of this season, Stingley hasn't exactly looked like the All-Pro talent he was over the course of last season. And really, that disappointing start could be said about a vast majorty of the Texans' output in the secondary.
For Stingley, he's allowed his highest passer rating when targeted throughout his career (87.3), while also failing to haul in a single interception through his first six games.
A large part of those lapses can be attributed to Houston's increased use of zone coverage. Stingley has played zone on 76.6% of his coverage snaps, up from 63.3% in 2025, and he's allowed 146 yards in those coverages–– already 41 more than he allowed throughout the course of 2025 (107).
This week though, the Texans could be preparing to decrease that usage of zone that's taken a hit to their secondary's production.
Their starting safety, Reed Blankenship––known to be a better fit in zone coverages–– has been ruled out with a concussion/hand injury . Houston will likely start M.J. Stewart next to Calen Bullock and hope to spark some similar success within this pass defense as was seen through 2025.
And that adjustment comes at a perfect time, because the Texans will be up against one of their more challenging matchups at wide receiver in Malik Nabers; someone who's seen 35 total targets over the past two games he's played in en route to hauling in over 23 receptions, 286 yards, and a touchdown.
The Texans can't afford to let Nabers have another explosive day against their defense. Nabers will be the centerpiece of the New York offense–– especially for a scoring attack led by J.J. McCarthy in his first start–– and any strong performance on his behalf will likely allow the Giants to stay within striking distance of an upset on the road.
So that's why Stingley Jr. needs to have a statement game here. Odds are, he's going to see a lot of Nabers over the course of this Sunday. We've seen just how badly an elite receiver can have their way against this Texans defense this season ( look back at CeeDee Lamb's stat line from Week 4 ), and a repeat performance here certainly wouldn't be ideal.
Not only would shutting down Nabers boost his individual stock after an up-and-down start to the season, but the Giants' ability to put points on the board takes a significant hit if their No. 1 target is completely shut out by one of the league's best cornerbacks.
Without Nabers making a huge impact, the playmaking for the Giants' offense comes down to the likes of Isaiah Likely, Malachi Fields, Darnell Mooney, and their currently dysfunctional running game committee.
That's a much easier assignment for the Texans to handle, and only becomes possible if Stingley holds up his end of the bargain for a standout day covering one of the league's best receivers on the other end.
