title: What's Going on With Hyped Chargers OL Reinforcement Branson Taylor?
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers offensive line is once again a problem for the team, seemingly being the curse of the entire franchise. In 2026, the team is 0-6 and the season is likely over, but the one thing the fans want to see is Justin Herbert return to form and be protected.
Herbert having protection and playing well gets rid of the funk that has been his play this season. Trade rumors, retirements, etc ., all dominating the season's conversation need to end and the only way to do that is to get the team's superstar QB some help.
That was expected to happen a few weeks ago, with Branson Taylor, the Chargers' 2025 sixth-round draft choice, returning from injury.
Taylor, a former sixth-round pick, spent the majority of his rookie season on the practice squad. This was due to Taylor being obviously completely overmatched against NFL talent during his debut preseason and not earning a spot on the active 53-man roster.
His only action for the year was his lone start in Week 18, against the Denver Broncos. The Chargers had no reason to play their starters, giving Taylor the opportunity to show he had grown throughout his rookie season. While there was some good, there was a lot of bad. His future with the team seemed close to over.
Year 2 for Taylor had him return and completely turn himself and likely his career around . All offseason, the coaching staff were 'wowed' by his turnaround, giving him a real chance to start at guard for the team. While he was beat out by the veteran Kayode Awosika , going from cut candidate to a contending starter is a massive win for the young offensive lineman.
Chargers HC Jim Harbaugh on LG Branson Taylor: "It's been an incredible offseason...It's carried into training camp." "The reports coming back from Ben Herbert and staff were, 'Branson, wow'."
When the 2026 NFL season finally started, Taylor was placed on injured reserve, serving as a major halt to his momentum toward playing time. The Bolts have once again seen plenty of offensive line injuries and are looking for anyone who can play real NFL snaps.
Taylor was designated (21-day window activated) to return on Oct. 5. Since then, Taylor has yet to see a single snap and has been a complete afterthought on the Chargers' offensive line. The team has seemingly rolled with their two rookie sixth-round draft choices, Alex Harkey and Logan Taylor , even with both of them playing behind B. Taylor in the preseason.
Chargers HC Jim Harbaugh announces they are opening the return windows for LG Branson Taylor and TE Scott Matlock. Not yet for LB Denzel Perryman
To wrap up, you had a second-year pro earn his right to contend for a starting spot, with injuries halting his ability to play early in the year. However, upon returning, he should still be a first-off-the-bench sort of interior lineman. Instead, when injuries began to mount for the team, B. Taylor found himself still on the bench and not playing.
It could be one of two things. The Chargers see the writing on the wall for the season and want to see their rookies get playing time, holding out hope for one of them to make a name for themselves with positive momentum heading into 2027. Or, it can be that B. Taylor is not healthy yet and was activated too early.
If Taylor was activated too early, what does that say about the Chargers' front office? Were they so desperate for OL talent after having 100 million in cap space that they jumped the gun on B. Taylor's return?
The likely outcome of this entire situation, now that starter Awosika is back, is that B. Taylor returns to the bench and becomes buried on the depth chart, as he has not played any snaps this season compared to the 100+ snaps played by L. Taylor and Harkey. A weird ending to what seemed like a fun redemption arc by a former sixth-round pick.

title: Chargers Get Their First Win of the Season...On Their Bye Week
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-6, losing six straight to start the 2026 NFL season, the same season when the team was truly expected to contend for a Super Bowl. Pretty much nothing positive has happened for the squad since Sept. 13, the day the team started playing football in the regular season.
With the team continuing to lose, fans have had no choice but to look for other avenues to be happy or excited about their football team. Whether it is trading for or trading someone away , switching coaching staffs , etc., fans are looking for anything to change what is not working.
The biggest avenue is the NFL Draft, the place where all 32 teams come out of the three-day marathon feeling victorious and excited for what is to come in the ensuing NFL season. As Chargers fans, the draft excitement has come early, with the majority of us paying close attention to where the team is slotted to select in the upcoming highly touted 2027 NFL Draft.
Since the losses began, the Chargers have always placed in the top five of the estimated draft order, but never No 1. Having the first overall selection in the draft gives the team much flexibility, enough so to complete a rebuild of the roster in just one NFL Draft.
During the team's bye week, the Chargers were unable to achieve another loss to help their draft status, but instead were able to see their tanking competitor, the Miami Dolphins, win a game over the New York Jets, allowing for the Bolts to be the only winless team in the NFL and achieve the coveted #1 overall draft choice.
With this unfolding, the Bolts can either take a look at what is touted to be a generational prospect, Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, and select him to be the weapon that Justin Herbert deserves, or the team could upset the fans further by trading back and gathering a lion's share of draft capital.
Trading back is usually a great way to rebuild the roster, but passing on someone like Smith is also a great way to anger your fanbase. Either way, the team is now in the driver's seat to rebuild their roster with the maximum amount of capital, giving fans something to be excited about heading into the 2027 NFL season. Thank you, Miami Dolphins.

title: NFL Trade Rumors Hint Chargers Getting Calls, But Making Perplexing Decisions
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers don’t really have a bye week if we consider the extensive work they need to put into fixing an 0-6 team. Keep in mind the bye is a key time to watch NFL trade deadline factors around the NFL, too.
Jim Harbaugh and the Chargers could, after all, attempt to lure the Dallas Cowboys into a Khalil Mack trade . Jerry Jones loves his splashes and the Chargers need all the future-minded assets they can get.
Despite sitting as one of the more obvious sellers in the entire NFL ahead of the trade deadline, though, the vibes coming out of Los Angeles don’t suggest as much. In fact, the lack of inaction on the coaching staff, especially with Mike McDaniel’s offense, suggests more of the same in all facets.
A shame, considering NFL trade rumors say the Chargers are getting plenty of calls.
Rest assured the NFL sees what’s happening to the Chargers and plenty of teams are picking up the phone.
According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler , the Chargers continue to receive calls, but are also “still giving the impression they are standing pat.”
It hardly stops there, either.
According to ESPN’s Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter , Khalil Mack is a guy drawing interest, but the Chargers “have given no indication that they are willing to make any trades at this time” and they “insist they are trying to win games.”
As Chargers fans have seen though, insisting they're trying to win is quite a bit different than actually, you know, winning games.
The reality? The Chargers are right to publicly suggest they’re still trying to win and won’t sell. They need some sort of leverage in trade talks, no matter how flimsy it might be.
It’s not like the Chargers don’t have appealing pieces. Mack is a Hall of Famer in the making who can go help a contender. And the Chargers should probably do right by him. They also have cornerbacks like Donte Jackson who might interest contenders.
We’re talking minimal return on trades here, but something is better than nothing. Better to have a bunch of assets and cap space before potentially blowing up the coaching staff than what they have now.
There’s another small wrinkle that is unfortunate, yet true: Trading Mack and others helps the draft outlook. The Chargers won’t outright tank. But sending away some productive players boosts the chances they finish with the No. 1 overall pick.
Some won’t want to hear that, but it’s simply where the Chargers are right now. There are layers to the trade deadline situation here, and right now, publicly denying they’re going to sell doesn’t mean much. It’s a must.

title: Could Chargers Lure Cowboys, Jerry Jones Into a Khalil Mack Trade?
full_text:
For the Los Angeles Chargers , one name that could make sense in a potential trade conversation is Khalil Mack. While the idea of moving a veteran pass rusher within the season would come with plenty of complications, the Dallas Cowboys could be an intriguing trade partner if Jerry Jones is willing to listen.
The Cowboys have lost a major piece of their defensive identity with Micah Parsons no longer in the picture, losing him over a season ago. And nobody has quite stepped it up yet.
Mack may not be the long-term answer, but he could give them a proven veteran who knows how to disrupt opposing quarterbacks.
For the winless Chargers, the question is whether the return would be worth sacrificing one of their most experienced defenders.
Jerry Jones has never been a general manager who shies away from making headlines, and a potential deal for Mack would certainly attract attention. Even at this stage of his career, Mack brings qualities that extend beyond his sack totals. His ability to set the edge, recognize blocking schemes and force quarterbacks away from their preferred throwing lanes can make a difference throughout an entire game. He also has experience playing in high-pressure situations, something that could benefit a Cowboys defense trying to establish its identity without an elite player similar to Parsons.
There is also the appeal of acquiring a player who would not need an extensive adjustment period to understand his responsibilities. Mack has spent years competing against some of the league’s best offensive tackles and quarterbacks. For a team trying to improve during the season, that experience matters.
Of course, they would have to determine whether the potential upgrade justifies the compensation required to acquire him. The Cowboys could pursue younger edge rushers or look for a more affordable option, but those alternatives do not necessarily provide the same immediate impact. The Chargers would also have to be willing to negotiate. Mack remains a valuable part of their defensive rotation, and the Bolts cannot afford to weaken its own pass rush simply because another team has a more obvious need.
From the Chargers perspective, trading Mack would be a difficult decision, particularly if the team believes it can compete deep into January. A defense built around generating pressure needs reliable players who can win their matchups. Mack’s presence gives another weapon when the team needs a crucial stop.
However, the situation changes if the Bolts believe they can receive meaningful draft compensation or address another roster weakness through a deal. Every potential trade comes down to opportunity cost. Keeping Mack preserves a proven contributor, while moving him could create resources to strengthen the roster elsewhere.
Still, they should not move him simply to make a deal happen. A midseason trade needs to improve the team’s outlook, not just create an interesting headline.
Whether Jerry Jones would be willing to pay the price is another question entirely. The Chargers have little reason to give away a player who can still contribute to their defensive ambitions. A Mack trade is far from guaranteed, but the football logic is there. If they want an experienced pass rusher and Joe Hortiz receives an offer they cannot ignore, this is a conversation that could become more interesting as the deadline approaches.

title: Chargers Bye Week Rooting Guide: Tracking NFL Trade Deadline Factors to Know
full_text:
For the Los Angeles Chargers , the bye week isn’t about looking at the AFC West anymore.
Now, it’s all about the NFL trade deadline .
Were this a normal year for the Chargers, the bye-week advice would be to track the AFC West. But the Kansas City Chiefs (5-0), Denver Broncos (4-2) and even the Las Vegas Raiders (3-3), like 99 percent of the NFL, have fully distanced themselves from the 0-6 Chargers.
Given this torrid state of things for Jim Harbaugh’s club, the attention during the bye week turns to the idea of both buying and selling at the NFL trade deadline .
Don’t scoff too hard at the idea of the Chargers buying at the NFL trade deadline. They’re stubborn . They haven’t fired Mike McDaniel or changed  anything, really, implying that they think more of the same will be a good thing, perhaps even far into 2027.
To that end, maybe they look to buy long-term talent capable of helping them not necessarily this year, but years down the line while easing off free agency and draft needs.
The Jacksonville Jaguars are also on bye, but keep them in the back of the mind because of a trade candidate like former first-round wideout Brian Thomas Jr.
Look at the Indianapolis Colts vs. Minnesota Vikings too. If the Colts keep losing in the aftermath of firing a general manager, someone like guard Quenton Nelson could become available. Keenan Allen is still there too, for whatever that’s worth.
There’s also the Cleveland Browns vs. Tennessee Titans to watch. The Browns are 4-2, but losing to the terrible Titans could change how they approach the deadline. Someone like Jerry Jeudy has been labeled a trade candidate. Everyone on the Titans could be for sale.
Then there’s the Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals . After already trading Marvin Harrison Jr., a fall to 2-5 could mean the Cardinals cough up names like pass-rusher Josh Sweat.
The Chicago Bears already won on Thursday night and the popular idea, which is also understandable, is the Chargers shipping Mack back there to give him a chance at a title.
The Dallas Cowboys aren’t really a contender at 2-4 and play Monday night, but keep them in the back of the mind because Jerry Jones loves his splashy moves.
Locally, the 2-4 Los Angeles Rams fancy themselves contenders and like to burn the future of the present, so if they beat the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, they become a possible Mack trading spot.
And while the New York Giants look so-so before a game against the Houston Texans, there’s always an outside chance the Harbaugh brothers link up for a trade.
Generally speaking, any team with a chance of the playoffs is worth watching for injuries, too. It’s not just Mack: The Chargers have excess talent at spots like cornerback they could also trade away, even if it’s minimal draft pick return. Teams desperate to stay in the hunt at the deadline tend to look toward the bottom of the standings first for obvious reasons, and well, the Chargers are right there.

title: Rams Remain Noncommittal on Myles Garrett's Return to Practice Ahead of Week 8
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams remain hopeful that edge rusher Myles Garrett will return to practice sooner rather than later . As the Rams prepare for their Week 8 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers, Garrett is nearing a potential return. While the Rams haven’t established an official timeline, outside reports have consistently pointed to a six-week recovery.
After missing the Rams’ game against the Las Vegas Raiders, Garrett has officially missed six games and is now just over six weeks removed from knee surgery. A six-week timeline was always seen as a worst-case scenario for Garrett, and he has now reached that point. Still, McVay remained mum on Garrett’s potential return to practice this week.
“I'm not sure yet. I have not decided on those things,” McVay said. “Once I get with Reggie and talk about the approach for the week. Then I will follow their guidance based on where he's at and how he's feeling.”
Late last week , NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport reported that Garrett was likely to return to practice this week and could play in Week 8. McVay even said on Friday that Garrett returning to practice next week was a possibility, but that he’d wait to talk to Garrett and the team’s training staff to come to a decision.
It’s no real surprise that the Rams remain coy on Garrett’s injury, as that’s how they’ve handled it since the beginning . Garrett was initially held out of practice late in training camp due to knee swelling. While he played in Week 1, Garrett didn’t feel like himself and was placed on injured reserve the following week.
Before Garrett returns, the Rams will want to be sure that he is fully healthy and ready to practice. They’ve waited this long and will want to ensure that Garrett is at 100 percent when he gets back on the field.
McVay is scheduled to speak to the media again on Wednesday. At that time, McVay may have more information about Garrett’s status. If Garrett isn’t practicing by Thursday, it seems unlikely that he’ll return this week. When the Rams designated Keagen Trost to return from injured reserve, they opened his 21-day window on the Thursday before the game.
If Garrett does return to practice and ends up playing this week, it would provide a huge boost to the defense. While the defense has played well, it has struggled to generate consistent pressure on opposing quarterbacks. The Rams rank 27th in sack rate this season.
With Garrett now more than six weeks removed from surgery, the focus shifts to when he will be cleared to practice and how quickly he can get back on the field. At 3-4, the Rams are entering an important stretch of their season and could certainly use Garrett back in the lineup as they look to build on their win against the Raiders.

title: Rams Week 7 Snap Counts: Blake Corum's Rise Changes Running Back Outlook
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams had to manage several injuries on Sunday against the Raiders , which meant increased roles for a handful of players. Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell were asked to step up in place of Adams at wide receiver. Ty Hamilton made his presence felt without Kobie Turner. However, one of the bigger developments of the week was how the Rams rotated at running back. Blake Corum took a significantly larger share of the offensive snaps, raising questions about Kyren Williams’ role moving forward.
The big story out of Week 7 for the Rams was the increased usage of running back Blake Corum . That was the third-highest snap share of his career and the second-highest this season. Corum saw 45.2 percent of the offensive snaps back in Week 2. That was also the last time that Corum had more than 10 carries in a game.
Corum had 17 carries to Kyren Williams’ 16. However, prior to the final drive, Corum actually had 17 carries to Williams’ 11. The Rams had a very balanced rushing attack and found ways to get both players involved. We’ll have to see if the Rams can keep that type of usage between the two players moving forward.
Heading into Sunday’s game against the Raiders, there were major questions about who would step up in place of Davante Adams. The answer was simply nobody . Konata Mumpfield had one catch for 15 yards and played 43 percent of the snaps on offense. Behind him was Tutu Atwell, who played 35 percent of the snaps and wasn’t targeted once.
The Rams increased their usage of 13 personnel, lining up with three tight ends on 52.3 percent of their offensive snaps. Throughout the game, the Rams rotated Mumpfield and Atwell while Jordan Whittington was very clearly behind them. With the trade deadline coming up, the Rams need to seriously consider trading for a wide receiver.
Without Kobie Turner, the Rams needed to figure out how to replace him defensively. It wasn’t just one player. The Rams have depth on the defensive line, and they took advantage of it by increasing several players' roles. Aaron Donald saw 73.5 percent of the defensive snaps, which was his highest for the season. Tyler Davis saw more than 40 percent of the defensive snaps for the first time this year.
Ty Hamilton and Larrell Murchison also saw slight increases in their roles. The Rams will hope to get Turner back in a few weeks. The Raiders struggled along the interior of their offensive line, and the Rams will face tougher tests going forward. However, Sunday was still a positive for what that group can do in Turner’s absence.

title: Rams Player Grades: Running Game Leads the Way in Week 7 Win Over Raiders
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams got one of their most complete wins of the season , defeating the Las Vegas Raiders, 35-21. It was a team effort led by the running game and a strong defensive performance. Here are this week’s position grades based on their performance against the Raiders.
Matthew Stafford was very efficient against the Raiders . He didn’t need to do anything special and played within the offense. That’s exactly what was needed from him on Sunday. Stafford had a passing success rate of 63.3 percent, which led the NFL in Week 7. While the Rams’ quarterback still isn’t pushing the ball down the field, he finished with three touchdowns and became the franchise leader in touchdown passes.
The engine of the Rams’ offense on Sunday against the Raiders was the running game . They rushed 33 times for 192 yards and had a touchdown. Blake Corum and Kyren Williams became the first Rams running back duo since Marshall Faulk and Trung Candidate in 2001 to each have 90 rushing yards in the same game. Williams did have a fumble, which continues to be an issue. However, outside of the fumble, Williams and Corum were fantastic.
There continues to be a significant drop-off at wide receiver behind Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. With Adams out, Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell rotated as the second wide receiver. Mumpfield had one catch for 15 yards while Atwell had nothing. If the Rams make a trade at the deadline, it needs to be for a wide receiver.
With the Rams missing Adams, they leaned on the tight ends in the passing game. Colby Parkinson, Davis Allen, and Tyler Higbee combined for 12 receptions. Parkinson did have a pass go off of his hands that resulted in an interception. However, Allen had two touchdowns in the red zone.
The offensive line was very good against the Raiders. The success that Corum and Williams had in the running game was a testament to the offensive line winning in the trenches . Stafford was also kept clean. With Alaric Jackson back in the lineup, the offensive line played much closer to what we’re accustomed to seeing from that group.
Without Kobie Turner, the defensive line played well. While Kirk Cousins had time, the Rams still sacked him twice.Ty Hamilton had one of the best games of his career and made his presence felt against the run. The Rams had a 26.7 percent stuff rate on defense, which was the fourth-highest in the NFL. Aaron Donald still doesn’t have a sack, but his pressure on the two-point conversion led to a bad throw. This group stepped up despite being short-handed.
Despite not having Nate Landman, the Rams’ linebackers had their best game of the season. Omar Speights was great in a full-time role, and Shaun Dolac filled in nicely. Speights did have two missed tackles, but also had two tackles for loss. Dolac was almost perfect alongside Speights and there’s an argument that he deserves a more extended look.
Jaylen Watson allowed two catches on 10 targets and has settled in nicely in the Rams’ defense. If he can stay healthy, Watson and McDuffie are a great cornerback duo. It’s going to be very difficult to throw against this Rams team. Josh Wallace filled in nicely again, and Emmanuel Forbes had a key pass breakup on fourth down. Where the Rams have struggled is at safety and with their tackling angles. Jaylen McCollough was credited with three missed tackles on Sunday.
Brandon McManus made his debut for the Rams on Sunday, but wasn’t tested. He went a perfect 5-for-5 on extra points. The Rams also recovered a crucial onside kick to put the game away. However, the kickoff coverage unit remains a liability. Each of the first two kickoff returns went over 35 yards. It’s simply not good enough.

title: 10 Takeaways From Rams' Win Over Raiders: Blake Corum Sparks a Much-Needed Victory
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams beat the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, 35-21, to improve to 3-4 on the season. It was the type of win that the Rams needed after a disappointing loss last week. They seemed to find their identity, leading to a complete team win. There’s a lot to talk about after that one. Let’s jump into this week’s 10 takeaways.
The Rams continue having slow starts on offense. To start the game, the Rams went three-and-out after three consecutive passes. While they scored on their next four drives, the Rams haven’t scored an opening drive touchdown all season. The Rams also came out flat in the second half. Instead of extending the lead and picking up where they left off, the Rams again went three-and-out. The Rams should be able to find success with their scripted plays at the beginning of each half. They need to find a way to start faster in games.
It wouldn’t be a Rams football game if we didn’t talk about special teams. The Rams didn’t have any back-breaking mistakes, but the win can’t hide the mistakes that did happen. On the opening kickoff, the Rams allowed a 36-yard return. The next return went for 42 yards. Later in the game, the Rams touched a kickoff that should have been a touchback and got the ball at the 20 instead of the 35. The Raiders also had a successful fake punt. In games with tight margins, these are mistakes that matter. Those mistakes didn’t come back to hurt the Rams on Sunday, but there is still room for improvement.
Two of the Rams’ best games running the ball this season have been games in which Blake Corum was used consistently alongside Kyren Williams. The answer to the Rams’ running game isn’t one or the other. McVay needs to find ways to get both players into a rhythm. They combined for 33 carries for 192 yards against the Raiders. Corum led the Rams’ first touchdown drive and then had two touchdowns called back because of penalties. Williams might be the engine, but Corum is the spark. He continues to provide the explosive plays that the Rams’ run game needs. Williams and Corum also became the first Rams' running back duo to have 90 or more yards in the same game since Marshall Faulk and Trung Candidate in 2001.
Kyren Williams and Blake Corum's rushing charts shows exactly why they work well together. A lot more green/consistency from Williams, but Corum brings big-play ability. The answer to a dominant Rams' run game is using both in a 50-50 split. pic.twitter.com/TFVhtWlDac
Coming into the game, Matthew Stafford led the NFL in passing attempts. While the Rams built an early double-digit lead, McVay also committed to the run earlier in the game, which opened things up in the passing game. The presence of the run game allowed the Rams to get to their play-action passing game and get the tight ends involved underneath with misdirection. This shouldn’t be the expected game script every week, but it shows how much a consistent, balanced offensive approach makes everything easier.
For much of the season, Matthew Stafford hasn’t been great. He’s been good in moments, but he’s lacked some consistency. Against the Raiders, Stafford was efficient and simply took what was available. In the first half, he went 17-for-19 for 148 yards and had three touchdowns. With his third touchdown, Stafford became the Rams’ all-time leader in passing touchdowns, surpassing Roman Gabriel. The game may have been different during Gabriel’s era, but Stafford still accomplished the feat in nearly half the time. This is the Stafford that the Rams need more consistently. The big games against the Bills are nice, but if Stafford can simply keep the offense on track, it will put the offense in a better spot going forward.
For as good as the offense was against the Raiders, the passing game still feels one-dimensional and constricted. Stafford averaged 4.9 air yards per attempt. It’s the second consecutive week he’s averaged fewer than five air yards per attempt. Prior to that, he hadn’t done so in 23 consecutive games. The Rams need a player who can stretch the field and create explosives in the passing game.
This wasn’t the Raiders offense of old that the Rams were going up against. Coming into the game, the Raiders ranked fifth in EPA per pass and sixth in passing success rate. At one point, the Rams were holding them to -0.96 EPA per pass and a zero percent success rate. The defense held the Raiders to 5-for-19 on conversion downs. They also got a stop on a two-point conversion to keep it a two-score game in the fourth quarter. The defense was dominant in the first half and did enough to close it out late in the game.
For much of the season, the Rams haven’t had an identity that they could fall back on. Some of that had to do with injuries, but they weren't the only reason. Against the Raiders, the Rams got back to the team they wanted to be coming into the year. They had a dynamic rushing attack that operated out of 13 personnel and leaned on the play-action passing game. When the Rams' offense went quiet for the entire third quarter, they were able to lean on their rushing attack to put the game away late. This is what the Rams need to lean on going forward.
While the Rams were impressive in Week 2, Jaxson Dart got injured early in that game. The Raiders may have been on a three-game losing streak, but two of those losses were by three points to the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills. Had the Rams played like they did last week, they likely would have lost. It may have gotten tense at the beginning of the fourth quarter, but this was a complete team win. The Rams played good, complementary football and now have a win that they can build on.
This was a turning point in the Rams’ season. There is still a lot of work to do and the Rams need to show that they can stack wins. However, they found an identity on offense that they can lean on and got a win against a solid team when they needed it. After last week, the Rams needed a win they could feel good about, and the way they beat the Raiders provided exactly that. It’s hard not to overreact to one win, but this was a step in the right direction. When we look back at the Rams’ season in two months, it’s possible this win is seen as where things began to change.

title: Monday Morning Rambling: Rams Rediscover Winning Formula Against Raiders
full_text:
Following last week’s loss to the Arizona Cardinals, the Los Angeles Rams had officially hit rock bottom as they dropped to 2-4. While a 2-5 start once seemed impossible for a Sean McVay-led football team, it was hard to have confidence in anything this Rams team did or predict what they’d look like on a weekly basis. After beating the Las Vegas Raiders, 35-21 on Sunday, the Rams may have finally figured out what kind of team they want to be .
Coming into the season, one of the main talking points was how the Rams were going to lean into the 13 personnel that they had so much success with in 2025. With two running backs, the Rams were going to more evenly split their carries to give the running game a consistently fresh feel to it.
However, through the first six weeks of the season, no quarterback threw more passes than Matthew Stafford. Prior to Sunday’s game against the Raiders, Kyren Williams had 80 rushing attempts to Blake Corum’s 47.
There was certainly some context for why the Rams were so pass-heavy, but the offense still needed to get back to the basics and take a more balanced approach. That’s exactly what they did against the Raiders, and the results spoke for themselves.
For the first time this season, the Rams had more rushing attempts than passing attempts. Corum led the Rams with 17 carries as he and Williams combined for 33 rushes for 192 yards and two touchdowns.
The Rams operated out of 13 personnel on 52.3 percent of their plays, the highest rate for any team in a game this season. With the balanced rushing attack, the Rams were able to lean more on play action. Their 56.7 percent play action rate was the highest for any team in a game this season.
With a more balanced approach and by leaning into the identity this team was meant to have, the Rams had a 63.1 percent offensive success rate. That is in the 99th percentile since 2016 and the fourth highest of the McVay era. It was the 25th highest in any game since 2016.
There’s little doubt that Matthew Stafford has regressed from last year. With that in mind, McVay made things simpler for his quarterback and allowed the running game to carry the load. It can certainly be argued that’s how it should’ve been all along.
During the 2021 season, McVay got used to Stafford being able to sling the ball all over the field without consequence. In the three-game stretch that became known as “No Win November,” Stafford threw the ball 127 times. Over the next six weeks, the Rams got back to the basics of leaning on the run game, with Sony Michel recording 18 or more carries in each game. The Rams went 5-1 during that stretch.
Sean McVay and Matthew Stafford are certainly a perfect match for each other. However, that can sometimes lead to McVay leaning on his quarterback’s arm too much. After dropping to 2-4, the Rams just needed to get back to the basics, and that’s exactly what they did. While they went three-and-out after three consecutive passes on the opening drive, it was much more balanced from that point forward. The Rams scored a touchdown on their next four drives. On those drives, the Rams ran the ball 16 times for 103 yards.
The Rams have shown the ability to win games this season. However, they have not been able to stack wins. After beating the Giants, the Rams blew a 16-point lead to the Broncos. Following the win against the Eagles, the Rams had a field goal blocked in overtime, preventing them from winning against the Bills.
If the Rams are going to recover from a 2-4 start, they need to start stacking wins. They won’t have any reason not to as they face the 0-6 Los Angeles Chargers next week, followed by the Washington Commanders and Arizona Cardinals. If the Rams get Myles Garrett back within the next week or two, it’s possible that they finally start to hit their stride. With Garrett back, the vision of what the Rams wanted to be coming into the season might finally start to come together.
When all is said and done, we might look back on the Rams beating the Raiders as a turning point in the season. While it may have “only been the Raiders,” the Rams aren’t in a position to discount wins. The Rams played their most complete game to date and found their identity while doing so. That’s something they can build on.
At some point, the narrative around the Rams’ wide receiver depth is no longer that they aren’t being used, but that they just aren’t good enough. Without Davante Adams in the lineup, Konata Mumpfield was the only wide receiver outside of Puka Nacua to have a reception. He had just one catch for 15 yards. Last season, the Rams ignored their need at cornerback, and it cost them. If the Rams don’t add a wide receiver at the trade deadline , it could have the same impact once the playoffs come.
The Rams were without Nate Landman on Sunday as he missed the game with a concussion. Without Landman, the Rams had Omar Speights and Shaun Dolac at linebacker. Speights was the primary linebacker throughout the game, but Dolac played well in his limited snaps. The Rams’ linebackers played well, especially against the run. It’s hard to see the Rams benching Landman, but Dolac took advantage of his opportunity.
There might be something to a running back not being able to get in a rhythm with a consistent rotation. However, this is the Rams’ running game at its best . In games when both Corum and Williams have had 10 or more carries this season, the offense has delivered two of its best performances outside of Week 1 in Australia. Giving Corum a consistent role in the offense gives defenses something else to prepare for.
It’s certainly possible to hand out multiple game balls for the win against the Raiders. Matthew Stafford hit a milestone, becoming the franchise leader in touchdown passes. Davis Allen scored two touchdowns. Additionally, Jaylen Watson had a good game. However, Corum provided a spark for the offense, and had it not been for two penalties, he would have scored three touchdowns. He finished with 17 carries for 93 yards and showed why he should be used more alongside Williams.
The Rams ran the ball 33 times. Again, it’s the first time this season that the Rams have had more rushing attempts than passing attempts. That’s not how things are going to shake out every week as the Rams aren’t going to have a double-digit lead to work with. Still, it shows that when the offense is balanced, everything works together.
As mentioned earlier, it’s very possible that we look at this game against the Raiders as a turning point in the season. Now, the Rams have to start stacking wins. They should be able to do that against a Chargers team that has struggled to find its own identity, despite them coming off of their bye.
Through seven weeks, the Rams are 3-4 and sit in third place in the NFC West. They still have an opportunity to get to the bye week in a good spot. With that said, they need to show some consistency week to week. Sunday’s win was a good start, but they finally have an identity they can build on going forward.

title: Rams Winners and Losers: Blake Corum Makes His Case for Bigger Role Against Raiders
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams got a much-needed win on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders . After struggling to find their identity through six weeks, the Rams leaned on the run game and got good performances at all levels of their defense. The win didn’t come without its mistakes, but overall the Rams will be happy with this one. Let’s get into winners and losers.
It was very clear from early on that the Rams wanted to get Blake Corum more involved in the offense and the run game. His creativity as a runner and ability to generate explosives helps open things up in the run game . Corum technically scored three times, but two were called back for penalties. He finally got in the end zone in the fourth quarter to put the game away. Corum finished with 17 carries for 93 yards, falling just seven yards short of his second career 100-yard game.
While Stafford only had 47 yards passing in the second half, he was a very efficient 17-for-19 in the first half. With the run game opening up play action, Stafford was able to hit his tight ends more and take shots downfield. He finished with 0.17 EPA per pass and went 6-for-9 against the blitz. This is the version of Stafford that the Rams need on a weekly basis. He’s capable of making the special throws, but the Rams need Stafford to just be efficient and take what’s available to get the offense rolling.
After last week’s loss to the Arizona Cardinals, in a moment of frustration, Williams said that the offense lacked energy because he wasn’t on the field. It may have been a nothingburger, but Sunday was a reminder that Williams needs to focus on his game and the rest will follow. In the third quarter, Williams let the Raiders back in the game with his second fumble of the season. Williams sucked the energy out of the offense. The fumbling issues continue to be his Achilles heel. He finished one yard shy of 100 yards, but the turnovers matter.
The Rams were without Nate Landman on Sunday and Speights filled in nicely in a full-time role. Speights was great against the run, finishing with six tackles, including two tackles for loss. Shaun Dolac deserves more opportunities on defense after adding three tackles of his own. Nate Landman is a captain and has a knack for forcing turnovers, but the Rams looked good at linebacker against the Raiders.
With Kobie Turner out, Ty Hamilton got more of a run on defense. Hamilton made his presence felt in the run game and put together one of the better performances of his career. For a player who has struggled at times, Sunday was promising. Hopefully it’s a sign of him turning the corner and showing that he can step up in a big way when his number is called.
It didn’t hurt the Rams on Sunday, but without Davante Adams, the offense needs a second wide receiver to step up. Mumpfield was targeted just twice and had one reception for 15 yards that he almost fumbled away. The Rams either need to trade for a wide receiver to fill the void left by Adams or they need more from Mumpfield. They won’t get away with no production from that spot against a better secondary.
Without Trent McDuffie, the Rams were short-handed in the secondary. However, Jaylen Watson stepped up in a big way. He allowed two receptions on 10 targets and just 17 yards. Watson became the first defender since Kool-Aid McKinstry in Week 17 of 2024 to allow two or fewer receptions on at least eight targets. He also forced six tight-window throws, which is the second most this season for any defender.
It’s probably fair to just put the defense as a whole here. The Raiders may have had their issues coming into the game, but they still had one of the NFL's top-five passing attacks. After the first half, the Raiders had -0.42 EPA per pass and a 35 percent passing success rate. The defense came up big in moments, forcing back-to-back empty red zone possessions to start the second half. The Raiders were 1-for-5 in the red zone on Sunday. On conversion downs, the Raiders were 5-for-19. That’s a credit to the Rams defense.

title: Rams Find Their Identity When They Needed It Most in Dominant Win Over Raiders
full_text:
For much of the first six weeks of the season, the Los Angeles Rams had struggled to find an identity. While they may still be a team with questions, the Rams got closer to finding out who they wanted to be against the Las Vegas Raiders, winning 35-21 to improve to 3-4.
The Rams started with a three-and-out on offense, but then got back to what they do best. Through the first six weeks of the season, no quarterback had more passing attempts than Matthew Stafford. It looked like the offense was headed for a similar game script after head coach Sean McVay called three straight passes to start the game.
After Matt Gay missed from 51 yards out for the Raiders, it was all Rams.
Running back Blake Corum provided the spark to ignite the offense on Sunday afternoon. Corum had four carries for 22 yards on the second drive before Stafford found tight end Davis Allen in the end zone out of play action.
Corum led the Rams with 17 carries for 93 yards and a touchdown. He and Williams combined for 33 carries for 192 yards and two touchdowns. It was the first time this season that the Rams had more rushing attempts than passing attempts on offense.
Following a 12-play, 80-yard drive, Stafford hit Allen in the end zone for a second time. From there, the Rams kept rolling. Wide receiver Puka Nacua may have been questionable going into Sunday’s game, but there was no question about his impact.
Another TE touchdown on National Tight Ends Day 🗣️ Matthew Stafford connects with Davis Allen for a Rams TD! LARvsLV on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/i5Y41M07Tt
Nacua entered Sunday’s game questionable after suffering a calf injury during Thursday’s practice. He had seven first-half receptions, which was one more than his six receptions during the entirety of last week’s loss to the Arizona Cardinals.
When Stafford hit Nacua for his third touchdown pass of the afternoon, he also became the Rams’ all-time franchise leader in touchdown passes, surpassing Roman Gabriel. Gabriel threw 154 touchdown passes over 130 games in 11 seasons. Stafford did it in 63 games across six seasons. He is the only quarterback to lead two franchises in touchdown passes.
Puka Nacua adds six more to the board for the Rams 🐏 LARvsLV on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CJMINNvBOA
Stafford went 17-for-19 in the first half with 148 yards and three touchdowns, and finished with 195 yards. Nacua had eight receptions on 10 targets for 68 yards and the touchdown.
To finish the first-half rampage, Williams took a toss to the left and scored from 17 yards out to give the Rams a 28-3 lead.
It wasn’t just the offense that came to play on Sunday. Defensively, the Rams completely shut down a Raiders offense that entered the week ranking fifth in EPA per pass and sixth in passing success rate. At one point in the first half, the Raiders were averaging -0.96 EPA per pass with a zero percent success rate.
Two of the Raiders’ first four drives resulted in a three-and-out. Cornerback Emmanuel Forbes broke up a pass on fourth down to force a stop and turnover on downs without Trent McDuffie in the lineup.
Great coverage by Emmanuel Forbes Jr. 👏 LARvsLV on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/fHpuq5XfJX
As the Raiders tried to get something going in the second half, the defense once again came up with plays in big spots. Facing a 4th-and-2 in the red zone, they got pressure on Kirk Cousins to force an overthrow and turnover on downs.
Following a Williams fumble, the defense got another fourth-down stop to force a second straight empty possession, which would prove to be important later. The Raiders finally got in the end zone in the fourth quarter when Cousins found wide receiver Tre Tucker for a 37-yard score, snapping a streak in which the Rams’ defense hadn’t allowed a touchdown in 20 straight drives.
Despite a stronger overall performance, the Rams took their foot off the gas and nearly paid the price. What seemed like a harmless touchdown that brought the Raiders within two scores at 28-12 turned out to be the start of a comeback attempt.
On the first play of the next drive, a Stafford pass went off the hands of Colby Parkinson and ended up an interception. Four plays later, Cousins hit Ashton Jeanty in the end zone for a touchdown. However, the Rams stopped the two-point conversion to make it 28-18 and keep it a two-score game.
Kirk Cousins floats it to Ashton Jeanty for the TD 🙌 LARvsLV on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/mppf0nxfCw
Needing to steal back the momentum, the Rams faced their most important drive of the game. On 3rd-and-2 from the Raiders’ 43-yard line, Stafford found Tyler Higbee for a 15-yard gain, and then three straight runs by Corum put the offense back in the red zone for the first time in the second half.
While Corum had two touchdowns taken away because of penalties earlier in the game, the third time proved to be the charm. Corum scored from four yards out to cap off his impressive day, putting the Rams back in control and ending the comeback attempt with a 35-18 lead.
Blake Corum takes it into the end zone for 6️⃣ LARvsLV on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/p3m08vLO0K
The Raiders kicked a late field goal, but the Rams closed out the game with an eight-play drive to drain the clock. With three kneel-downs by Stafford, the Rams secured the win.
It may have gotten shaky in the third quarter, but at points in the game, the Rams looked as good as, if not better than, they have at any point this season. With 33 rushing attempts split evenly across Corum and Williams combined with a heavy dose of 13 personnel, the Rams seemed to finally find an offensive identity they’ve lacked all season.
Coming into the game, the Rams were staring at a potential 2-5 record and their worst start of the McVay era. Instead, they got a win in a fashion that many have come to expect. This was a do-or-die type of win, and the Rams showed up in a big way. They looked much closer to the team many thought they would be at the beginning of the season.
Now, the Rams face their next challenge of being able to stack wins. They head back to SoFi Stadium next week to take on an 0-6 Los Angeles Chargers team and will have every chance to do so. Now that they’ve found an identity they can lean on and have had success with it, the Rams may finally have a foundation to build on.

title: Sunday Morning Rams Notebook: Puka Nacua Expected to Play, Myles Garrett Update, Remembering Lawrence McCutcheon
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams enter Week 7 in a must-win situation against the Las Vegas Raiders . At 2-4, the Rams are staring at a potential 2-5 start and are in desperate need of a win to avoid digging themselves into a hole too big to climb out of.
With that said, several storylines have emerged this week that are worth exploring further, including updates on Puka Nacua’s status for Sunday and Myles Garrett's recovery. Let’s dig into this week’s Sunday Morning Rams Notebook.
During Thursday’s practice, Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua left early with a calf injury . Much like Nacua’s groin injury that he suffered in practice in Week 2, head coach Sean McVay said that Nacua felt he wasn’t able to have the same power and full explosion that he was used to.
Nacua did not practice on Friday and was listed as questionable. However, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter , the Rams are optimistic that Nacua will play against the Raiders. Schefter said, “As one source said, ‘as long as there aren’t any setbacks, we feel good about him being able to play.’”
Rams are optimistic that WR Puka Nacua, who is questionable for Sunday’s game due to a calf injury, will play vs. the Raiders. Nacua was feeling better Saturday and, as one source said, “as long as there aren’t any setbacks, we feel good about him being available to play.” pic.twitter.com/mI22MZNcCj
Schefter reported that Nacua underwent an MRI on his calf Thursday that came back better than the Rams had hoped. It is expected that Nacua will work out on Sunday, but Schefter noted that he was feeling better on Saturday. As we get closer to the game, things seem to be trending in the right direction, but he’s still one to monitor.
There was some surprise this week when head coach Sean McVay said that Myles Garrett wouldn’t return to practice. Later in the week, ESPN’s Dan Graziano noted that Garrett would likely be out another two or three weeks at least.
It is possible that Garrett doesn’t play for another few weeks, but he could be returning to practice sooner rather than later.
“I was told on Myles Garrett that it is likely that he returns to practice next week,” said Ian Rapoport on The Pat McAfee Show. “I believe that’s seven weeks from the injury, so could potentially play Week 8. But Myles Garrett is likely to return to practice next week is actual good injury news for the Rams.”
. @RapSheet shares an update on Myles Garrett's knee injury and when he will return to play 👀⬇️ (via @RichEisenShow ) pic.twitter.com/u5pLuhvURk
Just because Garrett returns to practice doesn’t mean he will play.The Rams have remained cautious with Garrett throughout the process, and that likely wouldn’t change. Garrett returns, that would simply open his 21-day practice window, and then the Rams can see how he feels from there.
McVay was asked whether Garrett would return to practice during his media availability on Friday. “That's a possibility. I've told you guys, I'll wait to talk to Myles, D. ElAttrache, Reggie, and those guys, that that is a possibility for next week.”
If Garrett returns, it would be some rare good injury news for the Rams, who have seemingly dealt with another injury every time they turn a corner. He would certainly provide a boost to the defense, which has struggled to get to the quarterback and ranks 26th in sacks.
It’s no secret that the NFL is working to expand internationally. This year, the Rams played the first NFL regular season game in Australia in Week 1 because of the team’s marketing rights in that area. The NFL held nine international regular season games this season. However, under the collective bargaining agreement, the NFL has approval to play a maximum of 10 international games, and it’s very possible that Tokyo, Japan, is next on the list .
This week in Paris, NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell was asked about Tokyo and said, “Listen, Tokyo is clearly on our list, whether it’s next year or the year after. It’s coming at some point in the near future.”
What makes Tokyo interesting is that the Rams are the lone team with marketing rights to Japan. If the NFL were to play in Japan, the Rams would make the most sense. The Rams weren’t happy about playing in Australia in Week 1 and only arrived around 24 hours before the game. Maybe it doesn’t happen, but given the NFL continuing to expand internationally, it’s something to keep an eye on.
Ever since the Rams drafted Ty Simpson, the pick has been criticized in the media. Those criticisms have only gotten louder as the Rams have lost and continue to get injured. Given the lack of overall talent in the 2026 class, many believed that the Rams should simply wait until 2027.
However, approaching one draft with an eye already on the next can be dangerous. It’s easy to forget that the 2026 quarterback class was also supposed to be loaded. Players like Drew Allar and Cade Klubnik didn’t take the steps that many expected them to.
That same thing is currently happening with the 2027 quarterback class. Tom Pelissero of The Ringer wrote about the situation this week .
“Several high-ranking NFL executives and scouts expressed skepticism this week that some, if not a majority, of the projected top QBs will even enter the 2027 NFL draft,” wrote Pelissero. “That includes Manning, who was the clear preseason favorite to be the No. 1 pick.”
Pelissero added that Oregon's Dante Moore hasn’t played since he suffered a concussion in September. Additionally, CJ Carr, Darian Mensah, LaNorris Sellers, Julian Sayin, and Austin Simmons could return due to the NCAA’s move to a five-for-five eligibility model.
Many of those quarterbacks have been inconsistent anyway. The overall point is that the highest-ranked quarterback on ESPN’s current 2027 draft big board is only eighth. There may be better depth this year at the position, but the talent at the top isn’t what it was thought to be last April. The Rams’ draft can certainly be criticized, but if the Rams had conviction on Ty Simpson and he works, that was the right pick. Where a conversation can start to be had is in the second round.
On Friday, the Rams announced the passing of running back Lawrence McCutcheon. According to the team, McCutcheon lost a battle with Parkinson’s disease. McCutcheon's passing comes just days after former Rams running back Marshall Faulk announced his own Parkinson’s disease diagnosis this week.
There are certainly all of the things on the field that McCutcheon will be remembered for. When he left the Rams in 1979, he was the team’s all-time leading rusher with 6,186 yards. He was a five-time Pro Bowler and earned second-team All-Pro honors after rushing for 1,109 yards in 1974.
For many, McCutcheon was their favorite player as they started watching the Rams. In the Super Bowl, he threw a touchdown pass to Ron Smith, giving the Rams a 19-17 lead heading into the fourth quarter.
The first Super Bowl TD pass in #Rams history was made by Lawrence McCutcheon, when he completed a 24 yard pass to Ron Smith. #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/tc5cR9Iff0
While McCutcheon is mostly remembered for what he did on the field, he was also a devoted family man, serving as a husband, brother, father, grandfather, and great-grandfather. After his playing career, McCutcheon remained deeply connected to the Rams and the Los Angeles community. Anyone who wants to do their part in remembering McCutcheon can donate to the Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson’s Research.

title: Rams vs. Raiders: Position-by-Position Breakdown Reveals Surprising Advantages
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams take on the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7, hoping to avoid a 2-5 start. While the Rams have been the better team on paper in most weeks, they simply haven’t found the consistency to put it all together. Now, with injuries across the roster, they may not be the better team on Sunday. Here’s a position-by-position breakdown for Sunday’s game against the Raiders.
Even with Matthew Stafford not playing as well this season, the Rams will still have the advantage at quarterback in most games. However, that may not be the case against the Raiders. This isn’t to say that Kirk Cousins is better than Stafford, but he’s been better this year. Cousins’ 0.14 EPA per pass is seven times higher than Stafford’s in 2026. Stafford has more upside, but he’s been very inconsistent. Cousins has also been the fourth-best quarterback when under pressure this season while Stafford ranks 23rd. Advantage: Raiders
The Raiders simply don’t have the infrastructure offensively to properly support Ashton Jeanty. With Mike Washington possibly out, the Raiders could be short-handed at running back. When the Rams have run the ball, Kyren Williams and Blake Corum remain two of the most consistent pieces of the offense. Advantage: Rams
I’ll add a caveat here that if the Rams have Puka Nacua available on Sunday, they have the clear edge. However, without Nacua, the Rams would be relying on Tutu Atwell , Konata Mumpfield and Jordan Whittington. It’s not any better with the Raiders, who have Tre Tucker, Cody White, and Jalen Nailor. Without Nacua, this is even, and the Raiders may have a slight edge. Advantage: Even
With Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer, the Raiders have one of the best tight end duos in the NFL. The Rams’ tight end group is solid with Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson, but it doesn’t match what the Raiders have. With Bowers and Mayer, the Raiders’ offense runs through the tight end position. Advantage: Raiders
There is a lot of upside with the Raiders’ offensive line. Kolton Miller is good at left tackle and they signed both Spencer Burford and Tyler Linderbaum in free agency. Additionally, they have a high-end draft pick in Jackson Powers-Johnson at left guard. However, Linderbaum has been a disappointment this season. The Rams will get Alaric Jackson back from suspension and should have their starting offensive line at full strength. Advantage: Rams
Tyler Linderbaum's game vs the Bills was very bad. The #Raiders need more from him. If Klint Kubiak's offense is going to have success the Center needs to be that anchor. So far we have not gotten that. https://t.co/SJ8794eNtA pic.twitter.com/o1co5JNgxU
Coming into the season, the Rams’ defensive line was seen as a deep group. That group has really been tested this season with Myles Garrett out, and now, with Kobie Turner and Poona Ford on injured reserve, it’s going to be tested even further. These are two similar groups, each with a star player on the edge in Maxx Crosby and Byron Young. However, Aaron Donald is still clearly the best player on the interior. Advantage: Rams
The Rams are going to be short-handed at linebacker with Nate Landman out with a concussion. That could mean more Shaun Dolac, but the Rams will also rely on Eric Kendricks off the practice squad . The Raiders have the edge here with Quay Walker and Nakobe Dean. Advantage: Raiders
Even without Trent McDuffie, the Rams are set to have a huge advantage in the secondary. Hezekiah Masses started the year strong but has since dropped off slightly. Eric Stokes has also struggled. The Rams have gotten good production out of Josh Wallace, will still have Jaylen Watson available, and have seen strong play from Quentin Lake. Advantage: Rams
This is a Rams special teams revenge game if there ever were such a thing. The Raiders will have former Rams special teams coordinator Joe DeCamillis, kicker Matt Gay, and long snapper Alex Ward. It should almost be expected for the Rams to lose on something special teams-related. Advantage: Raiders

title: 3 Critical Matchups the Rams Must Win vs. Raiders to Avoid Falling to 2-5
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to play the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7. This will be a must-win game for the Rams as they look to avoid a 2-5 start. While the Raiders may have been seen as a guaranteed win in recent years, that’s not the case this season. The Raiders have played well and nothing is guaranteed with this Rams team. Let’s dive into the three biggest matchups to watch.
For the most part, Warren McClendon stepped in well for an injured Rob Havenstein. So much so that when Havenstein was healthy at the end of the year, the Rams simply stayed with McClendon and then didn’t draft a replacement when they could have in the first round. However, there were signs that McClendon may not be what the Rams needed when he allowed 11 pressures over three playoff games, including five against the Carolina Panthers and four against the Seattle Seahawks.
McClendon has allowed a 6.3 percent pressure rate, which is the highest among Rams offensive linemen this season. The right side with McClendon and Dotson has been a liability in pass protection at times. Maxx Crosby has a 19.4 percent pressure rate this season and does line up over the right tackle. The Rams are going to need McClendon to hold his own in pass protection and give Stafford time to attack a vulnerable secondary.
The Rams are going to need to replicate what the Bills did against Crosby last week. Outside of Crosby, the Raiders don’t have an interior threat capable of drawing attention. The Bills consistently chipped Crosby or had a guard ready to help in case of an inside move. Last week, the Raiders had an average time to pressure of 3.21 seconds, which was their slowest of the season.
It’s unclear what the Rams are going to be working with at wide receiver against the Raiders. Davante Adams is already out, but after Puka Nacua injured his calf, his status is uncertain as well. That would leave the Rams with Konata Mumpfield as their top wide receiver option along with Tutu Atwell.
The Rams' lack of wide receiver depth is especially unfortunate this week because the Raiders' cornerbacks can be exploited. The Raiders rank 26th in EPA per pass allowed. Hezekiah Masses and Eric Stokes have been susceptible to giving up big plays. The Raiders have given up a 7.2 percent explosive pass rate this season, which ranks 30th.
If the Rams are going to win this game, they are going to have to win their matchups on the perimeter at wide receiver. They will likely lean on 13 personnel, but at some point, a wide receiver will need to win an individual matchup. The Rams won’t be able to just lean on Tyler Higbee at tight end.
Even if the Rams are without Trent McDuffie for a second straight week, it’s easy to like their matchups against the Raiders’ wide receivers. Tre Tucker is the only Raiders wide receiver with over 250 yards this season. The next closest is Cody White with 108 yards.
Brock Bowers has a team-high 28 receptions this season, while Michael Mayer has also been a key contributor. The Raiders’ offense runs through their tight ends. Bowers has been great when healthy this season. However, the Rams have done well keeping opposing tight ends in check. Quentin Lake held his own against Trey McBride last week. Bowers is the most explosive player on the Raiders’ offense. If the Rams can mitigate the damage from Bowers and let the receivers beat them, they’ll see that as a win.
