title: Dolphins Saturday Mailbag: Why Fans Should Want to See Victories
full_text:
Part 1 of the pre-Jets game Miami Dolphins On SI mailbag:
So me and my sons are flying up for the game. Even though we want a top draft pick next year, can you give us a reason to root for a win?
Hey Mark, because the biggest thing you should want to see this season is progress from the young players, namely all the recent draft picks, as well as from Malik Willis. And the Dolphins starting to win some games certainly would be a sign of progress, which might provide more optimism than winding up with a higher draft pick in 2027 than with more and more losses.
Hello Alain, which of the Dolphins and Jets has the better future outlook with their current QB situation? Or is the present irrelevant, and both are likely to find themselves in a future competition to acquire the best prospect that might provide hope in challenging the top of the division?
Hey Ricky, this is a very good question and the answer will come down to whether Malik Willis can take that step and establish himself as a bona fide long-term answer so the Dolphins can use their resources in other areas. If we’re looking at the totality of the roster, I think the Jets actually might be a bit ahead at this time, though it’s pretty close, but Geno Smith clearly is a stopgap for them. Also remember that the Jets have three first-round picks again next year and if they can nail the quarterback, that could set them up for a pretty drastic turnaround sooner rather than later.
I don’t see everything that you say, but I’ve yet to hear you proclaim what you would do, only what you would not do, with the first overall pick. So that being said, as things stand right now and we’ll pretend like the Dolphins have the No. 1 pick and not the Chargers. Who would you select at this very moment with the No. 1 overall pick for the Miami Dolphins?
Hey Dana, you haven’t missed anything because my take always has been that I don’t like the idea of Jeremiah Smith first overall because of positional value (or lack thereof) and I’ve also said that I need the season to play out in college football before I decide which prospect I would prefer. To answer your question, my first preference at No. 1 would be trading down, hopefully not too far down, and picking up additional draft picks. If that’s off the table, based on what I know right now and subject to change, I’d be inclined to go with either Texas edge defender Colin Simmons and might even consider Leonard Moore, the cornerback from Notre Dame. I still don’t have a QB prospect that screams “must take” right now.
Hey Davis, if you’re asking why the Dolphins waived him in terms of this being a big surprise, my answer to you would be that it shouldn’t have been a big surprise. While Duck did show potential at times for the Dolphins in 2024 and in training camp last year, it’s not like he was an established player. And that Miami decided he didn’t rank higher than any of the three newcomers they have — Jaylin Simpson, Marcellas Dial Jr. and Reece Taylor, all of them claimed off waivers, mind you — and that should tell you all you need to know.
Greetings Alain! Had to take an emergency trip to Central Florida last week & on way back was caught in one of the infamous traffic jams around Miami area, so I listened to the Collective.  I then noticed I was in the stadium area & I was creeping along & y'all were talking about the season; the irony wasn't lost on me. This season is meant to creep along, but it gets lost on us fans sometimes. Not sure if he's been asked, but do you think Hafley regrets no 7 on 7's to build some chemistry between QB/receivers? Also to get receivers better familiar with proper routes? Final question: Is Chris Bell's lack of separation due to still recovering from knee injury? Not knowing the assignments? Something else? As always, look forward to both All Dolphins and Dolphins Collective podcasts (best out there) and all the great written content on Miami Dolphins on SI.Com.
Thanks as always, Dave. I don’t think there’s any question that Bell’s knee injury still factors in his ability to separate at the time, but it’s also fair to ask what his ceiling is in that department once the injury is a thing of the past because I don’t think that ever was considered his forte. Hafley explained his disdain for 7-on-7 work in training camp as not being representative of what players will do in games, and I’m thinking he wouldn’t be about to second-guess himself there. And if that 7-on-7 that wasn’t done was replaced by 11-on-11 sessions, then the Dolphins didn’t miss out on that kind of work.
Do you think the Dolphins' staff will be less likely to activate or play injured players due to the history of injuries at that crap field?
Hey Lloyd, it’s a very interesting point you raise because MetLife Stadium historically has been rough on players, for sure. That said, no, I don’t think decisions will be made specifically because of that surface. If the Dolphins decide, for example, that Caleb Douglas is ready to go, I don’t think Jeff Hafley wants to go down the road of being afraid of something bad happening because the game is at MetLife Stadium.
I need your honest opinion here. Do the Miami Dolphins have the smallest shoulders for a coach and general manager duo in the NFL?
First off, I always give my honest opinion. Never a need to preface a question with that. Second … huh? Smallest shoulders? You mean, Jon-Eric Sullivan and Jeff Hafley are not physically imposing? So? And I haven’t studied or examined other coach/GM combos to see where they stand among their peers.
What weapon not named Ollie Gordon steps up on offense on Sunday?
I think Malik Willis comes back from the bye with his best performance of the season. If you’re asking for somebody other than the QB, then maybe I go with Greg Dulcich, who’s due to have a big performance in the passing game.

title: Breaking Down the Louis News and the other Week 7 Dolphins Saturday Moves
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins will get a second rookie back when they face the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on Sunday.
Safety Kyle Louis was activated off injured reserve Saturday, meaning he'll be ready to return to action for the first time since sustaining a knee injury in the season opener against the Las Vegas Raiders. Louis' availability had been trending positively all week, culminated by his full participation in practice Friday, though he remained listed as questionable on the final injury report of the week.
Along with activating Louis, the Dolphins also made their two weekly practice squad elevations, this time with edge defender Max Llewellyn and kicker Zane Gonzalez.
The move with Gonzalez basically was a given since the Dolphins don't have a kicker on the 53-man roster after releasing Riley Patterson on Tuesday, while the move with Llewellyn suggests that Rob Beal Jr. will miss a fourth consecutive game because of the hamstring injury he sustained in the Week 2 loss against the San Francisco 49ers. He was listed as doubtful on the Dolphins' final injury report of the week.
Llewellyn, the rookie seventh-round pick out of Iowa, will be making his second appearance. He played five snaps in the 35-13 loss at Levi's Stadium.
Louis will become the fifth safety on the active roster, joining Dante Trader Jr., rookie Michael Taaffe, Zayne Anderson and Julius Wood.
A linebacker at the University of Pittsburgh, Louis was switched to safety at some in training camp and in an ideal world he could become a good nickel defender because of his coverage ability. Before he was injured, Louis also had become a gunner on the punt team.
Given that he hasn't played since the opener, it's probably fair to expect Louis to play mostly, if not exclusively, on special teams against the Jets.
But regardless it's great to have him back.
He is the third player the Dolphins have designated to return from IR so far this season after DT Kenneth Grant and LB Trey Moore. Grant also has returned to the active roster, while Moore remains on IR and was designated to return on the day of the cuts to 53 to preserve a roster spot for somebody else.
Each team is allowed eight IR designations in the regular season.

title: Three Bold Predictions for the Miami Dolphins Against New York Jets
full_text:
The 0-5 Miami Dolphins take on the 2-4 New York Jets in Miami’s first divisional game of the 2026 season. Both teams are looking to keep their seasons from going completely off the rails, so let’s make some predictions for this Week 7 matchup.
Sunday will mark the return of rookie receiver Caleb Douglas, who has missed the past three games with an ankle injury. Adding his size to the top of the depth chart should bump everyone else to a more natural position, and there may be no bigger benefactor than Malik Washington.
Washington has quietly put together an impressive third season, tallying 50 or more scrimmage yards in four of his first five games. He has also established himself as a favorite target of quarterback Malik Willis, who has thrown his way 36 times this year (more than double the second-place mark).
As Miami looks for sustainability, targeting Washington underneath seems like a potential solution, and he has the agility to make defenders miss in space. His ascension, Douglas’ return, and Willis likely needing quick answers against a Jets defense that ranks eighth in blitz percentage is a recipe for a big day for Miami’s most experienced receiver.
This matchup features two passers who have done a poor job mitigating pressure this season. Both rank top 12 in time to throw, top three in pressure rate allowed, and top five in sack percentage.
The Jets are well equipped to take advantage of Malik Willis’ indecision. Their defense ranks in the top eight in pressure rate, and is tied for sixth in total sacks through six weeks.
The Dolphins, on the other hand, have been inept up front. Their four sacks are half the next-lowest team in the NFL, and all four came against Kyler Murray and the Minnesota Vikings in Week 4.
With two weeks to prepare, a quarterback who is willing to hang in the pocket, and the potentially dumb luck that Miami’s sacks have come in a bunch, this feels like a perfect opportunity for the Dolphins’ defensive front to make its mark, even if Malik Willis’ play leads to a similar outcome on the opposite side of the ball.
Ollie Gordon's development in year two has been a revelation. His footwork looks substantially better than it did in 2025, and he’s made the most of his elevated opportunity. Gordon’s rushing yards over expected per attempt is ninth among qualified rushers, per NextGenStats.
The Jets have a very sound defense on a per-run basis. Their EPA per rush allowed is tied for third best in football, and they’re right around the middle of the pack in terms of yards-per-attempt. They have, however, struggled to stop runs in the backfield. Their stuffed run rate is seventh-lowest, and they’re allowing over a yard and a half before contact per carry, which ranks ninth-worst.
Miami’s massive offensive line has opened up big lanes for Gordon in recent weeks. He has a 20+ yard carry in each of the last two games. Now, against a defense that particularly struggles to generate displacement, it wouldn’t be shocking to see the left-side duo of Paul and Proctor give Gordon a runway that he can use to get downhill and put his massive frame to work against New York’s defensive backs.

title: Vikings Week 7 Stock Report: Cashman Among Risers, Murray Falls After Gritty Win vs. Colts
full_text:
The Vikings are now the last undefeated team in the NFL , thanks to their elite special teams and suffocating defense. The offense, meanwhile, is still working out some wrinkles despite featuring some top-end talent.
After beating up on some bottom-feeder teams over the past few weeks, the real tests are just around the corner for Minnesota. So who is trending in the right direction, and who needs to step things up with the 4-2 Lions up next?
After a dominant performance against the Colts with 12 tackles and two sacks, Blake Cashman is playing some of the best football in the entire NFL right now. Heading into Week 8, he's first on the Vikings in tackles and tackles for loss, and second in sacks and passes defended. While not typically regarded as a household name, he's well on his way towards First-Team All-Pro recognition.
Cashman's contract is up after 2026 (like multiple other key starters), and the Vikings will have to shell out a pretty penny after what's shaping up to be his best season yet.
If Donovan Jackson wasn't already out for the year, Will Fries might very well be on the trade block. Since signing a monster contract to join Minnesota, Fries just hasn't figured things out in purple. Sunday's game was another sub-par performance, and Fries graded out as the fourth-worst offensive player by Pro Football Focus ' metrics with a 59.8.
The Vikings' interior was shaky all game, but while Joe Huber and Blake Brandel have inexperience on their side, Fries is running out of time to put things together.
Smith notched his 40th career interception in the win over Indy, and just one look at head coach Kevin O'Connell's post-game locker room speech tells the whole story of how important "The Hitman" is to the Vikings.
Harrison Smith hasn't played especially well this season, but Sunday's pick off of Daniel Jones (h/t NFL) to end the game was a step in the right direction. The Vikings still haven't found the perfect recipe at safety just yet, but it's clear Smith still has some savvy left.
HARRISON SMITH GETS THE INT! VIKINGS ARE 6-0 ‼️ pic.twitter.com/stul8J8hWe
For as flashy and mobile as Kyler Murray can be, he's also been very boring this year for Minnesota. That's been both good and bad, because while he has protected the ball and made smart throws, he's also been inaccurate at times and almost never pushes the ball downfield.
The Vikings are about to enter the teeth of their schedule with Detroit, Buffalo, Green Bay and San Francisco next month, and Murray isn't playing to the level the offense needs him to be yet after a hum-drum 150-yard performance this week.
Jake Golday played a season-high nine defensive snaps on Sunday, and his role looks to be expanding every week. His competition—Ivan Pace Jr.— has been trending the opposite direction , and if Golday can continue impressing during the week, he may carve out a respectable reserve role. The Vikings don't especially have a huge need for him right now, but the future starter is starting to get some valuable reps.
Yes, the Vikings are 6-0 and haven't lost a game in quite literally a calendar year, but it's also fair to question if Minnesota is winning in spite of their head coach on some level.
This is not a 'Fire Kevin O'Connell' post, as he has done a good job overall, but the handling of the J.J. McCarthy trade and leading an offense that is still struggling even in Week 7 deserve some criticism.
O'Connell is still the answer at head coach, but it's alarming, to say the least, that his offense will almost certainly be the reason the Vikings get booted from the playoffs.

title: Caleb Banks Injury Concerns Could Thrust Domonique Orange Into a Bigger Vikings' Role
full_text:
A major theme this season has been the Vikings' patience with their 2026 rookie class . While those rookies are growing and developing, the Purple and Gold have relied on their more experienced players on the roster to be major contributors.
That philosophy has had an interesting impact on first-round pick Caleb Banks and third-round pick Domonique Orange, who were selected to eventually replace last year's starters —Jonathan Allen and Javon Hargrave—after they were both released back in the offseason.
Former United Football League standout Jalen Redmond is having a fantastic season on Minnesota's defensive line and played 54 of Minnesota's 59 defensive snaps in Week 7. Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins had the next most defensive line snaps, playing 46 reps.
Banks and Orange played 12 and 13 defensive snaps, respectively, in Sunday's victory over the Colts . Since the Vikings are bringing them along slowly, the lower snap counts make sense from a development perspective.
However, Banks limped off the field against the Colts after being down and did not return to action. If he is forced to miss time with that injury, this could be an opportunity for "Big Citrus" to set more defensive work against the Lions in Week 8.
Orange has played 91 defensive snaps this year for Minnesota. Although he participates on special teams as well, he has four tackles this season, with one of those being for a loss against the Packers in the season opener. His 42.9 defense grade on Pro Football Focus is far from ideal , but three of his last four performances were higher than that mark. He's also averaged a run-defense grade of 57.4 in the last games after averaging 46.1 in the first two.
Assuming he doesn't play on Sunday, the 15.7 defensive snaps that Banks averages per game could be up for grabs.
Some of those could go to Orange, and if he can get about 25 defensive snaps against the Lions on Sunday, it could show how much he has developed since joining the team. That would be his career-high defensive snap count, besting his 24 reps against the Bears in Week 2.
The Lions run the fourth-most offensive players per game (66.3), so there should be more than enough opportunities to get on the field.
Developing Orange is even more important when looking at the long-term value of the defensive lineman. While staying on top of the NFC North or remaining undefeated is great, this team is in position to potentially be a scary playoff team, and having him as an asset to rotate into defensive coordinator Brian Flores's squad would be extremely valuable.
At only 22 years old, Orange should have a long NFL career in front of him. Getting him experience and evaluating his development in Week 8 could go a long way in preparing the young defender for a long and prosperous tenure with the Vikings.

title: Jakobe Thomas's Uphill Battle to Vikings Playing Time Became Steeper After Week 7
full_text:
It was extremely disappointing to see rookie defensive back Jakobe Thomas listed as one of the six players declared inactive for the Vikings' Week 7 victory over the Colts on Sunday .
Thomas' inactive designation follows the trend of him being sidelined for every game this season after joining the team as a third-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, meaning that he has never been active on game day since joining the team.
The 23-year-old safety has been patient in waiting for his opportunity to get on the field while others at his position struggled , but the solid play of his peers will make his case for playing time more difficult.
With Thomas inactive on the sideline, veteran Harrison Smith, versatile defender Josh Metellus, and fifth-year defensive back Theo Jackson all had good games against the Colts.
Smith had four tackles, half a sack, and the game-clinching interception. Meanwhile, Metellus finished second on the team in tackles, bringing down seven Colts ball carriers. Jackson tied for the third-most tackles on the team with five. They all graded well on Pro Football Focus , too :
Even fellow rookie S Jacob Thomas saw four defensive snaps, bringing his total to a modest 26 on the year.
These performances from Smith, Metellus, and Jackson take pressure off defensive coordinator Brian Flores and head coach Kevin O'Connell to make a change at safety. That will make Thomas's chances of being active in Week 8 on the road against the Lions, who average the second-most points (30.7) and total yards (397.3) per game this season.
Now, Thomas is in a position where he needs to continue working hard in practice to make a good impression on special teams coordinator Matt Daniels. Getting his foot in the door on special teams seems like the most logical way to earn a role on game day, even if it isn't the flashiest way to do it.
Interestingly, Thomas is one of only two rookies selected in the first 100 picks of the 2026 to be inactive for every game this season, with the other being Broncos defensive lineman Tyler Onyedim.
By now, Thomas has to be hungry to see some regular-season action. But the former Miami (FL) defensive back needs to continue to be patient until his opportunity comes. In the meantime, he can continue to learn a lot from players like Smith, Metellus and Jackson to be ready for when O'Connell, Flores & Co. give him the green light to be active on game day... eventually.

title: Aaron Jones Avoids Devastating Injury: Expect More Jordan Mason Going Forward
full_text:
The Vikings' offense wasn't exactly firing on all cylinders in their 16-10 win over the Colts on Sunday , and the unit was given an even bigger reason for concern moving forward. After all, lead running back Aaron Jones Sr. left with a knee injury in the fourth quarter and didn't return. Given how some people were worried about the Vikings potentially overusing Jones in recent weeks , there was good reason to be concerned after the late-game exit.
Fortunately, the Vikings dodged a major bullet coming out of Week 7. On Monday morning, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that Jones's injury " is not considered to be significant at this time ," with one of Schefter's sources labeling it as a "day-to-day" situation.
Vikings RB Aaron Jones’ knee injury that he suffered during Sunday’s win over the Colts is not considered to be significant at this time, and a source described him as “day to day.”
Given the day-to-day nature of the injury, it sounds like Minnesota isn't close to ruling Jones out of the upcoming Week 8 clash with the rival Lions. At the same time, since the 31-year-old RB is already banged up and it's only the end of October, the Vikings should lean even more on the freshly returned Jordan Mason.
After missing four games and resting throughout the bye week with a fractured thumb, Mason finally made his long-awaited return to the Vikings' RB room against the Colts.
The Georgia Tech product accounted for 15 of Minnesota's 29 backfield touches, converting them into 68 rushing yards for an average of 4.5 yards per carry. His 67.2 run grade was also the 12th-best among RBs with double-digit carries in Week 7 , according to Pro Football Focus .
Jones, meanwhile, wasn't nearly as productive until his untimely exit (26 yards on eight carries), while veteran running back DeeJay Dallas didn't even see a touch despite being a game-day elevation from the practice squad.
It's possible Jones still won't be 100% come Sunday, giving the Vikings every reason to roll with Mason as the RB1 against the Lions. He's proven he can handle plenty of responsibilities in his limited appearances so far, converting 30 carries into 127 rushing yards and a touchdown. That's on pace for a 255-1,080-9 stat line in 17 games, making Mason one of the best "backup" RBs that any team could have.
Rolling with Mason as the bell-cow back against the Lions could be exactly what Jones needs to recover after carrying the same role during his counterpart's absence. Even if the Vikings trade for a difference-making RB like the Colts' Jonathan Taylor , keeping the backfield as fresh as can be for as long as possible is in O'Connell & Co.'s best interest—especially if a deep playoff run is the ultimate goal.
When it comes to the upcoming NFC North clash, it should be business as usual for the Vikings' backfield plans.
Few teams run the ball as often as Minnesota does. In fact, the Bears (35.1) and Ravens (30.2) are the only teams that eclipse the Vikings' 30.1 rushing attempts per game. The love for running is a big reason Jones averaged 21.3 carries per game during Mason's absence, including a season-high 25 against the Saints in Week 5.
It's hard to imagine the Vikings straying from that strategy, so it wouldn't surprise me if Mason sees 15 to 20 carries against the Lions. He's already recorded the low end of that range 10 times in 63 all-time appearances, with a career-high 28 coming back in Week 1 of the 2024 season. The increased responsibility didn't hurt his production, either:
If he can play, the Vikings can still give another five to eight carries to Jones to keep him involved, but not overused. Throw in a few carries for quarterback Kyler Murray and maybe an opportunity or two for Dallas, rounding out the ideal game plan on the ground.
Riding the hot hand is never a bad idea, and that's exactly what the Vikings need to do this weekend. Mason can clearly handle a bigger role, and keeping him there will not only help Jones return to full health but could also help the Vikings' offense, which is still desperately looking to unlock its full firepower.

title: Harmon's Longship Week 7: 4 Vikings Thoughts on Win vs. Colts, Trade Urgency, Offensive Struggles & More
full_text:
MINNEAPOLIS, M.N. — Another day, another foe vanquished. The Vikings returned from their bye week with reinforcements in tow to face a struggling Colts team. After three hours and plenty of offense-induced frustration, the Purple and Gold once again walked away victorious in a 16-10 “thriller."
Just like that, the 6-0 Vikings are the last unbeaten team in the NFL , but judging by some of the discourse around them, you’d think they haven’t won a single game. The duality we saw hints of early in the season has become painfully clear over seven weeks: if the Vikings stumble before the finish line, their lackluster offense will be to blame.
Let’s break down what happened and what’s to come.
There was plenty of reason to be optimistic that the Vikings’ offense would finally get on track heading into Sunday’s game with the returns of Christian Darrisaw, Jordan Addison, T.J. Hockenson, and Jordan Mason.
Unfortunately, the unit seemed to regress from the performance they put together in New Orleans two weeks ago. Kyler Murray and the passing game showed little life until late, totaling only 139 net passing yards. Murray flashed his patented mobility, wowing the U.S. Bank Stadium crowd with a 35-yard scramble that set the Vikings up near the goal line (h/t: NFL).
Kyler Murray with a 35-yard run to pick up the first down 🏃 INDvsMIN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/GSqLond1o9
Justin Jefferson was almost a non-factor. With only four receptions for 44 yards. Jordan Addison had an even slower day, with two catches for 20 yards. Jauan Jennings doubled his season total in receptions, with two catches for 34 yards. Murray and Jennings also had a near-touchdown that they couldn't connect on.
Murray’s best throw of the day was a dime to Addison, who made a toe-tap snag near the goal line, only for the play to be called back on a Blake Brandel hold. Murray eventually connected with Hockenson for a key fourth-quarter touchdown, showing the passing game had some life after all.
The story of the passing game remains the same through six games: potential explosive plays either result in near misses or are called back due to penalties.
The good news for the struggling Vikings offense? The team’s stellar defense made sure the Colts and quarterback Daniel Jones had an even worse day. Jones was sacked four times and threw an interception in a performance that included a whopping 64 net passing yards thanks to the Vikings’ suffocating pass rush. Minnesota’s 85.2% blitz rate against Jones was the highest since Next Gen Stats started tracking the metric in 2016.
The Vikings defense blitzed on 85.2% of Daniel Jones' dropbacks, the highest blitz rate by a defense in a game in the Next Gen Stats era (since 2016). Minnesota generated pressure on 60.9% of those blitzes, with all four its sacks coming when blitzing. #INDvsMIN | #Skol
Linebacke r Blake Cashman had a stellar performance, with eight tackles, four pass breakups, and two sacks (h/t: Doug Farrar).
Blake Cashman of the @Vikings may have had the best game any linebacker has enjoyed this season. Eight solo tackles, two sacks, four run stops, four pass breakups. Absolute animal. pic.twitter.com/wflIL9rISG
Cashman, Andrew Van Ginkel, and Isaiah Rodgers will certainly leave new general manager Nolan Teasley with tough choices, as all three have been incredibly impressive in the last year of their current deals. Franchise legend Harrison Smith secured the win with his 40th career interception, an outcome I predicted last week.
This defense is too stellar to waste, but there are real concerns about this offense's sustainability. So, what comes next?
The good news? We didn't learn many new things about this Minnesota squad in Week 7. The bad news? The offensive concerns only seem to be growing as a very tough schedule approaches.
The Vikings’ offense desperately needs a boost, and it seems unlikely that head coach Kevin O’Connell and his unit can find it as currently constructed. If Minnesota’s identity is going to be rooted in running the ball and leaning on a stellar defense, they need a running back who can carry the load and hit home runs.
Luckily, they got a close look at one yesterday when Jonathan Taylor punched in an early  38-yard TD . (h/t: Colts).
Jonathan Taylor breaks through! 📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/lcFr4An7JV
Taylor (or an equivalent back) may be the key to making this team truly successful in the playoffs , a formula Teasley knows well from last year’s championship run in Seattle. While Aaron Jones has fought valiantly, his lack of downfield explosiveness and repeated injuries make him hard to count on long-term.
But a room led by Taylor, with Jones and Mason in support? That may be something special.
I would like to start with a special thank you to the Falcons for their 29-20 upset victory against the previously undefeated Niners, giving the Vikings sole possession of the NFC’s top seed. Granted, it’s late October, but any cushion is valuable going forward. The Lions beat the Packers in a close one, 20-17.
The Vikings head off to the Motor City to face the Lions next Sunday in what should be a great battle between a strong Detroit offense and an elite Minnesota defense.
After Detroit, the Vikings return home to face the Bills on Monday Night Football on Nov. 9, take on the Packers in Green Bay six days later, and head to Mexico City a week after that to battle the 49ers. They’ll wrap up the month against an increasingly feisty Falcons team at U.S. Bank Stadium on Nov. 29.
If you are unsure about this Vikings team, we’re all about to find out together what they’re truly made of.
The Vikings will meet the Lions for the first of two divisional matchups next Sunday in Detroit. The Lions’ defense provides a unique set of opportunities and challenges for the struggling Vikings offense. Detroit’s 21 sacks are tied for the league lead, while the unit also allows the most yards per game (391) to opposing offenses.
Their offense has proven to be one of the league's most explosive squads in the NFL, posing the biggest challenge yet to Flores’s stellar squad.
This matchup could be a statement game for the Vikings, who want to silence doubts against a difficult divisional opponent. Holding their offense at bay will be important, but the Vikings' offense will have to show up if they want to leave Ford Field victorious.

title: Vikings' Snap Count vs. Colts: Biggest Winners, Losers & Role Changes in Week 7
full_text:
It was a struggle, but the Vikings managed to defeat the Colts in Week 7 . It took all four quarters for the Purple and Gold to emerge victorious at U.S. Bank Stadium, but they stayed undefeated for the season.
The 16-10 win came from the combined efforts of several Vikings players and a good game plan from head coach Kevin O'Connell and defensive coordinator Brian Flores. Knowing who to use in those situations put Minnesota in good positions throughout the game.
There were clear winners and losers from the Minnesota Vikings' snap counts against the Indianapolis Colts. Let's take a look at some of the interesting parts of the snap counts from the Purple and Gold's Week 7 contest.
The Vikings have liked using tight end Ben Yurosek in situations where he can help as a pass blocker. That preference led to him playing 30 offensive snaps against the Colts, assuming the role previously held by Josh Oliver before his injury.
Yurosek's role seems to be primarily as a blocker, since he wasn't targeted with a pass. Despite that, he played over half of Minnesota's offensive snaps and nearly three times as many as fellow backup tight end Gavin Bartholomew. At the end of the game, Pro Football Focus awarded Yorusek solid grades for pass protection (75.3) and run blocking (69.5) .
In Minnesota's game against the Saints in Week 5, fullback Max Bredeson played 20 offensive snaps. That number dropped to 11 against the Colts on Sunday, making it seem like he isn't as big a part of the game plan.
Bredeson is losing pass-blocking snaps to Yurosek, and that should be concerning. Not only that, but Minnesota can't be giving their opposition a tell as to what type of play they are running, so to keep the threat of a pass, the team has to keep Bredeson off the field, even on some run plays.
Minnesota signed Kyle Van Noy this offseason to provide a backup/rotational edge rusher who can give Dallas Turner and Andrew Van Ginkel some rest during the game. However, he has played so well that the Vikings are forced to play him more.
Van Noy played 24 defensive snaps on Sunday, which is interesting since Van Ginkel only sat out seven snaps and Turner rested for 11. Since his 24 snaps add up to more than the 18 that he would have rotated in for, it is clear Flores wants to use him in packages alongside his fellow edge rushers.
It is sad to see Ivan Pace Jr. continue to be an afterthought in Minnesota's defense. Against the Colts, he played only four defensive snaps. This might be more than the two he had against the Saints in Week 5, but it still isn't a good sign for his future contribution.
Pace won't be taking any reps from his fellow interior linebackers. Blake Cashman and Eric Wilson played all but one snap on defense each, meaning there aren't opportunities for him to earn more time on the field.
DeeJay Dallas had one of the most interesting weeks of any Vikings player. On Saturday, Minnesota announced the veteran running back's release , but signed him to the practice squad and elevated him to the 53-man roster for the game against the Colts.
Dallas actually played in that game while rookie Demond Claiborne was inactive. He only had six snaps, but it says a lot that the Vikings released him , then signed and promoted him, and still chose him to play over a sixth-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.

title: 3 Studs & 2 Duds From Vikings' Week 7 Win Against the Colts
full_text:
The Vikings gave fans a scare in Week 7 . Coming into the game against the Colts with a 5-0 record, the Purple and Gold trailed until the fourth quarter, when the team was able to outscore their opponents 10-0.
The 16-10 victory over the Colts keeps the Vikings undefeated, but it took a team effort with several key players stepping up when others struggled to have a positive impact on the outcome of Sunday's game.
The defense once again did its job. Although it allowed a rushing touchdown to superstar running back Jonathan Taylor, defensive coordinator Brian Flores's unit continues its streak of not allowing a touchdown in the fourth quarter and finishing games strong.
With that in mind, let's look at the latest studs and duds for the Vikings as their perfect season continues.
It was a lot of fun watching defensive lineman Jalen Redmond work against the Colts' offensive line. He had a huge day for Minnesota, finishing with five tackles and a half-sack while registering a hit on Indianapolis quarterback Daniel Jones.
Redmond will be a priority restricted free agent after this season. The 27-year-old defender is making an extremely strong case this season to earn a huge payday to re-sign with the Purple and Gold while allowing the rookie defensive linemen time to develop.
Speaking of rookie defensive linemen, it is great that the Vikings are being patient with Caleb Banks , but now that Minnesota is seven weeks into the season, it is time to see more from the No. 18 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
Banks— who also limped off the field at one point (h/t ESPN 's Kevin Seifert)—finished the game against the Colts with one tackle. It is time to start expecting more from a first-round pick to start feeling good about his future instead of wondering when he will finally make an impact on a game.
Rookie DL Caleb Banks has been limping and is now coming off the field for medical attention.
Welcome back to the Vikings, Jordan Mason. His presence on Sunday was huge, since Aaron Jones has been a workhorse while dealing with a sprained ACL and left the game against the Colts after aggravating his knee .
Mason was the only running back besides Jones to take a snap against Indianapolis. He carried the ball 17 times for 68 yards, averaging 3.4 yards per carry. With him back in the lineup, Jones should have time to heal and rest.
The Vikings' starting center has been good this season despite a shaky training camp, but he struggled to protect starting quarterback Kyler Murray and create space in the run game against the Colts.
A 34-yard pass from Murray to Jordan Addison was erased in the fourth quarter due to a holding call. That penalty could have been disastrous for the Vikings if they hadn't turned it into a 52-yard Will Reichard field goal.
The MVP of this game was linebacker Blake Cashman. He did it all for the Vikings against Indianapolis.   leading the team with 12 tackles while defending four passes and hitting the opposing quarterback three times, registering two sacks.
Cashman was everywhere on the field on Sunday. In fact, the Vikings shared on X that he is the first player in over 20 years to have four pass defenses and two sacks in a game. The last time that happened was Alex Brown of the Bears in 2005.

title: Anthony Richardson Trade Is Worth Vikings' Consideration Under the Right Conditions
full_text:
After firing general manager Chris Ballard, the Colts have emerged as a potential trade partner for the Vikings in recent weeks. That said, there's no better time than now for the Vikings to try to acquire quarterback Anthony Richardson.
The Purple and Gold face uncertainty when it comes to the QB room past the 2026 NFL season since Kyler Murray is on a one-year deal and could benefit from adding a young quarterback with proven potential and starter experience.
Earlier this month, court records showed that Richardson was arrested on a misdemeanor marijuana possession charge following a traffic stop in Carmel, IN, on Oct. 12. He already slid down the Colts' depth chart after Daniel Jones's arrival, but this latest situation could be the straw that broke the camel's back.
For starters, unlike Indiana, Minnesota is a state where it is legal to consume recreational cannabis. This arrest wouldn't be a big deal for the Vikings, but it could significantly decrease the cost of trading for the former No. 4 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft.
Richardson hasn't started a game for the Colts since Week 15 of the 2024 season. Since then, he's played only 14 snaps for Indianapolis and doesn't seem to be in a position to work his way back into a starting role the Colts anytime soon.
On the other hand, having Richardson in the Vikings' quarterback room would add competition for whoever Minnesota brings in during the offseason—either via trade, free agency or the 2027 NFL Draft—and raise the floor for the future of the position.
As a pro, Richardson has been a flop. He completes only 50.6% of his passes and has thrown 11 touchdowns to 13 interceptions while being sacked 21 times for a 144-yard loss. Still, his mobility has been on display, as he's rushed for 634 yards and 10 touchdowns on 115 carries. In 2024, he was a top-10 QB when it came to rushing yards per game (45.4, 3rd), rushing TDs (six, T-3rd) and yards per carry (5.8, 9th) despite playing only 11 games.
Richardson will be an unrestricted free agent after the Colts declined the fifth-year option on his rookie deal. If they don't intend to bring him back, the Vikings should be interested in the potential success an experiment could bring.
Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell would need to take Richardson on as a project and keep developing him. Based on the potential that led to him being a top draft pick, there is hope he could turn his career around in Minnesota, especially if he's inspired by the Purple and Gold's ongoing success.
If O'Connell and the Vikings still believe, they need to talk to Colts interim GM Ed Dodds about acquiring Richardson for a potential Day 2 or 3 pick in next year's draft. They need to strike while his value is at an all-time low, and anything higher would be an issue.
Perhaps it was foreshadowing, but O'Connell's words to Richardson after the Vikings' 21–13 victory over the Colts on Nov. 3, 2024, suggest that he believes the young quarterback has the talent to become a great player in the league, despite his struggles.
O'Connell might be able to put that faith to the test first-hand soon.

title: Vikings Week 7 Report Card: Grading Every Position After Sunday's Win Over Colts
full_text:
If it ain't broke, well, maybe try and fix it a little bit. The Vikings—once again— extended their perfect season thanks to an elite defense and a good enough offense against the Colts on Sunday.
Minnesota defensive coordinator Brian Flores's unit showed why it is the best in the league, while the offense still looks to be figuring things out in the 16-10 victory. Still, a win is a win, and the Vikings move to 6-0 on the year with few complaints from the Purple and Gold's fanbase.
As is tradition around here, let's get into some grades for the polarizing team.
Kyler Murray looked a bit out of sorts coming out of the bye, missing multiple throws throughout the day. Still, despite the off-target throws and pedestrian 150 yards through the air, Murray saved his afternoon with 39 yards on the ground, including a late 35-yard bomb that led to the only touchdown of the day.
The offense with Murray under center is still a work in progress, it seems, and a generational defense has allowed them to take their sweet time. Still, at some point field goals aren't going to be enough, and Murray will have to bring his best with the high-octane Lions and Bills up next.
Jordan Mason returned and looked like he did exactly what he was supposed to do: move the chains and grind away at the defense. His long was just 12 yards, though, and the Vikings are still lacking that explosive playmaker in the backfield who would take the offense to the next level. Aaron Jones was mostly stymied on the day until slashing through on a late 17-yard rush that also sent him to the blue medical tent.
Jonathan Taylor, meanwhile, gashed the Vikings with a 5.3-yard average and gave them a potential glimpse of what a possible trade could look like . Mason and Jones form a solid duo, but with Mason's lack of explosion and Jones' knee hanging on by a thread, the ice is thinning in Minnesota's backfield.
We had a Jauan Jennings sighting, who doubled his catches and quadrupled his yards for the season in one afternoon. Whether or not the two-catch game was enough for the Vikings to hang up on any general managers who come calling , though, is another question, but it was a nice rebound out of the bye.
Justin Jefferson still has yet to notch 100 yards in a game this season after reeling in just 44 against the Colts, and either Murray or head coach Kevin O'Connell (or both) needs to remedy that soon.
T.J. Hockenson and Gavin Bartholomew are forming a nice little duo at the tight end position. Without Josh Oliver, the Vikings haven't missed a beat, and Hockenson is clearly a favorite of Murray's. He snagged the only touchdown of the day for the Vikings and is slowly building a case to return again in 2027.
Hockenson is first on the team in catches and second in yards after six games.
The interior of the Vikings' line struggled with the Colts' defensive front. Will Fries is cruising for a one-way ticket out of Minnesota next season after another rocky game, and Joe Huber may not be the final answer at left guard with the trade deadline approaching. The Minnesota front has allowed three or more sacks in five games this season, and the run game hasn't been especially fruitful either.
The Colts attacked the Vikings' run defense and enjoyed some decent success, racking up 154 yards on the day. Their best run—a 38-yard Taylor TD—went right at rookies Domonique Orange and Caleb Banks, who got blasted out of the way.
Jalen Redmond is still clearly head and shoulders above the rest of the D-line , and if there were a weakness on defense, their depth here might be it.
Blake Cashman might be the best linebacker in football right now.
Twelve tackles, two sacks and a near interception against Indy propelled the Vikings to a dominating defensive performance. While Dallas Turner may get the national spotlight, Cashman is on track to be a first-team All-Pro. Kyle Van Noy added valuable reserve snaps once again with a TFL and has been the best signing of the summer.
The Vikings' secondary wasn't really tested by Daniel Jones and the Colts, but Harrison Smith called game with a fourth-quarter interception (h/t NFL)—his 40th of his career and Jones's seventh of the year.
HARRISON SMITH GETS THE INT! VIKINGS ARE 6-0 ‼️ pic.twitter.com/stul8J8hWe
The Vikings still have yet to allow a fourth-quarter touchdown this season, and Smith ensured that streak continues into Week 8.
All dreams come to an end eventually, and Will Reichard's epic field-goal streak came to an end on a blocked kick in the second half. Still, his leg has won more games for the Vikings this year than the entire offense, and he'll continue to be one of the most important players on the roster. Myles Price shook off a brief injury scare, but had a mostly quiet day outside of his opening 46-yard return.

title: 3 Things That Mattered Most in Vikings' 16-10 Win Over Colts in Week 7
full_text:
MINNEAPOLIS, M.N. — The bye week came and went, leaving the Vikings to make their return to action on a chilly Sunday afternoon.
Legendary play-by-play announcer Paul Allen sounded the Gjallarhorn as the Vikings kicked off their third home game of the season in pursuit of their first 6-0 start since 2009. Former Vikings safety Cam Bynum received a warm welcome in his first game back at U.S. Bank Stadium after leaving for Indy in free agency in 2025. That said, the Vikings' 16-10 win over the Colts on Sunday was defined by another lackluster showing from the offense, as defense and special teams once again carried the team to victory.
As the perfect season continues, here's what mattered most in a game that left more questions than answers as the Vikings improved to 6-0 with a win against a potential trade partner .
If you were hoping that Sunday’s game would build on the hints of promise shown in Week 5’s matchup against the Saints, you certainly walked away disappointed.
The first drive of the game would paint a picture of what was to come, as the Vikings wasted a great opening kick return from Myles Price by unsuccessfully running four times in a row for a turnover on downs in Colts’ territory. Luckily, the O did just enough in the fourth quarter to secure the win. Kyler Murray flashed his legs on a 35-yard scramble before finding T.J. Hockenson in the end zone (h/t NFL) to celebrate National Tight End Day.
A TD for T.J. Hockenson on National Tight Ends Day 😌 INDvsMIN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/E0aOAL9M10
It’s hard to tell whether head coach Kevin O’Connell has become too cautious as a play caller or if Murray is being too cautious as a quarterback, but something has to change if the Vikings' offense wants to compete with some of the best teams in the league in November.
Can defensive coordinator Brian Flores win NFL Coach of the Year? No, but the Assistant Coach of the Year award may already have his name stamped on it.
Minnesota's defense stole the show once again, taking a quick break to allow potential future Viking Jonathan Taylor a chance to check out the U.S. Bank Stadium end zone. After that, the defense locked in, bringing a relentless attack on Daniel Jones all afternoon, resulting in four sacks and a total of 44 yards for the Colts’ offense. Veteran linebacker Blake Cashman in particular had a monster day (h/t NFL), with two sacks and nine tackles on the afternoon.
Blake Cashman steps up for the sack 😤 INDvsMIN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/MSl2dfO6k7
The Vikings’ defense continues to prove itself as a championship-level group. The only question is whether the offense can carry its own weight when Minnesota matches up against some of the NFL's top offensive units.
Kicker Will Reichard officially passed Gary Anderson’s franchise record of 35 straight successful field goals on Sunday, further proving the immense value he’s brought to the team since being drafted in 2024. On his next attempt, the third-year kicker had a 59-yarder blocked that left the home crowd in shock.
While Reichard’s heroics this season have been a fan favorite storyline, it’s further proof of the offense’s inability to consistently find the end zone. This trend desperately needs to shift if this team wants to contend in January. In the meantime, Vikings fans should hope that Reichard’s miss leads to a new streak that carries him clean through the playoffs.

title: Veteran OG Eligible to Return Off IR — Do Patriots Activate Him This Week?
full_text:
FOXBORO — Could the New England Patriots end up getting some help back this week against the Miami Dolphins? It's not out of the realm of possibilities.
Offensive guard Greg Van Roten , who has been on injured reserve for the last four game with a thigh injury, is eligible to return to the active roster this week. Speaking to reporters Monday afternoon, Mike Vrabel shared that the team has considered making that transaction this week.
"Probably won't see him today, but maybe this week, we'll see where that goes" the head coach said prior to practice. "I think him and (safety) Dell (Pettus) are eligible potentially to try and get back out there and kind of see where that goes, but we'll have to make a decision."
Van Roten is one of several offensive linemen who's gotten banged up this season. After Mike Onwenu broke his ankle in Week 2 against the Pittsburgh Steelers, Van Roten stepped in to help fill that hole at right guard. He would practice as the starter all week in practice and start against the Jacksonville Jaguars the following game.
But Van Roten would get hurt in that game and be ruled out. He'd be replaced by converted tackle Walter Rouse, and was placed on IR two days later.
The Patriots have also seen Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and Ben Brown (knee) get hurt in subsequent weeks. Last week against the Chicago Bears, the Patriots rolled with Rouse and Matt Pryor as their starting guards.
"I think the protection, I mean, I’m sure it could have been better. We just had some critical penalties," Vrabel said postgame. "Being able to handle the environment, third-and-short, whatever it may have been, and those are certainly unfortunate. That’s just beating ourselves. But I think I mean, I’m sure they played okay. I’m sure they played hard. Just without seeing it though it’s hard to say. But I know they competed."
Pryor has experience all over the offensive line and could earn a larger role if Van Roten doesn't return.
"Matt's done a nice job," Vrabel saaid. "Matt's come in, he's protected well. I think that he's still getting comfortable, but he's ... tough to get around. He's got heavy hands and he gives us a chance most of the time."
The Patriots could end up getting Brown back this week, as he suited up for practice as reporters were in the locker room. Should Van Roten return, he'll have three weeks to be activated to the 53-man roster or his season is over.
The Patriots will be back on the practice field in two days, which will be another opportunity for them to make a decision on the veteran guard. They also have one more week to make a decision on tackle Marcus Bryant, who's been designated to return off of IR with an ankle injury .

title: Patriots Release P Bryce Baringer from IR: Here's Why They Did It
full_text:
The New England Patriots are reportedly making a roster move on the special teams front.
As reported by NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the Patriots are releasing veteran punter Bryce Baringer. The 27-year-old, who has been the team's top punter since being drafted in 2023, was currently on IR for an injury suffered in the preseason.
Baringer was the Patriots' sixth round pick in 2023 and won the job as a rookie. In the seasons that's followed, he punted in 51 games, tallying 219 total punts for 10,500 yards. He had not missed a game prior to his injury.
In the Patriots' second preseason game against the Philadelphia Eagles, Baringer would leave the game and be replaced by rookie quarterback Behren Morton. He would be placed on IR as part of roster cuts, but without a designation to return.
All season, the Patriots have been struck by the injury bug — leaving a numbers crunch for them to deal with.
They're only permitted to have eight players return from IR in the middle of the season, and have already used two designations on wide receiver A.J. Brown and offensive tackle Marcus Bryant. Other players that are expected to contribute this year — including Mack Hollins, Romeo Doubs, Alijah Vera-Tucker, Greg Van Roten and Dell Pettus — have all been put on IR and could return by the end of the season.
That means that the Patriots had to make a decision on Baringer , who was in the final year of his four-year rookie contract. Instead of letting him sit on the sidelines for the rest of the year, the Patriots do right by Baringer and releasing him. He's now free to sign with any other team.
Baringer was also one of several Patriots remaining who had played for Bill Belichick before he left after the 2023 season (Christian Gonzalez, DeMario Douglas, Marcus Jones, Rhamondre Stevenson, Brenden Schooler, Christian Elliss, Mike Onwenu, Hunter Henry, Christian Barmore and Jeremiah Pharms Jr. still remain with the organization).
Releasing Baringer leaves just Wishnowsky on the roster as the only punter. Wishnowsky, who signed with the Patriots' practice squad ahead of Week 1, has been the lone punter this season and has played relatively well.
Originally starting as a practice squad elevation, Wishnowsky was signed to the 53-man roster on Sept 22 . He's played in all seven games, punting the ball 22 times for 1,037 yards and three touchbacks.
Reports from Schultz and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport indicate that Baringer is fully healthy, meaning that the Patriots would have needed to move on from Wishnowsky if they wanted to bring Baringer up to the roster. It doesn't seem like Baringer would have lost the job had he not gotten injured, but it's hard to pull Wishnowsky out after he's been punting the ball well.
The Patriots have also reportedly made a move to their practice squad, re-signing edge rusher Jose Ramirez. They'll need to make room for him.

title: Calm Down Patriots Fans, A.J. Brown Will Be Just Fine — And Here's Why
full_text:
FOXBORO — A.J. Brown cost the New England Patriot s two draft picks, including a first rounder, this summer via trade. So far through three games, he hasn't lived up to that trade package — recording just nine receptions, 101 yards and no touchdowns.
Since returning from IR with his high-ankle sprain, Brown has only caught three passes against the New York Jets and Chicago Bears on 16 targets (including 10 in his return against New York). To put it bluntly, it hasn't worked out so far.
Head coach Mike Vrabel, speaking on WEEI's The Greg Hill Show, was asked about if he has any concerns for his top wideout as he looks to try and find more consistency on the field.
"No, I don’t have any concern," Vrabel said. "No."
Is it time to panic about Brown? Like Vrabel said, no. The former Pro Bowler will be able to figure it out and start stacking up some good days — but he'll need to do it soon. This week, the Patriots will play host to the Miami Dolphins, who won their first game of the season yesterday. It's a very winnable game for the Patriots and a real opportunity for Brown to make his mark.
During the summer, his budding connection with Drake Maye was one of the many highlights of training camp. Brown's ability to go up for balls and come down with them was going to be a godsend for this offense. It hasn't come to fruition yet.
Against the Jets, Brown caught three balls — while dropping several more. That performance alone got him plenty of grief online, but it was clear the rust was being shaken off (even though Brown won't say that).
"I thought that he dropped a few passes, and then the other night there was a contested catch that — I’ve seen him make those plays in the past, I’ve seen those plays get called for DPI, and I’ve seen those plays be good plays by the defense down the field," Vrabel said. "So, I don’t think anybody has to press here or anything else. I think we just have to get back into a rhythm offensively with the guys that we have."
Exactly. The Patriots offense, one that was a bit out of sorts against the Jets and very streaky one week later, needs to start firing on all cylinders. Injuries at the wide receiver position (Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs are both on IR) haven't helped, but that's why Brown is here.
But the reason to be confident in Brown is centered around his quarterback. Maye is playing some great football right now and has seemed to break out of his early season struggles. Now, instead of playing sloppy football, the 24-year-old is making play after play after play .
A lot of those plays have gone to Rhamondre Stevenson , Hunter Henry, Eli Raridon and DeMario Douglas — all players who haven't missed extended time with injuries. Brown could easily join that party.
His slow start won't last all season. Sooner or later, he'll break out and grab 100+ receiving yards and a touchdown. Maybe it's this week at home.

title: Most Important Patriots Postgame From Week 7 — And What They Mean Going Forward
full_text:
Sitting at 4-3, the New England Patriots aren't lighting the NFL on fire. But they've played well in their wins, and in their Thursday Night Football loss to the Chicago Bears , they also had enough chances to try and win the game.
Instead, a Superman effort from the Bears offense — mainly Caleb Williams and Luther Burden III — sent the Patriots home with a 30-24 defeat. It was a game that the Patriots could have pulled away in, but too many opportunities went to the wayside.
"I think it's hard to say, 'Shoulda. Woulda. Coulda.' I definitely think we — I'm proud of the guys for the effort," Drake Maye said. "I think we did some good things and we got a lot of stuff to clean up. And we got to get back from the rest this weekend and get back after we had another one on the road, a division game."
Here are some of the biggest postgame quotes from the Patriots , both from the podium and inside the locker room, after their primetime loss to Caleb Williams and the Bears.
For most of the game, the Patriots trailed. They got behind big in the first half, but Rhamondre Stevenson's heroics to close the opening frame got them within a score. But the Bears roared out of the locker room to another scoring drive. It continued to be back-and-forth, but the Patriots were just one step away for most of the game.
Mike Vrabel on the offense's productivity: "We moved it however we needed to move it and sometimes you are going to have days like that. I thought we'd be able to run it a little better. We didn't, but then our best players were putting the ball in good spots most of the time and making good decisions. That's how it goes, we'd have liked to run the ball a little bit better. But, it didn't happen tonight."
Drake Maye on his end zone interception: "Yeah, I mean, we hit the same thing, the same exact play, it was later in the game. So, I like my chances in there and just — yeah, it's frustrating. So I know that was a big turning point in the game and I know I let my team down."
Christian Gonzalez on dealing with an illness throughout the game: "I woke up and I though it was allergies, and it was a lot more. ... It ain't none at the end of the day."
Hunter Henry on rookie tight end Eli Raridon: "(He's) great, man. Just continuing to get better and growing that confidence. A lot of fun to play with."
A.J. Brown on how he saw Chicago's defense attack him: "I think they did a really good job. Early on, (offensive coordinator) Josh (McDaniels) tried to do a really good job of getting me involved and Drake just was taking what they were giving. They were trying to take me away early on, and that's just kind of how the game played."
Charles Woods on the difficulty of defending Caleb Williams: "Anytime a quarterback that's mobile as him gets out the pocket, they definitely put stress on DBs. Then we have to cover the second play."
The Patriots played two games in five days, and looked worn down — especially after all the injuries that struck. They certainly needed the three days off that they were given this weekend.
But now a new challenge emerges, and it's about bouncing back to play a winnable game against the Miami Dolphins. As it stands right now, the Dolphins sit in the cellar of the AFC East with a 0-5 record and really don't look like they have anything going for them long term.
After a loss against a Super Bowl-like team in Chicago, the Patriots can't afford to look past a team that should beat without any issues. It starts with Maye playing clean football again, the defense wrapping up and making the tackles they need to and the offense capitalizing on their opportunities.
We'll see in a week's time if the Patriots were able to flush the primetime loss and get back into the win column.

title: Patriots Legend Pokes Fun at Christian Gonzalez's Uniform Number
full_text:
There might not be a position for the New England Patriots that's so consistently good every single season more than the cornerback position. Ever since their days in the American Football League, the Patriots have always seemed to have a shutdown cornerback.
That trend has carried over to the present day, as Christian Gonzalez has cemented himsrlf as the latest addition to the shutdown cornerback lineage. But still, there's one thing that makes him stand out from the rest ... and it's drawn some jokes from another member of that cornerback fraternity.
Ty Law, arguably the greatest Patriots cornerback of all time and a Pro Football Hall of Fame inductee, kicked off the team's unofficial theme of the top cornerback wearing No. 24. Since Law donned the number as the Patriot's first round draft choice in 1995, Super Bowl champions Darrelle Revis (2014) and Stephon Gilmore (2017-2020) also wore it.
It's become part of the fabric of New England. Instead of retiring the number for Law, the Patriots have had it passed on. But Gonzalez — who certainly could stack up — blazed his own path, choosing No. 0 as his jersey in 2024.
That drew some jokes from Law this week.
On the fourth episode of "Forged in Foxborough," Law spoke about Gonzalez — who was seen signing his record-setting four-year, $135 million contract extension — and his choice of uniform numbers.
"Because of the success that I had with the number, 24, everybody's always gonna compare to me," said Law, who was inducted into the Patriots Hall of Fame in 2014.
"Then you had Darrelle Revis. He come in, 24. Super Bowl. Then you got Stephon Gilmore, 24. We were all those type of corners and we just happened to all be wearing the same number. Christian Gonzalez, yeah, he broke the rule dammit, you supposed to be wearing 24 Christian."
Gonzalez's career has been filled with a lot of uniform numbers. After being assigned No. 50 during his first training camp, he donned No. 19 in the preseason. Then the regular season hit, and he wore No. 6 for the first few games of his career.
He would miss most of the season with a torn labrum, and then become the first Patriots player ever to wear No. 0 the following year. When Gonzalez was drafted in 2023, Joshuah Bledsoe was wearing No. 24. He'd be released the following summer and undrafted rookie Dell Pettus would end up taking it (he's still wearing it to this day).
"He's making his name on his own right being the same type of player," Law continued. "Outside of Christian not wearing 24, that's a bad boy. He's gon' start his own thing."
Gonzalez has been off to a great start to his 2026 season, playing in five games and racking up 15 tackles and five pass breakups. He's yet to grab his first interception, but limited stars Jaxon Smith-Njigba and D.K. Metcalf in his matchups against them.
He's been a major part of a Patriots defense that's been the best part of the team seven weeks in. His contract extension, the largest in franchise history, got done before Week 1 in Seattle — helping set the tone for how the team wants to lock down their homegrown talents.
"We're excited to have him for hopefully a long time," head coach Mike Vrabel said.
Law, Revis and Gilmore all won Super Bowls with the Patriots, and now it's up to Gonzalez to join that elite group — this time with his own uniform number.

title: 3 Positions the Patriots May Address at the Trade Deadline
full_text:
After seven weeks, the New England Patriots are sitting in the thick of the AFC postseason race. They're 4-3, coming off a hard-fought TNF game against the Chicago Bears and now have a long break before their divisional battle with the Miami Dolphins.
But this team is far from perfect, and there are some holes that could be plugged up by the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Could the Patriots swing a trade to add some new help for the late-season push?
Here are three positions that the Patriots could potentially look at to bring a new face in via trade.
The Patriots have three running backs on the roster right now, so it might not make a lot of sense to add another one to the mix. But other than Rhamondre Stevenson, the Patriots haven't been able to get consistent week-after-week production from their backups.
TreVeyon Henderson, who was expected to have a large role this year in the passing attack, has really struggled on the ground — and carried the ball just three times on Thursday. Corey Kiner, a hard runner, just doesn't have the NFL experience yet for a larger workload.
So maybe the Patriots look to find some help with a receiving option. Tony Pollard, who was rumored to potentially join the Patriots through a trade last season, has 349 yards and one touchdown on a bad Tennessee Titans team. He fits the mold of a Josh McDaniels running back in this offense.
Injuries have depleted the interior of New England's offensive line . Mike Onwenu broke his ankle, Greg Van Roten was placed on IR one week later, Aliijah Vera-Tucker was just placed on IR this week and Ben Brown is dealing with an ankle injury. It's not a deep unit right now.
The Patriots have gotten inspiring play from backups Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse, but that pair — one that wasn't even with the team during the preseason — could be improved on ahead of the postseason. So maybe the Patriots try to swing for the fences with a new starter.
This one might be a pipe dream, but Quenton Nelson has been one of the league's top guards since being drafted by the Indianapolis Colts. If the Patriots want to try and get some additional protection for Drake Maye once the weather turns colder, finding a starting guard could help.
Another position banged up, the Patriots were without Carlton Davis , Channing Canada and Karon Prunty against the Bears. Charles Woods has stepped up in Davis' absence, and both Marcus Jones and Christian Gonzalez have been their usual selves. Kindle Vildor is also on the 53-man roster, rounding out that position group for now.
There is always room to try and bring in some new blood to shut down some of the receivers coming up on the Patriots' schedule. They're tasked to go against Justin Jefferson, Jaylen Waddle, D.J. Moore, Christian Watson and Garrett Wilson later this year, and while those guys will certainly be lined up against Gonzalez, another injury could be dangerous.
There are several guys who have seen their names tossed around trade talks, including Philadelphia's Kelee Ringo and Riq Woolen, Tampa Bay's Zyon McCollum and Los Angeles' Donte Jackson. A lot of this would depend on the health of Davis , who's dealt with a neck injury for the last few games.

"It's a thin margin when you play good teams," Mike Vrabel said postgame. "We did some good things. But again, didn't do enough. We didn't get enough stops in the red zone and we didn't convert our red zone opportunity the one time, so. That's probably the difference in the game."
