title: Giants Ride Cam Skattebo’s 124 Rushing Yards to a 27-21 OT Win Over Texans
full_text:
The New York Giants entered Week 7 of the NFL season needing a spark in their running game.
On their first overtime possession, running backs Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary delivered an big bang, the duo combining for 72 ground yards in just two plays, as the Giants defeated the Houston Texans 27-21 at Reliant Stadium.
Making his first start for New York after being acquired via trade with the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 28, quarterback J.J. McCarthy demonstrated calm composure while showcasing his skill set. The Michigan product finished the game by finishing 20-for-28 for 252 yards.
Skattebo rushed for 124 yards on 17 carries and one touchdown, in his return to the offensive mix after being held without a carry in Week 6 against the Saints. As for Singletary, his 41 total yards included the 30-yard game-winning score.
For the Texans, quarterback C.J. Stroud went 17-for-28 with 153 yards and two touchdowns, while running back Woody Marks ran 19 times for 66 yards.
With the win, the Giants improve to 4-2-1 through seven games in the 2026 NFL season.
The Texans used their home-field advantage on their opening drive, gaining 25 yards on six plays. New York’s blitz kept Stroud from logging big gains, and a four-yard pass to Xavier Hutchinson was ruled incomplete after officials determined Hutchinson trapped the ball rather than catching it.
Ultimately, the added yardage meant little to Houston kicker Ka’imi Fairbairn, who made a 58-yarder to give the Texans a 3-0 lead.
The Giants wasted little time in responding, as McCarthy led his team on a nine-play, 66-yard drive on the team’s first offensive possession of the day. Skattebo contributed a six-yard run to take the Giants near midfield.
Still, the drive was unquestionably highlighted by a 42-yard deep ball from McCarthy to receiver Malik Nabers, who beat Texans cornerback Kamari Lassiter in one-on-one coverage.
J.J. DEEP to LEEK!! 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/djyIdZteKI
On the ensuing snap, running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. rushed for the two-yard touchdown, giving the Giants a 7-3 lead.
While the Giants couldn't add to their advantage before the end of the first quarter — due to a missed 56-yard attempt from rookie Dominic Zvada — the Texans earned the first points of the second quarter on a seven-play, 39-yard drive. The series ended with a 57-yard field goal from Fairbairn, cutting New York’s lead to 7-6.
Big Blue responded once again on the ensuing drive, as McCarthy led them 78 yards on nine plays for their second scoring drive of the afternoon. The Giants were paced by an 11-yard run from Skattebo and a 17-yard reception by Nabers.
The gem of the series took place on 1st-and-10 from the Houston 30, when McCarthy connected with tight end Thomas Fidone II. The 2025 seventh-rounder hauled in a 29-yard pass, his first NFL reception.
Thomas Fidone WIDE OPEN 🔥 #NationalTightEndsDay 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/iJYPOQbKfC
Two plays later, Giants quarterback Jameis Winston took a one-yard sneak into the end zone, extending the lead to 14-6.
Houston, however, was determined to prove itself beyond its 2-4 record. Stroud led the Texans on an eight-play, 90-yard drive as the clock wound down in the second quarter.
The highlight of the series came on a 43-yard strike to receiver Tank Dell, who was playing in his first NFL game since Week 16 of the 2024 season. Stroud capped the series by finding Marvin Harrison Jr. for a six-yard score, his first as a member of the Texans. Houston’s two-point conversion was successful, tying the game at 14.
With less than a minute remaining in the half, the Giants had a chance to take the lead — thanks in part to a 27-yard completion from McCarthy to Nabers. Unfortunately for Big Blue, Zvada missed a 44-yard attempt (his second misfire of the day), keeping the score locked at 14-14 at the half.
The Giants and Texans traded defensive stands and miscues before beginning a 14-play, 80-yard drive late in the third quarter. Despite a 14-yard completion from McCarthy to receiver Malachi Fields, New York’s ground game dominated the series — particularly Skattebo.
The second-year rusher sparked the drive with a 19-yard run from his team’s own 29-yard line. The Giants capped the drive with a 16-yard touchdown run from Skattebo, complete with a celebratory backflip. Following the Zvada extra point, the Giants took a 21-14 lead, while draining 8:18 from the clock.
HE WILL NOT BE DENIED 😤 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/ReAKg8Thp0
With a defensive stand needed to keep Houston in check, the Giants defense yielded 48 yards on nine plays. Texans receiver Xavier Hutchinson delivered an 11-yard carry, taking his team into New York’s red zone. Stroud capped the drive with a three-yard touchdown pass to Hutchinson. Fairbairn added the point-after to tie the game at 21 with 52 seconds remaining in regulation.
After winning the coin toss, the Giants chose to kick, giving the Texans first possession in overtime. New York held its ground against the home team, forcing a punt after only three plays. Linebacker Kayvon Thibodeaux nearly intercepted Stroud on 2nd-and-10, but couldn't secure the pass. Following that sequence, New York got its chance to score in the game’s extra period.
On 2nd-and-1 from their own 28-yard line, the Giants' run game took over.
Following a nine-yard pass completion from McCarthy to Nabers, Skattebo ripped the longest run for the Giants this season. The 42-yard run put Big Blue deep within Texans territory. Reserve back Devin Singletary showed why he is called “Motor” as he powered his way to the end zone for the 30-yard touchdown run.
SINGLETARY SEALS IT 🔥 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/NEB091GEyG
FINAL: Giants 27, Texans 21
Giants running back Tyrone Tracy suffered a hamstring injury in the second quarter after completing a seven-yard run. After limping off the field to the sideline, Tracy was deemed questionable to return. He returned to action in the second half.
Giants linebacker Zaire Barnes remains a force on special teams. The third-year veteran added one  special teams tackle against the Texans.
Barnes entered this Week 7 matchup tied for the league lead with 10 special teams tackles. Barnes has recorded at least 1 special teams tackle in every game this season and also forced a fumble in Week 3 on the opening kickoff.
The Philadelphia Eagles (2-4) will host the Dallas Cowboys (2-4) at Lincoln Financial Field for a Monday Night Football matchup. The final game of Week 7 will kick off at 8:15 p.m. ET.
The Washington Commanders (1-4-1) are on a Week 7 bye. They return in Week 8, hosting the Eagles for a Sunday Night Football showdown at Northwest Stadium.
The Giants will attempt to get healthy during their Week 8 bye. They will return to action on Nov. 8 for a Week 9 game against Philadelphia at Lincoln Financial Field. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET.

title: Giants vs. Texans Live Updates: Score, Analysis and Highlights From Week 7
full_text:
The New York Giants (3-2-1) travel to Houston on Sunday to face the Texans (2-4), with redemption on their minds.
Last week, in their 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints (a game the Giants had no business losing but somehow found a way to), Big Blue did not play well in any phase.
The goal this week was to clean up a lot of the problems across all three phases, including defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson’s very direct characterization of players not running to the ball as “traitors” on defense , the embarrassing communication issues on special teams, and the lethargic rushing attack, which head coach John Harbaugh hopes someone will take the bull by the horns .
It won’t be easy. Despite their 2-4 record, the Texans are just starting to get into a groove. They’ve won their last two games, against the Titans and Jaguars, and have the league’s 10th-best offense and fourth-best passing offense. Their defense is probably the best the Giants have faced since their Week 2 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
But the Giants, who this week made the switch to quarterback J.J. McCarthy, are hoping the offense, which has struggled since its Week 1 domination of Dallas, gets a much-needed injection of adrenaline.
McCarthy, who had a successful, extensive showing in last week’s loss to the Saints (albeit against a softer defense), more closely matches the skill set of injured starter Jaxson Dart.
That means the 20-30% of the playbook (the RPO and designed runs) that the Giants had to drop when they lost Dart will be restored. The hope is that bringing that element back will help the lethargic rushing attack.
There are other factors to consider. For one, the health of the team’s top three offensive tackles (Andrew Thomas, Jermaine Eluemunor and Marcus Mbow) is a big question mark, with the latter two listed as questionable for Sunday.
Suffice it to say, this is not a good week for the tackles to be gimpy, not with an afternoon against NFL sack leaders Will Anderson Jr., Danielle Hunter and Jadeveon Clowney on the dance card.
On the other side of the ball, the Giants defense just lost another key starter in inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds, the defense’s “quarterback.” That’s not good news for a run defense that ranks 29th in yards allowed per game (135.5) and 31st in average rushing yards allowed per play (5.05).
If there is a hint of good news for Giants fans to lean on, it’s that even if the Giants lose this week, they will still be in first place in the NFC East. Dallas and Philadelphia are playing each other, and Washington has a bye.
Still, it would make for a much better afternoon if the Giants can go into their Week 8 bye with an upset win, giving themselves and their division lead a little more padding.

title: Brandon Stephens Is Slowly Becoming an Unnecessary Jets Headache
full_text:
Fresh off a humiliating 28-25 loss to the previously winless Dolphins on Sunday, the Jets find themselves at 2-5 as they continue to struggle to put positive results together with a much-improved roster on paper.
In that loss alone, the Jets had a 100-yard rusher, a 100-yard receiver, a defense that surrendered just seven second-half points and a quarterback who went for 287 yards and three touchdowns. That ultimately did not matter in a rock-bottom performance that featured another poorly executed game plan from the coaching staff.
While head coach Aaron Glenn deserves much of the blame for his continued struggles with game management, it is still up to the players on the field to do their part and make a strong impression.
Now in his second season with Gang Green, cornerback Brandon Stephens is one of those examples: he's someone who is exceptional against the run and versatile at multiple positions, but has struggled to create turnovers in his career.
In his last four games alone, Stephens has allowed opposing QBs to go 11-of-16 (68.8%) for 167 yards and a TD when targeted, which is good for an average of 15.2 yards per catch. For reference, he only allowed seven completions on 13 targets for 78 yards (11.1 yards per catch) in his first three games.
With a career average of 12.1 yards per catch allowed, that is not exactly the type of performance he needs to be displaying in Year 2 of a three-year contract.
It's safe to say, Stephens needs to step up—and soon.
To his credit, Stephens does have three broken-up passes in the last four games, but he has also failed to come away with a single interception this season and none at all since he recorded the only two picks of his career in 2023 with the Ravens.
Sure, the Jets have only one interception as a team this season (Minkah Fitzpatrick), so it is not like Stephens is alone in that regard. This was also a defense that gave up 28 points to a team that hadn't led this season and couldn't stop the run if it tried, in a disappointing all-around performance by the entire group against the Dolphins.
That said, a lot more is expected from Stephens as a starting corner alongside Azareye'h Thomas. For comparison, Thomas has 33 tackles, two tackles for loss and five passes defended. Stephens, meanwhile, has 19 tackles, one tackle for loss, six passes defended and one fumble recovery in the same number of games.
While a player's success is not solely determined by those respective stats, there is clearly some room for improvement for a starting corner with the talent that Stephens possesses. According to Pro Football Focus , Stephens has the 38th-ranked overall grade (65.1), as well as the 27th-ranked coverage grade (68.1) and 53rd-ranked run-defense grade (61.8) out of 103 qualified CBs.
That is an indication of the potential that Stephens brings, but it has not been enough as of late with the Jets facing an uphill climb the rest of the season.
He is still under contract with a $14 million cap hit in 2027 , per Spotrac , but the Jets have a $12 million out in the offseason that they can use if they feel he hasn't done enough to justify keeping him at that cap hit for his final year. Adding that to the over $96.8 million that New York is projected to have would help general manager Darren Mougey be one of the most powerful spenders in March.
Along with his durability and run-defense skills, Stephens has shown flashes of high-level play in heavy man-coverage schemes throughout his career, but he has mostly been inconsistent when he is isolated without any safety help. That said, he has the prototypical size (6'1", 215 lbs) for his position and the athletic traits suited for press-man when those opportunities arise.
While Fitzpatrick has the team's lone interception this season and safety Dane Belton has proved to be the best offseason signing with a team-high 56 tackles, the rest of the secondary has not really stood out on a consistent basis. Even Jarvis Brownlee Jr., who has been a bright spot for the defense but was a healthy scratch in Week 7, ranks lower than Stephens in overall grade (60.3), coverage grade (63.1) and run-defense grade (58.2) from PFF .
That alone should not measure a player's success, but it does show things could be a lot worse for Stephens.
With that in mind, he will likely get more opportunities coming his way against the Raiders' sixth-ranked scoring attack (26.1 ppg) on Sunday. If Stephens cannot figure out how to create some turnovers and get more consistent stops, he may not be around Gotham much longer.

title: Biggest Decision Aaron Glenn Got Wrong vs. Dolphins (And What Needs to Change in Week 8)
full_text:
Just when it looked like things could not get much worse for the Jets this season, a humiliating 28-25 loss to the previously winless Dolphins took place on Sunday and dropped them to 2-5 in what is shaping up to be another season to forget in Gotham.
While injuries to key players like running back Breece Hall (groin) continue to plague this roster , the Jets finally had their top-three receivers on the field with Adonai Mitchell returning from a finger injury and appeared poised to take care of business on Sunday.
Even though rookie Omar Cooper Jr. shined once again (five catches, 115 yards, one touchdown) and running back Braelon Allen impressed (17 carries, 104 yards), the Jets immediately fell behind and never recovered after allowing the Dolphins to score on each of their first two possessions.
Coming into Week 7, the Dolphins were the only team that had not led at any point this season and lost RB1 De'Von Achane (torn ACL) for the season. On Sunday, they never trailed and Ollie Gordon II went for 103 yards and a TD on 23 carries, which proved vital in one of the key matchups going into the game .
That said, this was still a game the Jets were in position to win if they executed better in key moments. Look no further than the end-of-half TD from the Dolphins prior to the break, and how Glenn once again paid the price for his baffling clock management.
Following a punt, the Jets had the Dolphins backed up at their own nine-yard line, only trailing by seven points with 8:44 remaining in the first half. Not only did the defense allow quarterback Malik Willis to convert a fourth-and-two to keep the drive going, but they also let the Dolphins take the clock all the way down to six seconds and stretch their lead to 21-7.
Despite having all three timeouts in his pocket, Glenn refused to use either of them. It was one thing to allow Miami to go all the way down the field in methodical fashion, but why not start using the timeouts following the two-minute warning to at least give your offense enough time to try to score some points?
Instead, Willis ran in for the two-yard score (h/t NFL) and extended the Dolphins' lead to 14 just before the break.
Malik Willis lowers his shoulder for the touchdown MIAvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TVRwL1sULm
Glenn is now 0-8 against divisional opponents and has been outscored 107-6 in the final two minutes of the first half in his 24 games as HC of the Jets. Chalk this up to the latest instance of him fumbling a game away on the sidelines and the clock management woes that have plagued his tenure in Gang Green.
To make matters worse, Glenn called a timeout within the first five minutes of the second half to prevent his offense from getting a delay of game. A back-breaking 63-yard TD pass from Willis to rookie WR Caleb Douglas put the finishing touches on the game late in the fourth quarter, but the bizarre timeout usage—or lack thereof at the end of the first half—helped put the Jets in that predicament and made Glenn's seat even hotter than it was entering the day .
The frustration did not reside solely on Glenn's shoulders as offensive coordinator Frank Reich once again failed to get WR1 Garrett Wilson involved in the game plan. Worst of all, the Jets had a first-and-goal at the one-yard line, but had to settle for a 33-yard field goal instead of tying the game. Gang Green was an improved 3-of-4 in the red zone, but not without some more issues that simply cannot happen in a close game at home.
That said, this was a game in which the Dolphins were in control throughout, which only made Glenn's decision to hang onto the timeouts that much more puzzling when he had the opportunity to at least give the offense the ball back on a day that a lot of positive things were happening compared to recent weeks.
As the Jets remain home to face the 3-4 Raiders on Sunday, the pressure remains firmly on Glenn after reaching a new low against the Dolphins . Although Las Vegas has been competitive so far, its defense is 29th in the league in points allowed per game (28.1 PPG), so perhaps the Jets can find something and take advantage of that weakness.
However, as ESPN' s Rich Cimini noted after the Week 7 loss, Glenn is the ninth coach since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger "to begin his career with eight straight division losses" and "the fifth coach to do it in the last 30 seasons (Jim Schwartz, Matt Eberflus, Pat Shurmur, Leslie Frazier)."
Aaron Glenn becomes the 9th head coach since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger to begin his career with eight straight division losses. He’s the 5th coach to do it in the last 30 seasons (Jim Schwartz, Matt Eberflus, Pat Shurmur, Leslie Frazier). ESPN Research. #Jets
While that only applies to divisional opponents, that is not the type of list you want to be on, and it's another reason why Glenn's seat continues to reach a boiling point . Going forward, his focus must be on getting off to better starts, executing key plays and being more aggressive with his game and clock management.
After all, the offense was not bad on Sunday, especially when you consider the bad spot it was put in, with the defense surrendering the TD drives to begin the game. Glenn simply needs to be more aggressive with his play-calling and come out of the gates swinging with something to prove.
If not, it could be more of the same with a tougher schedule on the horizon as another season slips away for the Jets.

title: Jets Week 7 Awards Paint Grim Picture for What's to Come in Gotham
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Another season. Another year for Jets fans to tune out the organization before Halloween .
Of course, can you really blame them after Sunday's loss?
New York went into a home contest against a winless Miami team and got outplayed and coached for the entire contest. The Jets' 28-25 loss not only dropped them to 2-5 , but it made people wonder whether they will ever become a winning organization again.
As always, we have some Jets awards to hand out after a humiliating loss like that. Let's get to it.
After the 2025 season, the excuse was that Glenn was a first-year coach. He just needed time to get players who fit his scheme. After Week 2, the excuse was that it was just a single loss and the team was competing at a high level. In Week 6, the excuse was that the Jets' losses came at the hands of playoff teams, not inferior opponents.
The reality is that the Jets under Aaron Glenn are what their record is. They are not just 5-19 in a year and a half, but they are 0-8 in the AFC East. They have lost blowouts and close games. They never seem to make the right play or call to win.
That is the lone takeaway under Glenn as a head coach. After Sunday's loss to Miami, in which the team was outcoached by a first-year staff and outplayed by a 0-5 roster, the question of whether Glenn can turn around the team has been answered .
And it seems like it will lead to an inevitable coaching search again.
Omar Cooper Jr. is a future star in the NFL. All he has to do is stay healthy.
New York watched their 30th overall pick lead the team in targets for a second straight game, and he was rewarded with a six-catch (h/t NFL), 115-yard game and a score. Along the way, he was the first Jets rookie to record back-to-back 100-yard games since Al Toon in 1985.
Here comes Omar Cooper Jr. 👀 MIAvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/dSXEZjYYD4
Quarterback Geno Smith shared high praise for rookie WR after the game.
"(Cooper) played a great game," Smith said. "Obviously, we all can do a lot better in some areas, but (he) made plays when necessary. We all fought to the end, but it just wasn’t enough."
So long as Cooper continues to make big plays and be hard to bring down after the catch, he must be New York's second receiving option behind Garrett Wilson .
It's inconceivable. Superstar receivers across the NFL are all schemed open and targeted more than other players around them. Garrett Wilson seems to be the only receiver whose offense is deliberately looking the other way when he's open .
Wilson saw just three targets all game on Sunday and recorded two receptions. Throughout the contest, he was running open over the middle of the field, but either the quarterback's read or final decision went to a different player.
That cannot happen in the modern NFL. If the star receiver is open, the team needs to get him the ball because it's the best chance they have at winning. It should be no coincidence that the team's offense has failed in key areas each of the last two weeks, with Wilson coming behind Braelon Allen in targets and touches.
Offensive coordinator Frank Reich and Smith have a role in this. Even if Smith touted his chemistry with New York's top wideout.
"I think we’ve got great chemistry," Smith said. "When we get our opportunities, the plays are there. We’re still building. That’s just a part of the process, but so far, I think we have tremendous chemistry."
Smith can tout his chemistry with Wilson all he wants. The tape says something different . And it's completely unthinkable to see how the Jets are the lone team struggling to get the ball to their best player.
Going into Sunday, the Dolphins were the second-worst passing offense in the league and the eighth-best rushing unit. The goal for New York's defense was simple: get pressure on Malik Willis and get extra guys in the box to fortify their run defense.
What happened? The exact opposite. Willis picked apart New York's defense from the very first snap and the Dolphins ran for 156 yards on the ground. In their last two games played, the Jets have given up 304 yards to the Dolphins and Patriots.
This unit has regressed all season. They don't have a semblance of tackle depth to generate pressure in the pocket; they aren't getting consistent pass rush from their edge rushers, and their secondary is taxed because of it.
Despite all the talk about Glenn's "superpower" being play-calling , this entire group was outclassed throughout Sunday. Miami averaged over five yards per play and dominated at the point of attack.
"That’s really puzzling to me," Glenn said. "It just seemed like they were falling forward on everything. And even the ones that we had them knocked back, they still fell forward for three or four yards, and you can’t have any leaky yardage like that."
This group is in serious trouble with the Bills and Chiefs coming up on their schedule.
Jets fans deserve better. There's really no reason the fanbase should expect Gang Green to magically beat some of the high-powered teams on the schedule. The team has proven that even games against "inferior" competition aren't exactly safe.
That leaves the fanbase watching a team out of the running before Halloween ... again. It means fans must choose between rooting for the team to win games and hurt their draft stock, or lose out and secure the rights to a top rookie quarterback.
New York fans have been here before. They are looking at a playoff drought that will extend to 16 years this season and an 11-year run of finishing below .500. After the game, Glenn even tried to curry favor with the fans by showing understanding of their pain.
Fans don't care about improvement on the field, though, if it means the end results aren't changing. And there is the issue.
Without changed results, the Jets are the same as they have ever been.
And the fans deserve better.

title: Jets' Garrett Wilson Malpractice Should Cost Frank Reich His Job After Loss vs. Dolphins
full_text:
Another Sunday, another disappointing Jets loss. This, however, came at the hands of their winless division rival, the Dolphins, who beat Gang Green 28-25 at MetLife Stadium .
Recurring mistakes have plagued Gang Green’s season, with poor coaching decisions and an inability to capitalize in the red zone and on short-yardage at the forefront of the team’s issues. Another concern is offensive coordinator Frank Reich’s inability to consistently utilize star wide receiver Garrett Wilson .
Although the former Ohio State Buckeye leads the team in receptions (37), receiving yards (444), and touchdowns (3), the majority of that production came during the first three games. His involvement in the offense has decreased over the past four weeks:
Garrett Wilson first 3 games
Garrett Wilson last 4 games
Even worse, in the last four games, Wilson has been targeted more than six times just once, posting seven receptions for 104 yards and a touchdown against the Browns in Week 6. In the other three games combined, Wilson has logged just nine receptions (13 targets) for 97 yards. For a receiver of his caliber, this is unacceptable.
With New York sitting at 2-5 and Wilson’s frustration becoming increasingly apparent (h/t Glenn Naughton), Reich’s inability to get his best offensive weapon involved raises questions about whether he should stay in the position.
A frustrated Garrett Wilson has some words for Geno Smith on the @nyjets sideline as he's been a non-factor with the Jets trailing the winless Dolphins 21-14. Smith appears unmoved. pic.twitter.com/esmJHlbXi7
Reich knows Wilson is a special talent. Earlier this month, he compared Wilson to a "masterpiece" (h/t Jets), explaining that he and the coaching staff continue to discover new ways Wilson can impact a game.
“If it’s a masterpiece of art that you’re looking at, if it’s a true masterpiece, you kind of keep coming back and looking at it, and you see it and appreciate different aspects of it every time you look at it,” Reich said. “But also to learn to try to figure out, ‘Oh, he can do this, he can do that. How do we fully utilize the things that he can do?’”
Garrett Wilson 🤝 masterpiece pic.twitter.com/4bPQ7t4ntk
Reich also emphasized the importance of spreading the ball around while acknowledging that he wants Wilson to get a lot of targets. However, the Jets’ offense hasn’t operated as if it were trying to get Wilson involved, and the unit’s production has been underwhelming.
Although New York is averaging more total yards per game than it did through seven games last season, its scoring average has barely increased, rising from 18.4 to 19.6 points per game. Reich’s approach, particularly his inconsistency involving Wilson, has played a key role in the team’s lack of wins.
The recipe that’s resulted in wins for New York is when the offense feeds Wilson. When Wilson is targeted seven or more times, the Jets are 2-2 this season. When he receives fewer than that, New York is 0-3.
Although targets alone won’t determine the game’s outcome, the Jets have a better chance when Wilson is involved. Even head coach Aaron Glenn recognizes the importance of committing to Wilson.
Last week, Reich acknowledged that Glenn regularly reminds him to get him the ball , reported by Sports Illustrated 's Nick Faria.
“AG (Glenn) is always in my ear if Garrett hasn’t gotten the ball for a little bit,” Reich said. “He’s like, ‘Hey, don’t forget, boom, get our playmakers the ball.’”
The fact that Glenn has to remind Reich to get him involved raises serious concerns about the offensive coordinator’s game planning and in-game adjustments. While Glenn takes the blame for Wilson’s low usage (h/t SNY Jets ), it’s Reich’s responsibility to create opportunities for him.
He had the right plan on the opening drive against Cleveland . Wilson recorded three receptions (four targets) for 70 yards and a touchdown. Reich used Wilson creatively, moving him between the slot and outside to give different looks and opportunities to make a play.
This is what Reich needed to replicate. Instead, he failed to do so in the past two games.
Now, Wilson is starting to become visibly frustrated with his lack of targets and the offense’s poor play. If this continues, Wilson’s patience with the franchise could eventually wear thin and end in a departure as soon as the Nov. 10 trade deadline .
While that’s unlikely, the Jets can’t let this continue any further . Reich’s tenure with the Jets could end sooner rather than later if he doesn’t start making Wilson the focal point of the passing game.

title: Faria's Focus Week 7: 5 Jets Thoughts After Loss to Dolphins Drops Gang Green to 2-5
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — It isn't even Halloween, yet the Jets' season is effectively over .
Gang Green's struggles reached their pinnacle in Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Dolphins , a team that was 0-5 going into the contest and hadn't even recorded a lead at any point this season. The Jets had a 100-yard rusher, a 100-yard receiver, and a quarterback throw for nearly 300 yards and it wasn't enough.
Bad teams always make mistakes when it matters most. The Jets are a bad team, no matter what they say or the talent on the roster shows.
Jets fans are rightfully furious after a loss such as Sundays. It's time to give my five thoughts moving forward for the organization.
Last season, Aaron Glenn got the Jets job because the general consensus believed him to be a culture setter, someone who could hire great coordinators, and could even call plays if needed on defense.
Through a year and a half, where has that gone?
Well, New York is 5-19 with Glenn at the helm, and 0-8 in AFC East play. The Dolphins, a team obviously looking to soft-tank the season, still found a way to beat Gang Green's improved roster. No matter what Glenn has said, it's hard to build a culture with results like that .
As for hiring coordinators, the Jets repeatedly struggle to get the ball to start wideout Garrett Wilson —a fact that has left their head coach and quarterback flummoxed when asked about it on Sunday.
"I think we all can do a better job of finding ways to get him more targets and more touches," Geno Smith said. "But again, the ball has to go where it goes based on the coverage, and hats off to them for the game plan they had."
Offensive coordinator Frank Reich's inability to scheme up touches for Wilson has left fans frustrated beyond belief. It also didn't help that when Wilson was open, the quarterback didn't get him the ball either. In both cases, Glenn has taken the mantle of blame for that.
The numbers are what they are, though. New York has found big plays in their offense, but has struggled to find consistency throughout a game. That is a play-calling failure and, in turn, a failure of the head coach as he struggles to find someone to run his offense.
Then there are his own play-calling issues. New York went into Sunday against a Dolphins team hoping to secure a top pick this year in the 2027 draft to get a quarterback. Instead, the Jets defense was shelled by Miami, giving up 156 yards on the ground and failing to record a turnover.
Glenn's play-calling "superpower" was nonexistent on Sunday.
That leads us to the reality of where the Jets are. Glenn's superpower isn't what New York wants it to be. Unfortunately, any superpower starts and ends with his inability to turn the ship around. It's not exactly hard to picture this team entering a new coaching search after this season is over.
If you told me at the beginning of the season that a Jets star was going to be "Wally Pipp'd," my first guess would have been that something happened to Geno Smith. I could never have predicted Braelon Allen would become the most productive running back the Jets have seen so far this year.
Allen ran 17 times for 104 yards on the ground while gaining over six yards per carry. He also added six catches for 30 yards during the game while leading all pass catchers in targets. We've already talked about how insane that is with Wilson on the team, but still. This season, Allen has rushed for 418 yards on 91 carries. That's a projected 1,000-yard season and a healthy 4.6-yard-per-carry average.
Breece Hall has been a star for the Jets offense for years now, but the writing is on the wall. As the second-round running back works his way back from an injury suffered in Week 3, the Jets have no other choice to make. They need to split carries or even feature Allen more when Hall is 100% .
For those who don't remember, Wally Pipp was the Yankees' first baseman who got a headache and sat out a game for Lou Gehrig . Pipp never got his job back and watched as Gehrig became one of the greatest baseball players of all time.
Allen is probably not going to be a superstar like Gehrig, but it's clear he's earned a starting role for the Jets ahead of Hall.
The Jets had a really bad day yesterday. No one is going to dispute that. However, the team should feel great about their future.
And a first-round rookie's performance remains a big reason why.
When the Jets inevitably draft a future rookie quarterback in 2027, they'll do so knowing they have a collection of receivers who can get the most out of the young signal-caller right away. Garrett Wilson is an obvious star, but Omar Cooper Jr.'s performance over the last two weeks has been one for the record books.
Cooper caught six passes for 115 yards and a touchdown (h/t NFL) on Sunday, including two passes that went beyond 50 yards. His work after the catch is a perfect complement to Wilson's pass-catching ability over the middle of the field.
The @nyjets rookie Omar Cooper Jr. finds the end zone for the second-straight week MIAvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TqzjdFlxY4
Not many rebuilding teams have two receivers with the ability to record 1,000-yard seasons on their own. It's obvious, though, that the Jets are in a great place with their offensive talent and any rookie should find success early with that.
If you thought the Jets' defensive performance has been bad recently, just wait. It's about to get a whole lot worse.
New York's biggest problem this season has been an inability to stop the run. While many people will point to their edge rushers and their consistent struggles against rushing offenses, the reality is much more alarming.
The Jets don't have the defensive tackles needed to win with this type of alignment they want to run.
Darrell Jackson Jr. is a late-round rookie and has been thrust into the lineup more due to injuries. Harrison Phillips and Jowon Briggs have both struggled mightily so far this season. Then there are the players unable to perform due to injuries. David Onyemata has been effectively lost for the season and T'Vondre Sweat left Sunday's game with a knee injury.
So where does that leave New York? With a massive gap in the middle of the field and a defensive tackle room that is one of the worst in the NFL.
Until this position group gets fixed, the Jets' defense will continue to get gashed by their opponents. In their last two games combined, the front seven has given up 304 yards rushing.
It's also going to get a lot worse moving forward.
We've already touched on how much Glenn has failed as Jets head coach, but I think it's also obvious to point out that the team is going to inevitably move on from this staff after this season. It's hard to envision a path in which the Jets somehow win six of their final nine contests.
That leaves the Jets in familiar territory: at the outset of another head coaching search and looking through mock drafts to see who could end up with Gang Green in 2027.
There are a lot of lessons to learn from Glenn's failings over the last two seasons. The chief point, though, must be that the organization desperately needs to find an offensive-minded head coach with experience in developing young quarterbacks. Gone are the days when the team should hire "culture-setters" because they "know what it takes to succeed."
New York needs fresh ideas.
Coaches who understand the modern NFL are about out-scheming an opponent rather thanf someone who can keep a locker room together. They need someone who can control an offense and overwhelm the opposition on that end, not someone who coaches with the sole idea of building through the defense.
If Glenn's failings are going to teach the Jets anything it's this: offense breeds wins. Wins breed culture.

title: Jets Postgame Quotes That Matter From Aaron Glenn, Garrett Wilson & More (And What They Revealed About Week 7)
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — If the Jets were going to turn around their season, a Week 7 contest against a winless Dolphins roster seemed to be the perfect time to do so.
Instead, the organization watched for 60 minutes as the Jets were humiliated in front of the MetLife Stadium crowd in a 28-25 loss to a Dolphins team that—until that point—had not even held a lead for a second going into the contest in 2026.
After the game, a quiet Jets locker room and staff tried to summarize how the team could lose a game like that. Here are some of the most important quotes that matter from that time, as well as what they say about Sunday's loss.
The situation: Miami had the ball and a 14-7 lead deep in Jets territory at the two-minute warning. New York had all three timeouts late in the first half. Instead of taking any of the team's timeouts to preserve some time for the offense, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn opted to hold them and watched as the Dolphins completed their over 8-minute drive with a score.
New York was left with six seconds on the clock and went into the half down 14.
Glenn's reasoning afterwards? He believed they would get a stop.
To summarize, Glenn believed his defense would get a stop, and that's why he didn't use any timeouts. Even if the Dolphins were stuffed three times on run plays, the team still would not have had a chance to possess the ball based on their coach's decision.
On Monday morning, Glenn even defended the decision:
"They have time to get more first downs to negate the timeouts that we have, so we call timeout then we’re using those,” Glenn said. “They get another first down, then they can run the clock out.”
Does any of that make sense? Do the Jets have a coaching problem ? I'll leave that up to you to decide.
When teams play the Seahawks, everyone knows they need to find a way to stop Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Seattle still finds a way to get him the ball.
When organizations battle the Steelers, teams know DK Metcalf is the player to stop.  Pittsburgh still finds a way to get its top receiver the ball.
When teams play the Jets, everyone knows Garrett Wilson is the lifeblood of their passing game. Somehow, the Jets have been powerless to give their star receiver the ball .
Wilson saw just three targets on Sunday after finishing with just six the prior week. New York's inability to scheme their star receiver open and deliver accurate passes to him remains a conundrum for the organization.
One Glenn takes responsibility for.
" I’m going to put that on myself, of him not getting the targets that he needs," Glenn said. "Because trust me, that’s in the game plan, to make sure that he gets the ball. So, we have to do everything we can to make sure we do that."
But game planning is only half the problem. Wilson was open throughout Sunday's contest, but Geno Smith simply didn't throw him the football. After the game, the quarterback explained why.
"I think we all can do a better job of finding ways to get him more targets and more touches," Smith said. "But again, the ball has to go where it goes based on the coverage, and hats off to them for the game plan they had."
A quiet and frustrated Wilson tried to rationalize the issues afterward:
During the game, CBS picked up a clip of Wilson seemingly yelling at Smith at one point in the game. Wilson said the two were just "collaborating" along the sideline. On second viewing, it seemed Wilson was yelling more towards passing game coordinator Seth Ryan than Smith.
Still, it's something the team will have to monitor as they consistently struggle to get their star the ball.
The big question Sunday was whether the Jets believed that Glenn was the right man for the job. After a 5-19 stretch and a 0-8 mark in AFC East play, it's a fair question to ask.
That said, the players were steadfast in their belief in their coach.
"Because he's a great leader, former Jet," Joe Tippmann said. "He's somebody who wants to win and we want to win. We follow AG."
In Smith's eyes, the team is on track, even with the results not toally where the team wants to be.
That's the question on the minds of many fans waking up on Monday morning. Why should fans stay bought into a team that is about to see its playoff drought hit 16 seasons and 11 years of their team finishing below .500?
In the eyes of Glenn, it's all about improvement.
"I know what the bottom line of this game is, and it’s all about winning. But I do know this, that this program, when we first started, we knew the things that we wanted to see improve," Glenn said. " I do see the improvement in what we’re doing. I understand the fans’ frustration. I really do. I promise you I do. But the thing is, I do feel like this program is going in the right direction."
To their stars, though, the Jets understand talk is cheap. There needs to be results.
"I like to think we’re heading in the right direction. 2-5 is not a good spot, though," Wilson said. "We’re the only ones that can get ourselves out of it. Got to keep chopping and hope that it all comes together here soon."

title: Writing on the Wall for Aaron Glenn Is Crystal Clear Despite Jets' Ongoing Belief
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Aaron Glenn is a nice guy. He wanted to be the person who would turn around the New York Jets, the same team he was a Pro Bowl star for over two decades.
Had he never gotten into coaching, the 54-year-old would have gone down as a franchise legend.
Instead, his legacy as a player is now being overshadowed by his time as head coach.
Glenn is a concern for the Jets. So much so that the Jets may have no choice at the end of the year but to move on from him. Their latest humiliating home defeat at the hands of another division rival could be the final nail in the coffin.
The numbers are what they are. In a year and a half under Glenn, the Jets are 5-19. That includes a 0-8 mark in the AFC East. Those numbers are second-worst in team history, only ahead of Rich Kotite and worse than the collective records of Adam Gase, Robert Saleh, and Lou Holtz.
It's not as though the team is devoid of talent either. New York has a second-overall pick at edge rusher with 5.5 sacks to begin his career, a young offensive core of stars, and a talented secondary that seems to be getting better each week.
Yet despite the talent, the team still isn't good enough, and it showed on Sunday.
The formerly 0-5 Dolphins didn't play with a lead for the first six weeks of the season. Against the Jets, though, the team led from the first quarter on . Making matters worse is the fact that the Jets had a 100-yard rusher, a 100-yard receiver, a defense that forced their opponent into just seven second-half points, and a quarterback who threw three touchdowns...
Glenn's words have tried to calm fans since he was first hired. All they have done, though, is come up with empty promises and guarantees. The team's talent has improved, but the coaching staff continues to make mistakes when it matters most.
On Sunday, the Jets didn't call a single timeout with minutes left in the first half. After the game, Glenn gave a confusing answer as to the reason why.
"Maybe we should have called our timeouts to get it back, but at that point, we just felt like we were going to stop them and be able to get the ball back," Glenn said. "That's something that we should have done is use our timeouts."
These are the kinds of in-game management decisions that Glenn has routinely failed to make throughout his head-coaching tenure in New York. It also highlights how much of the team is held back on the field by coaching mistakes.
After one year, those mistakes can be forgiven. After two years and minimal changes, those mishaps aren't just mistakes. They are the breakdown of what the coaching staff is.
And it's hard to see the era led by Glenn changing into anything more than it already is.
Despite the lack of wins, the main reason Glenn has watched his team play hard is that they still believe in his plan. Despite a three-point loss, the fourth one-score defeat for the team this year, the Jets remained steadfast in their belief that their head coach is the right man to turn the team into a winner.
"Because he's a great leader, former Jet," Jets guard Joe Tippmann said. "He's somebody who wants to win and we want to win. We follow AG."
But the reality is that while the players still have the coaching staff's back, their lack of effectiveness on the field is a final precursor to the reality of the team being unable to find success with Glenn as head coach.
If you ask the players, the team is still heading in the right direction despite their 2-5 mark.
"I like to think we’re heading in the right direction," Garrett Wilson said. "We’re the only ones that can get ourselves out of it. Got to keep chopping and hope that it all comes together here soon. Make it come together."
But for all the defense of Glenn the Jets have, the reality is that his record and struggles have shown to be more than just a learning curve . This is who this staff is. This is who Glenn is as a coach, and it might just be time to move on.
If anything, it seems like the writing is on the wall at the very least.

title: Jets Week 7 Report Card: Grading Gang Green's Rock-Bottom Performance vs. Dolphins
full_text:
There was no denying that Sunday's AFC East tilt against the Dolphins was a must-win game for the Jets if they truly wanted to keep their season afloat. As is the trend this season, though, the Jets completely laid an egg in a 28-25 loss to a previously winless Miami team that had no business coming to MetLife Stadium and getting a win.
Head coach Aaron Glenn has already found himself in the hot seat with poor decisions, while offensive coordinator Frank Reich has consistently failed to get the ball to his best playmakers. Those struggles reached a boiling point on Sunday after allowing the Dolphins to immediately march down the field for an opening-drive touchdown that set the tone for the rest of the game.
Instead of improving their record to 3-4 and taking care of business on their home soil, the Jets find themselves at 2-5 and staring at their latest lost season with a brutal gauntlet ahead of them going forward. Granted, the red zone struggles were nonexistent this time around (3-of-4), but a loss to a team that had previously failed to even hold a lead speaks volumes.
Before the Jets turn their attention to a Week 8 home game against the Raiders, let's hand out some grades for each unit following another frustrating loss.
Quarterback Geno Smith finished the game 23-of-30 for 287 yards, three touchdowns and one interception. It was his second game of the season with a trio of TD passes, with two going to tight end Mason Taylor and his second in two weeks to rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. This 60-yard strike to Cooper (h/t NFL) eventually led to the TD connection between the two a few plays later and got the Jets back to within one score in the third quarter.
Geno zipped this one into Omar Cooper Jr. for a 60-yard gain MIAvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/EeuCoD4kwN
Despite the accuracy and resiliency down the stretch to keep his team in the game, Smith was not without his flaws. The offense failed to establish much consistency following the opening-drive TD, while Smith held onto the ball too long and threw a costly interception with points on the table in a one-score game in the second quarter, which proved even more costly in a tight game.
For the second week in a row, Cooper looked like a star in the making with five catches for 115 yards and a TD. In addition to a three-yard score, Cooper had explosive plays of 52 and 60 yards and became the first Jets receiver with at least 100 yards in consecutive games since Al Toon in 1985.
As impressive as Cooper continues to be, Garrett Wilson (two catches, 26 yards) and Adonai Mitchell (zero catches on three targets) were nowhere to be found. Granted, a lot of that resides on the shoulders of Smith for not looking Wilson's way as the team's WR1. Still, Wilson appeared to be a huge winner with Mitchell returning to action from a finger injury, and that was far from the case after another lackluster performance.
It was only fitting on National Tight Ends Day that Taylor went off for five catches, 62 yards and two TDs on an average of 12.4 yards per reception. The second-year TE capped off his two-TD performance with this sensational grab late in the fourth quarter (h/t ClutchPoints ) to keep the Jets in the game.
Geno Smith finds Mason Taylor who MOSSES his defender in the end zone 🙌 Jets trying to make a comeback! pic.twitter.com/yGQsFI7Aab
While Taylor put together the best performance of his young career and made several contested catches, the only thing keeping this grade from being maxed out for this group is the lack of help he received from the other TEs. Rookie Kenyon Sadiq was held to just one catch for six yards and Jelani Woods had one reception for minus-1 yard, leaving some room for improvement.
While Breece Hall was sidelined once again with a quad injury , Braelon Allen had another productive afternoon with 17 carries for 104 yards and an average of 6.1 yards per rush. He even broke free for a 27-yard gain and added six catches for 30 yards in the passing game, good for his fourth multi-reception game this season.
Isaiah Davis, meanwhile, did nothing to contribute, with just one carry for five yards as his future remains firmly on the line . Allen will remain in this position until Hall returns to action, and his explosiveness has been key to providing some balance on this shaky offense, which should only lead to more opportunities even when Hall is back to full strength.
Once again, the unit up front paved the way for a solid ground attack and opened up lanes for Allen to exploit. At the same time, the O-line still gave up a pair of sacks and struggled to protect Smith. When the pressure ramped up and the game was on the line, continuity and penalties became an issue for a unit that cannot afford to see its depth tested with Max Mitchell (concussion) and Dylan Parham (knee) battling injuries.
Those issues were particularly on display when center Josh Myers was called for a false start on a crucial third-and-six in the fourth quarter. The Jets only trailed 21-17 at the time, but they ultimately went three-and-out on that possession and punted the ball right back to Miami, which would score the decisive TD on the next drive.
Although Kingsley Enagbare and David Bailey were credited with 0.5 sacks and preseason darling Nate Lynn recorded his first sack of the season, the D-line continued to struggle against the run with 103 yards and a TD allowed to Ollie Gordon II, marking the fourth time in as many losses over the last five games that they have surrendered at least 100 rush yards.
They also gave up back-to-back scoring drives to begin the game and even failed to contain QB Malik Willis , who passed for 208 yards and two TDs on an offense that ranked 31st in passing yards per game (153.6 ypg) coming into Week 7. There were a few bright spots from this unit, but the failure to consistently get off the field and close out short-yardage situations was a huge detriment.
Amid what has been a breakout season for Jamien Sherwood, who is also coming off a team-high 11 tackles in the Week 6 loss to the Patriots, his future continues to become clearer after recording the third-most tackles (eight), two tackles for loss and two passes defended against the Dolphins. He was joined by Demario Davis, who contributed three tackles (two solo) and two passes defended.
Despite that, it was still too easy for a Miami offense that is tied for the fewest points per game (14 ppg). The Dolphins had 24 first downs (to the Jets' 19), were a perfect 3-of-3 in the red zone and averaged an efficient 8.9 yards per pass. Overall, it was a struggle to clog up the running lanes and keep the Dolphins out of rhythm, which allowed them to extend drives and control the time of possession (34:36-25:24).
The secondary unit was disappointing, with absolutely no answers for tight end Greg Dulcich (five catches, 86 yards) and rookie wideout Caleb Douglas (two catches, 70 yards, two TDs). This was only Douglas's third career game and his first two NFL TDs, the most crushing of which took place in the fourth quarter when a deflating 63-yard score (h/t NFL) extended Miami's lead to 11 with over four minutes to play.
Caleb Douglas took this one all the way. MIAvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hb8mEQrB80
Not only did this group not force a single turnover, but the inability to slow down Willis in the air and on the ground (eight carries, 37 yards, one TD) and make enough key plays to swing the momentum was disappointing against a Dolphins team that had only topped 20 points once this season. The late score from Douglas was the only one allowed in the second half, but the poor start to the game put the Jets behind and never gave them a chance to set the tone early.
Although kicker Jason Sanders has been solid this season, given the doubts surrounding him before it even began, he wasn't at his best on Sunday, with a make from 33 yards and a missed 40-yarder to begin the second…

title: 3 Jets Look Like Bigger Trade Candidates After Humiliating Loss to Dolphins
full_text:
There's no way to put it nicely: Sunday afternoon's 28-25 loss to the Dolphins was nothing short of humiliating for the Jets. After all, the rival Dolphins entered Week 7 winless and among the NFL's laughing stocks, seemingly the perfect opportunity for head coach Aaron Glenn & Co. to claw within one game of a .500 record.
Instead of beating up on an easily beatable opponent, the Jets trailed the entire game as miscues on both sides of the ball suddenly had the Dolphins looking like the opposite of the AFC East's worst team. It's the type of defeat that likely not only defined Gang Green's season, but also Glenn's time in Gotham.
Heading into Week 8 with a 2-5 record, Jets general manager Darren Mougey will likely be doing much more selling rather than the buying fans wanted ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline . A roster retooling is needed to turn things around, after all, so don't be surprised if these three players become even bigger trade candidates after losing to the Dolphins.
A strong preseason performance led to Jarvis Brownlee Jr. having a big role with the Jets early in the 2026 season. He started the year off strong, too, with the veteran slot defender picking up Pro Football Foc us coverage grades of 82.0 and 70.0 in his first two games , all while playing 79 defensive snaps.
Unfortunately, that's as good as it's gotten so far.
Since then, Brownlee has finished with a grade of 59.4 or worse in each of his last four games, allowing 14 catches on 19 targets (73.7%) for 128 yards and a touchdown without any pass breakups or interceptions. The downward-trending performance forced Glenn to make a change on Sunday, scratching Brownlee while rookie CB D'Angelo Ponds took his spot in the lineup.
Although the Jets didn't win, Ponds looked solid, finishing with a 68.6 defensive grade while playing a season-high 30 snaps (32 combined in three previous games). He only allowed one five-yard catch and a 56.3 passer rating on two targets, giving the Jets even more reason to keep playing him over Brownlee.
Two years remain with cap hits of $1.08 million and $1.19 million on his contract , per Spotrac; Brownlee could easily be moved by the Jets before the trade deadline. It's becoming clear that he isn't a long-term solution in Gotham, so New York might as well see what it can get in a potential deal— especially if the team wants to fully unleash Ponds .
The Jets' wide receiver room has become healthier in recent weeks, with Tim Patrick, Omar Cooper Jr. and Adonai Mitchell all healing up since October began. While that's good news for New York's passing outlook, it's bad news for Isaiah Williams's hopes to get (and stay) on the field.
It's been a quiet season for Williams, who's done nothing of note since recording 73 receiving yards and a touchdown against the Bears in Week 4. The former undrafted playmaker recorded one 16-yard catch the following week and has now gone the last two appearances without a single target. Making matters worse, he only saw 22 offensive snaps in those games after averaging 46.6 in the five previous games.
He isn't even much of a factor on special teams anymore. After returning nine kicks and five punts in the Jets' first three games, Williams sits at two and five, respectively, in the last four.
Set to hit restricted free agency in March, it's hard to imagine Williams sticking around. That's even more true if Cooper continues to put up 100-yard performances while Mitchell gets his footing back. With his cap hit just over $1 million and there's no real loss by moving on from him, the Jets could explore a potential Williams trade in the coming weeks.
The 2026 season is a big year for veteran safety Andre Cisco, who's due to become an unrestricted free agent this winter. That said, an early injury to offseason arrival Minkah Fitzpatrick seemingly opened the door for Cisco to prove himself last month , whether that meant securing an extension with the Jets or impressing another team that could target him in March.
Much to his dismay, Cisco's outlook was dealt a major blow once Fitzpatrick returned to begin October. Since Week 4, the former Jaguars third-rounder has played only three, one, two and nine defensive snaps. It doesn't help that he's struggled to capitalize on the diminished opportunities, finishing with the worst coverage (28.8) and overall defensive (27.8) grades among Jets defenders in Week 7, per PFF .
It's clear that Cisco has fallen out of favor, and it's hard to see him turning things around as long as Fitzpatrick and Dane Belton hold on to their starting roles. A $2.2 million cap hit means the Jets shouldn't have an issue moving on from Cisco via trade, and doing so would allow them to see what they've got with certain defensive backs on the taxi squad, including Mory Bamba, Jordan Clark and Sam Womack III.

title: 4 Studs & 4 Duds in Jets' Week 7 Loss to Dolphins: Glenn Crumbles, Cooper Shines & More From Sunday
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Just when you think the Jets season couldn't get any lower, they find a way to hit rock bottom.
On Sunday, rock bottom was found, and there may not be an opportunity to get back up in the future.
The Jets were desperate for a win against their AFC East rival Dolphins . Instead, the 0-5 Dolphins came away with a shocking 28-25 victory within the confines of MetLife Stadium, dropping the Jets to 2-5.
Perhaps it was a bad omen of things to come when the Dolphins offense came out firing with a seven-play touchdown drive to open the game. They scored on three of their first four offensive drives of the game, including one at the end of the first half that ate up over seven minutes of game action to take a 21-7 lead going into the break.
The Jets made it a game in the second half, cutting the deficit to four going into the final quarter. But a 63-yard touchdown pass, coupled with a clutch fourth-down conversion late in the contest, sealed the team's fate.
As always, there's plenty of studs and duds to look through after a loss like that. Let's go through those now.
Few things actually looked good for the Jets on Sunday. One of their bright spots came from second-year tight end Mason Taylor. The LSU product outjumped an opposing corner in the first quarter to muscle his way for a 13-yard touchdown (h/t NFL).
It's National Tight Ends Day and Mason Taylor is joining the party MIAvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/F72SqDOTVz
It was the kind of play that highlighted the effectiveness of Taylor—someone who can make plays in the receiving end while also using his abilities as a blocker to make a positive impact. He made almost the exact same play late in the game to cut the deficit to three.
In total, Taylor finished with five catches, 62 yards receiving and two scores. It was his first two-touchdown game of his career.
Taylor is a good player. One the Jets can use in the future.
There's no sugarcoating it. This was a disaster for Jets head coach Aaron Glenn . The loss drops him to 0-8 in the AFC East. It was also a game in which he was going against a first-time head coach and a team without a win. Instead of coming out inspired, the Jets looked flat in all areas of the game.
Glenn touted his play-calling prowess during the offseason, but the Dolphins were prepared for everything he threw at them. A team that did not have a lead going into the game yet this season had a comfortable lead throughout the contest.
It's not like the team could point to player execution either. New York did not call a timeout once in the first half despite having multiple opportunities to give the ball back to their offense with a chance for last-minute points. After not calling a timeout in the first half, Glenn inexplicably called a timeout within the first five minutes of the second half to save his offense from a delay of game.
And when the team needed a stop most, the Jets gave up a 63-yard touchdown to close out the game. The loss moved the Jets and Glenn to 0-8 against AFC East opponents.
A loss like this feels more like the beginning of the end for Glenn's tenure. The team believes in him, but in a results-driven business, the Jets are simply not good with him at the helm. And it might be time to start looking elsewhere.
New York's best offensive player on Sunday, besides the work of Mason Taylor, was wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. The first-round rookie caught five passes for 115 yards and a touchdown (h/t NFL). He became the first Jets receiver with 100 yards in back-to-back games since Al Toon in 1985.
The @nyjets rookie Omar Cooper Jr. finds the end zone for the second-straight week MIAvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TqzjdFlxY4
Much will be made about the Jets' inability to get Garrett Wilson the ball (and we'll get to that shortly), but Cooper seems to be a star in the making. One that the Jets will be able to use to great affect in their offense.
General manager Darren Mougey should be thrilled he was able to trade up for the Indiana star. He's become vital to this offense.
Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich has been around many great receivers over his playing and coaching career. Never before have we seen a staff be unable to get the football to a star receiver like this .
New York's offense targeted Wilson just three times on Sunday and watched the star catch two passes for 26 yards. After the game, Geno Smith said the Dolphins were keying on Wilson throughout the game and making sure they wouldn't beat him, but that isn't necessarily what happened either. New York simply didn't manufacture touches for him.
Whether it was the team's screen calls to Adonai Mitchell, Cooper or Allen, the Jets opted not to try to force the ball to Wilson. The fact that they seem to be the one team in the NFL that simply doesn't know how to get the ball to their best player is disheartening.
And that's before the Jets bungled many other play-calling opportunities, including needing to kick a field goal despite having a first-and-goal at the opponent's one-yard line during the game.
Reich has not been up to the task so far this season. With the amount of talent the Jets have, this is arguably one of the more disappointing staff breakdowns over the last few years.
New York has a very uncomfortable conversation to have in the near future. While star running back Breece Hall has been out with an injury, Braelon Allen has become one of the franchise's best players. On Sunday, he ran for 104 yards on 17 carries for a whopping 6.1 yards per carry average.
Allen still lacks breakaway speed and there were a couple of plays that could have been long touchdowns if he were faster, but he remains a bell cow for this offense. When Hall does return, New York will have to start splitting carries between the two RBs . There's simply no feasible reason they can take Allen off the field anymore.
Sunday was a disaster for the Jets organization. One group was worse than any other, though, and that was the team's defense. New York gave up 28 points to a Dolphins team that had one of the worst offenses in football. They couldn't stop the run, gave up back-breaking penalties and missed key tackles as well.
Going into Sunday, the Dolphins were the only team that had played without a lead for the first six games of the season. They led for a majority of the game against the Jets, recorded over five yards per play, and controlled the ball for nearly 35 minutes.
Worst of all was the run defense. New York has given up 304 combined rushing yards in the last two weeks. It may get worse with the Chiefs and Bills waiting on Gang Green's schedule.
This group has to play a lot better going forward.
New York struggled to get any consistent pressure on Malik Willis on Sunday. While David Bailey and Kingsley Enagbare shared a sack, it was Nate Lynn, a free-agent pickup during the preseason , who made the most of his chance to make an impact.
Lynn recorded his first sack of the season on a key third down in the second half to give the Jets a chance to take the lead late. New York may have squandered that opportunity, but Lynn is a player who clearly needs to be a part of the defensive line rotation going forward.
The numbers show an efficient and successful day for Geno Smith and the Jets offense.
Smith ended the game with 23-for-30 passing, 287 yards and three touchdowns to go along with a first-quarter interception, implying Smith was perfectly fine on Sunday.
The tape will tell a different story.
Reich gets blamed for not getting Wilson the ball, but Sunday had more to do with Smith not targeting him than the actual play calls. Throughout Sunday, Wilson was running open over the middle of the field on several routes. For whatever reason, Smith didn't throw the ball. He also held onto the ball too long and seemed happier to check the ball down rather than get it to an open target.
Simply put, while the numbers showed he had a good game, the tape…

title: Final Week 7 Injury Report Gives Desperate Eagles Offense a Huge Boost
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — It’s not exactly the cavalry riding to the Eagles’ offensive rescue for Monday night’s home game against the Cowboys , but it’s better than nothing.
Just hours before kickoff, Philly filled its three spots on the 53-man roster, adding:
Calcaterra and Stowers have yet to play this season after being placed on injured reserve before the season opener. What’s interesting about these three names is that Zach Ertz is not among them . The thinking had been that the Eagles made a deal with the veteran tight end to return to Philly in exchange for adding him to the roster at some point.
This feels like the point, yet it didn’t happen.
Ertz is out of practice squad elevations, so the only way he can play again for the Eagles is to be added to the roster. Clearly, the team is higher on Calcaterra and the rookie Stowers right now.
Speaking of the practice squad, the Eagles elevated outside linebacker Keyshawn James-Newby for a second straight game and running back Elijah Mitchell.
Meanwhile, Saquon Barkley is expected to return to the lineup after missing two games with a hamstring injury. Adding Mitchell gives the Eagles three running backs for Monday’s game, as he and Barkley join Dameon Pierce.
The return of Barkley and Dickerson should help the Eagles find some traction in the running game, and that would help Tanner McKee, who will make his second straight start in place of injured Jalen Hurts.
In last week’s loss to the Panthers, McKee attempted 45 passes while running the ball just 12 times against a Panthers defense that was one of the worst at stopping the run in the league. The Bay Buccaneers showed the Eagles how bad that run defense was on Sunday when the Bucs torched Carolina on the ground, with 49 runs for 258 yards. Baker Mayfield threw just 11 passes.
Yet, the Eagles insisted on letting McKee throw the ball and never took advantage of the Panthers’ inability to stop the run.
A more balanced attack against the Cowboys might help the Eagles snap a four-game losing streak. Having McKee throw the ball another 40-plus times doesn’t feel like a recipe for success, especially with the Eagles missing their top two playmakers—DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Tay Wicks (ankle).
That leaves the Eagles with a decimated receiver corps that includes rookie Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore.
Dickerson will be playing his first game since the season-opening win over the Washington Commanders. He was placed on injured reserve the day after the game with a bone bruise.
Cornerback Jakorian Bennett (knee) was ruled out for the game against Dallas.
In addition to Smith and Wicks being ruled out in Saturday’s final injury report, the Eagles ruled out defensive back Michael Carter (abdomen) and OLB Nolan Smith (concussion).
Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard was listed as questionable with an ankle injury, but he is expected to play. Outside linebacker Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) was questionable on the final injury report , but he has yet to be ruled out at the time of writing.

title: 3 Eagles in Danger of Landing on the Trade Block With a Dud vs. Cowboys in Week 7
full_text:
Given the way the season has gone for the Eagles, there's a real chance they could be sellers leading up to the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, Nov. 10 .
If the Eagles continue to slide down the standings in the NFC, they may look to recoup some value for guys that they don't view as long-term pieces.
They have three games remaining before the deadline, starting with a Monday night matchup with the rival Cowboys in Week 7. Here's a look at three Eagles players who could potentially be on the trade block after an underwhelming performance against Dallas.
Hollywood Brown has been a complete nonfactor for the Eagles through six weeks of the 2026 season. He's appeared in just one game for Philly and hasn't logged a single reception. But if he's ever going to have an impact for the Eagles, it will be against the Cowboys on Monday night when Philadelphia will be missing its top two receivers, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks.
Without Smith and Wicks, the Eagles and backup quarterback Tanner McKee will be forced to rely on the rest of the receivers on the roster, including Brown. If he doesn't play much or make an impact with the Eagles—who are in desperate need of production at the receiver spots—that should tell you all you need to know about his standing within the team.
Brown could already be considered a trade candidate heading into the deadline, and another quiet performance against Dallas will only hammer that home.
Pretty much the exact same logic that was applied above to Brown could also be applied to wide receiver Elijah Moore, who has also been a non-factor for Philly. Moore has appeared in four games this season, but he has just one reception for four yards.
Again, there should be increased opportunity for other receivers like Moore (and Brown) to step up against Dallas and fill the void left by Smith and Wicks. If Moore is unable to do so, then there's no reason for the Eagles not to try to move him prior to the deadline.
On the other hand, if he can demonstrate some value, perhaps the Eagles would want to hang onto him for the rest of the season.
Tariq Woolen won a ring as a cornerback for the Seahawks last season, and when the Eagles signed him to a one-year deal in free agency, they probably envisioned him filling a similar role in Philadelphia.
However, at this point it's pretty clear that the Eagles probably won't be competing for the Super Bowl this season, and Woolen could potentially fetch a decent return in a trade . If the Eagles don't view him as a piece that they're likely to bring back in free agency next year, it would make sense to try to get some value for him while they still can.

title: 3 Pending Eagles Free Agents Already Deserve Contract Extensions
full_text:
With a 2-4 record in Week 7, it isn't too early to start thinking about the future in Philadelphia. After all, the Eagles have a plethora of players heading to free agency over the offseason, with Spotrac listing 22 pending unrestricted free agents .
Many of those players won't be back in Philadelphia. That's just the way the business of the NFL works. Roster turnover is inevitable. However, a few upcoming UFAs have shown Eagles general manager Howie Roseman that they're worth bringing back based on what we've seen early this season.
Moro Ojomo is currently playing in the final year of the four-year rookie contract that he signed in 2023, and he's a guy that the Eagles should certainly consider bringing back.
Over the course of his current contract, Ojomo has developed into a key contributor for Philadelphia, even though he's often overshadowed on the line by star defensive tackles Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis. He has appeared in 40 straight games for the Eagles over the last three seasons and he's tallied 20 quarterback hits, eight tackles for a loss and six sacks during that span. He's a reliable rotation piece who can come and provide support on the D-Line without the production of the unit falling off.
That's valuable for a team to have.
But just because the Eagles should try to retain Ojomo doesn't mean they will be able to. The Eagles already have a ton of money tied up in the defensive line between Carter and Davis, and they have a bunch of other areas that they'll also need to address. So, there's a possibility that keeping Ojomo won't be financially feasible for Philly. The Texas product will assuredly have other suitors in free agency.
It's a new era for the offensive line in Philadelphia. Mainstays Lane Johnson (retired) and Cam Jurgens ( traded to the Ravens ) are gone, and Landon Dickerson seems unsure about his own future in Philly. So the Eagles need to start building for the future on the line, and retaining a guy who has started in 26 games for them and showed a lot of promise would be a good start.
Tyler Steen moved into a starting spot with the Eagles last season after receiving limited opportunities during his first two years. He's been solid in the role and has posted respectable Pro Football Focus grades , despite struggles elsewhere on the line.
At just 26, Steen should have plenty of productive play ahead of him, and it would be good if he could do so in an Eagles uniform.
Veteran offensive tackle Fred Johnson signed a one-year, relatively cheap deal with the Eagles in free agency in March, and the Eagles could potentially look to sign him to another such deal in free agency next offseason to retain inexpensive, experienced depth on the offensive line.
Johnson has only played 14 offensive snaps so far this season, but he played nearly 60% of snaps last season and over 40% when the Eagles won the Super Bowl two years ago. He isn't exciting and doesn't necessarily offer much upside, but he does offer a decent depth piece at good value. Every team needs guys like those.
The Eagles will assuredly address the offensive line in the 2027 NFL Draft, but a few returning faces wouldn't hurt.
