title: 'Players Over Plays:' Nick Sirianni Hinting at a Return to Roots Is Already Benefiting One Eagle
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — The much-ballyhooed shift to a Shanahan/McVay-like offensive scheme has been a dud early in the 2026 season for the Eagles.
And there are subtle hints that head coach Nick Sirianni is about to rewind to his broader philosophy of “players over plays.”
The lip service toward offensive coordinator Sean Mannion’s watered-down version of the hybrid West Coast philosophy now claims some kind of all-inclusive adaptability.
Quarterback Tanner McKee— in for the sidelined Jalen Hurts —said the team’s offensive system aligns with his skill set because of that “adaptability," something that in theory allows coaches to adjust week to week without being locked into one approach.
“I think there’s a lot of different ways that this offense could be run,” McKee said. “I’ve said it before, it’s really wordy. Sean wants to be able to have the freedom to change different things in the game, week to week, whatever it is. And so he’s not trapped into one way of calling plays, running the offense, whatever it is. And so that’s freeing as a player.”
McKee emphasized that the freedom places added responsibility on the players.
Sirianni has described a similar philosophy of balancing a foundational system with in-season adjustments tailored to available personnel and opposing defenses.
“Your job is to go out and to try to win every game the best way that you can,” Sirianni said. “Yes, you want to have a system in place to be the bones of your operation, but while also understanding that you want to attack the defense of what they’re playing and with the strengths of your players,” Sirianni said. “That’s always a fine line. We know we have good players that can execute a lot of different things, but ultimately, it always is players over plays.
“It will always be players over plays.”
Sirianni added that the core values of a program have to be a constant; in his case, that’s the “tough, detailed, together” mindset that the Eagles have adopted.
Everything else—schemes, schedules, and practices—can change.
“We’ve adjusted some things because we’re doing everything we can on our end to be able to go out there and be successful,” said Sirianni.
McKee noted that each week the Eagles' offense targets defensive weaknesses alongside the strengths of the current personnel and the plays the unit has practiced most.
“Each week you attack defenses in a different way. Each week you attack, obviously, the weaknesses of the defense of that week, but also the strengths of the offense,” he said. “What guys are available, what plays do we like, what plays do we run well, what plays do we have a lot of reps on. That was one thing that me and Jalen talked a ton about."
Reviewing tape from his Week 6 start in a loss to the Panthers , McKee identified areas of focus that fit the need for precision within a variable system.
“Communication needs to be at a premium, especially at the quarterback position. I think when anybody is not on the same page, doesn’t know what to do, I feel like there’s always part of that goes on the quarterback,” the Stanford product said. “And then I think settling down a little bit, a little bit quicker. I think I got quick with my feet a couple times at the beginning of the game, trying to get the ball out, being a little rushed. And so I think just trusting my footwork, trusting my reads, getting through progressions, will ultimately benefit me.”
McKee also stressed better efficiency, particularly under center and against the blitz, and his part in that.
“I think efficiency. Efficiency and being on the same page. Staying on schedule,” McKee said when discussing needed improvements. “There are times if it’s a bad play, don’t make a bad play worse. Obviously, taking care of the ball. Sometimes as a quarterback, the best play is to throw the ball away and not take a sack.
“As a quarterback, I think you have to have some damage control. There are plays that, you know, sometimes the defense just gets you. … And so, as a quarterback, you have to be able to diagnose that, have some damage control, and live to see the next down.”

title: Steelers Missing Piece to Being Serious Contenders
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have once again gotten off to a strong start.
Entering a crucial Week 8 matchup with the Cleveland Browns, the Steelers are sitting at 5-2 and currently own the No. 6 seed in the AFC.
In the midst of a three-game win streak that it'll look to push to four before its Week 9 bye, it's not hard to feel optimistic about what stands ahead of Pittsburgh this season.
At the same time, if they want to be considered real contenders in the conference, the Steelers do have some clear needs that must be addressed.
Their biggest missing piece is evident, too, and it'll come as no surprise to anyone.
Pittsburgh was active in filling its hole at wide receiver this offseason by acquiring Michael Pittman Jr. from the Indianapolis Colts and selecting Germie Bernard in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft.
Bernard has certainly panned out thus far, recording 254 yards and a touchdown while making three starts. Pittman Jr., on the other hand, was placed on the reserve/injured list with a foot injury ahead of the Steelers' Week 5 game against the Indianapolis Colts and seems incredibly unlikely to return at the earliest possible date, which would be in Week 10 after he misses the required minimum of four games.
Roman Wilson (finger) also landed on IR in the lead-up to Week 6, and Ben Skowronek (calf) has missed two contests in a row as well.
DK Metcalf has bounced back after a rough start to the year, posting a combined 276 yards over his past four games, but he hasn't proven himself to be a true No. 1 receiver in a Pittsburgh uniform up to this point.
The Steelers' offense has been incredibly conservative during the 2024 and 2025 seasons with former offensive coordinator Arthur Smith calling the plays, and that has remained true under first-year head coach Mike McCarthy.
Through seven games, Aaron Rodgers ' average depth of target of 7.42 yards ranks No. 21 among 34 quarterbacks with at least 100 dropbacks this season (per SumerSports ).
His 61.6 percent completion rate and -0.13 EPA/pass both rank No. 25 under that same criteria, and his big time throw rate of 3.2 percent (per Pro Football Focus ) is tied for No. 22.
Rodgers has just seven completions over 36 attempts on passes of 20-plus yards (per SumerSports), which comes out to a 19.4 percent completion rate that comes in as the fifth-worst mark in the NFL.
The future Hall of Famer has played pretty well overall, but Pittsburgh is still severely lacking any semblance of an explosive passing game, which will hold it back long-term.
Getting Wilson back at some point should help in that regard, and he would make up a decent enough trio with Metcalf and Bernard. Still, the Steelers would really benefit from adding a dynamic playmaker at receiver who can separate and generate big plays consistently.
Finding a player who fits that bill at the trade deadline is easier said than done. With that being said, however, paying whatever it costs and taking a chance on someone like Brian Thomas Jr. is the exact type of high-reward move Pittsburgh has to seriously consider.
Thomas Jr. has taken a huge step back over the past two seasons since the Jacksonville Jaguars brought Liam Coen in as their head coach, but the 2024 first-round pick proved he has star-level talent after posting 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns as a rookie.
Other options that could intrigue the Steelers include Quentin Johnston (Los Angeles Chargers), Jerry Jeudy (Cleveland Browns), Dontayvion Wicks (Philadelphia Eagles) and Stefon Diggs (Washington Commanders), though none of them offer as high of a ceiling as Thomas Jr. would.
It is hard to build an explosive passing game around a 42-year-old quarterback who's in the middle of his final season, though the Steelers have to make a concerted attempt to do just that.
They have a fantastic run game with Jaylen Warren leading the way as one of the top running backs in the league, and if they can start leaning on their pass game more by adding a legit receiver before the trade deadline, their offense has a chance to do some real damage moving forward.
If Pittsburgh is going to snap its seven-game losing streak in the postseason and make some noise as a contender in the AFC, doing so is an absolute necessity.
From the moment the Steelers put an end to the Joey Porter Jr. saga by trading him to the Dallas Cowboys in Week 4, there was always a possibility that cornerback would become an area of concern.
Jamel Dean is capable of being the team's No. 1 corner, though Asante Samuel Jr. and Daylen Everette are volatile options next to the former on the boundary. Sean Murphy-Bunting and Terell Smith were solid veteran additions as depth pieces, but neither should be expected to step in and play at a high level if called upon.
For that reason, a trade for a proven starter who can play opposite Dean would make sense for Pittsburgh.
The other position group that could potentially use reinforcements to help the Steelers become more of a complete team and have a chance of competing with the AFC's top squads is inside linebacker.
Payton Wilson has made some strides in his third NFL season , and Patrick Queen is coming off his best game in quite some time in Pittsburgh's Week 7 victory over the New Orleans Saints.
That tandem has fallen short often, however, and while Elandon Roberts may eventually factor into the team's plans while currently residing on the practice squad, a more consequential move to bring in a real difference-maker could pay dividends for the Steelers' defense.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers' Aaron Rodgers Sets New Record in Win Over Saints
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers were victorious in their Week 7 contest over the New Orleans Saints, defeating their NFC South opponent by a final score of 16-10. The Steelers return home with a 5-2 record and plenty of work to do before they meet the Cleveland Browns in Week 8.
The Steelers mustered a single touchdown in the win, but the offense showed signs of life. A 51-yard bomb from quarterback Aaron Rodgers to wide receiver DK Metcalf was the deep ball the offense has been trying to connect on for the past year and a half. Running back Jaylen Warren ran all over the Saints defense, putting up 137 total yards.
That pass to Metcalf carried more significance than helping the Steelers put points on the board. When the wideout hauled in that deep pass from Rodgers, it was the 95th time that the 42-year-old QB has thrown a completion of 50 yards or more. With that completion, he became the NFL's new all-time leader in that statistic.
What Rodgers and the Steelers care about the most is the explosive play he and Metcalf combined for. As nice as it is to have the recognition of being the first all-time on a list like 50+ yard completions, Rodgers is likely smiling about the breakthrough that the offense finally had.
The big knock on the Steelers, even throughout this current winning streak, is their offense lacks splash. And that is predominantly true, as Rodgers has found a way to succeed with the dink-and-dunk approach.
But on that deep pass to Metcalf, Rodgers used the bait of playing around the line of scrimmage to open up a shot downfield for his top receiver.
And hopefully, that pass unlocked something. Aside from Metcalf, the Steelers have rookie Germie Bernard trying to show his elusiveness in open space. Third-year pass-catcher Roman Wilson is currently on the Injured Reserve, but when he returns, the Steelers might have even more use for his speed on the outside.
That 51-yard pass to Metcalf was a record-setting one for Rodgers, but more importantly, it was a tone-setting pass for the offense in a crucial victory.
Aaron Rodgers is bound for the Hall of Fame. The Super Bowl winner and four-time MVP has put together one of the most illustrious careers of any NFL quarterback.
It's not like Rodgers needed another achievement to earn his place in Canton, Ohio, but this is yet another feather in the cap of the 42-year-old. He can add it to the long list of accolades to celebrate when he is enshrined in the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Might Have Their Answer at LB
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers may have a long-term solution at inside linebacker.
The entire position group has largely underperformed since the beginning of the 2025 season, with both Patrick Queen and Payton Wilson being the biggest culprits.
That tandem has started to turn things around, however, and while Queen deserves his fair share of credit after how well he played in Pittsburgh's 16-10 Week 7 win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris, it's Wilson who has really taken the reins.
The 2024 second-round pick still isn't a finished product, but he's shown flashes of becoming a star in the middle of the Steelers ' defense.
Since training camp, Wilson has turned heads with how he's flown around the field and made plays in Patrick Graham's defense.
That's carried over to the regular season, and the strides he's made as a run defender has been evident as well. Wilson's not exactly polished in that aspect of his game, but it's still a far cry from how he performed in 2024 and 2025.
In a game where Pittsburgh held New Orleans to just 18 yards on 17 rushing attempts, Wilson was consistently around the ball and was paramount to the Steelers' success in shutting down the Saints' ground game.
The 26-year-old's biggest play of the game came in coverage, though. Tyler Shough had been carving up the Steelers' defense through the air, particularly underneath, and drove New Orleans down to Pittsburgh's 10-yard line while trailing 13-10 about halfway through the third quarter.
Wilson put an end to the Saints' 14-play drive, however, by jumping a throw to Chris Olave and returning it to the Steelers' 29-yard line.
Payton Wilson anticipates the pass perfectly and picks off Shough in the red zone PITvsNO on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/7QIPlOfibh
New Orleans did not score for the rest of the game, and Wilson's clutch interception is one of the main reasons why Pittsburgh was able to come away with the win at the Stade de France.
Wilson's deficiencies against the run really held him back over the first two years of his NFL career, during which he was largely viewed as a good coverage linebacker and not much else.
He's ever-so-slightly starting to shift that narrative, though, given how he's improved as a run defender. On the flip side, Wilson has allowed the fourth-most receiving yards (258, per SumerSports ) among linebackers with at least 250 snaps this season.
The 26-year-old clearly has the tools to be a well above-average coverage defender, as evidenced by his interception off of Shough, though consistency is a bit of an issue for him as of now.
Furthermore, Wilson's missed tackle rate of 14.9 percent is the 10th-worst amongst linebackers with a minimum of 250 snaps (per SumerSports).
He's grown into an exciting player who's developing into a stronger run defender, and his standout athletic traits for the position provide him with a high ceiling.
Wilson still has to put all of the pieces together, namely in terms of continuing to grow against the run and being more steady in coverage, but there's reasons to believe he could stick around for a prolonged period of time in Pittsburgh.

title: One Change Has Sparked Steelers' Offense
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are 5-2 following their 16-10 victory over the New Orleans Saints. After a whirlwind of a weekend that saw the team fly to Paris, France, play a football game, and fly back to Pittsburgh, this team enters Week 8 exhausted but full of momentum.
Sitting at the top of the AFC North standings, the Steelers now shift focus to the Cleveland Browns, their Week 8 opponent and divisional rival. The Steelers will have to find a way to overcome a nasty Cleveland defense that has helped them also jump out to a 5-2 record.
It's a clash of strengths between these two foes. The Browns bring a top-rated defense, while the Steelers have found a new life on the offensive side of the ball under head coach Mike McCarthy. But comparing the offense this year to last season reveals a startling discovery. It turns out that the Steelers are not that much different this year in terms of offensive execution.
There is one clear difference, however. And that difference is running back Jaylen Warren.
One of the biggest criticisms of the Steelers' offense last season under Arthur Smith and Mike Tomlin was their lack of pass game. They weren't able to put up explosive plays in the air and despite Aaron Rodgers' best efforts, the passing game never became a threat. According to game data from SumerSports, the Steelers' Expected Points Added (EPA) on passing plays ranked 16th in the NFL and 19th in success rate. By contrast, their run game ranked 12th in EPA and 10th in success rate. Steelers analyst for Steelers Now Derrick Bell shared an interesting bit of statistics comparing the team's offenses in 2025 and 2026 through seven games that illustrates this exact point.
Comparing the 2025 and 2026 Steelers offenses through the first 7 games: 2025: EPA/play: 18th Success rate: 17th Dropback EPA: 19th Dropback success rate: 26th Rushing EPA: 7th Rushing success rate: 6th 2026: EPA/play: 20th Success rate: 22nd Dropback EPA: 27th Dropback success… https://t.co/5NNKMQjauC
This season, the Steelers' offense has made some splash plays in the passing game and Rodgers has had some strong individual performances along the way. Still, the numbers show that this team hasn't come that far in their aerial attack. So far this season, the Steelers rank 26th in overall EPA per play as well as per pass play. Their success rate in the pass game is a measly 41.8%, ranking 22nd in the NFL.
The Steelers find themselves amongst the likes of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the Miami Dolphins, the Indianapolis Colts and the Tennessee Titans through Week 7 of the regular season.
Once again, the run game is the complete opposite. The run game is 7th in the NFL in EPA per rush play. The success rate leaves a bit to be desired, at just 42.5%, but that figure is tied for 12th in the league currently.
Those numbers in 2025 got Arthur Smith fired. In 2026 they are being celebrated as progress.
And when you watch Jaylen Warren play, it's easy to understand why this offense is being lauded. Yes, Rodgers has played well, throwing 13 touchdowns and just five interceptions over the first seven games. He's completed 61.6% of his pass attempts, and he's made some crucial plays with his legs.
But the star of the offense is Jaylen Warren. It's undeniable. And what Warren does at an elite level is gain yards after contact. SumerSports has tallied 28 impact plays for Warren so far, the second-most of any running back in the NFL this season.
The thing is, it's not because the play design or offensive line play has paved the way for free runs. It's been quite the opposite. Warren is averaging 1.61 yards before contact per rush attempt, which ranks 21st amongst all NFL backs with at least one touch in 2026.
Getting to Warren isn't that helpful, as most defenses have discovered. After contact, he just keeps moving. He's posted 397 yards after contact, the sixth-most amongst NFL running backs. Per rush attempt, he's gaining an additional 3.84 yards after the first tackle attempt, which stands 8th in the NFL.
And if you think Warren is elite after contact while running the ball, just put him in space and see what happens. He's one of the most utilized running backs in the passing game this season, with 24 receptions on 34 targets. His 294 receiving yards are the second-most in the NFL among backs, and his 344 yards after the catch ranks first across all running backs with at least 10 touches, according to data from SumerSports.
And as Warren goes, so too does the Steelers' offense. Right now, he's playing like an MVP candidate. If that continues, the Steelers will stay right in the mix of the AFC North race. If he falters, the Steelers will too. That's because the only change in Pittsburgh this season is the focus and emphasis on Jaylen Warren.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers' Aaron Rodgers Farewell Tour Has Finally Begun
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- I don't know who put the chains on Aaron Rodgers' neck after the Pittsburgh Steelers' win in Paris. I do know it let us all in on something the NFL world has been missing out on.
Aaron Rodgers' Farewell Tour.
@AaronRodgers12 rocking all the chains on the flight home from Paris 💎 @CamHeyward (via @Rudolph2Mason ) pic.twitter.com/z0gOrYRFtg
The Steelers are having fun. This team is winning, overcoming injuries, sticking together and finding success, all while enjoying their time together. And it's all backed by their quarterback, who, very quietly, is marching through his final NFL season. Now, he may be doing it with a little more noise behind him from the fanbase and the players.
An NFL locker room can look one of two ways for a journalist. If the team is losing, or barely getting by during a season, it's gloomy. Players are quiet, there isn't much going on and no one wants to talk.
If the team is winning, it's a complete 180. You'll walk by players and they'll say, "What's up?" You hear a ton of laughter and players joking around. Everyone seems to be in a good mood, and you can feel the lightness and the excitement about practice or a game in the air.
The Steelers locker room is light as air right now.
They're a 5-2 football team that's fighting for the top spot in the AFC North, who believe in each other and are winning games through different parts, and different players, on this team. That's exactly what you're looking for in the NFL, and Pittsburgh is well aware of it.
Then, there's Rodgers. The 42-year-old quarterback hasn't made a big deal of his final season, and neither have the Steelers.
This won't be a situation where the jumbotron puts up "Thank You, Aaron" and he walks through the crowd and cries while hugging all of the fans. Rodgers is not Ben Roethlisberger in the city of Pittsburgh, but the fans are starting to believe in this guy. And when you believe in your team's quarterback, you believe in the team.
Rodgers is making Steelers Nation a believer, and they'll be right behind him through his final run because of it.
There's a magic to a farewell tour. Everyone has one they remember most, whether it's Ray Lewis and the Baltimore Ravens, Peyton Manning and the Denver Broncos, or Jerome Bettis and the Steelers. You remember how different the team felt, and how the eventual goodbye of an iconic player just felt like it couldn't go any other way but by holding up a Lombardi Trophy.
Not everyone gets that moment, and maybe Rodgers won't. But the belief that it's possible is always stronger when the farewell tour feels real.
With chains on his neck, sunglasses on his face and a grin from a Steelers legend standing next to him, Rodgers not only officially became a member of Steeler Nation, but his last rodeo in the NFL became overwhelmingly real.
How far will this farewell tour go? We'll find out. But the magic is real, and when it is, you just never know what's going to happen in the NFL.
Noah Strackbein is a Publisher for On SI, covering the Pittsburgh Steelers since 2019. A Jessup, PA native, Noah attended Point Park University, where he fell in love with the Steel City and everything it has to offer. You can find Noah's work at Steelers On SI and weekdays as the hosts of All Steelers Talk.

title: Steelers Can No Longer Avoid CB Troubles
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers held the New Orleans Saints to just 10 points during their international contest in Paris, France. The performance helped earn the team's fifth victory of the season and a temporary share of the AFC North divisional lead.
Since the defense surrendered just 10 points, the Steelers defense is in great shape, right? In many ways, the identity of this team lives and dies with their pass rush and defensive line. After disrupting Saints quarterback Tyler Shough, it's clear that their front seven is dangerous.
Contrarily, the secondary is still in flux. The team gave up their lone touchdown thanks to being outmatched by the Saints' speed on the outside. Since the team traded Joey Porter Jr., the team has lacked another capable boundary corner. The defense has attempted to weather the storm, but they need to add a cornerback via trade immediately.
The additions of guys like Sean Murphy-Bunting and Terrell Smith were smart ones. With injuries running through the secondary, adding that depth gave the team some breathing room over the past few weeks. Sadly, that hasn't solved the issues in the pass defense. If anything, it's kicked the can on addressing a problem that's been brewing for months.
The Steelers have to address their inefficiencies at cornerback through a trade. It's not the ideal situation for finding that player, but they need another starter to pair with Jamel Dean, preferably one who has the speed and physicality that defensive coordinator Patrick Graham yearns for.
There are a few paths the Steelers can take if a trade must happen. Whatever direction they go, they must target the type of player they lost when they traded Porter Jr. - someone who is excels in man-to-man coverage schemes and can be a disruptive force in tight.
A commonly named trade target right now is Philadelphia Eagles veteran Riq Woolen. A big-bodied, physical cornerback who won a Super Bowl with the Seattle Seahawks last season, Woolen provides a ton of what the Steelers are missing right now.
Another low-cost option that I would encourage the Steelers to look toward is Washington Commanders veteran Rasul Douglas. Douglas is a former 2017 NFL Draft pick who has excelled with multiple organizations. The 31-year-old defended 13 passes last year with the Miami Dolphins, and he's already recorded an interception and five pass breakups with the Commanders this season.
For a seventh-round draft pick, the Steelers could add a player who makes that stop at the goal line against the Saints.
There are bigger names to target, instead, if the Steelers want to add a bona fide starter for 2026 and beyond. One player they recently faced could be a solution. Tampa Bay Buccaneers Zyon McCollum is a former fifth-round pick, but he's been a steady starter for several seasons.
Following his rookie contract, he signed an extension that pays him an average salary of $!6 million through the 2028 season. That's only a few more million per season than they currently pay Jamel Dean, so it stands to reason that the organization would happily take on McCollum's remaining deal.
The Bucs are also going through changes. Their salary cap situation skyrockets with quarterback Baker Mayfield's extension taking effect in 2027. The team will need to shed some salary, and the Steelers might be the beneficiaries of Tampa's troubling situation.
A big swing or a quick addition, it doesn't really matter. The Steelers cannot ignore their issues at cornerback any longer. They have to add immediately to give their defense a complete lineup for the first time in 2026.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: How Aaron Rodgers Helped Payton Wilson Make Crucial Play in Steelers Win
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers need both sides of the ball to have success if they want to have a strong season and both sides have shown they'll do what it takes to achieve that.
The Steelers got a big win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris, France in Week 7, with the defense playing an important role in the 19-10 victory.
Linebacker Payton Wilson made one of the best plays in the Steelers' win with an interception in the third quarter, as the Saints were threatening to score.
Wilson doesn't make this play without the help of none other than Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers, showing the camaraderie between the offense and defense.
The Saints were just 10 yards out from a big touchdown to start the second half, which would've given them their first lead over the Steelers in the game.
Saints quarterback Tyler Shough tried to find wide receiver Chris Olave on 2nd-and-7, but Wilson cut the route and made the interception, giving the Steelers possession and keeping them in the lead, 13-10 midway through the third quarter.
We'll be taking that 😏 @payton_wilson21 pic.twitter.com/SPSaIHFNGT
After the game, Rodgers made sure to point out how he may have helped Wilson come up with that interception. How? Wilson made that play because of his work in practice.
"Did it help that he picked me off in practice on a very similar play this week?" Rodgers joked.
AWESOME: Aaron Rodgers asked #Steelers LB Payton Wilson if intercepting him on a similar play in practice helped him make today’s game-changing interception. Wilson said it did, then joked he took the practice pick to the house. Great back and forth 😂😂 pic.twitter.com/A7WtqYz4yv
“That’s honestly just a credit to our coaches and what we do every day in practice," Wilson said on his interception. "I mean, I’ve repped that play, no lie, more than 20 times now."
“And Coach Simo' [Jason Simmons], PG [Patrick Graham], Scott [McCurley], they all do a really good job of that space away from three, two-by-two. Pretty much all throughout the NFL, that’s where they’re gonna attack.
“So just gambling a little bit and undercutting it, having to defend that play against him [Rodgers] a lot throughout training camp and just in practice has really helped. So, just credit to those guys, put me in those situations enough to trust myself to go do it.”
The Steelers offense had a decent game, but wasn't effective enough to beat the Saints on their own, forcing the defense to show they could do what was needed.
Pittsburgh was fantastic against the run, allowing just 18 yards on 17 rushes from New Orleans, shutting down a big part of their offense.
Shough did have a solid game, completing 30-of-38 passes for 278 yards, but threw just one touchdown, and the Steelers held the Saints scoreless in the second half.
The Steelers almost had two fumble recoveries, but both were overturned , which would've made their own performance more special.
Steelers linebacker Patrick Queen came up big with a huge sack on 3rd-and-10 with 6:40 remaining in the fourth quarter, which represented the Saints' final drive of the game.

title: Where Steelers Stand in AFC North After Saints Win
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers continued their strong 2026 season with another win, which is important for their standing in the AFC North.
The Steelers stood strong defensively and defeated the New Orleans Saints 16-10 in Paris, France, for a big Week 7 victory.
Pittsburgh improved to 5-2 on the season and has won its past three games, which include victories over the Indianapolis Colts at Acrisure Stadium, 34-22 in Week 5, and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , 26-19 at Raymond James Stadium in Week 6.
The Steelers are winning consistently at a crucial part of the season, but they aren't the only AFC North team doing well.
Cleveland Browns* (Tiebreaker)
The Steelers are tied for first place in the AFC North with the Cleveland Browns, who are also 5-2 in 2026.
Cleveland leads the AFC North, as they defeated Pittsburgh 27-24 at Huntington Bank Field in Week 4, and hold the tiebreaker.
The Browns got another 27-24 win, as Andre Smzyt hit a 32-yard field goal as time expired for the road victory over the Tennessee Titans.
All five of the Browns' wins this season have come within one score, and they now have back-to-back wins after beating the Baltimore Ravens at home 13-10 in Week 6.
The Cincinnati Bengals scored 35 unanswered points and defeated the Ravens 35-13 on the road for a big Week 7 win.
Cincinnati scored all 35 points in the second half and also has back-to-back wins, defeating the Miami Dolphins 31-24 on the road in Week 5.
The Ravens have lost back-to-back games after starting 4-1, with quarterback Lamar Jackson missing these last three games.
The Steelers and Browns face off for the second time in 2026, with Acrisure Stadium as the location for this historic rivalry in Week 8.
Cleveland hasn't won in Pittsburgh since a 48-37 victory in the AFC Wild Card Round on Jan. 10, 2021, and they haven't won a regular season game there since Oct. 5, 2003, 22 straight defeats.
It should be a battle of both defenses, and the Steelers almost beat the Browns, tying it up at 24 late after trailing 21-7, so expect revenge to play a factor for the Steelers in this one.
The Bengals play the Titans and will also look to add to their winning streak and stay near the top of the AFC North.
Baltimore has a tougher challenge, travelling to face the Buffalo Bills, which would also be harder if Jackson is still out injured.

title: 6 Winners, 3 Losers From Steelers Win Over Saints
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are rolling .
With their 16-10 victory over the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France in Paris, the Steelers are now 5-2 and in the midst of a three-game win streak.
Pittsburgh still has some issues it has to clean up, but it's hard not to feel good about the way things are trending heading into Week 8.
With that, here are the Steelers ' winners and losers as they fly back home.
Though Watt didn't earn credit for his forced fumble on a sack of Tyler Shough in the second quarter after the call on the field was overturned after review, the 32-year-old was still stellar for the Steelers.
Along with his takedown of Shough, Watt finished the day with four pressures (per SumerSports ) and was getting into the backfield consistently while also helping out against the run, per usual.
Fautanu's gone through some struggles in his move from right tackle to left tackle this season.
Chase Young gave the 2024 first-round pick all he could handle and then some, with Fautanu allowing a total of four pressures and two sacks to the former AP Defensive Rookie of the Year (per SumerSports).
That makes it back-to-back rough outings for Fautanu, who was also far from his sharpest in Pittsburgh's Week 6 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Wilson's made some serious strides in Patrick Graham's defense.
The 26-year-old's biggest play of the day came on an interception of Shough in the red zone with the Steelers leading 13-10 about halfway through the third quarter.
New Orleans did not score for the rest of the contest, and Wilson deserves plenty of credit in that regard. Not just for his pick, though, but his support in the run game as well.
Wilson wasn't the only inside linebacker who showed out in this one.
Queen hadn't exactly been living up to expectations this season, with that continuing from a disappointing 2025 campaign.
He turned the time against the Saints, though, coming up with a drive-ending sack on New Orleans' last series of the game while also leading the Steelers with 10 tackles and making more of an impact than usual against the run.
Queen nearly hauled in an interception on the Saints' first drive of the contest too.
Ramsey was instrumental in helping lead Pittsburgh to a comeback win over the Bucs , though he took a step back in France.
He was still helpful as a blitzer and against the run, though he had some lapses in coverage. In total, Ramsey allowed 70 yards and a touchdown in coverage (per SumerSports).
With Sebastian Joseph-Day (triceps) having been placed on the reserve/injured list this week while Derrick Harmon (foot) had already been on IR for two weeks, the Steelers really needed Benton to step up along the interior of the defensive line.
He did exactly that, batting down a pass at the line and posting two tackles for loss to go with two pressures.
Rico Dowdle deserves his flowers, posting a total of 86 yards on 15 touches, though it was Warren who once again stole the show out of the backfield for Pittsburgh.
He continues to prove that he's one of the NFL's elite running backs, rushing for 101 yards on 18 carries to go with three catches for 36 yards for a total of 137 yards from scrimmage.
Freiermuth did convert a 3rd-and-9 with an 11-yard catch in the third quarter, though he also dropped a great throw from Aaron Rodgers down to around the 10-yard line just a few plays later.
Freiermuth had just 20 yards over two catches as five other Steelers finished with more receiving yards than he did.
Rodgers kept building on what's been an incredibly solid final season for the future Hall of Famer.
He went 19-of-30 for 212 yards and a touchdown through the air while also showing off his wheels a bit, picking up a first down with an eight-yard run on third down that essentially clinched the win for Pittsburgh during the final drive of the contest.

title: Referee Grades: Steelers vs. Saints Was Tough to Watch
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints battled in an historic international contest, giving the Paris, France, crowd their first taste of NFL action.
The Steelers, for the second year in a row, were part of the NFL's inaugural contest in another country. As the league expands its global footprint, the Steelers have been right at the forefront.
Unlike the Steelers' win over the Minnesota Vikings in Dublin, Ireland, in 2025, this year's international game is likely to be overshadowed by the officiating crew's performance.
Once again, the referees controlled another contest for the wrong reasons. Both teams were frustrated with the officiating crew, and a deeper dive reveals they were justified.
It was a day to forget for the officials, who should receive a failing grade for their performance in the latest Steelers' win.
Today’s Steelers-Saints game marks the first time Bill Vinovich has officiated a Saints game since the infamous no-call in the NFC Championship Game more than 7 years ago. The Saints are playing in Paris. pic.twitter.com/vHoQOz8Fp9
Things didn't get off on the right foot between the Steelers and the officials, right from the first offensive series.
Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers tried to connect with wide receiver DK Metcalf on a fade route toward the end zone. Metcalf and the Saints cornerback engaged in hand-fighting and physicality as the route developed, but what most saw was the defensive back's free hand tugging on Metcalf's chest plate.
Now, Metcalf was still able to get both hands up in an attempt to get the ball, and the officials can point to that after the fact.
Despite this, being in a one-on-one matchup and having a free hand on the receiver's equipment as he goes up for the ball usually draws a flag automatically.
This time it didn't, incensing Rodgers and effectively putting a target on their back for the remainder of the contest.
For that, the refs received a D-, and they should feel thankful they avoided an outright fail.
Did I love watching left guard Mason McCormick leaping on top of the pile as rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard picked up 20 yards late in the first half?
Did the officials make the right call, flagging the guard for joining the pile too late?
Once upon a time, this was a common practice in the NFL, but it's one of the plays the league wants completely eliminated due to injury risk. Sadly for McCormick, this was an A+ call and the right one.
Two of the most egregious calls against the Steelers were unnecessary roughness calls levied against wide receiver Brandon Smith and linebacker Payton Wilson.
Let's start with Smith, who was blocking a Saints defensive back in the first half. As the play ended, the two continued jawing at one another. The Saints defender pushed Smith back, and in response, the Steelers receiver pushed his facemask into his opponent's.
What made the call feel so off was that the action hardly felt like an escalation. More likely, it was the reaction that the officials caught. Either way, it was not worthy of throwing the flag.
They could have redeemed themselves in the second half, but instead they made another pair of awful calls against both teams. During the first series, they called rookie Saints guard Jeremiah Wright for a personal foul.
Here's the thing: he didn't do anything unnecessary. He was battling Keeanu Benton one-on-one, and he finished the block all the way to the ground. It's how he's been taught to play his entire life, but suddenly it was a penalty.
On the very next play, the Steelers were on the receiving end of a blunderous call. Linebacker Payton Wilson tracked down Saints running back Alvin Kamara and forced him out of bounds.
Wilson began the tackle along the sidelines, and the two fell into the Steelers' bench, but Wilson was called for a personal foul.
All three of these calls were terrible. Not one met the criteria for a personal foul, and each was a normal, routine football play. That's an undeniable failure for the crew on those calls.
As the third quarter wound down, there was a hiccup in the flow of the game. The Steelers' offensive drive was halted after Saints edge rusher Chase Young sacked Rodgers.
That forced the field-goal unit out for a 39-yard attempt, but it took several minutes before kicker Chris Boswell could knock his third field goal of the day through the uprights.
The reason for the delay was that the officials and the scoreboard operations team were struggling to get on the same page.
Head official Bill Vinovich had to stop the play on separate occasions before the snap, so he could correct the game and the play clock.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Seahawks May Get RB Reinforcements At Perfect Time
full_text:
Seattle Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson had his best performance of the season in the team's 20-3 win over the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday, but they still need to get healthier at the position.
Presumed starter Zach Charbonnet hasn't played yet this season, rookie first-round pick Jadarian Price has missed the last four games and Velus Jones Jr. suffered a hamstring injury in the Week 7 win.
However, reinforcements could be on the way just in time for the Seahawks to mount another winning streak that puts them back atop the NFC. That seems almost like a necessity at this point, after they lost three of four games from Weeks 3-6.
Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said there was a chance Charbonnet was going to play against the Chiefs, and ESPN's Ian Rapoport told the Pat McAfee Show he expected him to "play a lot" in that game. Then the Seahawks ruled him out.
Charbonnet is returning from a torn ACL and is trying to return after just a nine-month recovery. Thus, it makes sense for timelines to change and for availability to be difficult to determine, but Macdonald also said Charbonnet did not suffer a setback .
It would be strange if Charbonnet nearly played against the Chiefs, didn't suffer a setback and then also doesn't play in Week 8 against the Chicago Bears. So, there's good reason to hope he will make his season debut in that Monday night contest.
Price is also expected to practice this week , Macdonald said, per ESPN's Brady Henderson. He has 21 days to be added back to the active roster. What that means for Week 8 status remains unknown, but getting Charbonnet and Price back at the same time would be a major boon to the Seattle run game.
"For Rashid [Shaheed], early returns are positive." #Seahawks HC Mike Macdonald provides injury updates on WR Rashid Shaheed & LT Charles Cross from last night's game & timelines for RBs Jadarian Price & Zach Charbonnet. pic.twitter.com/raJx0PhizC
Charbonnet and Price could be a legitimate one-two punch, much like Charbonnet and Kenneth Walker III were from 2023-25.
Wilson looked good against the Chiefs, rushing 24 times for 100 yards and a touchdown. That was an encouraging performance, but offensive coordinator Brian Fleury still had three running backs carry the ball. The Seahawks haven't had a chance to rely on one or two rushers yet this season.
This week's practice reports will be telling, and they would benefit greatly from getting some of their top talent back against the Bears. Wilson and George Holani can get it done, but it's not the ideal scenario.
A trade is still possible, but if both Charbonnet and Price are trending back towards healthy, the Seahawks should avoid seeking outside help.

title: NFC Playoff Picture: Where Are Seahawks After Beating Chiefs?
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are turning the corner after beating the Kansas City Chiefs 20-3 to snap a two-game losing streak.
The Seahawks find themselves at 4-3 , but that still is not enough to be in the NFC playoff picture after Week 7. Here's a look at where the Seahawks stand after seven weeks of action:
1. Minnesota Vikings (6-0) 2. San Francisco 49ers (6-1) 3. New York Giants (4-2-1) 4. Carolina Panthers (3-3) 5. Chicago Bears (5-2) 6. Detroit Lions (4-2) 7. Green Bay Packers (4-3, 3-3 NFC) 8. Seattle Seahawks (4-3, 1-2 NFC) 9. Atlanta Falcons (3-4, 3-2 NFC) 10. Los Angeles Rams (3-4, 2-2 NFC) 11. Philadelphia Eagles (2-4) - playing on Monday Night Football 12. Dallas Cowboys (2-4) - playing on Monday Night Football 13. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (2-5, 1-0 NFC South) 14. New Orleans Saints (2-5, 0-1 NFC South, 1-3 NFC) 15. Arizona Cardinals (2-5, 1-4 NFC) 16. Washington Commanders (1-4-1)
It's far more important to be inside the top seven at the end of Week 18 as opposed to Week 7, so this isn't time for the Seahawks to panic . However, if the playoffs started today, the Seahawks would be on the outside looking in.
The Seahawks gained a game in the NFC West standings after the San Francisco 49ers lost to the Atlanta Falcons, but they still have some work to do. All four teams in the NFC North are currently in the playoff picture, as the Minnesota Vikings are the lone undefeated team in the league, while the Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions, and Green Bay Packers are the three wild cards.
Those NFC North teams will beat up on each other as the season continues, which gives hope to a team like the Seahawks, who are hoping to return to the playoffs.
The Seahawks' next game comes on Monday Night Football in Week 8 against the Chicago Bears, who find themselves inside the playoff picture. A Seattle win would push them ahead of Chicago in the standings, so that means it's high stakes in prime time once again for the Seahawks.

title: Charles Cross Injury Update is Bad News for Seahawks
full_text:
One of the few bad things that happened for the Seattle Seahawks last night was Charles Cross departing late in the fourth quarter with an injury . Today, we received confirmation that the injury is significant, although perhaps not catastrophic. Per reports, Cross has a high-ankle sprain that is going to sideline him for at least 1-2 weeks. Emphasis on at least.
I say that last part because, typically, high-ankle sprains take longer than 1-2 weeks to heal up from, and that estimate strikes me as optimistic. Perhaps they have reason to believe that this one is more minor than typical, but I’m personally suspecting he’ll miss the next three games. After that, the Seahawks have a bye, and they play some weaker defenses coming up.
#Seahawks OT Charles Cross, who suffered an ankle injury on Sunday, has a high-ankle sprain and will miss time, the MRI revealed. The hope is he’s back in 1-2 weeks, but it depends on how rehab goes. pic.twitter.com/4yVx2jmupL
There’s also, for the moment, no real reason to rush Charles Cross back due to the Seahawks having a proven backup who has already come through for them before. Josh Jones, who will start at left tackle until Cross returns, played several games late in the season last year and got the job done. He’s not as good as Cross, but you can win with him.
However, it’s worth noting that this injury leaves Seattle without a real backup left tackle behind Jones. As it is, Jones was the only backup tackle Seattle was carrying on their roster for both the left and right sides. The practice squad options are Bobby Hart, who has always been a right tackle, and Logan Brown , who had a miserable preseason and doesn’t seem ready.
So I would anticipate that the Seahawks sign someone from free agency in the coming days. Nothing big or overly noteworthy, but a body who can get the job done on some level and some experience playing on the blindside. It’ll likely be a player we know very little about right now, but I don’t believe the team can move forward this thin at tackle on both ends.
What I really don’t like about this is the lost opportunity for this offensive line to build continuity. The Seahawks decided to prioritize synergy over talent this offseason, bringing back all five starters from 2025 and the offensive line coach. They wanted guys that knew each other and knew how to play together. So far, they’ve been unable to take full advantage of that.
Anthony Bradford played the opener and then missed the next five games. He returned last night , with obvious positive impact from that, but now Cross will miss at least some time. Hopefully, when Charles gets back, this line will get at least a few weeks to find the continuity again. It was most certainly a lot better last night, but the next few games might be bumpy.

title: Why Seahawks' Jaxon Smith-Njigba Should Win League MVP but Won't
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks (4-3) have one of the best rosters in the league, if not the best. It helps to have one of the league’s most punishing and efficient defenses, especially after a dominating performance in Week 7 over the Kansas City Chiefs . Offensively, the Seahawks took big steps forward to become more efficient.
​This is an offense that faced a lot of criticism with turnovers and a lack of a run game. Wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, however, has been one of the biggest reasons for the offense to stay efficient and develop. JSN remains the cornerstone of the Seahawks’ offense and plays so dominantly that he is easily the most valuable player. There should be a strong debate that should be league MVP after an impressive seven-week stretch.
JSN is one of the league’s most consistent and explosive offensive players. That was evident when he won Offensive Player of the Year last season . This season, he continues to transcend the Seahawks’ offense even despite some horrible moments from the run game, quarterback Sam Darnold and offensive coordinator Brian Fleury.
​Through the first seven weeks, JSN leads the league in receiving yards (867), targets (78), touchdowns (8), big plays of 20 yards or more (14), yards per game (123.9) and first downs (43). He is also second in receptions (58), fifth in yards after catch (274) and 19th in average yards per catch (14.9). JSN has 231 more receiving yards than the next leading receiver in New Orleans’ Chris Olave.
​He has accounted for at least 100 yards in six of the seven games played this season. Last season, he had nine games where he accounted for over 100 yards. JSN is on pace to break Calvin Johnson’s single-season receiving yards record of 1,964 yards with 2,023 yards at the rate he is going.
​Most of all, he is carrying the Seahawks’ offense by getting easy first downs when the running game might be struggling. He is also creating great separation from the opposing defensive backs and constantly getting open. Even if he is being focused on or double-teamed, JSN is still finding ways to contribute. He has been the most elite, consistent and reliable elite playmakers this season.
​Through the course of the first seven weeks of the season , JSN and Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff have been the most consistent playmakers. He has the track record, the name recognition, reputation and athleticism to be named league MVP at this rate. The biggest factor going against him is the history of the league MVP award.
A wide receiver has never won the award. It has been an award essentially given to quarterbacks. The last non-quarterback to be named AP’s League MVP was running back Adrian Peterson in 2012. Before Peterson, the last non-quarterback was LaDainian Tomlinson in 2007.
​If JSN were to have real traction for league MVP then it would have to because the top quarterbacks in league’s Los Angeles Rams’ Matthew Stafford and Green Bay Packers’ Jordan Love are still at the bottom half of their division while chasing stats. The league MVP voters like to acknowledge a team’s relevance in the playoffs.
The Seahawks are the reigning Super Bowl champions and are in the playoff chase again, but voters will likely feel more compelled to vote for a quarterback once they lead their team in the playoffs.

title: Seahawks Should Be Back in Super Bowl Conversation After Chiefs Win
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are making their presence known after a 20-3 victory against the once-undefeated Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7's edition of Sunday Night Football.
The win snapped a two-game losing streak for the Seahawks, as they have improved to 4-3 on the year. While the Seahawks remain in second place in the NFC West standings behind the San Francisco 49ers, they gained a game after the Niners lost their first game of the season to the Atlanta Falcons.
Still, just looking at the eye test suggests that Seattle will be incredibly tough to knock out in a playoff setting.
Much like last year, that "Dark Side" defense looks incredibly lethal. They surrendered a mere 213 yards against the league's top offense and held Patrick Mahomes out of the red zone for the entire game, something that has never happened in his entire career.
That fact alone means Seattle should be able to compete against any team in the league, which is a scary place to be in at this point in the season. There are still 10 games left on the schedule, but if the Seahawks play like they did against the Chiefs every week, no team is going to beat them.
The Seahawks are not 100 percent healthy, but they are expected to get some key players back in the coming weeks, most notably running backs Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet . That should make things a lot easier on the offensive side of the ball, but the defense is still this team's bread and butter.
As long as this current iteration of the defense can stay healthy, they are going to be extremely difficult to beat. If they can get linebacker Drake Thomas back very soon, that should also make things a lot easier for them down the line. If he can return by Week 12, which is right after the bye, that should keep the momentum for the defense going to the playoffs.
The Seahawks will now face another difficult test in Week 8 as they welcome Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears to town. Kickoff is scheduled for Monday at 5:15 pm PT inside Lumen Field. Fans can watch the game on ESPN or stream it on the ESPN app.

title: Hanich Panic Meter: Seahawks' Offense Regains Some Composure
full_text:
There was a lot of pressure from the Seattle Seahawks as Week 7’s Sunday Night Football game versus the Kansas City Chiefs turned into a must-win. There was a lot of criticism over the Seahawks’ offense with turnovers, bad play-calling and a lack of run game. The Seahawks showed they are a team to fear when they are not shooting themselves in the foot.
​ Seattle’s offense managed to compose themselves against a high-caliber Chiefs defense. While the offense’s performance is far from perfect, there was progress made to show this is a capable playoff-caliber offense. This offense had the chance to keep Seattle undefeated, but there is hope for them to get better.
​There were a lot of attributes where the Seahawks were criticized. One of the biggest was quarterback Sam Darnold’s decision-making, timing and turnovers . Darnold looked more comfortable in the pocket and made either the instant throws he needed to make or properly readjusted depending on the coverages. He finished completing 20-of-28 for 257 yards, a touchdown, an interception and a quarterback rating of 96.9.
​His interception thrown near the goal line wasn’t ideal and hurt the team, but he is far from the only person to blame. The running game was non-existent in the first half, with George Holani barely making it to the line of scrimmage on the previous running play. Finally, the intended receiver crashed into another receiver.
​The offensive line improved significantly between the disastrous performance in Week 6’s Thursday Night Football road game versus the Denver Broncos. They didn’t allow a sack on Darnold and gave him a clean pocket for most of the night. Seattle’s offensive line created solid push at the line of scrimmage and created solid opportunities for the running game to excel.
​More players were utilized and played more naturally. Brady Russell played most of the reps at full back. Running backs Emanuel Wilson and George Holani made great plays in the passing game. Tight end AJ Barner had a great performance as a pass-catcher and in three tush-push plays. The Seahawks’ offense did enough to extend drives and keep the Chiefs’ offense off the field.
​While Week 7 was certainly a big improvement offensively, there is still a lot to fix. The Seahawks finished with 153 yards on 41 carries for an average of 3.7 yards, but a lot of it was fluff stats to help put the game away. Seattle only averaged 3.1 yards in the first quarter and 32 yards and 90 yards through the first three quarters. Wilson and Holani showed better vision, but still lacked explosive speed needed to get the offense rolling with momentum and keeping the pressure off Darnold.
​Offensive coordinator Brian Fleury was at playcalling for the Seahawks’ offense, but there were still moments where the drives should’ve continued. The running game looked flat in moments and then another similar running play was called again. Seattle had more success running outside of the tackles, but it took a while to get there.
The offense should see a significant improvement across the board when either veteran running back Zach Charbonnet or rookie Jadarian Price returns or the front office trades for an immediate starter. The Seahawks could still keep Wilson as a bruising back, but he needs to be a backup. Once the Seahawks return some speed, they will be confident offensively.

title: 3 Observations from Seahawks Win Over Chiefs
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are impressing the NFL after becoming the first team to beat the Kansas City Chiefs this season.
They dominated Patrick Mahomes, Kenneth Walker III and the Chiefs , beating them handily by a score of 20-3. Here's a look at three observations from the game.
The Seahawks' defense came into the game as the top-ranked unit in the league, but they were definitely going to be tested against the number one offense in the league. The Chiefs came into the game averaging 414 yards per contest, but they managed to gain just 213 yards throughout the game. Meanwhile, the Seahawks had 410 yards of offense and clearly were the winner in this one.
It's further proof that the Seahawks' defense is the best in the league. If they can shut down the Chiefs, they could give every team in the league the same treatment. That should be a warning to the rest of the NFL that the Seahawks are not going away quite yet.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba continued his ascent as the league's top receiver. He led by over 130 yards for the receiving title going into the game and likely just extended that lead. He added another 150 yards to his total, along with a touchdown.
With 867 yards on the season in just seven games, he's on a remarkable pace and very well could be in the mix to not just be the Offensive Player of the Year but also the league MVP.
The one true blemish on the Seahawks for this game came late in the second quarter, when the team was driving and nearly had a touchdown in their grasp. An interception thrown by Sam Darnold to Chiefs cornerback Nohl Williams could have gone a lot worse.
Williams tried returning the ball all the way from one end zone to another and got a decent return off it, making it all the way to the Seattle 44-yard line. Had he gotten a few yards closer, the Chiefs could have kicked the field goal and made it a one-score game going into halftime. He also could have taken it to the house and really flipped the entire game.
Darnold was lucky that the damage was not worse on that pick, and it is something that could haunt them down the line in future games if he's not careful enough.

title: How the Seahawks Shut the Lights Off on Kenneth Walker III
full_text:
Former Seattle Seahawks and current Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III ran wild over five games . Then he ran back into the brick wall that he used to practice against every day.
Stopping Walker was the primary emphasis for the Seahawks’ league-best defense in their 20-3 win over the Chiefs on Sunday, and they exceeded all expectations in pursuit of that goal.
“We [had] to play in waves, because he’s still going to break tackles,” Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said postgame. “I’m sure he broke a host of tackles, because that’s what he does. So, we had to get people to the football, and that gave us the best chance. I felt the guys play like that; I felt like we played great team defense today.”
Walker entered the game with six rushing touchdowns and a per-game average of 133 rushing yards. The Seahawks hadn’t allowed a 100-yard rusher in 25 games — a streak that goes back to midway through the 2024 season.
The former Seahawks second-round pick had been unstoppable, but the Chiefs hadn’t faced a truly elite defense yet this season. Seattle is not just a good run defense; it may be the best in the NFL.
Defense prevailed. Walker turned 14 carries into just 36 rushing yards and added four catches for 21 yards. Neither Walker nor the Chiefs found the end zone the entire game.
Some Kenneth Walker III stats from tonight: - lowest success rate of any game this season (29%) and lowest yds/carry (2.6) - lowest rate of stacked boxes (7%) - lowest number of explosive runs (0) Seattle’s defense, man 😮‍💨
“Just getting after him, man,” Seahawks linebacker Ernest Jones IV said of how they stopped Walker in his tracks. “We knew, I mean, of course he’s been here. We know what type of running back was coming in here. But we don’t allow people to run through our defense, and that’s just us, and we were able to execute against a really good running back today and hold him to minimal yards in that category.”
On the other side, Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson had his best game of the season with 24 carries for 100 yards and a touchdown (4.2 yards per carry). Wilson had averaged just 3.5 yards per carry on 87 carries coming into the game.
The Seahawks’ defense proved it could completely nullify their former teammate, who is currently an Offensive Player of the Year and MVP candidate, and the offense showed that they didn’t need to keep him to win games. Those are major victories for this Seahawks team after snapping a two-game losing streak .
Seattle’s defense was still playing great during the losing streak, but this is another performance their confidence can fall back on as they reach the middle of the season.
“We can play. We can play. We go out there, and that’s our goal: shut you down, shut your lights out,” Jones said of the defense. “So, I think that’s big ups to the defense today. We came out there, executed, and we were able to go out there and stop a real good offense.”

title: 5 Winners, 1 Loser in Seahawks Big Win vs. Chiefs
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are making a statement with their 20-3 win against the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7's edition of Sunday Night Football.
After back-to-back losses, the Seahawks needed to bounce back strong , and they did just that against the Chiefs. Here's a look at the winners and losers from the matchup.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba looked dominant once again against the Chiefs. The NFL's leading receiver added to his total with 150 yards on nine catches and a touchdown.
JSN continues to establish himself as the best wideout in the game, and doing so against a really good defense like the Chiefs' only solidifies that.
The front seven stifled the Chiefs' offense all day long. Kenneth Walker III came into the game averaging 133 rushing yards per contest, but he managed to only gain 36 yards on the ground on 14 carries, good for 2.6 yards per carry.
By taking out Kansas City's top weapon, the Seahawks were able to take control of the game from there.
While Walker struggled for the Chiefs, his replacement, Emanuel Wilson, had one of his best showings of the season. Wilson gained 82 yards on 20 carries and had a touchdown of his own in the fourth quarter to secure the victory.
Wilson might concede some carries in the coming weeks to Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price as they return from their injuries, but he looks like someone who deserves a role within the offense.
Seahawks defensive back Ty Okada had the Seahawks' lone turnover of the evening. His interception in the second quarter, as the Chiefs were entering Seahawks territory, took away a bunch of momentum, and Seattle was able to capitalize with a touchdown on the ensuing drive. Okada's big play put the Seahawks on a path to victory, and he should be commended for it.
On a night when a lot of things went the Seahawks' way, Rashid Shaheed is the lone loser in the matchup. Shaheed suffered a knee injury that knocked him out for the rest of the game.
It remains to be seen how long Shaheed will be out, but his absence is definitely a loss for the Seahawks' offense.

title: Charles Cross Injury Update: Seahawks Left Tackle Leaves In Fourth
full_text:
Right now, things are going according to plan for the Seattle Seahawks. They hold a 13-3 lead, have the ball in scoring range, and there are less than five minutes left in the fourth quarter. However, the positive vibes of the moment were momentarily halted when Charles Cross exited with an injury. He walked off, but the severity of the injury is to be determined.
The star tackle, who was given a nine-figure contract extension last year, has been off to a strong start to 2026, if perhaps not quite perfect. Without him, Josh Jones takes the field, a position that he’s succeeded in before, and held his own last year for the Seahawks when Charles Cross missed a few weeks near the end of the season.
The Seahawks were able to score a touchdown to extend the lead to three scores without him, and with less than four minutes remaining now it's unlikely the team needs Cross to return, even if he can. This is one position where the Seahawks can feel relatively secure in their depth. However, Cross is a staple on a line that is just trying to get continuity back after Bradford's injury.
Cross looked to be in some pain and discomfort as he came off the field and onto the sideline. Whether that makes the injury serious is unknown as of now, but we likely won't find out until tomorrow at this point. Seattle may need to go to the practice squad for a week or two to give themselves some depth. Logan Brown is a frontrunner.
Again, the real issue is in the broken opportunity to continue to build familiarity with the offensive line all playing together. That is the main thing this unit has going for it, but so far they've had very limited opportunities to gel together because of injuries. Anthony Bradford was out from week two to now, and the Seahawks replaced him with a rotation of guards.
The Seahawks are about to run out the clock on a victory, so again, there's no real reason for Cross to go back in. Josh Jones is more than good enough to handle the responsibilities of the last few minutes of this one. But ultimately, this offense has little chance to be what it can be without Cross playing, and playing well.

title: 49ers Have 5 Pleasant Surprises Entering Bye Week
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are heading into the bye week at 6-1. Despite losing their most recent game , the season has featured plenty of surprises that have been better than expected.
Odighizuwa was a fantastic trade acquisition this offseason. The 49ers did not expect both Alfred Collins and CJ West to end up on the IR, but they were leaning heavily on those two. However, it is not an issue because of the presence of Odighizuwa.
He is on pace for the second most snaps of his career as well as a potential career-high in sacks. The bye week is coming at the perfect time for Odighizuwa, who should come out fresh.
Between Jaden Dugger and Gracen Halton, the 49ers found two defensive starters on Day Three of the NFL Draft. Dugger starts as the third linebacker, which is a minimal role. However, when Dre Greenlaw was suspended, he stepped in and started as the number two next to Fred Warner. He has been a great addition.
Halton has played far more than expected due to injuries on the line. Still, he has been excellent as a pass rusher and has started to take strides as a run defender. These two head into a much-deserved bye week.
This one is tough to add, because everyone knew that Evans would be great for the 49ers when healthy. The issue is that many were unsure how healthy he has been. However, it is a bit surprising just how good and impactful he is when he plays. He is still one of the top receivers in the NFL.  Still, health has been an issue holding him back.
Green has had a few down moments, but the overall trend of the year is that he has taken a massive step. He went from being pushed for his starting spot to pushing to sign an extension this offseason. The 49ers challenged him, and he has responded.
Morris is coming off his worst game, but the secondary finally broke after losing Upton Stout on top of Marques Sigle. With Nick Bosa and a few interior linemen also out, he could not slow down the Atlanta Falcons. Still, the defense has been great all season despite being undermanned. The credit has to go to Morris.

title: Why Mike Evans is the Real 49ers MVP
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers were extremely sloppy in their 29-20 loss to the Atlanta Falcons . No one played up to their capabilities, which wasn't surprising.
It's hard to hold this performance against the 49ers as something groundbreaking. This is a game that they will want to put behind them as fast as they can.
And with the Bye Week in full effect, it'll be easy for them to do. However, one thing did stand out emphatically against the Falcons, and that's Mike Evans being the real 49ers MVP.
Brock Purdy gets all of the praise and the MVP narrative push, but against the Falcons, he looked like a quarterback who couldn't perform without relying on Evans.
In fact, that's been the case since the moment Evans left Week 6 against the Washington Commanders with an Achilles injury. The 49ers' offense falls off significantly without him.
In the six quarters that the 49ers have been without Evans, they've mustered only 23 points. Purdy has only managed one touchdown pass and has thrown two interceptions in that span.
If you're a big EPA person: the 49ers offense ranked second in EPA per play with Evans at .193. They fall to -0.055 EPA per play without him in six quarters.
As great as Purdy has played this year, it's tough to argue that Evans isn't as important, if not more. For Purdy, he clearly needs Evans to excel, making Evans the real MVP, not him.
Maybe Purdy will excel again the more he can trust Jordan Watkins, Jacob Cowing, Brandin Cooks, and Christian Kirk. The odds are that he will need to.
It's not guaranteed that Evans will be back in Week 9 after the Bye against the Las Vegas Raiders. Evans is nursing Achilles tendinitis. That can hamper him for the next month or longer.
If Purdy wants to fuel his MVP narrative, he'll need to prove he can still excel without Evans. I'm not saying he needs to throw for over 300 yards and three touchdowns.
That's unfair. Purdy will struggle without Evans. That's a given, but can he still have a few drives where he's balling out?
He could've had an MVP drive against the Falcons in the end, had he not thrown his second interception on the second-to-last series of the game.
A touchdown drive there would've fueled his MVP narrative. Instead, he looks like a quarterback who needs Evans to thrive at an MVP level.
Having Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson back wouldn't have dramatically changed everything either. It would've been much better, but compared to Evans, it's night and day.
MVP talks surrounding Purdy should cool off until then.

title: One Change 49ers Must Make After Week 7 Loss to Falcons
full_text:
Losing 29-20 to the Atlanta Falcons is one of those games where the San Francisco 49ers have to shrug their shoulders and move on as quickly as possible.
They were sloppy for the vast majority of that game, with countless self-inflicted wounds. However, several factors were going against them heading into this matchup, which is why it was a predictable loss .
There shouldn't be a significant reaction to this loss, especially with the Bye Week in full effect. But there is one obvious change the 49ers must make after their Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
They must play rookie Ephesians Prysock over Jack Jones . It's time. There's no reason to be trotting Jones out there when he doesn't provide any positive impact.
Jones was solid in Week 1 against the Los Angeles Rams, but it was clearly a blip. His performance against the Falcons is more indicative of the player he's been throughout his career.
It felt like every time the ball was around Jones, he was drawing a penalty flag. I wouldn't be surprised if the Falcons made it a point to attack Jones, knowing he'd commit a penalty.
It's a wise plan. Why not go after the undisciplined player? It's free yards and conversions. That alone should tell the 49ers why they shouldn't play Jones anymore.
He's a liability when he's out there. If an offense gets excited to see him on the field, that's a massive problem. Now, that will probably be the same for Prysock.
He hasn't played this season and missed some time in training camp due to an injury. But at least Prysock can grow and learn from his mistakes.
Prysock is a rookie. He gives the 49ers long-term benefit. Jones doesn't provide that. He has no future with the 49ers. Why not let Prysock take his snaps?
At the very least, divide the playing time between Prysock and Jones. Maybe if the game is out of reach, you let Prysock play over Jones.
That way, Kyle Shanahan and Raheem Morris can see what he can do. It wouldn't be the wisest move to throw Prysock in a tight game. The pressure would be tremendous.
But they can pick the appropriate spots when they need a fourth cornerback on the field to play Prysock over Jones. It can't get any worse than trotting out Jones, the penalty machine.

title: 8 Winners and Losers From 49ers' Week 7 Loss to Falcons
full_text:
Despite playing sloppily for the majority of the game, the San Francisco 49ers were in it until the final minutes against the Atlanta Falcons .
Unfortunately, they couldn't get enough of their players to step up, leading them to lose for the first time this season, 29-20. Some players were close to having an amazing performance had they made a couple of extra plays. That said, here are eight winners and losers from the 49ers' Week 7 loss to the Falcons.
It looked like the 2025 season all over again when the 49ers leaned on Christian McCaffrey to carry their offense in the opening series. He was moving incredibly well, finishing the drive with a touchdown.
However, McCaffrey would exit the game later in the first half with a quad injury. Thankfully, he returned in the second half, rendering his injury minuscule. His exit initially caused concern, but since he came back and was fine, it's a tremendous win.
It wasn't a tremendous performance from the 49ers' offensive line compared to every other game this season, but they still played very well against the Falcons.
They helped clear rushing lanes for McCaffrey and the rest of the running backs. Brock Purdy was also only sacked twice and pressured 10 times on 42 dropbacks. That's a pretty sound outing.
Seeing how much of a step back the 49ers' offense took without Mike Evans was alarming. It's time to give Evans the credit for being the real MVP, and not Purdy. Their passing attack loses much of its lethality.
Evans' impact is second to none. Not even having Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson against Atlanta would've been the same as having Evans alone. This game cemented how valuable Evans is to the 49ers.
You would've thought Raheem Morris would've been locked in to play the team that fired him last season, but he wasn't. The 49ers' defense was fine up until the final four minutes of the second quarter.
From that point on, they weren't able to get enough stops against the Falcons' offense. They also weren't as fiery as they've been in every game this season. That falls on Morris as the leader of the defense.
Rookie Kaelon Black was so close to being a winner, but he wound up a loser because of his fumble in the second quarter. That fumble was the beginning of the end for the 49ers. They lost all of their momentum after that.
It's a bummer for Black because this was his breakout game. He rushed 12 times for 63 yards and a touchdown on a 30-yard run. However, once he fumbled, he only saw one more carry for the rest of the game.
The 49ers were close to rendering Black's fumble moot, but Osa Odighizuwa, of all people, fell for the fourth-down trap, where an offense attempts to draw a defender offsides for a first-down conversion since there are five or fewer yards to go.
As a borderline elite veteran, he shouldn't have jumped, giving the Falcons a new set of downs and allowing them to score a touchdown in the final seconds of the half. That derailed the 49ers.
It felt like every time Jack Jones was around the ball in pass coverage, he was drawing a penalty. The 49ers need to keep him buried on the depth chart and play rookie Ephesians Prysock. They gain nothing by playing Jones. At least Prysock gives them long-term growth.
Similar to Black, Watkins could've been a winner, but his two best catches of the game didn't count, including the touchdown pass early in the fourth quarter. If he reels those catches in, especially the touchdown, he would've been talked about as a savior today. Instead, it's just another game for him.
The MVP talk revolving around Purdy should sober up. He had his first mediocre game of the season, which isn't surprising. He's not working with much talent at wide receiver, but it also revealed that he's reliant on Evans to excel. Without Evans, he won't make many plays.
