title: 49ers' Week 7 Loss Reveals 4 Rising Players
full_text:
While the San Francisco 49ers lost in Week 7, they did see some performers step up and improve their stock. Who might come out of the bye week with more work or a greater appreciation for their role?
Mustapha started his third straight game after being benched to start the season. He allowed a touchdown but otherwise was strong in his start with a couple of impact tackles. Combining this with his Monday Night Football performance speaks to a player who is going to be hard to bench in the coming weeks.
Ji’Ayir Brown struggled again, so when Marques Sigle returns from injury, the 49ers might consider starting Mustapha next to Sigle. They have been the two best safeties this season.
Watkins has slowly but surely started to come around for the 49ers. He did not produce much in his rookie season due to injuries. Then, an offseason injury derailed the start of his 2026 season. He got on the field for Week 4 and produced 60 yards. However, the 49ers pushed some veterans over him in recent weeks. With Mike Evans out, he saw more work and put up 56 yards. He also had a game-changing touchdown reception that would have been an impressive catch.
With Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing rotating in and getting snaps, the team is better off playing Watkins as one of their best receivers and benching those two.
Thompson made the team as a UDFA. He saw some work in the first couple of weeks but suffered an ankle injury, causing him to miss multiple games. He came back in Week 6 and had a limited role. Then, Week 7 was the best game of his NFL career. He had a career-high 28 snaps, recorded his first career pressure, and had two quality run stops. Now, he can take the bye week to get completely healthy and mentally prepare for a home stretch.
Prysock was inactive for the first few weeks of the season. Then, he stepped in and played special teams for a few weeks. San Francisco only played him for two snaps in Week 7, but he saw the field for the first time.
Ashtyn Davis is a disaster as a backup slot, and Jack Jones has been picked on the outside. They should try Prysock as their fourth defensive back.

title: What We Learned About the 49ers in their Loss to the Atlanta Falcons
full_text:
We learned more about the 49ers from one loss this season than from all six wins combined.
In the wins, we learned that the 49ers can beat any team in the NFL, even the defending Super Bowl Champion Seahawks in Seattle, if Mike Evans is healthy. He's the biggest difference between the 2026 and the 2025 49ers. When he's on the field, Brock Purdy plays like Joe Montana, and Kyle Shanahan coaches like Bill Walsh.
But we also learned that Evans won't be healthy all season. He broke ribs in Week 3 and came down with Achilles tendinitis in Week 6, which cost him the last game and a half. He probably will have to play through this tendinitis the rest of the year. Plus, he just turned 33, and he missed nine games last year. So, the 49ers have to prepare themselves for life without him.
As currently constructed, they're bad without Evans. They could lose to any team in the league, even the Falcons, if Evans doesn't play, as we just learned. In the past six quarters that he has missed, the 49ers have scored just 23 points, even though they still have Shanahan, Purdy, George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey. That's pathetic.
And that's because Evans is their best player. And they know it. When he's on the field, Purdy can't help but throw him the ball because good things happen when he does. And Shanahan can't call enough plays for Evans because no one can cover him.
Evans is so good, they overused him early in the season. Went to him repeatedly just to beat the Seahawks in October, and that decision led to Achilles tendinitis, which might not go away completely.
As a result, Shanahan had to find someone else to feature against the Falcons. Of course, he chose Christian McCaffrey, who's too old to carry the offense at this point in his career.
Out of sheer necessity and desperation, Shanahan called six plays for McCaffrey on the opening drive alone, and he quickly injured his quad. Now, he's another injured veteran player the 49ers have to manage. Evans' Achilles tendinitis is having a domino effect on the roster.
That's the not-so-good news.
Here's the good news: The 49ers have a bye week, and Evans is coming back soon. So are Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson. De'Zhaun Stribling might come back as well. Which means the 49ers probably won't ever play another game with Jordan Watkins, Jacob Cowing, Brandon Cooks and Christian Kirk as their only active wide receivers.
But they probably will play more games without Evans and/or McCaffrey. And let's face it, George Kittle and Trent Williams most likely will miss a few games, too, considering neither ever has played all 17 games in a season.
As long as they have Evans, they'll be dangerous. Any time he's out, they'll be vulnerable. If he misses one playoff game, they'll probably lose it.
So unless the 49ers trade for another Hall of Fame wide receiver before the deadline, their season depends on Evans.

title: 3 Reasons for Optimism After 49ers Loss to Falcons
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers' 29-20 loss to the Atlanta Falcons was not pretty . However, there are some positive spins that can be taken away from the game. What can 49ers fans lean on after the loss?
The schedule makers did not make life easy on the 49ers. First, they gave them a Monday Night Football game at home, which is helpful. However, the downside to that is a short week ahead. The 49ers not only had a short week, but they also had to travel across the country and play the game at 10 AM on the West Coast.
So, due to the game being played 32 hours after the Falcons, the team could not acclimate as quickly. More than that, the 49ers had the bye week to look ahead to. It would be easy to rest some players that had questionable injuries due to the inconvenience and lack of time to heal.
It is easy to see how the game got away from them.
San Francisco could have had a few names come back this week, but the short turnaround and bye week made it easy to rest players. Beyond that, they had a three-game lead in the division entering the day. So, they could take things easy this week. The plus side to that is they should come out of the bye week much healthier.
Nick Bosa, Deebo Samuel, and Mike Evans should all be back. Demarcus Robinson and Marques Sigle are likely not too far behind. Plus, guys like George Kittle, Christian McCaffrey, and Trent Williams get a week to reset. The bye week was well-timed for the 49ers this year.
The loss is not going to stop the 49ers from buying. If anything, it exposed a few holes that might need to be plugged. The team is going to need some defensive line help. Wide receiver is also an expected addition at the deadline. Still, left guard has not been talked about much, but it has been established as a need.
The lack of cornerback depth was also exposed in the 49ers loss. These are positions that were not discussed and could have bitten them down the line. Now, the 49ers can address it at the trade deadline.

title: Two New 49ers' Trade Needs Exposed in Falcons Loss
full_text:
There have been three needs for the San Francisco 49ers that have been discussed for weeks. Most would agree that if San Francisco makes a move at the trade deadline, it will be a wide receiver, an edge rusher, or an interior defensive lineman.
However, after the 49ers lost 29-20 to the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7, there have been a few more needs that are starting to emerge. What else can the 49ers do at the trade deadline?
The team has been able to get by with Connor Colby for the past few weeks, but now it is starting to look like it is becoming a problem. Colby looked like he had taken a step in year two, but as the competition improved, he struggled.
It started against Byron Murphy and Leonard Williams against Seattle. Then, Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw got the best of him on Monday Night Football. The Falcons' interior is not great, but Gervon Dexter beat Colby consistently.
The 49ers have Carver Willis, but he is a rookie, and he has been hurt for most of the regular season. That would be a risk to put him in, even with a bye week to adjust.
Landon Dickerson of the Philadelphia Eagles and Quenton Nelson of the Indianapolis Colts could surprisingly be available. The 49ers might have to make a move.
Coming into the season, the 49ers secondary looked deeper than past years. Injuries have not helped, but the group is starting to get exposed. It might force a deadline move. Upton Stout and Marques Sigle are expected to come back soon, and that can remedy some of the issues.
However, San Francisco has had to play dime with Stout out, and their extra defensive back continues to be an issue. Jack Jones has been awful when the team plays dime. With Stout out, he started on the outside, and Deommodore Lenoir moved into the slot. It did not go well.
However, their other option is sticking safety Ashtyn Davis in the slot, and that does not work either.
Malik Mustapha was benched to start the season, Sigle was benched last year. Ji’Ayir Brown has played so poorly he will likely get benched when Sigle is back. All three are ahead of Davis, who is playing now. Whether it be a depth cornerback or safety, they could make a move.

title: 49ers' Grades After 29-20 Loss to the Falcons: Brock Purdy Loses the Game
full_text:
ATLANTA -- The San Francisco 49ers just lost 29-20 to the Atlanta Falcons . Here are the 49ers' grades for this performance.
Brock Purdy lost this game. To be fair, he didn't have his top-six wide receivers (Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Demarcus Robinson, De'Zhaun Stribling, Ricky Pearsall and Brandon Aiyuk). Still, he had George Kittle, Christian McCaffrey and Kyle Shanahan. Plus, Purdy had Jordan Watkins, who had a terrific game (more on him in a minute). If Purdy had put more air underneath his deep pass to Watkins, he would have scored a touchdown instead of getting tackled after a gain of 35 yards. In addition, Purdy threw two picks -- the first to a safety while trying to throw the ball out of bounds, and the second to a linebacker right in front of him whom he never saw. Finally, Purdy also turned the ball over on downs when he took a sack on fourth down. Purdy is still a good quarterback, but he can probably forget about the MVP Award after this performance. We thought he had improved, but it turns out he simply plays much better when Mike Evans is on the field (who doesn't?).
Christian McCaffrey was outstanding despite missing most of the first half with a quad injury. Kaelon Black also played well, minus his fumble. That was a crucial play in the game. Jordan James also fumbled, but the 49ers recovered. And Kyle Juszczyk caught a touchdown pass near the goal line. Overall, this position is not the reason the 49ers lost.
George Kittle caught eight passes for 88 yards despite the Falcons bracketing him most of the game, but also fumbled on the final drive. To be fair, the 49ers already had essentially lost at that point. Still, it's unusual to see Kittle put the ball on the ground.
Sure, they're a bunch of backups, but none of these guys turned the ball over. Of course, Christian Kirk did nothing -- I still don't know why the 49ers signed him. But Jacob Cowing was decent, and Jordan Watkins was good. He finished with three catches for 56 yards. One of those catches should have been a long touchdown, but Purdy underthrew him. He also had another play in which he was wide open deep, but Purdy never saw him. Finally, Watkins nearly made an incredible touchdown catch, but he didn't control the ball after hitting the ground. The emergence of Watkins as a legitimate threat is one of the main silver linings from this loss. The 49ers have to get him more involved in the offense after the bye week.
They gave up two sacks, but also helped pave the way for the offense to gain a whopping 5.3 yards per carry. This position group is the least of the 49ers' issues as they approach the trade deadline.
They limited Bijan Robinson to just 3.2 yards per carry, which is extremely impressive, but they also recorded zero sacks against a subpar quarterback who doesn't move particularly well. The 49ers just let him stand still unbothered all game like he was watching waves at the beach. They really need to trade for DeForest Buckner as soon as possible. They need more pass rushers.
Fred Warner had 13 tackles and Dre Greenlaw had 12. Impressive. And they didn't hit anyone helmet-to-helmet or out of bounds, which is even more impressive for them.
They gave up three touchdown passes and a 118.9 passer rating to Michael Freaking Penix Jr., which never should happen. Granted, the 49ers had no pass rush. Still, the coverage was so soft, it was hard for the defensive linemen to get home. That's because Upton Stout missed the game with a shoulder injury, and his replacement was Jack Jones, who's awful. When the Falcons picked on him, the 49ers replaced him with Ahstyn Davis, who's worse. Finally, the 49ers put Ephesians Prysock in the game, which was smart -- he's better than Jones and Davis. Strange it took the 49ers so long to figure that out.
They gave up multiple long kickoff returns, and Eddy Pineiro missed his fourth extra point of the season and his seventh kick in seven games. He is one of the worst extra-point kickers the league has seen since it moved back the extra point roughly 10 years ago. Too bad the 49ers gave him a four-year extension this offseason, because he's gotta go. The 49ers need to replace him before he costs them any more games. Because as poorly as the 49ers played, they would have been down just one score on the final possession if Pineiro hadn't missed an extra point earlier in the game. Cut him.
Raheem Morris' defense wasn't great, but it succeeded in its main objective, which was keeping Bijan Robinson in check. He never scored. The biggest reason the 49ers lost, other than their kicker missing yet another extra point, was the offense. It stunk. It turned the ball over five times -- two interceptions, two fumbles and one turnover on downs. The running game was working, and the 49ers had the lead in the second half, and yet Kyle Shanahan fell in love with the passing game, just like last week. He called 42 passes and just 21 runs, which is inexplicable considering the 49ers were missing so many wide receivers. Fortunately, the 49ers still are 6-1, and they have a bye week coming up, so Shanahan can look himself in the mirror, acknowledge that he coached poorly the past two weeks, and fix his mistakes. The Super Bowl run depends on it.

title: Analyst Names Bucs’ Biggest Emerging Need for 2027: Do We Agree?
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers were finally able to put together a complete game in all three phases in their 43-13 victory over the Carolina Panthers to keep them in the hunt for the NFC South title.
It appears to be a great sign of things turning around for the Bucs, who have gotten off to a slow start, sitting at just 2-5 on the season.
While it might appear that way, there is no guarantee that the team will play to that level as the rest of the year unfolds.
In fact, many still believe the Buccaneers will have one of the worst records in the NFL. That includes NFL Draft OnSI analyst Justin Melo, who identified Tampa Bay's biggest need when they pick eighth in the 2027 NFL Draft.
"It's been a disappointing season for a Tampa Bay Buccaneers team that entered 2026 with playoff aspirations, but a dominant Week 7 win over the Carolina Panthers restored some faith," Melo wrote. "With Baker Mayfield signed to an extension, strengthening the trenches on both offense and defense should be an offseason priority."
While strengthening the trenches is always a philosophy that usually nets success, it might not be the priority that most believe it would be.
Yes, Yaya Diaby will become a free agent after the season, but I would expect the Bucs to bring him back. With Diaby back, along with most of the rest of the defensive line and continued development of Rueben Bain Jr. and David Walker, we believe that there will be a bigger area of need for the Bucs in the 2027 NFL Draft.
The bigger need that has become excruciatingly evident is infusing elite, dynamic talent into the skill positions on offense.
The running game is in a great spot, but the Bucs absolutely could use upgrades at wide receiver and tight end.
Chris Godwin has been a staple for Tampa Bay, but his production continues to decrease over the years and he isn't getting any younger. Relying on him as a long-term foundational piece is not the route to take.
Emeka Egbuka has struggled dating back to the second half of last season, and while there is plenty of time for him to turn things around, the Bucs will need another playmaker to take the pressure off him.
The Bucs like what they have in Ted Hurst and Tez Johnson, but both are still young and not quite developed into receivers you can count on week-to-week or every down.
The Buccaneers' tight end situation isn't all that great either, despite Cade Otton signing a three-year extension this offseason. They would love to get someone who can make an impact game in and game out.
With Baker Mayfield getting extended right before the season, the franchise must give him the weapons to be successful over the next few seasons. If they are unable to, then the offense will continue to suffer, and wins will be tough to come by.

title: Buccaneers' Baker Mayfield Joins Exclusive NFL Company
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers shocked the entire NFL world on Sunday, demolishing the Carolina Panthers 43-13 for their second win of the season.
The Bucs dominated in every facet of the game, with the offense leaning heavily on the run game to the tune of over 250 yards and only 64 passing yards from Baker Mayfield.
While Mayfield didn't have to do much in the win, he was able to toss his 200th career touchdown pass that put him in elite company.
Mayfield only had one touchdown pass on the day that was caught by Tez Johnson, and it was just enough to get him onto this list.
Mayfield (200) joins Aaron Rodgers (540), Matthew Stafford (434), Kirk Cousins (314), Patrick Mahomes (276), Joe Flacco (272), Jared Goff (270), Andy Dalton (254), Dak Prescott (253), and Josh Allen (229). 98 of his touchdown passes have come as a Tampa Bay Buccaneer.
Mayfield will have work to do if he hopes to make his way further up the list, but it shines a light on what he has been able to accomplish through his up-and-down career.
Despite the lack of a passing game against the Panthers, the Buccaneers' running game and offensive line showed just how strong they can be.
Tampa Bay will likely continue leaning on the ground game with the likes of Bucky Irving, Kenny Gainwell, and Sean Tucker, but at some point they must figure out how to utilize the passing game to their advantage.
Zac Robinson and Mayfield will need to come together to find out the best way to do this. Behind the line of scrimmage passes and screens aren't going to cut it, so there must be some work done to figure out how to open up the field.
With the Atlanta Falcons heading to Raymond James Stadium for the Bucs' second divisional game, it will be pivotal for the offense, particularly the passing game, to get going.
Much like Carolina, Atlanta's offense has improved this season with Michael Penix Jr. back at quarterback. The defense will once again have to play up a level to prevent them from scoring, and if the offense can put up numbers like they did against the Panthers, then they could have a fantastic shot at coming away with their third win of the season and second division victory.

title: Buccaneers May Have an All-Pro Cornerback Candidate on Their Roster
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are riding high after a dominant 43-13 win over the Carolina Panthers in Week 7. Tampa Bay has struggled all year, but on Sunday, they did just about everything right to come away with a crucial division victory.
The offense has already been talked about plenty — it put up an unbelievable 258 rushing yards on the day — but the defense played an excellent game as well. The defense had a scoop and score for a touchdown and picked the ball off twice on the day, and it also got to Bryce Young in the backfield five times.
Another defensive player had an extra play that made him stand out, however. And there's some buzz after Sunday that he could be one of the NFL's best cornerbacks.
Former NFL player and current NFL personality Ryan Clark made a bold declaration after watching the Bucs dismantle the Panthers — that Bucs cornerback Zyon McCollum is the All-Pro corner for the first part of the season.
For those who know ball y’all get this! 1st quarter of the season All Pro Corner… Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ Zyon McCollum
McCollum has played quite well this year. He's generally locked down his spot on the field and hasn't been targeted as frequently as other corners, but so far, he has eight passes defended, one interception and 23 solo tackles.
He also has two points — he scooped up a block kick against the Panthers Sunday and took it back to the house, adding to the carnage.
McCollum has played quite well alongside fellow corner Jacob Parrish, but he'll have some stiff competition if he wants to be named an All-Pro. Cleveland Browns cornerback Denzel Ward has been playing lights out so far this season, and he nabbed another pick against the Tennessee Titans in Cleveland's win on Sunday, and Los Angeles Rams cornerback Trent McDuffie has also been strong.
Additionally, some people aren't as high on McCollum. He currently has a PFF grade of 60.8, putting him at 54th in the NFL among his position group.
The Bucs will have to string some more wins together if McCollum wants to be taken seriously among those other names. That started in Carolina, and the Bucs have another opportunity to do it against an NFC South opponent when they face off against the Atlanta Falcons next Sunday at Raymond James Stadium.

title: Grading the Buccaneers' Dominating Win Over the Carolina Panthers
full_text:
It was one of the most dominant games in franchise history as the Tampa Bay Buccaneers coasted to a 43-13 win over the Carolina Panthers.
Many deserve credit for this victory, and we will be going over all of it in this one. Let's go over the top grades for the Bucs' Week 7 win.
Baker Mayfield did not do a lot in his return game, and he didn't need to. However, he did finish with 64 passing yards and a passing touchdown, with zero turnovers on the day and a 109.7 quarterback rating. He was the handoff king in this game, and that's 100% okay.
It was one of the best rushing games in franchise history for the Buccaneers. Bucky Irving had 24 carries for 106 yards and two touchdowns; Kenny Gainwell had 14 carries for 88 yards, and even Sean Tucker had seven carries for 52 yards and a touchdown as well.
This is what a peak Zac Robinson game can look like, as he was able to generate some great rushing teams while serving as offensive coordinator of the Atlanta Falcons. Here's hoping for more of this in the future.
Emeka Egbuka missed this game with a concussion, and there is not much else to speak about here. Tez Johnson was the best thing for this group, as he finished with three receptions for 47 yards and a touchdown. Chris Godwin also finished with four catches for 27 yards.
The tight end room gets this grade purely off of their blocking ability. Cade Otton, Payne Durham and Bauer Sharp were instrumental in the Bucs having a gigantic game on the ground, and they deserve plenty of credit for that.
These guys were absolute units in this one. When you lead the charge for an offense that generates 258 rushing yards and three touchdowns, you are getting a good grade. This group rose to the occasion in spades, and that's with Benjamin Chukwuma filling in for the injured Luke Goedeke in this matchup.
The players in this group were absolute all-stars in this game. Yaya Diaby led the way with three sacks, putting him second on the team this season. Vita Vea had a sack as well, and Al-Quadin Muhammad had a sack that forced a fumble, which was recovered by Calijah Kancey for the touchdown.
Overall, the Bucs defense finished with six quarterback hits, eight tackles for loss and five sacks on Panthers quarterback Bryce Young.
Josiah Trotter was solid in this game and led the Bucs with 10 total tackles on the day and a pass deflection. However, Anzalone still struggles to make tackles, and SirVocea Dennis got beat on a 50-yard touchdown in this game. With Christian Rozeboom on the injured reserve with a finger injury, Trotter is the saving grace of this group.
The defensive line wasn't the only group that had fun today. Tykee Smith had seven total tackles, one pass deflection, and an interception. Rookie Keionte Scott had a blocked extra point that fellow corner Zyon McCollum returned for two points. Speaking of McCollum, he also had an interception in this game as well as a pass deflection. Jacob Parrish got involved as well, with good coverage and a pass deflection.
Danny Smith has this special teams unit humming lately. There was a muffed punt return by former Buccaneers receiver David Moore that was recovered by Bucs special teamer Ko Keift. There was also the blocked extra point by Keionte Scott that was returned for two points by Zyon McCollum.
Finally, kicker Chase McLaughlin continues to be the best thing about the team and made all of his kicks for 11 points.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly From Buccaneers' 43-13 Victory Over Panthers
full_text:
Through the first six weeks of the NFL season, we've had a lot of bad and ugly topics to discuss as it relates to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .
Week 7 was a different story, though, as the Buccaneers looked like the team that most people envisioned coming into the season. On Sunday, the Bucs completely dominated the Carolina Panthers in every facet of the game en route to a 43-13 victory on the road against the top team in the NFC South.
In a game the Buccaneers absolutely had to have, they finally executed with consistency and performed up to expectations.
Let's take a closer look at the good, the bad, and the ugly that we saw from the Buccaneers in their most impressive win of the season so far.
From the very start of the game, Bucky Irving established himself as the most dynamic offensive player on the field. Irving was patient, elusive, and explosive in space while rushing for 106 yards and 2 TD's on 24 carries.  Irving's unique ability to manipulate defenders by playing cat-and-mouse behind his blockers, and  then turning on the jets at the exact right moment to creative chunk plays was on full display in this game.
It wasn't just Bucky Irving, as both Sean Tucker and Kenneth Gainwell had plenty of success in their opportunities as well. The one constant? The offensive line. The entire unit was exceptional in this game, paving lanes in the run game while dominating the Panthers' defensive line.
The interior of Bredeson, Barton and Mauch really came to play in this contest, and they were clearly on the same page with whatever blocking scheme was being executed on a particular run.
Speaking of stepping up, even without Luke Goedeke in the lineup, Ben Chukwuma showed up in a big way by holding down the right side of the line, and his development as a quality reserve tackle so early in his career is a major positive for this team moving forward.
Bucs OL with one of the great first halves you’ll ever see. Obliterated Carolina on the ground and bought Baker a lot of time to make a couple out of structure plays
The Buccaneers' new offensive coordinator has taken plenty of heat, and rightfully so, for the team's poor offensive performance so far this year. That being said, it's important to give credit where credit is due, and Robinson deserves his flowers for sticking with what worked in Carolina.
It didn't take long for the Buccaneers' offense to assert their dominance in the run game, and Robinson had no problem sticking with that approach for the rest of the game as the Buccaneers rushed  for 49 times for a total of 258 yards on the ground, averaging over 5 yards per carry.
Not only did this allow the Bucs to control the clock and protect their lead, but it also ensured that Mayfield — nursing a recently dislocated thumb on his throwing hand — could, for the most part, stay out of harm's way.
Todd Bowles' defense looked like one of the NFL's best on this day. The vision Bowles has for his defense is a pressure applying group of front, backed up by a flock of ball hawks in the secondary, and that's exactly what we saw today, even without Antoine Winfield in the lineup.
Both Tykee Smith and Zyon McCollum came away with interceptions on the back end. Meanwhile, Calijah Kancey provided a scopp and score, which helped give the Buccaneers even more breathing room in the first half.
Sunday's game marks the first time that Tampa Bay's defense has amassed 5.0+ sacks and four-or-more takeaways in a single game since 10/26/25 at New Orleans.
Speaking of splash plays, the Bucs' gained some serious advantages in the special teams department today, with the punt coverage group recovering a fumble deep in Panthers' territory early in the game. Shortly thereafter, Tykee Smith blocked an extra point attempt, which McCollum then recovered and returned the length of the field for a rare 2-point addition to the scoreboard.
BLOCKED THE EXTRA POINT & TO THE HOUSE FOR ✌️ 📺: #TBvsCAR on FOX pic.twitter.com/G5ITN0VTcA
The Buccaneers defensive line had Bryce Young under serious duress for a good chunk of this game. When it was all said and done, the Bucs got home for 5 sacks on the day, with 3 of those coming from Yaya Diaby, who had a much needed breakout game in the sack department.
Al Quadin-Muhammad and Vita Vea supplied the other two QB sacks for the Bucs, and Kancey nearly got another one. The Buccaneers' offseason vision of a impactful committee of versatile defensive linemen applying pressure consistently materialized in this game, and would provide a big boost to the team if it continues in the weeks to come.
This is downright unfair considering the Bucs put up 43 points in a game where Mayfield was playing with a recently dislocated thumb, but if I have to nitpick, it would point to the lack of production through the air. Mayfield was 7/11 for 64 yards passing in this game, and although the team was wise to stick with the ground game, they'll need to develop a more balanced attack moving forward, which will require the passing game to wake up at some point.
Panthers really getting annihilated by a team that can barely throw a forward pass. NFC South is incredible
The trio of Irving, Gainwell and Sean Tucker made the Panthers' defenders at every level look downright silly in this game. As much as those Bucs' RB's ran with determination and elusiveness in this game, any time a team rushes for 250+ yards against an NFL defense, there's a problem.
Whether it was along the defensive line, the second level, or the secondary, Panthers' defenders simply could not bring down Buccaneer ball-carriers, and both the stats and tape will tell the same story.

title: Overreactions From Buccaneers' Blowout Win Over Panthers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers needed a win on Sunday to stay alive and keep their season afloat, and boy, did they.
The Bucs absolutely routed the Carolina Panthers, drubbing their division rivals 43-13 on Sunday. The Bucs move to 2-5 on the year, and now, they're not too far off the NFC South lead as they head into Week 8.
Here are our three overreactions from the victory over Carolina:
Tampa Bay's entire secondary has been excellent so far in 2026 — a rare bright spot for the team. But that unit has been anchored by Zyon McCollum, and week in and week out, he continues to show everyone why.
McCollum has allowed just 9.6 per depth of target attempted, and he got his first interception on Sunday against the Panthers and Bryce Young. He also returned a blocked field goal for two points, giving him a score on the year as well.
McCollum has been a lockdown corner all year, and he had his best game Sunday. He's probably not in All-Pro contention with how bad the Bucs are and his lack of picks, but if he strings together a few more turnovers, he may be impossible to ignore — he's playing to the level right now.
The Buccaneers still have plenty of struggles, and they're unlikely to make the playoffs with the rough start they've had. But with a win against the Panthers, they are very much still in this division race.
With the win, the Panthers fall to 3-3 and the Bucs stand at 2-5. They're now just 1.5 games out of that division lead, and what's more, they'll also play the Atlanta Falcons at home next week.
If they win that game next week, too? The Bucs will be 3-5 with a shot to contend for the NFC South lead. It seems ridiculous, but with how paltry the entire division has been in 2026, a string of wins together could put the Bucs firmly in sight of the playoffs after a disastrous beginning to the season. Who would have thought?
Bucky Irving proved himself to be an absolute gamechanger once again for the Bucs. In both wins Tampa Bay has had, he's put up a stellar performance, and it's clear he's a major key in what this offense wants to accomplish.
Irving had over 100 yards rushing on the day. He accounted for two of Tampa Bay's touchdowns, and he was undeniably the X-factor in Tampa Bay's big division win. He had an unbelievable 26 touches on the day, funneling the entire offense through his effort.
He's staked his claim as one of Tampa Bay's best weapons. The Bucs probably shouldn't give him almost 30 touches every game, but they might want to make sure their offensive gameplan revolves around him more often than not.

title: Buccaneers’ Todd Bowles Gets Blunt Criticism From Leonard Fournette
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have had far from the start to the season they wanted. They're currently just 1-5 and hold the worst record in the NFC, and another loss to the NFC South-leading Carolina Panthers on Sunday would almost certainly spell doom for the team's playoff hopes.
A lot of the criticism for that start has been directed toward head coach Todd Bowles. Bowles has made the playoffs in all but one of his seasons as head coach of the Bucs, but he's only had double-digit wins a single time and he's had a losing record twice during that time span.
Bowles has faced plenty of criticism over recent weeks from all sorts of people in the NFL world. One of those people has been a former player of his, Leonard Fournette, who played under Bowles as head coach for one year in 2022.
Fournette expounded on that criticism during an appearance on the 4th & South podcast he hosts with former NFL player Jarvis Landry, and he had some honest thoughts on Bowles stemming from the year he played under him in Tampa Bay.
Fournette told Landry that whenever Bowles yelled at the team, he didn't take it seriously — he also mentioned that Bowles' mindset as a defensive head coach made him, in Fournette's eyes, not pay as much attention to the offensive side of the ball.
"He might yell, but it's not one of those yells you take [seriously]," Fournette said on the podcast. "I respect him, but it's like, [when Bruce Arians] got on your ass, he got on your ass... by Bowles being a defense-minded coach, he doesn't pay attention to the offense as much. So I don't know — maybe favoritism?"
In Fournette's only year with Bowles at the helm, he put up 668 yards on 189 attempts with three touchdowns on the ground. He also had three receiving touchdowns on the year.
Fournette's words hold some weight, given that he's played under Bowles, but it's also one opinion among many when it comes to Bowles. Bowles won 10 games in 2024 and also won a playoff game with the Bucs in 2023, so he has a record of success in Tampa Bay, but the problems with his tenure have also manifested themselves year after year as well.
Bowles and the Bucs will try to reverse his fortunes, along with his team's, when they play the Panthers at 1 p.m. on the road Sunday.

title: Our Buccaneers vs. Panthers Score Predictions Are In
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers face a grim outlook for the rest of the season if they fall to 1-6 on the year. They can prevent that by defeating the Carolina Panthers on Sunday, but it won't be easy to win their first division matchup.
The Bucs will have Baker Mayfield back in the fold after a three-game absence, but will that be enough to get a win? Our staff goes over our predictions for Sunday's matchup against the Panthers:
It’s been tough sledding for the Bucs, but they might just have a chance to turn things around.
Division play begins this week against the Panthers, and all signs point towards Baker Mayfield being back.
While I do believe things will look better, I still think the offense is way off from being able to match Carolina’s offense, which will put up points.
I think the Bucs will have a chance to win the game on the final drive, but ultimately fall short once again.
Mayfield's return is spoiled by the Panthers in this one. I simply think that Carolina is the better-coached team right now and that Mayfield may be slow to start back up after returning from his thumb injury.
The Buccaneers have played so poorly this season that they’re already on the verge of switching their primary focus from postseason contention to the top pick in next year’s NFL Draft. Considering we’re not even halfway through the season, I’d consider this season to be a full-scale nightmare for any Bucs fan.
So, am I picking the Buccaneers to bounce back and take down the NFC South-leading Panthers in Carolina, you ask? No. I most certainly am not.
The Panthers head into the game with the top passing attack in the league, and Bryce Young is playing at a high caliber. The Bucs and Todd Bowles have done a fair job of defending these types of offenses this season.
My biggest concern is the offense for Tampa Bay. It’s quite obvious Zac Robinson’s offense doesn’t have an identity and even with Baker Mayfield coming back, I just don’t see it changing much. They’ll have to begin proving me wrong before I pick them to win games. Also, a reminder — the Cowboys are a bad football team.
Tampa Bay's defense will be tested by a Panthers offense that playcaller Brad Idzik has unlocked this season. Bryce Young is stretching the football down the field in a dominant way, so expect the Panthers to score points.
Don't expect the Bucs to do much on offense in return. Zac Robinson's offense has been scattershot this whole season, and while Mayfield should play better than Jalon Daniels, he'll be playing with an injured thumb after a year where he didn't start off so hot anyway. Bucs have to be able to run the ball on Carolina — if they can't, they have no chance of winning.
The Buccaneers still haven't given us a reason to pick them to win a football game. They're 1-5 as it stands, and every BucsGameday staff member thinks they'll be 1-6 whenever they wake up in the morning.

title: Bucs Tabbed As Sellers at Trade Deadline if They Drop to 1-6
full_text:
The 2026 season has not gone the way that the Tampa Bay Buccaneers had hoped.
They have limped to a 1-6 record and there are no real signs that they might turn things around.
The defense has played up to par thus far, but the real issues have been on the offensive side of the ball.
If the Bucs want to remain relevant in the NFC South race to make the playoffs, the first step would be coming away with a victory against the Carolina Panthers.
If they are unable to do so, it appears that they will become sellers ahead of the NFL trade deadline in November.
"Bucs still in NFC South hunt, but a loss Sunday would put them at 1-6," ESPN's Jeremy Fowler posted on X . "If that happens, some in league expect TB to entertain seller mode at that point."
Dropping to 1-6 would be detrimental for Tampa Bay, taking the wind out of the sails that are already barely flapping.
If they indeed do drop to 1-6, it's hard to disagree with Fowler's expectations of them becoming sellers at the trade deadline.
The Bucs' top players have not lived up to their potential or contracts, so being able to dump some of them in order to acquire young, developmental players and/or future draft capital could be the move given a lost season.
While the season wouldn't necessarily be lost at 1-6, the writing would be on the wall that there is little hope of coming away with a successful season.
With Todd Bowles' seat scorching hot, the Bucs staff could look completely different come the offseason. And in turn, the roster turnover could be pretty heavy, so why not go ahead and get a head start?
Tampa has some young pieces to build around, but if they are to lose and become sellers, names like Chris Godwin, Vita Vea, Yaya Diaby, Antoine Winfield Jr., and potentially others will be at the forefront of who could be dealt.
Taking on dead cap money from some of these guys if they were to be traded would be tough, but at this point, it could be seen as the right move as the Bucs look to rebuild a roster that has become stale in certain areas.

title: Baker Mayfield Gets Special Help From World Series-Bound Rays
full_text:
Buccaneers' star quarterback Baker Mayfield has received some help from an unexpected source. According to Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times, the Tampa Bay Rays have helped create a special glove for Mayfield to use while he continues to recover from a dislocated thumb injury he suffered in the team's week three loss to the Minnesota Vikings at the end of the game.
The glove was made by the Rays clubhouse attendant, Nick Bond, and was made with multiple versions in mind, depending on what fits best for Mayfield.
The injury Mayfield suffered was to his throwing hand, and he will look to retain a good grip on the ball going forward in both throwing and scrambling situations. Mayfield himself was a fan of the glove and said that it felt good when used:
“(It’s) not restricting because it’s on the backside. ... For me, just getting used to it. I don’t feel the difference. It’s just like me wearing a glove.” Mayfield said when asked about how using the glove helps him.
For the past three games, Mayfield has sat on the bench while backup quarterback Jalon Daniels has started in his place. Daniels has done decently in relief, posting 501 passing yards, three passing touchdowns, five interceptions, and 126 rushing yards in three total starts.
However, the offense will have a different dynamic with Mayfield in once more at quarterback than Daniels and should open up more of what the team is able to do.
Mayfield will have a good amount of improvement in return from his injury, as he was struggling to begin the 2026 season before he went down. Fresh off a $55 million-per-year extension that saw the Bucs commit to Mayfield as their guy for the foreseeable future, Mayfield posted 615 passing yards, two passing touchdowns, two interceptions, 65 rushing yards, one rushing touchdown, and a handful of fumbles lost in three starts.
Now, Mayfield will look to drag the Bucs out of a brutal 1- 5 situation where the team has many more questions than answers. Time will tell whether the Buccaneers are able to regain some of their form with Mayfield out there, or if the team continues to regress and we simply look forward to a pretty rough season coming to an end for this team.

title: JC Latham's Overlooked Breakout a Major Bright Spot in Dreadful Titans Season
full_text:
After capturing their first win of the season over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 6, the Tennessee Titans fell back down to earth in Week 7. Head coach Robert Saleh's group fell to the Cleveland Browns 27-24 on a game-winning 32-yard field goal by Andre Szmyt.
With their latest defeat to Cleveland, Tennessee is 1-6 and back to the drawing board . It's been a rough stretch for the Titans, who are now 1-12 at home since the start of the 2025 season.
Though it's been a disappointing season in Nashville, one of the major bright spots of the year so far has been right tackle JC Latham, who is quietly building a case as one of the best right tackles in football.
Though Tennessee's offensive line has been inconsistent in 2026, Latham has been a steady presence upfront. The 2024 No. 7 overall pick has allowed one sack and five quarterback pressures in 248 pass-blocking snaps, and has earned a 76.5 Pro Football Focus pass-blocking grade . Latham has also posted a 70.2 run-blocking grade and has used his imposing 6-foot-6 and 342-pound frame to be a tenacious force in the run game.
Over the last two games, Latham hasn't allowed a single quarterback pressure or committed a penalty. The 23-year-old is finally emerging as a plus starter for the Titans on the offensive line, and it's a major development for all parties.
The Titans must make a decision on Latham's fifth-year option next May, and if he maintains his high level of play, Tennessee won't think much about the choice. Latham is showcasing why he should stay in Nashville as a long-term piece and has started building his case for a lucrative contract extension.
Obviously, there's still a lot of football left to play in 2026, so it's too early for Tennessee to weigh Latham's contract situation heavily. However, it has to be on the Titans' minds with the Alabama product finally living up to his top-10 pick status.
A Week 8 road matchup against the 4-2 Cincinnati Bengals is next for the Titans. Tennessee is rapidly running out of time to turn around its season, and a loss to Cincinnati heading into the bye could set up a fire sale at the November 10 trade deadline. One player who should stay on the roster past that deadline is Latham, who is one of the few positives in another dreadful Titans campaign.

title: Grading Every Titans Position Group After Loss to Browns: Only 1 Unit Shone Bright in Week 7
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans weren’t able to keep the positive momentum rolling on Sunday, losing a 27-24 heartbreaker to the Cleveland Browns.
It was a game that started well for the Titans. The team immediately jumped out to a 14-0 lead, but it didn’t last long as they somehow went into the half trailing by three and were unable to recapture the lead.
You can count this as another game the 2026 Titans were in until the end, but ultimately couldn’t find a way to finish. This team has to start learning how to win these close games if they’re ever gonna start reaching their full potential. The Titans simply aren’t good enough to overcome the type of self inflicted mistakes they routinely make, and that’s exactly why they’re 1-6 going into Week 8.
This week’s grades aren’t exactly positive outside of a few standouts, so having said that, let’s go ahead and dive right into this week’s positional grades breakdown.
Ironically, this is probably one of QB Cam Ward’s better performances of the season. But that’s also part of the problem. At best, this was a slightly above average outing, so to call that one of his best of the year is obviously concerning.
Ward's ball placement continues to be a recurring issue that doesn’t seem to be getting any better, and it cost him on the interception that was thrown slightly behind the receiver.
That’s the type of margin of error that he got away with in college, but he’s quickly realizing that margin of error will cost you at this level, especially when targeting an elite corner like Denzel Ward.
He also had a horrendous miss late in the game on a wide open seam route to TE Daniel Bellinger. It would’ve been a walk in touchdown, but he fluttered it and it resulted in a missed opportunity that brought up 4th down.
Ward then made up for it the next couple of plays with some great throws and eventually got the team into the end zone. So in the end, that miss didn’t result in anything bad. But it is another example of what’s ultimately holding him back from being the player he wants to be.
Bad misses are gonna happen to every quarterback, but the great ones always make up for it. If he can continue doing that going forward, then he should be alright. Ward finished the game completing 20 of his 31 passes for 181 yards, and one interception.
RB Tony Pollard easily had his best day of the season , rushing for 129 yards and three touchdowns on 25 carries (5.2 YPC), while also adding 26 yards and three catches in the passing game.
The Memphis product is one of the Titans’ most intriguing trade candidates, and he certainly played like he’s trying to impress a contender enough to come get him.
The #Titans run game was an absolute wagon against Cleveland yesterday. Tennessee's offensive line and Tony Pollard put on a clinic all day pic.twitter.com/MfxXYs0Xu6
Whatever the case may be, he was phenomenal on Sunday and this grade reflects that.
This wasn’t one of this group’s better games. The tape is filled with poor routes, drops, and inconsistent effort at times. WR Carnell Tate led the way with 69 yards on five catches, but even he had a bad drop and another fumble that severely cost the team.
Tate is rapidly developing into a true number one wide receiver, but he has to fix some of the issues with his ball security after the catch. That’s now twice that’s happened this season and seems to be something he truly needs to work on this offseason.
As for everyone else, WRs Elic Ayomanor and Wan’Dale Robinson combined for just 51 yards and seven catches. Not exactly the type of performance to write home about, but Tate continues to be only real weapon this team can consistently rely on.
TE Gunnar Helm finally made his presence felt in the passing game, catching three passes for 24 yards, while Bellinger could’ve also had a touchdown but an inaccurate ball prevented that from happening.
The two also contributed to some nice runs throughout the game, so I think an average grade is more than fair in this case
The offensive line had a relatively solid game once again, allowing just one sack and nine pressures, according to PFF .
However, not being able to punch the ball in from the one yard line despite multiple tries is simply inexcusable. It’s not all on this group (some of the play calls were questionable), but had they been able to displace defenders off the ball, then there would’ve been more room to squeeze through for a yard.
With that said, they did play a big role in  Pollard having the best game of the season, so I’ll give them a C+ for their overall performance.
DT Jeffery Simmons once again had another solid outing, recording four tackles, two run stops, and two QB hits, while also impacting several other plays throughout the contest. DE Jermaine Johnson had another solid game as he continues to look more comfortable with each passing week. Johnson recorded four pressures, two tackles, and one run stop.
But aside from those two, it was a relatively quiet game from this group. And since Simmons and Johnson’s performances weren’t exactly dominant, I think an average grade suits their overall performance as a whole.
Rookie LB Anthony Hill Jr. continues to flash serious potential, totaling 12 tackles and one run stop, and one forced fumble while playing all 70 snaps on defense.
Unfortunately, he had a rough outing in the passing game, giving up 114 yards and nine catches on nine targets for 114 yards, per PFF .
LB Cedric Gray notably continues to see his snap count grow, totaling an identical 39 snaps as fellow LB Cody Barton. However, the two of them combined for just seven tackles, and one run stop, while allowing 22 yards on five targets in coverage.
Overall, it was nothing to write home about outside of a few plays from Hill, so I went with a C- here mostly due to their inconsistency in coverage.
You would think Browns rookie WR KC Concepcion was one of the top star receivers in the league with the way he looked on Sunday.
The former Texas A&M standout legitimately looking uncoverable at times, recording a whopping 129 yards on eight catches. The Titans are also fortunate that he dropped what would’ve likely been a big play for a touchdown, or his numbers would’ve looked even worse.
On a more positive note, CBs Cor’Dale Flott and CB Joshua Williams each had solid games, allowing a combined 18 yards on eight targets between the two of them. But aside from them two, QB DeShaun Watson picked this group apart with ease.
The Browns QB finished with 308 yards and one interception, while completing nearly 70 percent of his passes (25-of-36).
K Joey Slye was forced into double duty once P Tommy Townsend was knocked out with an injury, and he performed admirably in both. Slye went one-for-one in the kicking game while also landing his lone punt inside the 20.
Meanwhile, WR Chimere Dike cooled off after his incredible game in Indy, totaling just 61 yards on two kick returns and 14 yards during his lone punt return of the game.
Overall, it was a solid outing by this group. Slye’s unexpected versatility when needed most is what ultimately gives this group a B+.
Shaun is a longtime Titans fan who has years of experience in the field. He missed being on the team beat, and is here to change that. He also writes scripts for EA Sports' Madden games, where fans may have heard his work.

title: Titans Mock Draft: Examining Tennessee Taking a QB in the 2027 NFL Draft
full_text:
It's awfully early to be talking about mock drafts, I know. However, the 1-6 Tennessee Titans essentially confirmed all of our worst fears in yesterday's loss to the Cleveland Browns. The worst of all? Week 6's win looks more like a lucky break than a sign of progress right now.
Assuming things continue to trend in a downward direction, next year's draft will be pivotal for both the Titans' rebuild and Robert Saleh's tenure on the sideline. The 2026 draft was about taking playmakers to compliment the players in place.
The 2027 draft, on the other hand, would be about finding real difference makers if Tennessee keeps slipping. The possibility of taking a QB is unavoidable in that case.
NFLTradeRumors published their latest mock draft today in the wake of Week 7. By far the most controversial pick toward the top of the list is Tennessee taking QB Drew Mestamaker with their projected second overall pick.
That would mean the franchise lost faith in Cam Ward. It would mean that Robert Saleh's unending expressions of faith and confidence in the QB are misplaced. It would mean that the Titans are ready to embrace the new-QB process all over again, rolling the dice once more.
If that feels soon, it's because it is. All the same, Ward is trending in all the wrong directions in his sophomore season. In spite of an improved offensive line, a new coaching staff, and added weapons all around, the former first overall pick has taken a step back.
I do think Week 7 is too soon to be calling for the Titans to hit the reset button under center again. At the same time, Ward has struggled enough this season that I'm also not comfortable declaring that this possibility won't be relevant by the end of the year.
We're not there yet, but taking a QB isn't out of the question.
Ward is a historically bad 4-20 in his first 24 starts with the Titans. You can point the finger at OC Brian Daboll for some of his struggles, but I recall doing the same thing last season with Brian Callahan and Bo Hardegree. Somehow, Ward looks worse with Daboll.
Up to now, Ward has thrown four touchdowns to five interceptions. His QBR is 41.5 (28th in the league, per ESPN ), and the QB sits at 1,179 yards total. It's only year two, I know, but Ward isn't remotely on pace to match what was deemed a fair rookie season given the circumstances.
In the case that these trends continue and a new QB is on the table, it'd be hard to do better than Mestemaker given the current pool. What's more, you could justify the pick given Tennessee's current offensive makeup.
Mestemaker is currently on a ridiculous run as a junior with Oklahoma State. He's thrown for 20 touchdowns with the Cowboys, tallying 2,326 yards through seven games and building one of the most well-known highlight reels in college football this year.
His deep accuracy is unique in the 2027 class. Mestemaker's six interceptions are less a blemish and more a result of his leading one of the most effective offenses in the sport. He's second in passing yards in the nation, and fourth in touchdowns through the air.
Ward not working out in Nashville would be a nightmare for general manager Mike Borgonzi, but the silver lining is blaring. The Titans brought in Wan'Dale Robinson and Carnell Tate to catch passes. Their rebuilt offensive line, again, has taken massive leaps this year. OT JC Latham has been a bonafide star.
For as bad as Tennessee has been for years now, a new passer would be hard pressed to ask for a better scenario to step into. If this mock is a sign of things to come and the Titans start trending toward a QB, it's something fans should embrace.
But that's if - and only if - Ward continues to tick down. Barring a disaster, the former Miami Hurricane (who was a fifth-year college sensation in his own right), will have the rest of this season to prove his process. Beyond that, though?
I'd be less than sure of his safety blanket under center. QB is the most important position in the NFL, but it's also the most volatile.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: How Titans' Constant Goal Line Blunders Reveal Critical, Game-Losing Issues on Offense
full_text:
For the second time this season, the Tennessee Titans' offense knocked on the goal line less than a yard away from the end zone and was denied on four attempts.
Early in the second quarter, RB Tony Pollard made a leaping dive at the goal line, muscling his way to paydirt against teeming Browns defenders for a Titans touchdown. Briefly, the broadcast score bug showed 20-7 in Tennessee's favor.
The original call on the field was reversed.
On 2nd and goal from less than a yard out, 6'2" QB Cam Ward was shut down at the line of scrimmage. Next play, Ward bumbled around the pocket and decided not to throw, taking a sack for no loss.
Now staring at a 4th and goal, the Titans' offense trotted back onto the field. Pollard was stuffed yet again on a handoff up the middle, resulting in a turnover on downs. Cleveland reclaimed the ball and backed up on their goal line.
Heading into Week 7 against Cleveland, a struggling Titans' offense had only scored seven touchdowns all season. They were a yard away from their third touchdown of the day in less than two quarters.
The Titans wouldn't find the end zone again until the 58-second mark of the fourth quarter. Pollard topped off a late fourth-quarter drive with a touchdown, equalizing the game at 24-24. For the first time since 2022, Pollard accomplished a hat trick, three touchdowns in one game.
Pollard's scoring glory was short-lived.
Cleveland QB Deshaun Watson threw for 50 passing yards on three plays, dicing up the Titans' defense to set up a game-winning 32-yard field goal with under a minute left. The Browns climbed out of a 14-nothing deficit to defeat Tennessee in front of a home crowd desperate for a win.
Following the Titans' four straight misfired attempts at the goal line, Cleveland then scored 10 unanswered points. Tennessee's offense was unable to rekindle their momentum from earlier in the game.
While Tennessee's inability to score from less than a yard wasn't the sole reason for giving up an improbable 14-point lead to the Browns, it certainly altered their confidence on offense. Tennessee's next four offensive series would end in an interception, punt, fumble and punt. Cleveland would go onto outscore the Titans 20-10 after the first quarter.
Earlier in this season, in Week 4, the Titans failed to score on the goal line, which proved to be a game-swinging stop by the Baltimore defense. Early in the second quarter, Baltimore took a 14-7 lead. Tennessee drove nearly 70 yards down the field to set up a 1st and goal from the Ravens' eight-yard line to potentially tie the game.
Offensive coordinator Brian Daboll dialed up four-straight calls for Pollard to run up the middle. On fourth down from the two-yard line, Pollard was denied at the line of scrimmage .
It was an inexplicable sequence of poor play-calling. Daboll essentially called the same play four times in a row, leaving the Titans scoreless on their red zone trip.
The Ravens responded to their defense's stellar stop by driving 98 yards and scoring a touchdown to take a commanding 21-7 lead at home. A 14-point swing Tennessee wouldn't come back from. Similarly to Tennessee's loss to the Browns, the Titans' offense went without a touchdown until late in the fourth quarter.
In the end, Baltimore pulled off a narrow 24-18 win. The Ravens were scoreless in the second half. Their two-time MVP QB Lamar Jackson didn't return to the field after halftime due to an injury.
Through seven weeks, the Titans are tied with Pittsburgh for the fifth lowest touchdown percentage inside the red zone, according to Team Rankings . In 2026, the Titans scored a touchdown inside the 20 at a 47% clip, which is 10% worse than last season.
Tennessee has no go-to goal line scoring play. According to Chunkplay Stats , the Titans rank in the bottom 10 in goal-to-go touchdown rate and fourth-down conversion rate this season.
Although Pollard had a career day against the Browns, he's not a goal line brusier like the Ravens' RB Derrick Henry or the 49ers' RB Christian McCaffrey. Prior to playing Cleveland, Pollard had only scored one touchdown all season.
This season, Pollard has been handed the ball on 26 of Tennessee's 30 rushing attempts in the red zone. Daboll has made no effort for any other running back opportunities in the red zone. The Philadelphia Eagles have popularized a rugby-like formation with their QB Jalen Hurts. Behind Hurts are two players shoving the quarterback, diving across the goal line.
This play is known as the "tush push." The Titans haven't attempted a tush push this season.
Other teams like the Baltimore Ravens and Seattle Seahawks have experimented with the tush push by lining up a tight end under center, leveraging their larger frame to fight through opposing defenses.
Tennessee is yet to find a reliable scoring receiving threat this season. Talents like the Broncos' WR Courtland Sutton and the 49ers' WR Mike Evans have made careers out of their ability to score touchdowns on 50-50 jump situations.
According to Fantasy Pros , Ward is 13-27 passing in the red zone with four touchdowns and an interception.
His four red zone touchdown passes are to three different receivers; WR Wan'Dale Robinson is the only repeat scorer. Robinson hasn't scored a touchdown since Week 4 against Baltimore.
Other teams like the 49ers, Saints and Steelers often target their tight ends for red zone touchdowns. This season, Ward is 1-4 when targeting Titans' tight ends for zero touchdowns.
The Titans are directionless in the red zone, and it has directly resulted in two massive momentum-swinging outcomes that led to losses. It's hard not to wonder if the Titans could've scored at the goal line against Cleveland and Baltimore.
The Titans could have a salvageable 3-4 record. Instead, Tennessee is 1-6 with the playoffs virtually out of sight at this point.

A graduate from the University of Kentucky, he has previously been published by BloodHorse, KY Insider, and the Kentucky Kernel for multimedia sports coverage. title: Titans Mill: 2 Pressing Questions Raised by Tennessee's Defeat vs. Browns in Week 7
full_text:
Yesterday's matchup with the Cleveland Browns was supposed to be the Tennessee Titans' chance to prove a lot of people wrong. It was supposed to be the Titans' chance to break what is nearly a four-year drought without two straight wins.
It was supposed to be a lot of good things for Tennessee, who lost 27-24. That's a bad thing.
Much can be taken from the team's sixth loss, but in today's Titans Mill, I want to focus on two questions that were raised as a result of the team's shortcomings in Week 7. Starting with Cam Ward should be no surprise to Titans fans.
Just how long can Tennessee leave Ward out there to struggle? Robert Saleh has denied the possibility of benching Ward again and again - today, he even said that anyone blaming yesterday's defeat on Ward is "just trying to make ---- up."
The loss wasn't entirely Ward's fault by any stretch, but there's no other way to spin it: The QB has been subpar for weeks now.
Week 7 marked Ward's fifth straight game with an interception. It was the second of his last three games without a score, and the sixth of seven games this season in which Ward failed to break 185 yards passing. Those are not franchise numbers.
Ward is comfortably on pace to shatter the record for most losses for a QB in their first two seasons in the NFL, per PFF. Ward has 20 losses (and four wins). The record is 22. Ward has 10 more games left.
Waiting on development is one thing, but ignoring regression is another. Ward is regressing, and it's worth asking now more than ever what Tennessee plans to do if he continues to come up short.
On defense is where the other worry becomes apparent. In the Titans' Week 6 victory, Saleh's defensive line leveled six sacks against the Indianapolis Colts, with DT Jeffery Simmons forcing a critical fumble in the process.
Yesterday against Cleveland, that same unit managed just one sack. The Browns went on to stack up 491 total yards in a performance that was the night to last week's day for Tennessee's defense. CB Cor'Dale Flott managed to come down with a pick, and LB Anthony Hill Jr. caused a fumble.
But the d-line struggled to generate any pressure as the game went on, and QB Deshaun Watson had his way on the day as a result. Saleh said the Titans' tackling "sucked" vs. Cleveland, so at least he's aware of the problem here.
It was still a massive step back for a unit that looked like they'd broken the barrier, nonetheless. It's not a complete defensive picture by any means, but where other units seem to be improving (or at least finding stability), the d-line is falling behind.

title: Robert Saleh Denies Titans Have a QB Problem After Browns Loss, But Cam Ward's Stats Beg to Differ
full_text:
Any excitement that the Tennessee Titans earned from their Week 6 win over the Indianapolis Colts was more than betrayed in today's defeat. The Titans had the Cleveland Browns right where they wanted them in the first quarter, jumping out to a 14-0 lead through seven minutes.
What followed was a slow meltdown spelled by little to no consistent momentum. The offense scored late in the fourth quarter (on the ground, unsurprisingly), only for the Browns to march back down the field and easily secure a game-winning field goal, taking the victory 27-24.
The defense's regression is one thing, and that's issue is worth an entirely different discussion. But the hot topic right now is Cam Ward. More specifically, the topic is Ward's place in this offense.
Do the Titans have a QB problem? Robert Saleh doesn't think so, but Ward's numbers don't lie.
"I don't think it's a quarterback problem," Saleh said, when asked about the blame that has to go around as a result of the offense's consistent failures. "It's [the blame] all the way across the board. He [Ward] missed some throws that he's gotta make... but overall, there's enough to go around for everybody."
But who, exactly? Carnell Tate's fumble is the obvious example, but his five receptions for 69 yards led the team. The rookie WR also came down with a contested catch in the red zone that led to an easy game-tying score in the fourth quarter.
Tony Pollard did his part, scoring a tied-career-high three touchdowns and rushing for 129 yards. Ward was only sacked once today - the offensive line made good on their dues, too.
That leaves Ward himself. Look no further than the stat sheet for evidence that Tennessee's biggest issue is unfortunately under center.
Ward went 20/31 through the air, throwing an interception for the fifth week in a row. He's only thrown four touchdowns on the season up to now. Against Cleveland, the former first overall pick once again came short of 200 yards (with 181), while Deshaun Watson broke 300 for the other team.
Oh, and Ward didn't throw a score. We're past the point of patience and firmly in the realm of undeniable regression. With better protection and more playmaking options, Ward is worse this season than he was as a rookie.
The Titans wouldn't be 7-0 if Ward had improved; that isn't the point here. But could Tennessee have beaten the Giants in Week 3 if Ward hadn't thrown a pick on the goal line? Would the Titans have stood a chance against the Texans two weeks ago if the offense had generated a single touchdown?
Three or four wins would be a lot better than one and, even for the defense's faults, that unit has generated opportunities for the offense to pitch in. Even today, in allowing 27 points, the Titans had two takeaways.
If that doesn't sound like a QB problem, what is? The sooner Coach Saleh accepts that and opens the door to Ward's job, the sooner we see what the Miami product is made of when he's actually fighting for something in Nashville.
Until then, this is the product fans will have to get used to.

title: 3 Major Takeaways From Titans' Heartbreaking Home Loss to Browns: Tony Pollard's Career Game Not Enough
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans entered today's matchup with the Cleveland Browns coming off their first win of the season. Momentum like that can't be wasted for a 1-5 team and a first-year head coach with his back against the wall.
That makes today's result the most disappointing of the year so far. The Titans fall to 1-6 at home in a more than winnable game. Between blown leads and lapses on either side of the ball, it's hard not to feel worse than ever about this franchise.
Here are our three major takeaways from the Titans' 27-24 loss, starting with a bright spot.
Pollard had a career game against the Cleveland Browns last season. His 161 yards and two scores propelled Tennessee to a late-season victory on the road.
Today, with both Tyjae Spears and Nick Singleton inactive, the Titans' RB1 had himself another huge day. Pollard punched in three touchdowns (tied for a career high), chalking up 129 yards on 25 carries. Pollard added 26 yards receiving to his total.
In the final year of his contract, Pollard has been one of Tennessee's most reliable weapons. His future in Nashville remains unsure. However, he'll be forced to carry a massive load so long as Ward and this offense fail to generate momentum elsewhere.
Even in a loss, Pollard had his best game of the 2026 season against Cleveland, and one of the best games of his career. The 29-year old deserves real flowers.
After a slow start to his first campaign as a Titan, offseason pickup Cor'Dale Flott had his second straight interception today.
Flott picked off Deshaun Watson in the first quarter, lending the Titans some of the early momentum that allowed Tennessee to pull out to a 14-0 lead. That lead was lost, brought to a tie, and then Tennessee's defense fell apart on the final drive, ultimately losing. Deshaun Watson threw for an inexcusable 308 yards.
Still, especially compared to fellow signee Alontae Taylor's struggles in the secondary, Flott's rising ability to force turnovers is a promising trend for Saleh's defense. The d-line looked worse, and the Browns put up 27 points.
Flott gets credit nonetheless for his singular ability to force a turnover. You take what you can get, especially in a game like this one.
It would've been hard for Ward to fall short of his 11/22, 102-yard performance from last week's contest against the Indianapolis Colts. He got better today, but the Titans still need more from their QB.
Ward went 20/31 through the air for no scores, one interception, and of course, a loss. The second-year QB made a few passes that had to be blamed on his WRs. Carnell Tate fumbled, Wan'Dale Robinson dropped. It wasn't all on Ward today.
But Tennessee's passer still failed to make up for the defense's shortcomings today, with 181 yards. Where Saleh's defense won in spite of the offense last week, Ward failed to make up the necessary ground when the Browns' offense pulled away today.
The defense fell apart on the final drive, but are the Titans even in that position if Tennessee capitalizes on a goal-line opportunity to take a two-score lead in the first half? The Titans need more from everyone, though especially their first overall pick.

title: The 1 Obvious Way Titans Can Capitalize on Best First Half of Season and Beat the Browns
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans scored 14 points in the first seven minutes of today's game. Nissan Stadium was rocking at an undeniable season-high, and the home team appeared to be in full control of the contest against the Cleveland Browns.
As things typically go with the 2026 Titans, that momentum didn't last for the entire half. One goal-line stand by Cleveland was the difference between Tennessee retaking a two-touchdown lead early in the second quarter. What could've been a 21-7 advantage for the Titans melted into a 17-14 deficit at the half.
But this was still easily the team's best first half of the year, and there's plenty of reason to think that the Titans can build on that in the second period. Cleveland's offense is likely to keep testing Tennessee's defense through the air - Cor'Dale Flott already has a pick, but the Titans are on their heels.
A successful second half - and historic second straight win - is within reach for Robert Saleh's Titans. The team just needs to play to their strengths in the second half, and be unafraid of keeping their foot on the pedal if Tennessee pulls back into the lead.
That strength is clear: Tony Pollard is having a dominant game. Scheme for the veteran at all costs.
Cam Ward's second-quarter interception, thrown behind WR Elic Ayomanor and right into the hands of CB Denzel Ward, should tell the Titans everything they need to know about the offense today. Once again, the passing game isn't here, at least not reliably.
Pollard, on the other hand, has 16 carries for 92 yards and two touchdowns. He had a third score reversed, which led to that unfortunate fourth-down stand. Per PFF, he had the most first-quarter yards of any RB this season, with 87.
Still, this is Pollard's second breakout performance vs. the Browns in a row. Last December, the back rushed for a career-high 161 yards and two touchdown in a Tennessee victory. Something about this matchup works for Pollard, and the Titans shouldn't shy away from that.
The obvious complication here is the absence of both Tyjae Spears and Nick Singleton in the backfield. The Titans are trotting out fourth-string RB Michael Carter, who has yet to be trusted with a carry in today's matchup.
Again, Ward passing 7/11 for 58 yards, the aforementioned interception, and no scores, leaves Tennessee with little choice in the matter. As Cleveland's offense starts to pick up steam, it will likely be up to Pollard to help extend Titans drives in the final two quarters.
Trade candidate or not, our complaints about Pollard being used as a workhorse in this offense are moot today. The Titans need a win, and so long as Pollard is effective, he's the key.
